리뷰 원문 (agent-625ee0, `/code-review max --fix`, 15건 중 열둘 고침)

열 갈래로 보고 검증을 돌렸다. 관문은 초록이다(`cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`,
시험 1438 + CLI 539).

**고친 열둘**

1. `src/report.rs:363` — `torn_ids` 가 묶음이 선 **id 를 통째로** 뺐다. 그러면 그 id 를
   묶음과 나눠 쓴 **일 줄**까지 제 답을 잃고 접은 지도로 돌아간다. 재현: `argos-0002`
   일 줄이 미룬 에픽 `argos-e001` 에 들고, 같은 id 의 산 에픽 줄이 하나. `status` 는
   `deferred count 2`, `show --deferred` 는 한 줄, `ready` 는 `{"ready":[],"held":[]}`,
   기본 `show` 는 산 줄로 그렸다 — 표면 넷에 답 셋. 되묻지 못하는 것은 묶음 **줄**이다.
2. `src/nav.rs:250` — `Index::deferred_root` 만 id 로 남아, 곁의 `epic_of`·`milestone_of`
   가 자리로 답하는 것과 갈렸다. `show --all --tree` 가 어느 줄에도 `미룸` 을 안 달고
   평평한 `show --all` 은 앞줄에 달았다. 탐색기 숨김 토글·스피너·상세 표가 같이 갈렸다.
   `Index::shelved_at(at)` 을 더해 옮겼고, `deferred_root(id)` 는 막는 줄에만 남겼다.
3. `src/report.rs:1864` — `counted` 의 값싼 문을 `Shelf::nearest` 로 바꾼 것이 멤버 1만
   9천짜리 저장소의 `moai status` 에 98ms 를 얹었다. 값을 치르는 것은 흔한 **계획 안인**
   멤버 쪽이다 — 멈출 미룸이 없어 사슬을 끝까지 탄다. `off_rows` 가 줄 바늘로 한 번
   담고 문은 그것을 짚는다.
4. `src/report.rs:1777` — `Stand::deferred` 만 `roots.contains_key` 에 남아 한 `Stand`
   의 두 쪽이 다른 자로 셌다. 보드가 `0/2 미룬 1 미룸` 을 낸다.
5. `src/report.rs:3378` — `closable` 이 `unblocked_pick` 과 같은 물음(`has_open_child`)
   을 id 로 물었다. 술어 하나를 둘이 나눠 쓰게 했다.
6. `src/cmd/show.rs:281` — 트리의 남기는 자가 id 집합이었다. 같은 거르개에 목록은
   `미룸 1 숨김` 을 달고 트리는 그 줄을 그리며 아무 말도 안 했다.
7. `src/report.rs:299` — 읽은 칸이 done 인 묶음을 id 로 지워, 한 줄이 done 이라는 이유로
   같은 id 의 다른 묶음 줄까지 계획 안으로 돌아왔다. 값도 `미룬 묶음 수 × 줄 수` 였다.
8. `src/report.rs:259` — `debug_assert_eq!` 는 릴리스에서 접히고 그 뒤 `zip` 이 말없이
   자른다. 살려 뒀다.
9. `src/report.rs:6863` — 새 무작위 대조가 묶음 선 id 를 통째로 건너뛰어 1번을 구조로
   못 잡았다. 건너뛰는 것을 묶음 줄로 좁히고, CLI 회귀 시험을 더했다.
10. `src/tui/mod.rs:332` — 성한 저장소에서 `Ground.milestone` 을 String 으로 베끼고
    `torn_ids` 를 두 번 지었다. `kinds.len() == all.len()` 이면 id 가 다 다르다.
11. `src/report.rs:258` — `fold_roots` 가 `folded_by_id` 를 글자째 베꼈다. `fold_by_id`
    하나로 모았다.
12. `src/report.rs:197` — `put_off_in` 이 마지막 부르는 자를 잃었다. 걷어냈다.

**넘긴 셋**

13. `src/hook.rs:5820` — 훅의 `is_review` 가 네 자리에서 접은 지도를 짚는데, 짝인 초점
    (`wip` → `started`)은 이 회차에 줄로 옮겼다. hook.rs 는 옆 세션이 쥐어 범위 밖이다.
14. `src/report.rs:424` — `deferred_sources_in` 이 그 id 를 든 줄 전부의 걸음을 합치는데,
    이제 id 밖에 없는 표면은 뒷줄이 답한다. `show X --json` 이 `shelved_by: E2` 라 하고
    `ready` 는 `moai defer E1 E2 --undo` 를 낸다.
15. `report.rs:4656` 의 `duplicate_id` 경고에 `hint` 가 없다. 곁의 `unreadable_line` 에는
    있다.

title: 도로 집을 곳도 뒷줄이 댄다 — `deferred_sources_in` 이 그 id 의 줄 전부를 합친다
`duplicate_id` 경고가 고칠 명령을 안 댄다

text:
내가 정한 것 — 열둘을 받고 셋을 넘겼다.

**까닭 하나를 고쳐 받았다.** 리뷰 15번은 "도구 안에 빠져나갈 길이 없다" 가 틀렸다며
`moai rm <id>` 가 중복 id 에서 듣고 쓰기 문이 곧 열린다고 적었다. 재 봤다 — 맞다. 다만
`rm` 은 **앞줄**을 지운다(재현: 쌍둥이 둘에 `rm argos-0002` → `앞줄` 하나만 지워지고
`add` 가 곧 exit 0). 남기고 싶은 것이 앞줄이면 그 길은 그것을 지우는 길이라, 길이 있다는
것과 고르는 길이 있다는 것은 다르다. 이 고친 까닭으로 받았고 CHANGELOG 도 그 말을 뺐다.

**넘긴 셋을 어디로 보냈나**

- 13번(훅의 `is_review` 네 자리) → `moai-jk2u.ipf` 에 적었다. 그 이슈가 이미 "훅이 소속을
  아직 id 로 묻는다" 이고, hook.rs 가 풀리는 회차에 함께 본다
- 14번(`deferred_sources_in` 의 합집합) → `moai-kg6g` 으로 세웠다. 이 회차의 결정이 연
  자리라 이 에픽의 멤버다 — 넘긴 채 두면 `show <id>` 와 `ready` 가 서로 다른 미룸을 댄다
- 15번(`duplicate_id` 에 `hint` 없음) → idea `moai-5v5c`. 이 에픽이 내건 것과 무관하고
  한 줄짜리다

**높은 자리 하나도 넘어왔다.** 리뷰가 마지막에 댄 것 — 조상과 `members_in` 을 자리로
풀면 `torn_ids`·`shelved_at_line`·묶음 갈래가 통째로 없어진다 — 은 `moai-pth7` 이 이미
적어 둔 그 길이다. 그쪽에 이번 회차의 값을 적었다.

리뷰 moai-u3ta.0so 13번이 자리를 하나 더 댄다 (hook.rs 가 옆 세션에 잡혀 이 회차에서는 못 고쳤다).

`hook.rs` 의 `is_review` 가 네 자리에서 `report::put_off`(id 로 접은 지도)를 짚는다.
그런데 짝인 초점 `report::wip` → `started` 는 moai-u3ta 에서 줄마다 답하게 옮겼다.
`is_review` 위의 주석이 둘을 한 답으로 못박고 있으니, 지금은 그 주석이 거짓이다.

- 리뷰 줄의 id 가 두 번 서고 앞줄은 산 채 `in_progress`, 뒷줄은 미룬 에픽 밑이면
- `wip` 은 앞줄을 초점에 드는데 `is_review` 는 접은 지도를 읽어 거짓을 낸다
- `guard_review` 가 지금 쥐고 있는 그 리뷰를 "리뷰를 세우라" 며 막고, 그 파일의 쓰기는
  `duplicate_id` 가 다 거절하므로 시킨 대로 할 수도 없다

고칠 재료는 이미 섰다 — `report::shelved`·`shelved_in` 이 `all` 과 자리가 같은 배열을
낸다. 네 자리가 줄의 자리를 들고 그것을 짚으면 된다.

moai-u3ta 를 마치고 나서 — 이 길이 값을 두 번 더 받았다.

리뷰 moai-u3ta.0so 가 마지막에 댄 높은 자리가 이것과 같은 말이다: 조상과 `members_in`
을 자리로 풀면 `torn_ids`·`shelved_at_line`·묶음 갈래가 통째로 없어진다.

이 회차가 실제로 치른 값 —

- `torn_ids`·`shelved_at_line`·`Where.torn`·`Where.milestone`·`Ground.torn`·
  `Ground.milestone` 이 새로 섰다. 전부 "지도가 든 답이 이 줄의 것인가" 를 묻는 데만 쓴다
- `settled_groups` 가 id 로 재는 읽은 칸 때문에 **묶음 줄 하나가 아직 접은 지도로 간다**.
  그 갈래를 잘못 그어 표면 넷이 세 답을 낸 것이 리뷰 1번이다 — 이 회차에서 가장 무거운
  버그가 그 갈래에서 나왔다
- `Where::from_soil` 과 `Ground::in_soil` 이 성한 저장소를 가려내려고 `kinds.len() ==
  all.len()` 이라는 증인을 새로 든다

에픽 moai-jk2u 의 멤버가 이제 여섯이고(`moai-5km5`·`moai-jk2u.ipf`·`moai-kg6g` 이 열려
있다), 셋 다 같은 뿌리다. 펼치기 전에 잴 것으로 적어 둔 "이 길이 moai-jk2u 의 멤버를
정말 다 덮는가" 에 답할 재료가 이제 모였다.
model: anthropic/opus-5 (high — 미룸 지도가 쌍둥이를 가르지 못하던 자리)
model: anthropic/opus-5 tokens=381414 (max — 게이트를 건드린 읽기 경로, 리뷰 서브에이전트가 쓴 값)

note: 리뷰 열다섯 중 열둘을 받고 셋을 넘겼다. 가장 무거운 것은 `torn_ids` 가 묶음이 선 id 를 통째로 빼 표면 넷이 세 답을 내던 자리고, `counted` 의 98ms 를 `off_rows` 로 도로 세웠다. 넘긴 셋은 moai-jk2u.ipf(훅의 네 자리)·moai-kg6g(`deferred_sources_in` 의 합집합)·idea moai-5v5c(`duplicate_id` 힌트)로 갔다.

text: Next: moai-u3ta 와 그 리뷰 moai-u3ta.0so 가 develop 에 e11eb9d 로 들어갔다. 미룸은 이제 줄마다 답한다 — 접는 자는 `fold_roots` 하나고, id 밖에 없는 표면은 **뒷줄이 이긴다**(2026-09-23 사용자 결정). 에픽은 셋이 열려 있다 — moai-jk2u.ipf(훅의 네 자리, src/hook.rs 를 옆이 쥐어 못 했다. 리뷰가 자리를 하나 더 댔다), moai-5km5(제 epic 을 안 적은 앞줄이 뒷줄의 것을 입는다), moai-kg6g(`deferred_sources_in` 이 그 id 의 줄 전부를 합쳐 이번 결정의 계약 밖에 섰다). 앞의 둘은 groups() 가 내는 꼴이 바뀌어야 닫히므로 hook 파일이 풀리는 회차에 함께 본다. moai-kg6g 은 되돌리기 전에 moai-phzi 가 도로 열리지 않는지 재고 들어간다. 이 갈래가 세 회차 잇달아 p1 을 스스로 냈고, 이번 회차에 리뷰가 가장 무겁게 잡은 것도 같은 뿌리(묶음 줄 하나가 아직 접은 지도로 간다)라 moai-pth7 에 값을 적어 뒀다.

title: 릴리스 밖으로 낸 줄이 경고 둘을 세운다

text:
Review complete. All findings verified in real shells (sh/bash/dash) and against the committed manifest.

1. src/skill.rs:310 — The wrapper, not moai, now writes the hook's real stdout, so it takes the SIGPIPE moai used to swallow and ends the hook on 141 instead of 0 — breaking the line's own stated contract that every branch exits 0.
   Failure: Reader closes the hook's stdout before the shell's `printf` runs (claude cancelling, `| head`). Measured with a moai-faithful fixture (ignores SIGPIPE, exits 0): develop's line -> rc 0; this diff's line -> killed by signal 13 (rc 141) in both dash and bash. Per the doc's own table only exit 2 was ever measured against the client; 141 is unmeasured, and exit 2 is a hard gate on every tool call. FIXED: `trap 'exit 0' PIPE` after the existence guard (measured back to 0 on sh/bash/dash).

2. src/skill.rs:310 — `[ -z "$o" ] || printf '%s\n' "$o"` is the last command of an AND-OR list — the one position `set -e` does not exempt — so a stdout write error that delivers no signal ends the hook on 1 before `exit 0` is reached, on the ordinary success path.
   Failure: `set -e` shell, stdout not writable (EBADF/ENOSPC/read-only fd; no signal, so the PIPE trap never fires). Measured with a healthy `live` fixture: develop's line -> rc 0 on sh/bash/dash; this diff's line -> rc 1 on all three (`printf: I/O error` / `write error: Bad file descriptor`). Contradicts CHANGELOG.md:333 ("Nothing is blocked and the exit code is still 0, even under `set -e`") added by this same change. FIXED: `|| :` on that clause (rc back to 0 on all three).

3. src/skill.rs:312 — The notice `printf` has the same `set -e` exposure (pre-existing, but the line is under review and the contract is restated in this diff).
   Failure: `set -e` + unwritable stdout + a binary that cannot run (0644 fixture, exit 126): develop's line and this diff's both exited 1 on sh/bash/dash. FIXED: `|| :` on the notice printf too; the shipped line is now rc 0 in all 24 shell x fixture x flag combinations.

4. src/skill.rs:310 — `o=$(...)` moves the answer out of the data path: bytes moai has already written now sit in the wrapper's buffer and die with it, where the old line had already delivered them to claude's pipe.
   Failure: The manifest's own `timeout: 15` kills the hook process group (the doc measured this). A hook that prints a `deny` and then blocks (store lock held by one of this repo's six or seven sessions, git on a large history) delivered 53-82 bytes under the old line and delivers 0 under the new one — the refused write goes through. NOT FIXED: the capture is the recorded 2026-09-23 user decision; the doc's timeout paragraph, written for the old shape, now says so explicitly and flags it for the stamp work.

5. src/cmd/hook.rs:751 — `once_per_session` commits its marker to disk inside `cmd::run`, before the answer leaves the wrapper — so the same kill loses the board for the whole session, not for one call.
   Failure: `user-prompt-submit` builds the 17KB board, `once_per_session` writes the `board` marker, `print` emits the JSON, the wrapper is killed before its `printf`. The marker is on disk, so every later prompt in that session returns `Pass` and the board is never retried — and the `$o` guard cannot help, because nothing was written. A lost `deny` is re-derived next call; this is not. NOT FIXED (reported); noted in the main.rs comment, which previously accounted only for "this command's output".

6. src/skill.rs:311 — `[ -n "$o" ]` suppresses the notice for 126/127/2 as well — exits where the doc itself says stdout is guaranteed empty — and because the marker sits inside the suppressed group, nothing is recorded either: it is permanent silence, not a once-per-session throttle.
   Failure: `exe_name` falls back to the bare name `moai` when the path is not `quotable` or PATH's moai is the same file, and CLAUDE.md records that PATH's `moai` here is the OLD project's binary. Measured: a fixture doing `echo 'usage: ...'; exit 64` prints that text to claude as the hook's answer, emits no `systemMessage`, writes no marker, forever. NOT FIXED: the diff's own measurement (two objects on one hook's stdout are both discarded) says appending a notice after any stdout would lose both, so staying silent is defensible; flagged for the owner.

7. src/skill.rs:311 — `[ -n "$o" ]` is a proxy for "moai produced a decision" and the two are not the same predicate: a truncated decision counts as spoken, and a whitespace-only stdout is read two different ways.
   Failure: SIGKILL mid-write of a >PIPE_BUF line leaves `$o` = `{"hookSpecificOutp` — non-empty, so the fragment is forwarded and the notice withheld; claude cannot parse it and the write proceeds, with nothing said. Measured on sh/dash/bash: `printf ' '; exit 2` -> one space, no notice; `printf '\n\n'; exit 137` -> nothing forwarded AND the notice fires (command substitution already stripped the newlines). NOT FIXED (design); a shape test (`case "$o" in '{'*)`) would separate them.

8. src/main.rs:151 — The reorder is fail-open for the window it guards: a kill between `cmd::run` returning and `print(&lines)` now means an empty stdout, so the wrapper emits the notice and the tool RUNS — where the old order had already delivered the deny.
   Failure: PreToolUse decides `deny`; moai is SIGKILLed (container OOM, documented 2026-09-20 history) before `print`. Exit 137, stdout empty, wrapper prints only `systemMessage`, exit 0 -> per the diff's measured table the tool runs. The `$o` guard alone already covered "deny then panic", so the reorder adds no coverage for the named bug while widening this window. NOT FIXED: recorded user decision; the cost is now written down where it was only half written down.

9. src/main.rs:151 — Nothing pinned the two invariants the whole hook contract rests on — "the four notice fns write only to stderr" and "`print(&lines)` stands last" — and no behaviour test can, because every test reads the two streams through `Command::output()`.
   Failure: One `outln!` added to `carried`/`unjournaled`/`unread_journals`/`redirected` (the macro is in the same file, in scope) puts a non-JSON line ahead of the hook's verdict; claude discards the verdict, `deny` included, and every test stays green. FIXED: added `tests::the_notices_never_reach_stdout_and_print_stands_last`, a source scan in the shape of `git::tests::git_is_spawned_only_through_command`.

10. src/skill.rs:310 — `$(...)` ends at EOF on the pipe, not at moai's exit, so any future child holding fd 1 would wedge every hook until the 15s timeout — the exact hazard `merge_driver::Said` already abandoned pipes to avoid — and nothing guarded it.
    Failure: One `Stdio::inherit()` (or a grandchild keeping fd 1, e.g. a PATH shim of the mise/asdf/direnv shape named in `Said`'s doc) makes `o=$("$exe" hook pre-tool-use)` block past moai's own exit; claude then group-kills at 15s and the decision is lost, on every watched tool call. Clean today (every spawn site is piped or file-redirected). FIXED: added `skill::tests::nothing_hands_its_stdout_down_to_a_child`, plus the constraint in the doc.

11. src/skill.rs:128 — "passing the answer through untouched" (CHANGELOG) and "그대로 흘려보낸다" (doc) are measurably false: command substitution strips ALL trailing newlines, not one, and drops NUL bytes — on bash adding its own warning line to the hook's stderr.
    Failure: Measured against the shipped line: `{"ok":true}\n\n\n` (14 B) comes back as `{"ok":true}\n` (12 B); `{"a":1}\nx\0y\n` (12 B) comes back as 11 B with the NUL gone. Safe today only because `cmd::hook::run` returns exactly one line and serde escapes U+0000. FIXED: CHANGELOG and doc now state the real rule; added a `blank` fixture that pins the collapse.

12. src/skill.rs:987 — The one assertion that pinned "the hook line does not change the binary's stdout by one byte" was rewritten rather than restated — `live` was given a trailing newline and the old body came back as `bare`, whose assertion now blesses a newline being appended — while the contract sentence above it was left standing.
    Failure: No fixture emitted two trailing newlines or a NUL, so the two cases where the line really does change bytes had no cover, and a future change to the `printf` format would still read as consistent with the comment. FIXED: contract comment rewritten to the real rule (interior bytes unchanged, tail normalised to one newline) with each of the four fixtures named against the shape it pins.

13. src/skill.rs:1128 — The `set -e` arm of the test never reached any of the new code — only `lost` and `dead` ran with `-ec` — which is exactly the square the exit-1 regression above lived in.
    Failure: The suite was green while dash, bash and sh all returned 1 for `live` under `-ec` with an unwritable stdout. FIXED: `closed()` now takes flags and a signal/write-error mode, and asserts exit 0 for both the answer path and the notice path under `-c` and `-ec` on all three shells.

14. src/skill.rs:114 — The cost paragraph named the wrong mechanism and the wrong arithmetic, and retracted a statement that is still true: `o=$(simple command)` adds no process at all.
    Failure: `strace -f -c`: dash is one child (`vfork`) in both arms with `pipe2` 0 -> 1; bash is `clone` 310 in both arms with `pipe2` 232 -> 233. So "fork 하나" is false, "프로세스를 안 늘린다" should not have been retracted, and 0.30/28 is 1.07% not 1.2%. Worse, `/bin/true` emits 0 bytes, so the quoted figure is a floor, not the cost: measured in dash over 60 runs, 0 B and 17.5 KB are about +0.5 ms while 1 MB is about +36 ms. FIXED: paragraph rewritten around the pipe + read, arithmetic corrected, floor-vs-curve stated, and the board's lack of a length cap noted.

15. src/cmd/mod.rs:159 — Four doc sites went stale in ways the repo explicitly guards against, including the pair that `cmd::runnable`'s own comment says must be changed together, plus Korean term-table violations on newly written lines.
    Failure: `cmd::runnable` and `tests/cli.rs::skill_status_notices_a_vanished_hook_binary` both still said the notice fires on any non-0/1 exit with no mention of the empty-stdout condition — and that doc names the pairing ("한쪽만 고치면 둘이 갈린다"); both halves went stale together. The bold lead at src/skill.rs:91 and the CHANGELOG lead both stated the un-narrowed rule, and the "정상 갈래" paragraph still claimed the `printf` runs only inside the `case`. docs/korean-terms.md fixes cost as `비용` (`값` is the banned form) and 판(회차) as `번/때/경우`; the new lines used `치르는 값`, `드는 값`, `받는 값` and `판`. ALL FIXED.

## What was fixed

Working tree (uncommitted), on top of `develop...HEAD`:

- **`src/skill.rs` `fn command`** — the generated hook one-liner gained `trap 'exit 0' PIPE` (after the existence guard, so `hook_exe`'s `command -v -- "` prefix parse still works — putting it first broke `the_hook_exe_round_trips_through_the_manifest`) and `|| :` on both the answer `printf` and the notice `printf`. The shipped line is now exit 0 in all 24 shell x fixture x flag combinations I ran, including the pre-existing `set -e` + unwritable-stdout hole that `develop` also had.
- **Tests** — `blank` fixture (multi-trailing-newline collapse), a `closed()` runner covering real SIGPIPE and signal-less write failure under `-c` and `-ec`, `main.rs::the_notices_never_reach_stdout_and_print_stands_last`, `skill::nothing_hands_its_stdout_down_to_a_child`.
- **Docs** — corrected the fork/percentage/`/bin/true` claims, the "untouched" claims (CHANGELOG + doc), the stale bold leads in `src/skill.rs` and CHANGELOG, the `cmd::runnable` <-> `tests/cli.rs` pair, the test's byte-identity contract sentence, the tty-ordering and `once_per_session` costs of the `main.rs` reorder, and the Korean term-table violations.
- `.claude/moai-plugin/` re-blessed (`MOAI_BLESS=1`, version now `939.492.588`).

Verification: `cargo test` 1438 + 537 pass, `cargo fmt --check` clean, `cargo clippy --all-targets` zero warnings, and every branch of the committed manifest re-run in `sh`/`bash`/`dash`.

## What was skipped, and why

Findings 4-8 are the design of the change itself (`o=$(...)` capture and the `print`-last reorder), both recorded as 2026-09-23 user decisions with measurements attached. Reversing them is a behaviour change, so I wrote the costs down where they were previously half-written rather than undoing them. Two are worth a follow-up issue: **the buffered answer dies with a process-group kill** (measured: old line delivered the `deny`, new line delivers 0 bytes) and **`once_per_session` burns its marker inside `cmd::run`**, which turns that same kill into a session-long loss of the board. Also not fixed: the marker being planted before the notice `printf` (pre-existing, from `moai-f7up`) means a failed notice write silences that binary/event/exit-code for the session.

One operational note the branch does not state: the hook line points at the **main checkout's** `target/release/moai`, so nothing here takes effect until someone rebuilds release and re-runs `moai skill install` after the merge.

title: 미룸의 뿌리를 아직 id 로 묻는다

text:
moai-jk2u.ipf 가 훅을 줄에 묻게 옮겼지만 **이 줄은 그대로 남았다** — 리뷰 moai-jk2u.35i 1번이
그것을 실물로 재현했다. `Ties::epic_of` 는 `joined_in` 위에 서고, `joined_in` 은 제 `epic` 을
안 적은 줄에서 여전히 지도로 되돌아간다. 그 지도가 이 이슈의 자리다.

판 (고친 뒤의 바이너리에서 그대로 선다):

    argos-e001 epic / argos-e002 epic
    argos-0005       issue todo        epic:argos-e001
    argos-0005.aaa   issue in_progress (제 epic 없음 — 부모에게서 e001 을 물려받는다)
    argos-0005.aaa   issue done        epic:argos-e002

`show --json` 에서 앞줄의 `derived_epic` 이 `argos-e002` 다. 앞줄을 집은 세션에서
`moai add x -e argos-e001` 이 규칙 1 에 막히고 거절문은 `-e argos-e002` 를 내주며,
`-e argos-e002` 만 지나간다.

**계획이 세우는 멤버가 바로 이 꼴이다** — AGENTS.md 가 "The member carries no `epic` field
of its own" 이라 적어 둔 그 줄이라, 드문 판이 아니라 흔한 판이다. 고치면 `derived_epic`·
트리·`-e`·롤업이 함께 움직인다.

moai-jk2u.ipf 회차가 **2번(`report::rollups` 가 제 `Lines` 를 짓는다)을 이미 걷었다.**
`report::Ties` 가 `Lines` 와 종류 지도를 빌려 주고 `rollups` 가 그것을 받는다. 같은 회차에
`started_in` 도 `started_over` 가 되어 `shelved_in` 안의 한 벌을 걷었으니, 한 `places` 판정이
짓던 `Lines` 세 벌 가운데 둘이 없어졌다. 1번(`tui::Ground::here`)과 3번은 그대로다.

**새로 하나 붙는다** (리뷰 moai-jk2u.35i 14번). `Ties::stone_of` 는 `Ties::of` 가 이미 지어 둔
마일스톤 지도를 안 읽고 줄마다 `stood_at_line` 을 다시 돈다 — `milestones_over` 의 몸과 글자째
같은 식이다. 에픽이 안 풀리는 줄(이 저장소에서 약 21%)에서는 `BTreeMap::get` 한 번 대신
`fold_top` + `climb` 조상 걷기가 되고, 그 자리가 훅의 `nearness`(줄마다 최대 세 번)와
`places_in`(`집은 줄 × 워크트리`)이다.

고칠 길은 그 지도를 **줄 정체로 다시 짜는 것**이다(`off_rows` 가 이미 그 꼴이다). 그러면
한 번 짚기로 돌아오면서 쌍둥이도 저절로 맞는다. 훅의 더운 길을 바꾸는 일이라 재고 정한다.
model: anthropic/opus-5 tokens=359405 (max — 훅을 건드린 멤버, 리뷰 서브에이전트가 쓴 값)

리뷰 원문 (agent-a82fea9db43d1b6b7, `/code-review max --fix`, 15건 중 열둘 고침)

**Findings** (reviewer's own words, `file:line — summary` / `failure scenario`)

1. `src/report.rs:796` — The headline bug is NOT fixed for a row that inherits its
   epic instead of writing one — `joined_in`'s fallback still reads the id map, where
   the twin wins.
   Reproduced against the committed binary. File holds `argos-0005` (issue, epic
   e001), `argos-0005.aaa` (in_progress, no `epic`, inherits e001 from its id-parent),
   `argos-0005.aaa` (done, epic e002). Holding the front row: `moai add x -e
   argos-e001` is REFUSED, the refusal says `-e argos-e002`, and only `-e argos-e002`
   passes — verbatim the failure the commit message and CHANGELOG claim to have fixed.
   AGENTS.md says plan-minted members are exactly this shape ("The member carries no
   `epic` field of its own"), so this is the common member, not the rare one.
   `derived_epic` is also e002, so the hole is one layer down in `joined_in`/`groups`,
   not in `Ties`.
2. `src/report.rs:796` — `Ties::epic_of`/`stone_of` went through
   `joined_in`/`stood_at_line`, skipping the eclipse gate every other belonging reader
   applies.
   `argos-0008` written as `issue in_progress epic=argos-e001 tags=[review]` then as
   `milestone`. `show --json` has no `derived_epic`, the tree draws it under `(lost)`,
   `show -e argos-e001` skips it — but the Stop hook blocked with "Review issue
   argos-0008 is still open. Attach what it produced and close it", and rule 3 anchored
   `/code-review` on it. One binary, two answers; `duplicate_id` blocks the write it
   tells you to make. Violates `stands_in`'s documented gate (moai-53s2, 2026-09-23
   user decision) and AGENTS.md's "counted into no group anywhere".
3. `src/worktree.rs:1023` — The snapshot-dig gate closed for an eclipsed picked row
   that wrote its own epic, killing the rescue path `started` exists for.
   `footing.picked().values().all(|i| footing.claims(&all_names, i))` used to be false
   for an eclipsed row because `groups` had erased its id; with row-read belonging,
   `worktree-<its written epic>` claims it, the gate short-circuits,
   `holds`/`touched`/`unknown` are never read, and the agent worktree actually holding
   it is invisible. The comment at lines 1019-1022 asserts the opposite is true.
4. `src/hook.rs:7913` — `shelving_closes` asked the row and then re-folded the answer
   by id, so the back twin won again inside the function the diff converted.
   `held` is an id set, the loop ran over `latest`, and `.collect()` into a
   `BTreeMap<&str,&str>` keeps the last match. Front `argos-0002 in_progress epic=e001`,
   back `argos-0002 todo epic=e002`: the back line is not `done` so it survives the
   `!is_done()` filter and wins. `closing` then says deferring your work closes
   `argos-e002`, an epic the row you hold never wrote. The held rows were already in
   hand as the `wip` parameter.
5. `src/report.rs:1268` — `blinding_in`'s new justification comment states an invariant
   the diff's own test fixture violates.
   The comment says `picked` keeps "지도가 고르는 줄과 같은 뒷줄" and defers review to
   "`picked` 가 앞줄을 남기게 되면". `Laid::picked` is the last row *in a started
   column*, so when the back twin is `done` — exactly
   `the_hook_reads_belonging_from_the_row_not_the_id_map`'s fixture — it keeps the
   FRONT row. The stated trigger has already fired, and with row-read `claims` the
   folded and unfolded answers can genuinely differ.
6. `src/report.rs:754` — `Ties::default()`, documented as "아무것도 안 잰 것", answers
   belonging from the row's own fields.
   `Ties::default().epic_of(i)` returns `i.epic` and `.stone_of(i)` returns
   `i.milestone` (empty `by_id` makes `fold_top` return the row itself and `stood_at`
   stop on its own `milestone`), where the old empty `BTreeMap` pair returned `None`.
   Safe only because `nearness` early-returns on an empty name set and both users take
   the default exactly then. `counts_stones: true` on a value that measured nothing
   compounds it.
7. `src/report.rs:797` — `counts_stones` gated `stone_of` but not `stone_at`/`stones()`,
   so "don't count milestones" was still carried by an empty map — the idiom the flag
   was added to retire.
   `nearness` uses `stone_of` at depth 0 and `stone_at` at every ancestor depth.
   Populate `stones` on an `epics_only` bundle (the natural next step, since `Ties::of`
   builds both maps anyway) and `query::unread` counts the milestone axis for a row's
   ancestors while refusing it for the row itself — `[NEW]` appears via the parent's
   release but not via its own, with no compile error and no test.
8. `src/report.rs:1042` — `Ties` holds the one `Lines` but lent nothing, so a single
   `places` judgement built `Lines::of` three times and `kinds` twice.
   `Footing::laid` builds `Ties::of` (1st `Lines`), then `started_in` → `shelved_in` →
   `Lines::of(all)` (2nd), then `places_in` → `rollups` → `members_in(.., &Lines::of
   (issues), ..)` plus its own `kinds(issues)` (3rd). Each is a BTreeMap over every row
   plus `rooted_thoughts`; this file already records a 98ms `moai status` regression
   from one extra walk of that class. The bundle's own doc says "`Lines` 도 한 벌이다".
9. `src/hook.rs:7139` — `epics_of` and `shelving_closes` each ran a full
   `issues.iter().any(..)` scan per focus row to ask "is this id a live epic".
   O(focus × rows) id comparisons on the hook path, which runs on every tool call;
   `aside_in` passes an uncapped `focus`. One pre-pass into a `BTreeSet` makes it
   O(N + focus·log N). (The bundle's `by_id` cannot answer this — it keeps only the
   last twin, while `any` matches any line with that id.)
10. `src/hook.rs:5793` — The three-way "is this row tied to what I hold" predicate is
    written verbatim three times, in the three functions documented as having to agree.
    `close_in`, `guard_review` and `closing` each carry `unit.contains(id) ||
    ties.epic_of(i).is_some_and(..) || parent_of(..).is_some_and(..)`, and `closing`'s
    own comment says "규칙 3 과 같은 셈법이어야 한다". Agreement is maintained by
    copy-paste; this diff had to edit all three identically. One fix lands in one place
    and rule 3 starts naming reviews that `closing` never chases.
11. `src/report.rs:851` — `nearness` spelled the "ask the row at depth 0, the map above"
    rule once per axis — the exact shape review moai-jk2u.m60 #1 caught.
    Two independent copies of a two-axis invariant in the hottest function of the file;
    the previous round's bug was one axis migrated and the other left on the map, and
    the new test's own doc cites it.
12. `src/report.rs:812` — Four doc comments were left pointing at the mechanism this
    diff retired, one of them at a function that never existed.
    `ties()`'s new doc links `[put_off_in]`, which is nowhere in the tree, and names the
    wrong callers. `claims`' doc still says `query::unread` works "마일스톤 지도를 비워
    넘겨서" — the exact belief the change removed and which query.rs was rewritten to
    contradict. `claims_over` and `hook::unit_of`/`create_in` still say they receive
    "두 지도"/`report::ties`. The next reader reintroduces the empty-map idiom with no
    compile error.
13. `tests/cli.rs:9693` — The new test's two stated guarantees were not met by its
    fixture.
    The doc claims "대조군이 같은 파일에 선다 — id 가 하나뿐인 줄의 답이 바뀌면 여기서
    붉어진다", but every issue row written is a twin; only group rows are unique and none
    exercises `epic_of` on them. And the milestone axis asserts only the positive case,
    so a `stone_of` that still consulted the map in addition to the row would pass — the
    half the doc calls out as review m60 #1's finding is unpinned.
14. `src/report.rs:802` — `stone_of` recomputes per query the value `Ties::of` already
    stored in `stones`.
    `milestones_over`'s body is character-for-character `stone_of`'s expression, yet
    `stone_of` never reads the map. For the ~21% of rows with no derived epic that means
    `fold_top` + `climb` ancestor walks instead of one `BTreeMap::get`, at up to 3
    `nearness` per row per hook invocation and `picked × trees` in `places_in`. Keying
    the built map by row identity (the repo already does this in `off_rows`) would make
    it one lookup and twin-correct by construction.
15. `src/cmd/show.rs:480` — The defer axis 20 lines below the line this diff changed
    still reads the id-folded `deferred_roots` with the row in hand.
    `roots: report::deferred_roots(all)` is id-keyed (last line wins) and all three
    readers (show.rs:530, view.rs:1681, view.rs:1777) hold the row; `query::Where::
    deferred` already does it per-row. `shelved_by` in `--json` and the `미룸` line can
    name the twin's defer root, so `moai defer <that id> --undo` un-defers the wrong
    row. The CHANGELOG entry directly above this diff's is about this same axis.

**What I applied** — all fixes in the working tree, `cargo fmt --check` clean,
`cargo clippy --all-targets` clean, 1,980 tests pass (1,440 unit + 540 CLI).

- Eclipse gate restored (#2, #3, and the `rollups`-vs-`nearness` split): `Ties` now
  carries a kind map; `epic_of` routes through `report::stands_in` and `stone_of` gates
  on `is_eclipsed` first — the same shape `query::Where` already uses on both axes. I
  verified the new test assertion goes red without it (the Stop hook demands closing a
  review the session never picked up, on an id `duplicate_id` makes unwritable).
- `shelving_closes` asks the held rows (#4) instead of re-scanning `latest` by id, so
  the back twin can no longer win the map.
- `counts_stones: bool` → `stones: Option<..>` (#7), so `stone_of` and `stone_at` are
  gated by one value; `Default` is now honest about what it measured (#6).
- `Ties` lends its `Lines` and kind map (#8): new `started_over` replaces `started_in`,
  and `rollups` borrows — two of three redundant `Lines` builds and one `kinds` build
  removed per `places` judgement.
- `live_epics` hoisted (#9) in both hook sites; `in_unit` extracted (#10) and used at
  all three sites; `nearness`'s depth-0 dispatch written once (#11).
- Docs corrected (#12, #5): the broken `put_off_in` link and wrong callers, the stale
  empty-map sentence on `claims`, `claims_over`, `hook::unit_of`/`create_in`,
  `blinding_in`'s false premise, and `worktree.rs`'s rationale (which now names the gate
  that actually holds it).
- Test strengthened (#13): real unique-id control row, the negative milestone assertion,
  and eclipse assertions across `show --json`, `show -e` and the Stop hook.
- CHANGELOG corrected: it claimed "Every place that asked by id now asks the row".
  Finding #1 shows that is not true for inherited-epic members, so I added the qualifier
  naming the remaining hole.

**What I skipped, and why**

- #1 (inherited epic) — the real fix is in `joined_in`/`groups`, one layer below `Ties`,
  and it moves `derived_epic`, the tree, `-e` and rollups all at once. A `Ties`-local
  patch would make the hook right while every read surface stayed wrong, which is
  precisely the split `stands_in` forbids. The issue's own handover note already assigns
  this to `moai-5km5`.
- #14 (`stone_of` recomputation) — the fix is to key the milestone map by row identity;
  that is a measurable design change on the hook's hot path, not a review edit.
- #15 (`deferred_roots` in show.rs) — a different axis, outside this diff.
- `src/cmd/show.rs:463`'s now-dead `is_group` guard — behaviour-identical either way,
  and the comment above it documents intent (moai-fg0t), so removing it loses more than
  it gains.

받아들인 것과 넘긴 것 — 내 판단

열둘을 받았다(`7e925f7`). 가장 값이 큰 것은 2번이다. **내가 문을 일부러 건너뛰었다** —
`unit` 은 너그러운 집합이라 가려짐으로 걸러 내면 정당한 쓰기를 막는 쪽으로 기운다고 보고
`stands_in` 대신 `joined_in` 을 골랐다. 그 판단이 틀린 까닭은 둘이다. 하나, 가려진 줄에도
길은 남는다 — `epics_of` 가 그 줄을 `loose` 로 내고 거절문이 `--parent <id>` 를 주며 그것은
실제로 통한다. 둘, 리뷰가 낸 판은 진짜 막다른 길이다: Stop 이 `duplicate_id` 가 막는 쓰기를
시킨다. 도구 안에 길이 있는 쪽과 없는 쪽을 견줬어야 했는데 방향만 봤다.

4번도 내가 낸 것이다. 줄에 물어 놓고 그 답을 `BTreeMap` 에 id 로 담아, 고침이 없애려던 접기를
같은 함수 안에서 되살렸다. 집은 줄이 `wip` 으로 이미 손에 있었다.

스스로 검증한 것 — 지적을 그대로 믿지 않았다.

- **리뷰의 고침 위에 둘을 더 고쳤다.** `started_over` 가 `is_put_off` 문을 한 벌 더 두었는데
  `shelved_over` 가 그 문을 이미 들고 있다(같은 술어가 세 곳에 서고, 미룬 줄이 있는 저장소에서는
  목록을 한 번 더 걷는 값만 는다). 그리고 `stones` 를 `unwrap_or(&empty)` 로 때워, 에픽 축만 잰
  재료로 부르면 미룬 릴리스에 든 줄이 집은 줄로 **말없이** 남았다 — 갈라 말하고 제 손으로 재게 했다
- 12번이 빠뜨린 낡은 링크 하나를 더 찾았다(`in_started_columns` 의 `[started_in]`).
  `cargo doc --document-private-items` 로 훑어, 남은 경고 셋(`places`·`stranded`·`blinding`)이
  이 회차 전부터 있던 것임을 확인했다
- 1번을 고친 바이너리에서 다시 재현했다. 앞줄의 `derived_epic` 이 여전히 쌍둥이의 `argos-e002` 고,
  `-e argos-e001` 이 막히고 `-e argos-e002` 만 지나간다 — 리뷰 말이 맞다
- 관문을 다시 돌렸다: 1440 + 540 초록, clippy 깨끗, fmt 깨끗. develop 을 받은 뒤 한 번 더

넘긴 셋의 자리

- **`moai-5km5`**(p1 `#bug`, 첫 칸, 옆 세션의 다음 회차) — 1번. 물려받은 에픽은 `joined_in` 의
  되돌림이라 한 층 아래고, 고치면 `derived_epic`·트리·`-e`·롤업이 함께 움직인다. 재현 판을
  노트로 붙였다
- **`moai-wre3`**(p1 `#bug`, 이 에픽의 멤버, 첫 칸) — 15번. `deferred_roots` 를 읽는 셋이 줄을
  손에 들고 지도를 id 로 짚는다. 미룸 축이라 이 회차 밖이지만 에픽이 내건 것 안이다
- **`moai-6mnm`**(p2, 에픽·릴리스 밖) — 14번. 노트를 달았다. 그 이슈의 2번은 이 회차가 걷었다

**안 받은 것 하나**: `src/cmd/show.rs:463` 의 `is_group` 가드가 이제 죽은 것이라는 지적은 리뷰
스스로 안 고쳤고 나도 안 고친다. 답이 같고, 그 위 주석이 왜 묻지 않는지를 적어 둔 자리다
(moai-fg0t) — 가드를 걷으면 그 까닭이 코드에서 사라진다.

note: 열둘을 받아 7e925f7 에 실었다(가려짐 문·shelving_closes 의 id 접기·Lines 빌려 주기·in_unit·live_epics 따위). 리뷰의 고침 위에 둘을 더 고쳤다 — started_over 의 겹친 문과 빈 마일스톤 지도로 때우던 자리. 넘긴 셋은 moai-5km5(물려받은 에픽, 재현 판을 노트로 붙였다)·moai-wre3(deferred_roots 를 줄마다, 이 에픽의 멤버로 세웠다)·moai-6mnm(stone_of 가 지도를 안 읽는다).

text: model: anthropic/opus-5 (high — 훅이 소속을 id 로 묻던 여섯 자리)

note: 0942dc0 으로 develop 에 들어갔다. 소속을 묻는 재료를 report::Ties 한 벌로 모으고, 줄을 든 자리는 줄에 묻게 했다 — 훅의 일곱 자리와 report::nearness 의 첫 걸음, Footing::epic_of, query::unread. develop 바이너리로 거짓 거절을 재현했고 고친 뒤 통과한다. 남은 것은 moai-5km5(물려받은 에픽)와 moai-wre3(미룸 축)이다.

text: Next: moai-jk2u.ipf 와 그 리뷰가 0942dc0 으로 develop 에 들어갔다. 에픽은 둘이 열려 있다 — moai-5km5(제 epic 을 안 적은 앞줄이 뒷줄의 것을 입는다, 옆 세션이 쥐었다)와 moai-wre3(미룸의 뿌리를 읽는 셋이 줄을 들고 지도를 id 로 짚는다, 리뷰 moai-jk2u.35i 15번). 훅은 이제 줄에 묻지만 물려받은 에픽은 joined_in 의 되돌림이라 moai-5km5 가 닫혀야 끝난다 — 재현 판이 그 이슈의 노트에 있다. 성능 나머지는 에픽 밖 moai-6mnm 이고, 그 이슈의 2번(rollups 가 제 Lines 를 짓는다)은 이 회차가 걷었다.

title: 부모 id 에 쌍둥이가 서면 자식의 에픽이 파일 차례로 뒤집힌다
넘기는 값의 경계와 마일스톤 축에 타입이 안 서 있다

text:
리뷰 moai-jk2u.o78 4번이 남은 자리를 셋으로 좁혔다 — `epics_of`(src/hook.rs:7133), `shelving_closes`(7907), `unit_of_in`(5225, 규칙 1 과 3 이 먹는다). 셋 다 줄을 든 채 접은 지도에 묻는다.

moai-5km5 는 `report::groups` 가 내는 꼴을 안 바꿨다(접은 지도 그대로, 뒷줄이 이긴다). 그러니 그쪽 고침은 그대로 서고, 줄마다 묻는 자로 갈아탈 자리만 남는다 — `report::Handing::at` 이고, `Handing` 은 `report::tied`·`Soil.epic`·`Footing::laid` 의 `handed` 에서 받는다.

규칙 1 의 거절문이 틀린 `-e <에픽>` 을 대는 판이라 게이트 쪽이다. AGENTS.md 가 그 거절문을 그대로 치라고 하니 사람이 고를 자리도 아니다.

리뷰 moai-jk2u.o78 13번이 이 길과 같은 말을 또 했다. 뿌리는 `is_eclipsed` 가 **종류가 다른** 쌍둥이에만 서는 것이다 — 이 갈래의 버그는 전부 같은 종류 쌍둥이라, 도구가 `가려짐` 이라는 낱말을 들고도 그 판에는 안 쓴다.

값은 한 뿌리에 고침이 셋이 된 것이다. 바늘로 짚는 자리 배열(`off_rows`), 접고 되묻기(`fold_by_id` + `torn_ids`), 그리고 이번의 `Handing`. 표면을 더할 때마다 셋 중 어느 것인지를 사람이 고른다.

moai-w610 도 같이 본다 — `Handing` 이 임의의 한 줄을 고르던 자리를 한 칸 위로 옮겼을 뿐이라, 부모 쪽에 쌍둥이가 서면 자식이 다시 파일 차례를 탄다.

리뷰 moai-jk2u.o78 11번. moai-5km5 뒤로 `report::groups` 가 `Handing::over` + `fold` 두 걸음이고 `ties` 가 세 걸음이다. 예전에는 저마다 한 걸음이었다.

지나는 자리가 훅의 도구 호출마다다 — `hook::epics_of`, 닫을 때마다 `hook::shelving_closes`, 탐색기 적재마다 `query::unread`, 그리고 `edit -e none` 의 쓰기 경로는 락 안이다. 이슈 1,286줄짜리 이 저장소에서 한 번 부를 때마다 목록을 한 번 더 걷고 지도 한 벌을 지었다 버린다. `Footing::laid` 는 `moai show <id>` 에서도 그 접기를 먼저 치르는데 읽는 자는 `epic_of` 짚기 하나다.

거꾸로 싸진 자리도 있다 — `Soil::of`·`handed_of`·`ready`·락 안의 `read_of` 는 접기를 안 하니 예전보다 한 걸음 덜 간다. 그러니 재기 전에는 어느 쪽이 큰지 모른다.

`Handing::over` 안에서 접으면 차례를 적은 글이 셋이 되니(리뷰 14번이 경계한 그것) 재고 나서 정한다.

Reviewer's own words — `/code-review max --fix`, 15 findings, ranked most-severe first. Paths are relative to the worktree root.

1. `src/cmd/prime.rs:173` — `prime --json` was the one `derived_epic` producer left on the folded `report::groups` map, so after this diff one binary gives two answers to "which epic is this row in". Reproduced with the built binary: `argos-e001`/`argos-e002` epics, `argos-e001.aaa` twice (earlier line writes no `epic`, later writes `epic: argos-e002`, both `kind: issue` so neither is eclipsed). `show --json` and `ready --json` gave `derived_epic: argos-e001` for the bare row; `prime --json` gave `argos-e002`. `prime`'s human screen (via `epic_labels`) was already correct, so one command contradicted itself. `report::stands_in`'s doc names exactly these two surfaces and says 자는 하나다.

2. `src/report.rs:1262` — `rollups` receives the row-level `Handing` but still filters members against `picked`, an id-keyed map, so an epic holding no picked row is reported as being worked in a worktree. Rows: epic `argos-0001`, `argos-0001.aaa` (issue, todo, no `epic`), `argos-0001.aaa` (issue, in_progress, `epic: argos-0009`), epic `argos-0009`. `.filter(|id| picked.contains_key(id))` passes on the shared id, so `settle` turns both into `Place::At`. Before the diff both twins folded into `argos-0009`.

3. `src/view.rs:1485` — `moai ready`'s human screen prints an id-less `moai defer  --undo`, the exact symptom the previous review fixed. Reproduced: epic `argos-e001`; `argos-e001.aaa` twice (front deferred with no `epic`, back alive with `epic: argos-e002`); `argos-0009` `blocked_by: [argos-e001]`. `holding` puts the id in `by`, but `fold_roots` keys by id and the last row of that id is not deferred, so it is absent from `roots`. `undo` comes back empty and the renderer expands it anyway. `ready --json`'s `held` entry likewise carries `by` with no `undo`.

4. `src/hook.rs:7133` — the hook was not migrated: `epics_of`, `shelving_closes` (7907) and `unit_of_in` (5225) still answer a per-row question from the folded map while holding the row, so rule 1's refusal hands the agent the wrong `-e <epic>`. AGENTS.md tells the agent to run that refusal verbatim. Bounded only because `store::with_write` refuses every write while a duplicate id stands — but read surfaces are the only repair tool the operator has in exactly that file state.

5. `src/report.rs:2276` — `Handing` relocates the arbitrary pick one level up rather than removing it: `Handed::from` resolves the parent id through `by_id` (last row wins), so a child's epic still flips with file order when the PARENT id has twins. Reproduced: epics `argos-e008`/`argos-e009`; `argos-p001` twice as `kind: issue` writing different epics; child `argos-p001.aaa` writing no `epic`. Swapping the two parent rows flips the child's `derived_epic`. `moai status` names only `argos-p001` under duplicate ids — the child is silently re-homed and never reported.

6. `src/report.rs:463` — `deferred_sources_in`'s `roots ⊆ sources` contract stopped being structural: the old body seeded a key per root, the new one keys only when the walk is non-empty, and nothing in the signature or a check pins it. It holds only because `fold_roots` and `Lines::at` happen to agree and `shelved_over` zeroes `closed_by_hand` rows and done-reading groups before the fold. If either side's row choice shifts, `Held::undo` empties and `blocked_by_deferred`'s age falls into its `else { return "" }` branch with no signal.

7. `src/report.rs:2321` — the newtype's stated purpose is defeated at its boundary: `handed_of` returns a bare `BTreeMap`, `Handing::handed()` hands one out and `Handing::of_handed` accepts any one, so migrated and unmigrated sites still look identical. `Handing::of_handed(report::groups(all))` compiles and silently produces a wrapper whose `at()` layers `i.epic` on a value that already folded in the twin's written epic. That same untyped boundary is why `cmd/prime.rs` and five `hook.rs` sites kept compiling unchanged through the rename. The `tui::Ground` round trip (tui/mod.rs:337/376) is the only feeder, and no test exercises the explorer with same-kind twins.

8. `src/report.rs:549` — `Shelf::walk` resolved the ancestor row twice per step: `line` is already `lines.at(at)`, and `at_id(at, self.lines)` repeated the lookup, re-introducing the shape the comment six lines above says it exists to prevent. The two picks agree today only because `Lines::at` and the fold both resolve last-wins. Cost: one redundant `by_id` probe per ancestor step per row, on the `status`/`ready`/hook path.

9. `src/cmd/mod.rs:748` — `Read.epics`' doc states the opposite of what `handed_of` now returns ("`epic` 을 적은 줄도 든다"), and the reasoning built on it is unsound; `Board::epics` and `Picks::epics` carry the same stale claim, and `read_of`'s doc still names the deleted `groups_of`.

10. `src/report.rs:2326` — `handed_of`'s gate predicate was a hand-written second copy of `Handing::over`'s population filter, held together only by a doc comment asserting they are 같은 술어. Change `joins`, or add a clause to one side, and `handed_of` returns an EMPTY map for rows `Handing::over` does have answers for — and an empty map means "not built", not "no epic".

11. `src/report.rs:2144` — `groups_over` became `Handing::over(all, lines).fold(all)` and `ties` became `tied` + `fold`: two and three passes over `all` where each was one, on the hook's per-tool-call path (`hook::epics_of`, `hook::shelving_closes`, `query::unread`, and the `edit -e none` write path inside the store lock). `Footing::laid` pays the extra fold eagerly even on `moai show <id>`, whose only reader is one `epic_of` lookup, while its comment claims the opposite.

12. `src/report.rs:566` — the milestone axis is still a raw id-keyed `&BTreeMap` in every signature the epic axis just left, and in `Shelf::walk` the two axes sit three lines apart looking different only by accident. `mile_of` is threaded raw through `Shelf::new`, `shelved_over/in`, `deferred_sources_in`, `started_in`, `group_stands_in`, `shelved_at_line`, `Placed::Milestone`, `Soil::milestone` and `query::Where::milestone`. The trap is half-built: `tui::Ground::in_soil` deliberately stores an EMPTY milestone map when `torn` is empty, and only the `torn.contains` guard at query.rs:167 keeps it out of `shelved_at_line`.

13. `src/report.rs:2918` — root cause: `is_eclipsed` fires only when the twins' KINDS differ, so same-kind twins — the shape of every bug in this diff — are arbitrated silently and differently on every axis instead of being excluded once. The codebase now carries three separate remedies for one root cause: positional arrays keyed by `*const Issue` (`off_rows`), fold + `torn_ids` + per-row re-ask, and now a bespoke id-keyed `Handing`. The series is seven patches deep (moai-2m9p, moai-7iyc.rt6, moai-u3ta, moai-jk2u.wvn, moai-jk2u.olh, moai-jk2u.m60, moai-5km5/kg6g) and the count of `fold_by_id` maps is unchanged.

14. `src/report.rs:2215` — one rule, four spellings: `Handing::at`, `at_id` and `fold` each wrote out `joined_in(i, || from_id.get(i.id).copied())` verbatim, `nav::Ctx::epic_at` a fourth time, and `Placing::handed`'s two match arms were byte-identical. The next change to that order lands on `at` and leaves the defer walk, every folded-map consumer and the tree on the old rule.

15. `src/report.rs:1483` — several call sites switched to `Handing::of(all)`, which builds and discards its own `Lines`, at places that already hold or immediately build one. `group_members` builds one inside `Handing::of` and drops it, then builds a second for the milestone axis — and the comment three lines above is now false on both axes. `milestone_from_above`, which runs inside the store lock on every `moai edit --milestone`, builds four snapshot-sized structures where one `Lines` suffices. `held` and `blocks_of` have the same shape.

리뷰 moai-jk2u.o78 15번도 여기다. `Handing::of` 가 제 `Lines` 를 지었다 버리는 자리가 여럿인데, 옛 `groups(all)` 도 안에서 같은 것을 지었으니 이 회차가 낸 값이 아니라 원래 있던 값이다. 다만 `group_members`(src/report.rs:1603)와 `milestone_from_above`(2669)는 그 옆에서 `Lines` 를 또 지어 한 판정에 두세 벌이 서고, `milestone_from_above` 는 `moai edit --milestone` 마다 락 안에서 돈다. `Lines` 를 빌려 받는 `_over` 꼴이 이미 있으니 그리로 옮기면 된다.

받아들인 것과 넘긴 것 — 내 판단

셋을 그대로 받았다(`98a576c`). 1번이 특히 맞다. **소속 지도를 읽는 자리를 훑어 옮기면서
`cmd/prime.rs` 하나를 빠뜨렸다** — `report::stands_in` 의 주석이 그 표면 둘을 이름 대며
`자는 하나다` 라고 적어 둔 바로 그 자리다. 표면 목록을 문서에서 읽지 않고 `grep` 으로만
훑은 값이다. 2번은 나도 옮겨 놓고 못 본 자리다. 멤버를 줄마다 갈리게 해 놓고 그 멤버를
견주는 `picked` 는 id 로 둔 채여서, 한 회차에 한 축만 옮긴 moai-jk2u.olh 의 꼴을 내가 다시
냈다. 3번은 `report` 쪽 고침이 대는 약속을 그리는 쪽이 안 지킨 자리다.

스스로 검증한 것 — 지적을 그대로 믿지 않았다.

- 셋 다 재현판을 다시 돌려 봤고, 고친 뒤 시험이 옛 코드에서 붉어지는 것까지 봤다
- **리뷰가 쓴 이슈 id 가 없는 것이었다.** 코드 주석과 시험 열다섯 자리에 `moai-5km5.o0p`
  라고 적혀 있는데 그런 줄은 없다. 이 리뷰 이슈의 id 로 고쳤다
- 6번의 살아 있는 `assert!` 대신 `debug_assert!` 를 둔 판단에 동의한다. `roots` 는 부르는
  쪽이 짓는 값이고, 읽는 표면이 유일한 고침 수단인 깨진 파일에서 `moai ready`·`status` 가
  죽으면 되돌릴 길이 도구 밖에만 남는다
- 15번은 이 회차가 낸 값이 아니다. 옛 `groups(all)` 도 안에서 `Lines` 를 지었으니 수가
  그대로다. 그래도 `group_members` 와 `milestone_from_above` 는 그 옆에서 또 지으니
  moai-6mnm 에 적었다

**4번은 이 회차 안에서 닫혔다.** 리뷰는 `src/hook.rs` 가 diff 밖이라 넘겼는데, 그 사이
moai-jk2u.ipf 가 develop 에 들어와 `report::Ties` 를 세웠다. 그 `Ties` 는 소속을 줄에
묻지만 안에 든 지도가 여전히 접은 것이라, 리뷰가 가리킨 그 구멍이 그대로 있었다(그쪽
CHANGELOG 도 "물려받은 소속은 아직 안 덮었다" 라고 적어 두었다). 머지에서 `Ties.epics` 를
`Handing` 으로 바꿔 훅까지 한 자를 지나게 했다 — 별도 이슈가 아니라 이 머지의 몫이다.

넘긴 넷의 자리

- **moai-w610**(idea, 이 에픽) — 5번. `Handing` 은 임의의 한 줄을 고르던 자리를 한 칸 위로
  옮겼을 뿐이라, 부모 쪽에 쌍둥이가 서면 자식이 다시 파일 차례를 탄다. 자료에 답이 없는
  자리일 수 있어 idea 로 둔다
- **moai-a512**(idea, 이 에픽) — 7번과 12번. 경계가 안 막혀 있고 마일스톤 축은 아직 날
  지도로 다닌다. 둘 다 같은 움직임으로 닫힌다
- **moai-pth7**(idea) — 13번. 뿌리가 `is_eclipsed` 가 종류가 다른 쌍둥이에만 서는 것이라는
  말은 이 idea 가 가리키는 자리와 같다. 노트로 붙였다
- **moai-6mnm**(에픽·릴리스 밖) — 11번과 15번. 성능이고 막는 것이 없다

**고치지 않기로 한 것 하나**: 11번의 `Handing::over` 안에서 접기. 차례를 적은 글이 셋이
되는데, 그것이 바로 14번이 경계한 그 꼴이다. 재고 나서 정한다.

**관문**: cargo test 1444 + 542 초록, clippy `--all-targets` 깨끗, fmt `--check` 깨끗.
중복 id 판을 손으로 지어 다섯 표면(`show <에픽>` 멤버·트리·`-e`·`derived_epic`·굴림)이
같은 답을 내는 것까지 봤다.

앞 노트를 고쳐 적는다 — 그 셋은 moai-5km5 의 머지에서 닫혔다. `report::Ties` 가 소속을 줄에 묻게는 했지만 안에 든 지도가 여전히 접은 것(`groups_over`)이라, 제 `epic` 을 안 적은 앞줄은 그대로 뒷줄의 것을 입었다(이 이슈의 CHANGELOG 절도 "물려받은 소속은 아직 안 덮었다" 라고 적어 두었다). `Ties.epics` 를 `Handing` 으로 바꾸고 `Ties::epic_at` 을 그 id 의 줄에 묻게 해서 `epics_of`·`shelving_closes`·`unit_of_in` 셋이 한 자를 지난다. 이 이슈에 남은 일은 없다.

title: review — 미룸의 뿌리를 줄에 묻는 자리

text: Next: `/code-review max --fix` 가 뒤에서 돌고 있다. 끝나면 리뷰 원문을 노트로 적고, 받아들인 것과 넘긴 것을 마침 글에 적어 닫는다. 범위는 워크트리 가지 worktree-moai-wre3 의 커밋 하나(ac9f029)다.
Next: 고침은 워크트리 worktree-moai-wre3 에 ac9f029 로 서 있다. 시험 1444+543 초록, fmt·clippy 깨끗. 리뷰 moai-jk2u.jaq 가 끝나 고침을 받은 뒤 develop 에 머지하고 닫는다.

리뷰 moai-jk2u.jaq 이 같은 결로 둘을 더 댔다. 둘 다 이 diff 앞에 있던 것이고 막는 것은 없다.

4. `report::split_ids` 가 줄 수만큼 지도를 짓는다

- 미룬 줄이 하나라도 있으면 그 지도를 짓는다. 중복 id 가 없는 저장소에서는 반드시 비는데,
  비었다는 것을 알려면 다 지어 봐야 한다
- 리뷰가 쟀다 — 19k 줄에 미룬 에픽 하나인 저장소에서 `moai show` 한 판에 약 12ms
- `query::Where::from_soil` 과 `tui::Ground::in_soil` 은 `kinds.len() == all.len()` 으로 그
  문을 먼저 세운다. `report::Shelved::of` 만 그 지도가 손에 없다
- 고칠 길: 접는 걸음(`fold_by_id`)과 가르는 걸음이 같은 차례를 걷는다. 한 번에 둘을 내면
  값이 빠지지만 차례를 `fold_by_id` 한 몸에만 두기로 한 규약을 건드린다

5. `Shelved::of` 가 `Footing` 이 이미 든 `Ties`·`Lines` 를 다시 짓는다

- `cmd::show::one` 한 판이 `Lines::of` 를 셋, `kinds` 를 둘 짓는다. 그 명령은 145줄 뒤에
  `Soil` 도 지어, 같은 `roots` 와 `shelved` 를 한 벌 더 든다
- 리뷰가 쟀다 — 미룬 줄이 있는 19k 저장소에서 +133ms 가운데 37ms 이상
- 고칠 길: `Shelved::kept` 가 이미 서 있다(`Where::from_soil` 과 `Ground::here` 가 그 길로
  든다). `cmd::show` 가 `Footing` 과 `Soil` 을 한 벌로 묶는 날 그 길로 같이 든다

리뷰 원문 (agent-a325838545de6a042, `/code-review max --fix`, 15건 중 열하나 고침)

**Findings** (reviewer's own words, `file:line — summary` / `failure scenario`)

1. `src/report.rs:467` — Shelved::root gated the per-row lookup on torn_ids, which
   compares only is_some() — never the root value. Twins BOTH out of the plan but held
   there by DIFFERENT rows are not "torn", so both still got the folded last-line root:
   the exact bug the CHANGELOG claims to fix.
   REPRODUCED. argos-0003.eee twice, front under deferred epic argos-e001, back under
   deferred argos-e003. `moai show argos-0003` printed BOTH children as
   `deferred — under argos-e003`. The `moai defer argos-e003 --undo` that mark points at
   never deferred the front row.
2. `src/report.rs:467` — Same gate, worse variant: a front twin under a deferred epic
   beside a self-deferred back twin loses its defer mark entirely, because the folded
   answer is the back row's own id and view::deferred_for filters root == i.id.
   REPRODUCED. argos-0005.hhh front epic=argos-e001 (deferred), back with its own
   deferred_at. The front child rendered with NO mark while `show --deferred --all`
   listed it — one screen contradicting the other, which is the yardstick the new test's
   own doc sets.
3. `src/report.rs:473` — NEW divergence the diff introduced: Shelved::root answered GROUP
   rows per-row, but query::Where::deferred deliberately routes group rows to the folded
   map (torn.contains(id) && !is_group(i)) because settled_groups reads a group's column
   from members by id. The detail marked a group row deferred that show --deferred omits.
   REPRODUCED. argos-0004.ggg as an epic under deferred milestone argos-m001 plus an
   in-plan issue twin. `moai show argos-0004` drew `epic · deferred — under argos-m001`;
   `show --deferred --all` listed only argos-m001. Before the diff both sides said
   "in plan".
4. `src/report.rs:446` — Shelved::of lost the `any(is_put_off)` short-circuit
   deferred_roots had. Every moai show on a repo with nothing deferred allocated
   vec![None; n] and built an n-entry BTreeMap inside torn_ids, both provably empty.
   MEASURED: `moai show <leaf>`, 19k rows, zero deferred — 103.6 ms before vs 118.7 ms
   after, +15.1 ms (+14.6%); a microbench attributes 12.3 ms to the discarded 19k map.
   moai show is the hot agent path.
5. `src/report.rs:473` — root() found the row with `rows.iter().position(|x| ptr::eq(x,
   i))` — an O(all) linear scan per torn row, called once per child in view::detail — and
   Shelved retained the whole n-element at_line Vec plus the &[Issue] slice for the
   render's life.
   MEASURED +18.5 ms on a 19.5k-row fixture with 1000 torn children (~3.4 ms of pure
   scanning above the +15.1 ms); shape O(children x rows). off_rows in the same file
   already uses BTreeSet<*const Issue>, and its doc records the 98 ms moai status
   regression from this exact mistake.
6. `tests/cli.rs:10097` — The new test's comment "같은 id 가 둘인 파일이라 duplicate_id 로
   종료 코드가 0 이 아니다" is factually wrong for the calls it makes, and the test never
   asserted the exit code.
   MEASURED on that fixture: show <id> = 0, show --deferred = 0, show --json = 0; only
   status = 1. A future panic (exit 101) would surface as "줄이 상세에 없다" on empty
   stdout instead of naming the real failure.
7. `tests/cli.rs:10112` — The step-2 comment claims the folded map reddens both asserts;
   only one reddens, because the folded answer IS the back row's answer.
   A reader trusting it may delete the surviving assert as redundant, or mis-bisect a
   regression that reddens only one side.
8. `src/view.rs:1693` — view::detail has two root() call sites; the test drove only the
   child-row one with a torn id. The header slot was never exercised with a twin.
   The header is exactly where the group divergence above surfaces, and no test would
   redden.
9. `src/view.rs:164` — deferred_for's doc still named report::deferred_roots as where
   `root` comes from — the source the change exists to stop using.
   Someone debugging a wrong mark follows the doc to the folded map, finds it behaving
   exactly as documented, and concludes the mark is right.
10. `CHANGELOG.md:214` — The shipped entry claimed the whole "front twin wears the wrong
    root" class was closed; given the first two findings it was not.
    User-facing text tells the next reader the class is closed, so nobody re-measures.
11. `src/cmd/show.rs:533` — `if let Some(root) = seen.roots.root(issue)` shadowed
    `let root = commit_home(...)` thirty lines above; serde_json::to_string accepts both a
    &Path and a &str, so a mix-up would not be caught by the compiler.
    A later git read added below reaches for `root` and silently gets a defer-root id.
12. `src/report.rs:472` — NOT FIXED — split_ids still builds a full n-entry map on any
    repo that has a deferred row but no duplicate id. The other two torn_ids callers gate
    it on `kinds.len() == all.len()`; Shelved::over has no such map in hand.
    ~12 ms per moai show on a 19k-row repo with one deferred epic. Closing it needs either
    folding and splitting in one pass (duplicating the ordering CLAUDE.md insists lives
    only in fold_by_id) or changing fold_by_id's signature for its three callers — both
    well outside this diff.
13. `src/cmd/show.rs:483` — NOT FIXED — Shelved::of(all) rebuilds Ties/Lines that Footing
    already holds, and cmd::show::one builds a Soil 145 lines later carrying the identical
    roots + shelved pair. Shelved::over exists for exactly that handoff and has no caller.
    MEASURED: three Lines::of(all) and two kinds(all) per show; at least 37 ms of a
    +133 ms deferred-repo cost. Predates the diff (deferred_roots did the same), but the
    diff added the seam that would remove it.
14. `src/report.rs:446` — NOT FIXED — Shelved::over is pub with no caller, and validates
    only the LENGTH of at_line against all. A verdict measured over a different
    equal-length slice is accepted silently and every per-row answer is then wrong.
    Soil::of(x) then Shelved::over(y, soil.shelved) with x.len() == y.len() compiles,
    passes both asserts, and makes the detail and --deferred disagree with no diagnostic.
15. `src/report.rs:430` — NOT FIXED — Shelved::default() and no_twins(BTreeMap::new()) are
    identical values with docs claiming different meanings; Kinds encodes the same
    distinction as a named enum variant.
    A third view::detail caller reaches for Default because it is the shortest thing that
    compiles, and every defer mark vanishes from that screen with no compile error and no
    test failure.

**What I applied**

- `src/report.rs` — the gate now compares the **root value**, not `is_some()`. `torn_ids`'
  body was generalised into one shared `split_ids`, keeping the repo's "one fold body, one
  split body" rule, so `query::Where::deferred` keeps its boolean semantics untouched.
  `Shelved::root` now routes **group rows** to the folded map, matching
  `query::Where::deferred` letter for letter. `rows` + `at_line` were replaced by
  `by_row: BTreeMap<*const Issue, Option<&str>>` holding only split-id rows (the `off_rows`
  idiom already in the file) — O(log k) instead of O(n), retention down from n entries to
  typically 2. Added the `any deferred` early-out `deferred_roots` had, plus a
  `debug_assert` that makes a foreign row loud instead of silently falling back, and a note
  that the pointer key costs `Send`/`Sync` and why that is accepted.
- `tests/cli.rs` — new test
  `the_defer_root_is_asked_per_row_even_when_both_twins_are_out_of_the_plan` pinning all
  three reproductions plus filter/draw agreement; **verified it fails without the fix**
  (`앞줄이 뒷줄의 에픽을 달았다`). Fixed the two wrong comments, switched the reads to
  `ok()` so the exit code is checked, and added header-row coverage for a twin id.
- `src/view.rs`, `src/cmd/show.rs`, `CHANGELOG.md` — stale doc source, the shadowed `root`,
  and the over-claiming entry.

Verified: `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (it
caught a needless lifetime in my first draft, now fixed); **544 tests pass**; all three live
reproductions now behave correctly; `moai show` on the real tracker still exits 0.

**One design question worth putting to the user**

Group rows now answer from the folded map, which restores agreement between the detail and
`show --deferred`. But an epic sitting under a deferred milestone beside an in-plan twin is
reported "in the plan" by *both* surfaces — consistent, yet arguably wrong. Making groups
row-faithful everywhere requires `settled_groups` to become re-askable per line, which is a
larger change than this diff; I did not guess at it.

받아들인 것과 넘긴 것 — 내 판단

리뷰가 진짜 버그 둘을 재현해 냈고, 둘 다 내가 깐 전제가 틀려서 난 것이다. 문을 `torn_ids` 로
둔 것이 그 전제다 — 그쪽은 `Some` 인가만 견주는데 나는 "줄마다 갈리는 id" 라는 이름만 보고
갈라 준다고 믿었다. 이름을 읽고 몸을 안 읽었다.

**묶음 축은 사용자가 정했다.** 리뷰는 상세를 접은 지도로 되돌려 `--deferred` 와 맞췄고 나는
그 판단이 옳다고 보고 사용자에게 물었다. 사용자는 반대쪽을 골랐다 — 묶음도 줄마다 답한다.
그러고 나서야 리뷰도 나도 못 본 것이 드러났다.

- 바늘로 가르면 **목록이 통째로 어긋난다.** `cmd::show` 는 고른 줄을 `shown` 에 베껴 정렬하고
  `view::table` 이 그것을 `Where` 에 들이민다. 베낀 줄은 바늘이 안 맞아 그 표면만 말없이 접은
  지도로 돌아갔고 미룸 시험 여섯이 붉어져 드러났다. 리뷰의 `debug_assert` 가 그것을 잡았다 —
  고침이 아니라 그 한 줄이 이 회차에서 가장 값이 컸다
- 그래서 가르는 열쇠를 내용으로 바꿨다(`Mark`). 다섯이면 되는 까닭은 `Shelf::walk` 의 첫
  걸음만 물은 줄 제 것을 보기 때문이고, 그 위는 `Lines` 가 고른 진짜 줄에서 온다

스스로 검증한 것 — 지적을 그대로 믿지 않았다.

- **리뷰가 심은 id 를 하나하나 봤다.** 셋 다 실제로 선다(`moai-jk2u.jaq`·`moai-jk2u.m60`·
  `moai-wre3`). 지난 회차에 없는 id 를 열다섯 자리에 적던 일은 이번에 없었다
- 무작위 대조에서 **묶음 줄을 빼던 줄을 걷었다.** 3,000판이 초록이다 — 리뷰가 고친 판을 그
  대조가 다시 본 셈이고, 에픽 끝 리뷰의 고침을 다시 보는 눈이 없다는 값(moai-1d8f)을 이
  회차에서는 그 대조가 메웠다
- 리뷰의 고침 위에 넷을 더 고쳤다 — `torn_ids` 와 `shelved_at_line` 이 죽은 것을 걷고,
  `Shelved::over` 의 짝 없는 문을 닫고, `Default` 가 `no_twins` 와 같은 값임을 적었다
- 관문을 다시 돌렸다. 1444 + 544 초록, `cargo fmt --check` 깨끗, `clippy --all-targets
  -- -D warnings` 깨끗

넘긴 둘의 자리 — **moai-6mnm**(p2, 에픽·릴리스 밖). 리뷰 12·13번이고 둘 다 성능이며 이 diff
앞에 있던 것이다. 노트를 달았다.

미룸의 뿌리를 줄에 묻는다. 묶음 줄까지 줄마다 답하고, 거르는 쪽과 그리는 쪽이 한 자를 쓴다.

text:
Next: moai-wre3 과 리뷰 moai-jk2u.jaq 이 develop 에 들어갔다. 미룸의 뿌리는 이제 줄마다
답하고, 묶음 줄도 그렇다(2026-09-23 사용자 결정) — 거르는 쪽(`query::Where`)과 그리는 쪽
(`view::Seen`)이 `report::Shelved` 한 그릇을 쓴다. 가르는 열쇠는 바늘이 아니라 내용이다:
목록은 베낀 줄을 묻기 때문이다. 에픽에 열린 것은 없다. idea 셋(moai-w610·moai-a512·
moai-5v5c)은 이 에픽이 내건 것 밖이라 닫는 것을 안 막는다. 성능 나머지는 에픽 밖

/code-review medium (2026-09-25) — 5 findings, all taken in. Reviewer's own words:

> The diff is docs-only (plus test updates in `src/guide.rs`): it reverses the milestone
> rule from "attach the running release" to "work is never pulled into a running
> milestone". `cargo test` is green (1444 + 544 pass), `moai init --check` says `current`,
> and `plugin.json`'s version drop is expected (it is a content hash, not a counter). The
> problems are all internal contradictions the reversal left behind.
>
> Findings:
>
> - **`src/guide.rs:558`** (also `AGENTS.md:181`,
>   `.claude/moai-plugin/skills/moai/references/commands.md:289`) — the reversal missed the
>   one place that gives the opposite order in bold: "**If what came over is not the
>   milestone that is running, hang the running one on the epic yourself**", followed by
>   `moai edit <epic> --milestone <milestone>` and "Copy that id off the line `moai ready`
>   prints under its list for the running milestone". That is verbatim the act the new
>   bullet 100 lines later forbids ("Writing `--milestone <the running one>` on a row that
>   stood outside … say it to the person instead"). Both paragraphs are in the same
>   generated `AGENTS.md`, and the old one comes *first* in reading order, so an agent that
>   reads top-down will still pull an outside epic into the running release. The CHANGELOG
>   claims "an agent no longer writes `--milestone <the running one>` on a row that stood
>   outside", which this line contradicts. The test at `src/guide.rs:3221` still pins `"not
>   the milestone that is running"`, confirming the paragraph was left untouched
>   deliberately or by oversight.
>
> - **`src/guide.rs:1620`** — the new definition says `<milestone>` "is never a release you
>   picked for it", but the very next sentence still names the only source as
>   `MILESTONE_FROM` = "the line `moai ready` prints under its list for the running
>   milestone" (`src/guide.rs:269`), with "do not write it from memory". Following the
>   stated source yields precisely the running release the supervisor is forbidden to pick;
>   and for an idea standing under a *non-running* release that source gives nothing at
>   all, leaving the supervisor no way to fill the field as defined.
>
> - **`src/guide.rs:1615`** — `<milestone>` is redefined as "the release that idea already
>   stands under", with `none` only for "stands under none" and "nothing is running". A
>   shipped or deferred release the idea stands under now falls in neither `none` case, so
>   the supervisor fills its id in (reachable on the `p0` exception the same paragraph
>   grants). The worker then runs `moai edit <epic> --milestone <shipped release>` in brief
>   1 — re-opening a release that already went out, which is exactly what `promote`
>   deliberately declines to carry. Under the old wording ("the one that is running, or
>   `none`") a dead release could never be filled in. The brief's compensating "clear a
>   release that has already shipped or been deferred" branch is gated on `<milestone>`
>   being `none`, so it does not fire here.
>
> - **`src/guide.rs:2141`** — in the worker brief, "If `<milestone>` is `none`, nothing is
>   running" is now false: the supervisor doc two paragraphs above states `<milestone>` is
>   also `none` "for an idea that stands under no release", i.e. while a release *is*
>   running (the `p0` path). The worker is handed a false inference about repository state
>   and will skip brief 7-2's "If the epic ran inside a milestone, sort what you handed on
>   by the release bar" reasoning on wrong grounds.
>
> - **`src/guide.rs:670`** (low) — the new bullet enumerates exactly two doors into a
>   running release and says "neither is yours", but fork 3 in the same document
>   (`src/guide.rs:366`) has the agent itself run `moai add --from - --milestone <id>` after
>   the person's yes. That third, sanctioned door is not in the enumeration, so an agent
>   reading the bullet may refuse what fork 3 instructs.

text:
잰 것(2026-09-27, 워크트리 moai-mibi 의 dev 빌드로 쟀다).

**1. moai-jk2u 는 이미 13/13 으로 닫혀 있다.** 이 멤버의 제목이 묻던 "이 길이 그 에픽의 멤버
넷을 덮는가" 는 그래서 뜻이 바뀐다 — 덮을 것이 아니라, 그 넷이 하나씩 고치고 **남긴 것**이
무엇인가다. 아래 2·3 이 그 답이다.

**2. moai-w610 의 재현이 이 나무에서 그대로 선다.** 부모 id 에 쌍둥이가 서면 자식의 에픽이
파일 차례로 뒤집힌다.

- 판: 에픽 `argos-e008`·`argos-e009`, 같은 id `argos-p001` 이 둘(하나는 e008, 하나는 e009 를
  적은 `issue`), 자식 `argos-p001.aaa` 는 `epic` 을 안 적었다
- e009 줄이 뒤에 서면 `show argos-p001.aaa --json` 의 `derived_epic` 이 `argos-e009`, 두 줄의
  차례를 바꾸면 `argos-e008` 이다. 자식의 `epic` 필드는 두 판 다 없다
- `moai status --json` 의 `duplicate_id` 는 `argos-p001` 만 댄다. `lost_to_duplicate_id` 는
  안 선다 — 그 낱말은 다른 깨진 꼴의 것이다
- 그러니 **자식이 자리를 옮긴 것을 말하는 자가 아무 데도 없다**

**3. 뿌리는 `Handed::from` 의 `by_id` 다.** `groups_over` 는 이미 줄 제 `epic` 이 아니라
부모에게 묻지만(moai-5km5), 그 부모를 고르는 자가 `by_id: BTreeMap<&str, &Issue>` 라 한 id 에
한 줄, 곧 뒷줄이다. 쌍둥이 문제가 없어진 것이 아니라 **한 층 위로 올라간** 것이다.

**4. 걷어 낼 값은 적어 둔 것보다 크고, 배선은 작다.**

- `Kinds` 를 서명에 든 자는 셋이다 — `report::column`·`stands_on`·`stands_in`. 에픽 본문은
  다섯이라 적었다
- `Kinds::no_twins()` 증인은 **열아홉**이다(`cmd/mod.rs` 10 · `report.rs` 3 · `cmd/show.rs` 2 ·
  `view.rs` 2 · `cmd/add.rs` 1 · `cmd/edit.rs` 1). 여섯이라 적었다
- 곧 `group_stands_in` 이 `(Kind, id)` 로 답하게 하는 값은 서명 셋을 고치고 증인 열아홉을
  걷는 일이다

**5. 남은 멤버에 대한 판단.**

- `.pv6`(Handed 를 밖으로)와 `.rfn`(group_stands_in 의 답을 (Kind, id) 로)은 그대로 선다.
  순서도 그대로다 — `.pv6` 이 `.rfn` 의 재료다
- 막는 것은 `.wpj` 다. 자식 id 는 `<부모>.<꼬리>` 뿐이라 부모가 둘이면 **자료에 답이 없다**.
  고르는 것은 사람이고, 두 길은 이렇다 — (가) 그런 자식도 `(길 잃음)` 으로 보내고 새 경고
  낱말로 그 id 를 댄다, (나) 가려짐(`Kinds`)의 뜻을 넓혀 그 자리를 덮는다
- 권하는 것은 (가)다. 지금 하는 일(뒷줄을 조용히 입는다)이 바로 걷어 내려는 것이고, (나)는
  가려짐이라는 낱말에 둘째 뜻을 더해 `no_twins` 증인 열아홉이 무엇을 증언하는지를 흐린다
model: anthropic/opus-5 (medium — 재고 적는 걸음이라 코드는 안 바뀐다. 재현 판을 세워 쟀다)
Next: 재는 걸음(.zph)이 끝났다 — 증인이 열아홉이고 서명은 셋이며, 막는 것은 .wpj 의 사람 갈림이다. 다음은 .wpj 를 사람에게 묻고(권장: 그런 자식도 (길 잃음) 으로 보내고 새 경고가 그 id 를 댄다), 그 답 위에서 .pv6 → .rfn 을 잇는다.

사람이 정했다(2026-09-29): 부모 id 에 쌍둥이가 서면 그 밑의 자식도 (길 잃음) 으로 보내고, 새 경고 낱말이 그 자식 id 를 댄다. 뒷줄을 조용히 입는 지금 행동을 걷는 쪽이고, 이미 선 lost_to_duplicate_id 와 결이 같다. 가려짐(Kinds)의 뜻을 넓히는 길은 접었다 — no_twins 증인 열아홉이 무엇을 증언하는지가 흐려진다.

title: review — hook shell line: handoff mark, shape check, O_EXCL notice mark

note: moai-cgcm 로 펼쳤다 (이슈 1건)

text: Decided 2026-09-29 by the person (recommended option): the shell line confirms the mark. It passes a slip path (MOAI_HOOK_HANDOFF, named with its own $$ and the session id); moai writes the mark name there instead of creating the mark; the line creates it with set -C only after printf succeeded, and only from a slip it owns (-O) that is not a symlink (-h). No slip or an unwritable slip falls back to the old direct mark, so an old planted line still gets one board per session. Rejected: moving the mark after print() inside moai only (leaves the shell printf window). Residual (moai-ol3d): a verdict held in $o is still lost if the group is killed in the microseconds between moai exit and printf.

Decided 2026-09-29 by the person (recommended option): outside exits 0/1, $o counts as a verdict only when it matches {*}. Anything else (torn {"hookSpecificOutp, a foreign moai usage text + exit 64, a lone space) is dropped and the notice speaks — never two objects. Exits 0/1 still forward whatever moai wrote.

Decided 2026-09-29 by the person (recommended option): keep the mark in ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}, create it with set -C (O_EXCL, builtin, one winner among overlapping hooks). A loser stays silent only if the path is its own (-O) and not a symlink (-h); a squatted, linked or unwritable spot speaks every time. Rejected: a dir next to the user config (shell would have to mimic MOAI_CONFIG/XDG/HOME, needs mkdir -p, marks pile up forever). Foreign ownership is not tested (needs root); the symlink case is.

title: 브리프가 격리 세션에서 거절되는 git 명령을 이른다 — 714건을 쟀다

text:
Reviewer (code-review medium --fix, agent a2026ac2534eb0c86), range 3b5c2eeb..HEAD:

1. src/user_config.rs:1366 (medium) — `write_value` inserting a key that is not in the file yet, or replacing an old value that is not a string (`sort = 3`), never goes through `quoted`; `Value::from` is used as it is. A word holding `"` plus a tab or zero-width space comes out raw in single quotes: `sort = 'say "a	b​"'` (confirmed with a probe test). The `quoted` doc comment promises this never happens without a model.
2. src/user_config.rs:1321 (medium) — the second `merge_words` path (the key holds something other than an array) writes a fresh array of `Value::from` elements and skips `quoted`; confirmed `hidden = ['q"​', "b"]` with the zero-width space raw.
3. src/user_config.rs:1627 `unseen`/`escaped` (low) — the set misses the Hangul fillers (U+115F, U+1160, U+3164, U+FFA0), which draw as blank, and invisible format characters: tags U+E0001 and U+E0020–E007F, U+FFF9–FFFB, U+1BCA0–1BCA3, U+1D173–1D17A. Latent: `escaped` wrote `\u{:04X}`, which would mis-encode any character above U+FFFF once one entered the set.

Fixes applied: new-key and non-string-old paths go through `quoted(None, …)` (and `quoted(quote_of(old), …)` when the old value is a string); the fresh-array path builds elements with `quoted(None, w)`; the characters were added to `unseen`, and characters above U+FFFF escape as `\U` with eight digits. Tests were added for each, plus `a_multi_line_quote_holds_a_word_ending_in_a_quote`.

Angles checked and fine: the comment after the value is carried over (tested); multi-line `'''…'''`/`"""…"""` keep their style and `'''it''''` and `"""q\""""` read back correctly; single-quoted arrays follow the last string element in the in-place merge; escaping plus the reparse cannot change the word — the basic forms escape `\`, `"` and every control character, and the literal forms are guarded by the reparse check, which falls back to double quotes.

### What I fixed
The changes are in the worktree and not committed: `CHANGELOG.md`, `src/store.rs`, `src/report.rs`, `src/cmd/mv.rs`. The repo convention is a separate `fix:` commit for review fixes.

- **Finding 1 (temp files):** from the second name on, temp names now carry a random number unique to the process (`process_nonce`, computed once). The first name is still `tmp_name`, nothing is ever deleted, and "fail when every name is taken" stays. New test: `leftovers_of_a_dead_writer_with_the_same_pid_never_block_a_write`.
- **Finding 2 (tests):** dropped the three tautological asserts and added three scenario tests: deferred child, running milestone, and a blocked row that outranks its sibling. Each of the three mutations, plus removing the nonce, now fails exactly its own test.
- **Findings 6 and 10–13 (report.rs cleanups):**
  - `Picking` now holds its slice and a `Ties`, and skips the milestone map when nothing is deferred.
  - `closable_over`/`next_over` take Pickings, so the slice/array pairing can't be mismatched.
  - `was.open` replaces the needless sort.
  - `picks_in` is inlined into `ready_in`.
- **Findings 3, 7, 8, 14, 15:** corrected the doc comments, the CHANGELOG wording, the 11 broken links and the term usage.

**Verification:**
- I ran an equivalence check comparing the new `freed`/`ready_in` against the develop code on 6,000 random snapshots across three column configs: rows and order match exactly.
- rustfmt and `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` are clean.
- The full suite passes: 1473 unit tests (4 new) and 552 CLI tests.
- Unresolved doc links are back to the 146 that predate this branch.

- **Finding 4 (symlinks):** pre-existing. Fixing it means deciding whether writes should follow links.
- **Finding 5 (quadratic scan):** pre-existing. The fix would be one set per snapshot of "parents with an open child", shared by `unblocked_pick`, `closable_over` and `held`. Gating `closable` on the closed ids instead would narrow `freed`'s contract.
- **Finding 9 (work inside the lock):** outside the diff. It means restructuring `cmd/mv.rs` to derive the output after `with_write` returns.
- **Commit messages:** the bodies of 33a97870 and 8b8fa7ee also use 판 in the round sense. Fixing that needs a history rewrite, so I left it.

title: status and the hook resolve the timezone even when no deadline exists

text: model: anthropic/opus-5 (high — cmd/mod, view, tz and six command files; lazy timezone on the screen)

Reviewer text — /code-review xhigh --fix over develop..HEAD (d60b0a4a, 933a3e4a). Seven findings, none a correctness bug in code; five fixed in the working tree, two left.

1. CHANGELOG.md:15 — the entry claimed "the overview outside a .moai" went quiet and that the line stands only "where a deadline is judged". Only ready's overview went quiet; status prints the line even with no deadline. With TZDIR at nothing and TZ=Asia/Seoul, a bare `moai` / `moai status` outside a .moai still prints it; `moai status` in a repo with one plain issue and no milestone prints it too. It also left out `show --tree` and `show <id> --json`, which went quiet as well.
2. src/cmd/status.rs:41 — `report::status` still gets `ctx.zone()` up front (status.rs:41/276, hook.rs:158/176/181/358, tui.rs:189), so the session-start command resolves the zone even when no milestone has a `due_on`. On a static musl build every `moai` / `moai status` prints the line while drawing no time and judging no deadline.
3. src/view.rs:3887 — the yardstick test accepted any `.at(`. `.at(&crate::tz::System::default())` compiles in a call expression and passes, but that lock resolves on its own and `Ctx::zone_trouble` never sees it; times would fall back to UTC and the notice would vanish. The commit message said the compiler guards this; it only rejects `ctx.zone()`.
4. src/view.rs:2185 — `view::history` read `screen.zone()` before checking `journal.is_empty()`. Not visible today because `detail` always resolves first, but a caller drawing history alone with an empty journal would touch tzdb and print the notice without a timestamp.
5. tests/cli.rs:15399 — the new test did not cover `show --tree`, which shares the list's screen (show.rs:281); its doc said "the four" while checking five cases.
6. src/cmd/mod.rs:91 — the `Ctx::zone` doc still said only commands holding this value touch tzdb; screens now resolve through `Ctx::clock`.
7. src/cmd/mod.rs:120 — the name `Ctx::clock()` returns an unresolved timezone and is easy to confuse with the real clock (`MOAI_NOW` / `model::now()`). Maintenance cost only.

Fixed: 1 (entry names exactly what went quiet and that status, its overview and the hook still resolve), 3 (test requires `.at(ctx.clock())`), 4 (history resolves only in the non-empty branch), 5 (show --tree case added, doc corrected), 6 (doc amended).
Skipped: 2 — outside this diff; making report::status lazy puts I/O into a pure function, deciding "any deadline" in cmd/ puts issue judgement there, and moai-h2th/yz4j accepted the cost. 7 — the codebase already uses "clock" (시계) for the timezone in comments; a rename is taste.

text: Next: epic-end review moai-ydm7.ud2 (max --fix) is running on worktree-moai-ydm7; take its findings in, then merge per the brief

## Code review (max, `--fix`): install.sh upgrade and the new-release banner (moai-8rmw)

Reviewed the two epic commits (`389f610e...HEAD`) with 10 finder angles, one verifier per candidate and a final sweep. 26 candidates: 22 confirmed, 1 plausible, 4 refuted. The 15 most severe:

1. install.sh:254 — The plain one-liner (no --version) downgrades a moai that is newer than the latest release, without --force. ~/.local/bin/moai answers 'moai 10.0.0', latest is v9.9.9: `curl … | sh` replaces it and exits 0. lj5 and README only allow a downgrade when an older release is asked for with --version.
2. install.sh:224 — ours() follows symlinks, so a link to a dev build is taken for this moai and replaced by a plain file without --force; the dev build stays old and later cargo builds stop reaching PATH.
3. install.sh:171 — Recognising this moai depends on the merge-driver help sentence (src/cli.rs:520), and no test checks it against the real binary; the test fake copies the string. Reword it and every later upgrade is refused.
4. src/latest.rs:75 — UPGRADE is a fixed ~/.local/bin one-liner, but the banner shows it to whichever binary is running (a `--dir ~/bin` install gets a second copy; arm64 Linux / Intel Mac always die).
5. install.sh:252 — The same-version exit returns before the PATH-shadow check, so an older moai first on PATH is never mentioned.
6. install.sh:284 — When $dir/moai is a directory, the refusal prints a ready-to-run --force line, and running it moves the binary into that directory and reports success.
7. src/tui/draw.rs:741 — The upgrade part is appended last to a one-row banner clipped to the terminal width; it needs 104 columns (en) / 112 (ko), ~162 with a warnings part. The test checks only the unclipped string.
8. install.sh:166 — The 10-second probe limit does not bound the probe: a background child holding stdout blocks `$(…)` forever; one ignoring SIGTERM runs past 10s.
9. install.sh:150 — An existing directory the user cannot write to is only discovered after the download (raw `cp: Permission denied`).
10. install.sh:255 — order()'s `ne` falls into `*)` and prints '올린다', contradicting its own comment.
11. SECURITY.md:64 — Still promises an existing moai is never overwritten without --force, and does not say the installer now runs the existing file (as root under sudo).
12. tests/cli.rs:18201 — placed_moai writes the executable from the test process instead of write_exe/place_exe; ETXTBSY flakes.
13. install.sh:165 — `timeout 10 PROG` is coreutils syntax; BusyBox < 1.30 runs `10` as the program, so every probe fails.
14. README.md:67 — Says '--force is only for a binary the installer does not recognise', but --force also fetches the same version again.
15. CHANGELOG.md:11 — [Unreleased] is empty although the installer's user-visible behaviour changed.

### What I fixed (uncommitted in the worktree)
- install.sh: without an explicit version a moai ahead of latest is left alone (exit 0); symlinks (incl. broken) need --force; a directory at $dir/moai is refused even with --force; PATH note also on no-op exits, compared with `-ef`; probe answers go to a file under `timeout -s KILL 10`, used only if `timeout -s KILL 10 true` works; write permission checked before download; `ne` says a neutral "바꾼다"; given_* captured once, one `bare` variable.
- Banner: `latest::upgrade_line` picks the line for the running binary (~/.local/bin plain; elsewhere under home `-s -- --dir <dir>`; none for cargo builds, paths outside home, HOME=/, unserved machines). Stored on App in ask_latest.
- Docs: README, SECURITY.md, CHANGELOG entry, src/cli.rs help and docs/cli.md, contract note above MergeDriver doc line.
- Tests: 9 new integration tests (8 fail against HEAD's install.sh; the real-binary test fails when the probe string changes), one unit test for upgrade_line; placed_moai uses write_exe; install_cmd points MOAI_API_URL at a file.
- Sweep found four gaps in my own fixes (broken symlinks, path comparison, HOME=/, stray .crates.toml) — fixed and tested.
All pass: 1468 unit, 567 integration, fmt, clippy -D warnings, sh -n under dash/bash/bash --posix.

### Not fixed
- Banner clipping — the placement was the user's decision (options: second banner row, print on exit, detail pane).
- Mirror variables (MOAI_BASE_URL/MOAI_API_URL) not carried in the refusal line — undocumented knobs. Low.
- Tag in the banner line — rejected (longer, can pin a day-old cached tag).
- Wrapper scripts are still upgraded without --force — recognising by answers counts wrappers by design.
- No `timeout` on macOS — documented as intended.
- Commit ce27e0a0 uses 판 for "case" (docs/korean-terms.md) — needs a history rewrite.

Refuted: directories left by the early mkdir (2mo asked for that order), before/after messages (deliberate), shared repo-slug macro (breaks the main-branch test), banner computed twice per frame (older than this diff).

Also: epic moai-8rmw's body was the literal path of body.md; restore with `moai edit moai-8rmw -b - < <that path>`.

Review of c5dca2c7 (moai-4oab, write_atomic follows symlinks): max, --fix
Scope: git diff develop...HEAD. 10 finder angles, 15 one-vote verifiers, gap sweep. All 15 CONFIRMED, most reproduced with the dev binary. 11 fixed in the working tree; 3 (#2, #3, #4) share one cause and needed a user decision.

1. src/store.rs:670 — write_locked locks only <root>/.moai/lock, but the snapshot write now follows the link, so two trackers whose issues.jsonl reach one file hold different locks and silently lose rows; mv --from todo claim guard defeated too. Repro: B/.moai/issues.jsonl -> A/.moai/issues.jsonl, 24 concurrent adds, exit 0, only 14-17 rows remain; both sides won mv --from in 6 of 30. FIXED (Repo::far_lock).
2. src/store.rs:1403 — follow_links has no containment check, so a symlink committed in a cloned repo (.moai/issues.jsonl or AGENTS.md -> ~/.bashrc) makes routine moai add/init rewrite a file outside the checkout. Reproduced: init appended the ~29KB block (backtick spans a shell rc would run); add prepended a JSON row, breaking a gitconfig. Before the diff the link inside the repo was replaced instead.
