A third dotfile row would silently get `.gitignore`'s rules. The simpler form puts the block back into the `DOTFILES` table as a function column and drops `block_for`.
2. **`src/cmd/init.rs:237`:** the first line of the `DOTFILES` doc still describes three columns. The table now has two, and the paragraph added just below says so.
3. **Link resolution is written three times.** The tracker link is followed and checked against the root separately in `store::target_of` (the write refusal), `init::linked_snapshot` (the `.gitattributes` rule) and `status::tracker_linked` (the new notice). The three copies test for a link differently and fail differently. The simpler form is one helper in `src/path.rs` that all three call. The diff's own doc in `report.rs` says the notice exists because these resolve the link separately.
4. **`src/cmd/status.rs:187`, "셋" (three):** the `install_notices` doc and five other comments still describe three install notices. The link notice makes four, and it is not a fault, so the TUI and overview now permanently count it as one.
5. **`src/worktree.rs:1584`, `snapshot_at`:** it runs `git ls-tree` every time. Each base lookup now spawns 3 git processes instead of 2, even for an ordinary tracker file. This is the hook path that moai-h498 measured at 174ms. The fix is to call `git show` first and only run `ls-tree` when the blob could be a link.
6. **`src/cmd/init.rs:267`, `attributes_for`:** the linked rule hard-codes `text eol=lf merge=moai` instead of copying the tracker's own line. If the driver or attributes change, the linked file silently falls back to git's default merge, the bug moai-7myd fixed.

Two of your hypotheses didn't hold up. In `snapshot_at`, calling `git show` before the link check isn't wasteful, because both branches need its output; the waste is the unconditional `ls-tree`. === a18158a51a118fffd
I sent three efficiency findings to the calling agent. All of them are in `/home/coder/workspace/moa-issue/.claude/worktrees/moai-ydm7/src/worktree.rs`. No files were edited and cargo was not run.

1. **`snapshot_at` runs an extra git process every time (line 1589).** It now calls `git ls-tree` before every `git show`, so a normal tracker file takes two processes where one used to do.
   - **When it runs:** only for sibling worktrees that hold rows missing from the caller's tracker. In that state it hits every TUI reload, every `status`/`ready`/`show --worktree`, and the hook's refusal path, Stop check and post-compact start.
   - **Cost:** `git ls-tree` took 4–7 ms per call here. In the 8-worktree setup measured for moai-h498, spawns go from 10 to 15, adding about 20–55 ms per call. That gives back about half of what moai-h498 saved.
   - **Cheaper option:** run `show` first and call `ls-tree` only if the output is non-empty and doesn't end in a newline. Every tracker file moai writes ends in one, and link text never does. The other option is a single `git cat-file --batch --follow-symlinks`, but the git helper would need a version that can take stdin.

2. **Following a linked tracker costs two git processes per link hop and never checks for a cycle (line 1587).** A tracker linked one hop deep costs 5 processes instead of 2. A link loop committed at the base runs all 41 iterations, which is 82 processes (roughly 0.3–0.6 s) on every call for as long as that commit stays the merge-base. The same `cat-file --follow-symlinks` call handles the whole chain in one process and reports loops itself. The smallest fix is to stop when a path repeats.

3. **The per-HEAD cache is keyed on the wrong thing (line 615).** It's keyed by sibling HEAD, not by the commit they share as a base. In a worker session's hook check, every sibling forked after that worker shares one base. The same 1.8 MB `git show` (22–24 ms) plus parse then runs once per sibling instead of once. This redundancy predates the diff, which adds one more process to each repeat. Caching by base commit would fix it.

- **Checked, too small to flag:**
  - The same link is resolved twice per notices pass (in `linked_snapshot` and in `tracker_linked`). For a normal file that is two filesystem calls costing microseconds, next to the git processes that pass already starts.
  - `append_inside` adds two filesystem calls per journal write.

- **Stale comment:** the `side()` doc comment (lines 596–601) still says a miss costs two git calls; it's now three.
- **Today's state:** none of this is running right now. Every row in the two sibling worktrees is still in the main tracker. It starts to matter after the next `moai rm` at the root, or in a repo where branches commit their own rows.

Review /code-review max --fix (agent af783e2bb512c2379) — reviewer's own words, final report.

Ten finder angles, one verifier per deduplicated candidate (18, all CONFIRMED), and a gap sweep produced these 15, most severe first:

1. src/cmd/rm.rs:121 — When `--line` points at a readable line, the refusal says `remove that by id: moai rm <id>`. In the stale-number case this refusal exists for, that id is an unrelated live issue; when the id stands twice, `rm <id>` removes the copy the user meant to keep. Scenario: broken twin mid-file, `moai show` says line 2; another session runs `moai add`; `rm --line 2 --yes` prints `moai rm <the new issue>`. Running it deletes an issue nobody targeted. Reproduced. Contradicts moai-pp9i.gtc.
2. src/cmd/rm.rs:152 — `--yes` finds the line by number only. Any write that changes the row count (including the previous `rm --line`) renumbers the unreadable block, so `--yes` can remove a different unreadable line. Scenario: unreadable lines 3, 4, 5, with line 5 a newer binary's row. `rm --line 3 --yes; rm --line 4 --yes` removes 3 and the newer-binary row, exit 0, and the old output printed no text. Reproduced by 6 agents.
3. src/cmd/rm.rs:161 — The success text says the raw line is kept in the journal's rm entry. False when the line is over 64KB (`fit_bytes` cuts it) or when the journal append fails, and human mode never printed the text. Scenario: 70KB line: journal note ends in `…`. Journal dir not writable: exit 0, line gone, stderr says `write it again with moai note: ` with an empty id. Reproduced.
4. src/cmd/rm.rs:143 — File bytes reach the terminal unsanitized: preview text, id in `head()`, refusal id, the rm entry's note in `moai show` history, serde's message in `name_load_errors`. Scenario: a broken twin containing `ESC[2J` or an OSC title sequence clears the screen on `rm --line n`, and after `--yes` on every `moai show <live id>`. Reproduced under a pty.
5. src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:698 — The multi-row guard lets an id through only when all three sides are alike. Removing a twin with `rm --line` on one side conflicts with any side that kept it untouched, or removed it too (two identical panels). Scenario: base=[L,T], ours=[L], theirs=[L,T] or [L]: exit 1 both directions. Guard predates this diff (moai-2m94, moai-ijfy); the feature makes it common.
6. src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:583 — The keyed-first sort in `unkeyed` does not make the result a fixed point in general; `unpair`/`unkeyed` docs stale. Scenario: `carried` holds broken argos-0005 and `unpair` demotes argos-0001: answer [0002, 0005, 0001, stub], next merge swaps them. Found 9-26 times in fuzzing.
7. src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:766 — `kept`'s byte 3-way picks the trailing `\r` that `str::lines` leaves on the last line of a CRLF file with no final newline, so the answer writes `…\r\n`. Reproduced.
8. src/view.rs:2216 — The rm entry for a live issue's broken twin is filed under the live id and drawn as `removed`, so the live issue's history says it was removed. Reproduced.
9. src/cmd/mod.rs:346 — The hint `to remove one: moai rm --line <n>` prints under every unreadable line, including rows a newer binary wrote, which the tool carries on purpose.
10. src/cmd/rm.rs:95 — `rm --line --json` uses `removed` as a bool; `rm <id> --json` uses `removed` as an array. Unreleased, free to rename.
11. src/cmd/rm.rs:115 — `refuse` is a second reader of issues.jsonl outside `store`; without the lock its read and `repo.read()` can see two different files. FIFO repro.
12. src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:2628 — Two new both-ways tests only assert `contains(new bytes)`, and the new line contains the old line, so a regression emitting both variants stays green.
13. src/report.rs:5505 — The line number `rm --line` needs appears on no `--json` surface; only localized stderr (first 5 lines) or a refusal's text carries it.
14. src/cmd/mod.rs:346 — The hint drops `-C <root>` and `MOAI_HERE=1`, so copying it targets a different tracker. Reproduced. Low.
15. i18n/en.json:56 — For a live row plus its broken twin, the board's `duplicate_id` text offers only `moai rm <id>`, which removes the live issue. Reproduced.

Fixed: refusal lists current unreadable lines with ids and hands out no remove command (second read and `refuse.line_readable` gone); `--yes` prints the removed line sanitized, `rm.line_removed` no longer promises journal retention, new `rm.line_cut`; journal-failure notice no longer lists rm entries; `text::one_line`/`text::sanitize` in rm.rs, `view::entry`, `name_load_errors`; rm entry with no title renders as "removed an unreadable line" (`journal.remove_line`); `by_issue` puts unkeyed's keyed survivors into `carried` in id order, sort removed, docs rewritten; `keyed()` strips trailing `\r`; hint reworded, listing shows ids; `removed` renamed to `dry_run`; tests tightened plus new ones; docs and comments fixed; docs/cli.md regenerated, docs/recovery.md updated.

Skipped: binding `--yes` to the shown line (new CLI option, user's call — suggest member); relaxing the multi-row merge guard (relaxes moai-2m94/moai-ijfy user decisions — suggest member); JSON line numbers, `-C` in the hint, `warn.duplicate_id` wording (suggest ideas). Left alone: `paired`/`rows_alike` unification, `row()` re-parse cost, `not_found` vs `bad_target`, uncapped refusal list.

Review /code-review max --fix (agent a4ca4a81681b776c4). The reviewer's own words, final report.

1. src/cmd/rm.rs:181. When the hash doesn't match, the refusal prints the hash of the line that now sits at that number (`now {now}`) and says to look at the same number again. That hands over everything needed to remove a line nobody previewed, which is the failure moai-6nha was meant to stop. Scenario: unreadable lines are 2=A, 3=B, 4=C. A session previews line 3 (B, hash hB). Another session removes line 2, so B moves to 2 and C to 3. `rm --line 3 --yes --match hB` is refused with '(hash hB, now hC) … Look again with `moai rm --line 3`'. Retrying with `--match hC` removes C at exit 0 without anyone seeing it (reproduced). The refusal never says B is now line 2.
2. src/cmd/rm.rs:207. The preview's 'exact command to type' leaves out how the preview reached its tracker: `-C <dir>` and `MOAI_HERE=1`. The two refusal hints leave it out too. Scenario: in a linked worktree, `MOAI_HERE=1 moai rm --line 2` previews the worktree's own tracker and prints `moai rm --line 2 --yes --match H`. Run as printed, that command is redirected to the main checkout's tracker. Right after the split that tracker has the same bytes at line 2, so the hash matches and the root's line is removed at exit 0 (reproduced).
3. src/cmd/rm.rs:176. `--match` is bound to the line's bytes only. When a file holds byte-identical unreadable lines, running the same command a second time removes the second copy. Scenario: the file ends with two identical lines K (for example a newer-binary row duplicated by a hand-resolved merge; one copy should stay). `rm --line 7 --yes --match H` removes the first K. A retry after a timeout finds the second K at line 7 with the same hash and removes it too, at exit 0.
4. CHANGELOG.md:55. [Unreleased] has no entry for moai-fl7e, even though it takes back a promise in the shipped 0.1.2 notes: 'Everything either side touched still goes to a person', and a twin merged straight in at exit 0 was listed there as a fixed bug. Scenario: release notes are cut from this file (CONTRIBUTING.md:166-168). With base [G], ours [G], theirs [G, J], the merge now exits 0 and writes a duplicated id. Nothing in the notes says the rule changed.
5. CHANGELOG.md:30. The [Unreleased] `rm --line` entry still says `--yes` alone removes the line and never mentions `--match` or the hash. Scenario: a reader of the next release notes runs `moai rm --line 812 --yes` and gets bad_input.
6. src/cmd/rm.rs:177. `--match` is never checked for hash form. An empty or malformed value takes the write lock and is refused as not_found with a message saying the line 'moved or changed'. Scenario: a script's hash variable is empty: `rm --line 3 --yes --match ""` gives `not_found` 'line 3 is no longer the line shown (hash , now …)' about a line that never moved (reproduced).
7. src/cmd/rm.rs:221. `fingerprint` includes a trailing `\r` that the next moai write strips, so an untouched line's hash changes between preview and `--yes`. Scenario: a file ends in a bare CR on its last unreadable line. Preview prints h('J\r'). Any `moai edit` rewrites that line as 'J\r\n', which reads back as 'J'. `--yes --match h('J\r')` is then refused as 'moved or changed' (reproduced). `merge_driver::keyed` already strips this `\r` for the same reason.
8. src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:815. When the base doesn't match the sides, `both_kept` picks the smaller byte variant row by row. The result can be a group that neither branch ever held, which contradicts settle's own justification that the answer already stood on one branch. Scenario: base [G,H], ours [G,H,A,'B '], theirs [G,H,'A ',B], where A and B are broken twins of one id. Both directions write [G,H,A,B], a combination neither branch had (reproduced).
9. src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:730. Design limitation: because groups are compared as a whole, the everyday shapes around a twin removal still conflict. This follows the 2026-09-29 decision's wording. Scenario: base [G, J]. Case 1: ours removes J with `rm --line`, theirs runs `moai mv` on G, giving a conflict both ways. Case 2: both remove J and one also edits G, giving [G] vs [G'] as a conflict (reproduced). Resolving these safely needs a rule the user has not chosen; an unrestricted 'drop rows both sides removed' reopens the moai-2m94 silent revert.
10. i18n/en.json:670. `refuse.match_without_yes` says 'without --yes nothing is removed', which is false for removal by id. It and `yes_without_line` send the user back and forth between each other. Scenario: `moai rm <id> --match X` is told to add --yes. `moai rm <id> --yes --match X` is then told --yes goes with --line only (reproduced).
11. src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:2175. The new test `a_group_both_sides_changed_alike_is_the_same_bytes_both_ways` doesn't exercise the new base choice, and it rebuilds the existing `both_ways` helper by hand. Scenario: replacing `min_by(x, y, ..)` with `x` keeps the test green, while [I,J1,J2] against [I,J2,J1] would then give different bytes depending on merge direction.
12. src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:450. Stale comments. `keyed` still says settle hands a stacked id wholesale to a person. `Settled::Each` (l.201) quotes '같은 줄들', which the diff removed. The early-guard comment in `settle` (l.706) justifies the guard by a both-panels-empty marker that the new group branch can no longer produce. Scenario: the only function that builds duplicate-id groups documents a contract that is no longer true, which invites someone to 'fix' the one-side take back into a conflict on every merge.
13. src/cli.rs:1140. The `--yes` help ('With --line: remove it') and the matching line in docs/cli.md are incomplete now that `--yes` also needs `--match`. Scenario: `moai rm --help` implies `rm --line N --yes` removes the line; it is refused with bad_input.
14. src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:808. New doc comments use 판 in the 회차 (case) sense. Rule from CLAUDE.md: '용어는 docs/korean-terms.md 가 정한다', and docs/korean-terms.md:49 says '판(회차) → 번, 때, 회차, 경우, 벌' for new `src/**/*.rs` doc comments. Affected new lines: l.302, 715-725, 808, 2123, 2136, 2172-2173, 2433.
15. src/cmd/rm.rs:138. Cleanup: `line(.., yes: Option<Option<&str>>)` exists only to carry one refusal into `line`, and it splits the flag checks across two functions. The new tests also build `stdout + stderr` by hand instead of using the existing `text(&out)` helper. The comment on `RmArgs.matches` ('거절은 rm::run 이 한다') was only half true.

I fixed 14 of the 15 findings; one needs your call. `cargo test` passes (1506 unit, 582 CLI), clippy -D warnings and fmt --check are clean.

Fixed: mismatch refusal now names where the line you were shown stands now ({went}), no other hash, no look-again at the same number. Command routing: new `to_type` builds the preview command and the refusal hint through `init::away_root(repo.here(), ctx.chdir)` and `Warning::cli_hint`, adds `MOAI_HERE=1` when on; checked in a worktree. Hash: `fingerprint` counts identical copies and ignores a trailing `\r`. Flag checks: `--yes`/`--match` validated in `rm::run`, 8 hex digits required, `line` takes `Option<&str>`, `match_without_yes` names `--line` and `--yes`. `both_kept`: when the base doesn't match, returns the smaller side's group whole; checked that the result equals the ours file byte for byte in both directions. Merge-driver comments updated, 판 → 경우 in the new lines; group test uses `both_ways` with cases for twin order and bytes changed on different rows. Docs: two CHANGELOG entries, docs/recovery.md, `--yes` help, docs/cli.md regenerated. Tests: `rm_line_the_same_command_twice_leaves_the_second_copy`, `rm_line_preview_command_keeps_the_dir_it_was_given`, extended bad_input cases, unit tests in rm.rs; rm tests use `text()`.

Skipped: the conflicting twin shapes (9) follow the 2026-09-29 decision; resolving them needs a rule not chosen yet. Merging the two 3-way checks in `settle` into one (cleanup, restructures the merge path). 판 in the commit message of 922bd9fc (history rewrite only).

판단(리뷰 원문과 따로 적는다).

- 받은 것: 9번을 뺀 14건을 리뷰의 `--fix` 그대로 받았다. 테스트·clippy·fmt 를 다시 돌려 통과를 확인했고, 코드는 fix 커밋 하나, CHANGELOG 는 docs(changelog) 커밋 하나로 담았다
- 밖으로 뺀 것: 9번 → idea moai-z4wk(마일스톤 없음). 사용자 결정의 글대로 선 설계 한계이고, 충돌로 서니 조용한 손실은 아니다. 풀려면 새 규칙이 들어 사람이 정한다. 에픽이 내건 것(못 읽는 줄을 도구 안에서 다룬다)은 이것 없이도 선다
- 손대지 않은 것: `settle` 의 3-way 검사 둘을 하나로 합치기, 커밋 메시지의 "판". 리뷰의 판단에 동의한다
- 다섯 자리 확인: 새 항목이 옆 항목의 문서 주석을 가로챈 곳은 없다. 되돌리면 붉어지는지는 11번이 짚은 묶음 시험을 쌍둥이 둘로 다시 짜 닫았다. 한 자리에서만 세우는지는 해당하지 않는다. 주석과 문서는 12·13·14번으로 고쳤다. 새로 여는 길은 `to_type` 의 `here_wanted()` 가 환경 변수를 읽는 것뿐이고, 설정 파일을 새로 열지는 않는다

**What I fixed**
- **Duplicated ids when paging (K1):** all lines that share one id are now sorted and paged as a single unit, and a page never splits them. Healthy files behave exactly as before. In a file with duplicated ids, those lines now print next to each other, and a page can come out longer than `-n` so the duplicated lines stay together.
- **Empty and malformed time values (K2, K3):** an empty value is refused. Typed timestamps go through a new strict parser, `model::parse_instant`, which still accepts every stamp moai writes.
- **`--done` with a contradicting `-s` (K7):** refused.
- **Docs and help text (K4, K5, K6, K8, K9, the unreadable-stamp gap):** rewritten in the README, the `SHOW_LIST` help text and code comments. I regenerated `docs/cli.md` with `MOAI=target/debug/moai scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh`, so no release build was needed.
- **README and help examples (K15):** replaced, and I ran them verbatim against duckdb on a plain repo, a repo with an epic and an empty repo.
- **Double journal read (K17):** one read now serves both the notes search and `work`.
- **Refusal wording (the tree and single-id refusals, K19, K20):** the tree and single-id refusals now give the right reason. The count reuses `more_of`, with the command kept outside the translated text. The not-found message reuses `Fail::not_found`.
- **Other cleanups:** unnecessary timestamp parsing when no time filter is set (K27), one shared `query::cut` (K21), `-n` parsed straight to `usize` (K24), corrected `SortKey::Id` comment (K10), and wording fixes for the Korean terms rules (K12/K13).
- **Tests added:** paging over duplicated ids, empty/strict/contradicting time values, `--sort updated`, `ready -n` outside a repo, and a check that `--sort` words match the explorer's names.

**What I skipped and why**
- **Korean-only errors (K11):** translating them means changing `Filter::build`'s error type for both `show` and the TUI, and the older errors in `query.rs` are Korean too. Nothing in the tracker covers these; it should get its own item.
- **UTC days (K5):** the behaviour is your recorded decision (moai-efoc.ip5), so I only corrected its reasoning. You need to choose: keep UTC days (the same answer on every machine), or use the reader's local day to match the screen and deadlines. The second needs the time zone passed into `Filter::build`.
- **Continuing past a removed cursor under `--sort id` (K1b):** it would reverse the deliberate, tested `not_found` refusal.
- **Adding a cut count to `ready --json` (E4):** it extends the public JSON contract.
- **Low-value efficiency items (F1, F4, F5, K26):** each is either low value or lives in code the explorer shares.
- The README's "defaults to Korean" line is wrong, but it predates this branch.

Per CLAUDE.md these should go in as separate `fix:` commits, and the CHANGELOG still needs updating. The main files touched are `/home/coder/workspace/moa-issue/.claude/worktrees/moai-efoc/src/query.rs`, `src/cmd/show.rs`, `src/model.rs`, `src/cli.rs`, `README.md` and `tests/cli.rs`.

text:
Review of epic moai-wcy8 (`65d251dc..HEAD`, about 600 diff lines) is done and the fixes are applied to the worktree. Nothing is committed and the tracker is untouched, so review issue moai-wcy8.rbj is still open for you to record.

## Findings

```json
[
  {"file":"src/query.rs","line":170,"summary":"Where::noted lowercases every note of every row that id/title/tag/body did not match, on every keystroke of the live `/` filter, and again on Tab, arrow keys and every reapply after a reread.","failure_scenario":"Main checkout: 4,800 notes, 4.4MB. A query that matches no field, in All or Note scope, folds all 4.4MB per key. Measured with a rustc -O benchmark on the real note texts: 83-89 ms per key in release (roughly 10x in debug), against 0.4-0.9 ms on notes folded once."},
  {"file":"src/tui/mod.rs","line":619,"summary":"prepare and cmd::tui::run read and JSON-parsed every root's whole journal on every load, even when no search is active.","failure_scenario":"About 5.9MB is parsed on the UI thread after every TUI write, on SPC v w and on entering a project. The hub re-parses each expanded project's journal on every write there and keeps its notes, though `/` is disabled on the layer. `moai tui | cat` read the journal before refusing (probe confirmed). This goes against the file's own rule that history walks stay out of prepare because the loop calls it."},
  {"file":"src/tui/mod.rs","line":347,"summary":"An unreadable journal file now changes `moai tui`'s exit code, and nothing in the TUI says the search results are missing those notes.","failure_scenario":"A teammate's `.moai/journal/<mail>.jsonl` is 0600, a case store.rs calls common. `/` silently misses those notes. On a normal quit, stderr prints the chmod line and the exit status is 1, even if the person never searched. Launched outside `.moai` (here=None), any expanded project's unreadable file flips the exit code. The UNREAD list is never cleared, so a mid-session chmod does not help."},
  {"file":"src/store.rs","line":577,"summary":"The legacy `.moai/journal.jsonl` is read without the is_file check that files under journal/ get.","failure_scenario":"A FIFO there makes `show <id>` and `show -g` hang (probe: timeout 124). Since this diff it also hung `moai tui` before the first frame and on the UI thread in raw mode, where Ctrl-C is only a key. A link to /dev/zero reads until memory runs out."},
  {"file":"src/tui/draw.rs","line":2388,"summary":"The detail's matching-notes block was rebuilt on every frame (noted_lines, wrap, mark) with no cache, unlike the body.","failure_scenario":"`/moai` with the cursor on moai-wxkm.95w (385KB of notes) puts about 8,000 rows in the detail. The verifier measured about 600 ms per frame in the debug TUI; the release estimate is 18-40 ms per frame."},
  {"file":"src/store.rs","line":626,"summary":"journal_marks listed journal/ first and stamped the directory last.","failure_scenario":"A person's first `<mail>.jsonl` created between those two steps is never marked, but the directory stamp already counts it. That person's later notes are missed until the 60 s clock. worktree::heads stamps its directory before listing for exactly this reason."},
  {"file":"src/tui/draw.rs","line":2388,"summary":"The matching-notes block has no cap and sits above the body in All scope, even for rows matched by title or body.","failure_scenario":"On the real tracker, 'moai-' puts a block of 30 or more rows above the body on 62 of 767 rows at width 70. The body and its highlighted hits end up below the panel."},
  {"file":"src/tui/mod.rs","line":2391,"summary":"The `f` filter's `grep=` now matches notes, but the detail only draws matched note lines for `/`, because grep_query needs a leading '/'.","failure_scenario":"`f` then `grep=zebra` keeps a row whose only 'zebra' is in a note, and nothing on screen shows why it matched."},
  {"file":"CHANGELOG.md","line":63,"summary":"The [Unreleased] entry still says \"`moai tui`'s `/` does not look at notes yet.\"","failure_scenario":"That sentence is false after this epic."},
  {"file":"src/tui/mod.rs","line":357,"summary":"The journal marks chose their roots with their own rule (a copy of commit_roots' dedup loop plus an inline Repo::at) instead of cmd::show::home and at_home.","failure_scenario":"Correct today, but if `home` moves to repo.here(), marks and reads stop agreeing and no test goes red, because the tests only use Origin::default(). journal_of_rows' own doc warns about exactly this."},
  {"file":"src/query.rs","line":1772,"summary":"The_note_lines_that_matched_are_the_lines_the_filter_saw never runs the filter.","failure_scenario":"If only one side's folding changes (ς→σ, trimming), the detail goes empty for a row matched through its notes, and the test stays green."},
  {"file":"src/tui/mod.rs","line":302,"summary":"A new doc comment calls the project layer '층'.","failure_scenario":"CLAUDE.md hands terms to docs/korean-terms.md, whose table says 'layer | 레이어 | 층' (write 레이어, not 층) for newly written doc comments."},
  {"file":"src/tui/mod.rs","line":8162,"summary":"A test opens a directory with File::open and set_modified without #[cfg(unix)].","failure_scenario":"It panics on Windows; the same idiom in production code is unix-gated."},
  {"file":"src/query.rs","line":270,"summary":"GrepIn::Note => \"노트\" is Korean hard-coded outside the i18n bundle.","failure_scenario":"The English UI shows 'search·노트' and '/노트:…'. The other four scope names already do this."},
  {"file":"src/tui/draw.rs","line":2394,"summary":"The painted text can differ from the matched text.","failure_scenario":"A query with a trailing space, or one that straddles a wrap, gives a drawn 'matching notes' line with no highlight. Cosmetic, and the same limitation title and body already have."}

```

## What I changed

- **Notes load only when a search needs them.** They are read the first time a filter that looks at notes is applied (`/` in the all or notes scope, or `grep=`), and folded to lowercase once per load. Opening, rereads, writes and hub reads no longer touch the journal. When such a search is on, the background reread thread reads the notes too, so the UI loop doesn't. This fixes findings 1, 2 and 10, and most of 3.
- **Unreadable journals now only affect sessions that searched notes.** A browse-only session or the hub no longer exits 1 because of a 0600 journal file.
- **Store:** the legacy journal path is skipped unless it is a regular file, and the `journal/` directory is stamped before it is listed (findings 4 and 6).
- **Detail pane:** the matching-notes lines are cached the way the body already is. Leaving a project drops that cache and the project's loaded notes (finding 5).
- **Tests:** the weak test now checks the filter and the detail against each other, including İ and final Σ. I added tests for the FIFO case, the lazy load and the reread thread. The directory-timestamp test is now unix-only.
- **Other:** the CHANGELOG sentence and the 층 doc comment are fixed.

A final gap-sweep pass found that my first version of the lazy load read the journal on the UI loop after background rereads. That is fixed, along with a cache that survived leaving a project and an inaccurate CHANGELOG line.

All 1,522 unit and 590 integration tests pass, and clippy (`-D warnings`) and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. Re-running the probes against the new build: `moai tui` without a terminal no longer reads the journal, and a FIFO journal no longer hangs `show`.

## Not fixed (need a decision)

- **Finding 3, remaining part:** there is still no in-session notice when a journal file can't be read, and the unread list is process-wide and never cleared. How a long-running TUI should report this is a design choice.
- **Finding 7:** capping or moving the matching-notes block changes what the detail shows.
- **Finding 8:** showing why `f grep=` matched would add highlighting to the `f` filter.
- **Finding 14:** the fix belongs to all five scope names, not just the new one.
- **Finding 15:** cosmetic.
- **Commit 6346617e's message** also uses 층 and 값; fixing it needs a history rewrite.
- **A narrow race:** two journal files created within one clock tick can go unnoticed for up to 60 seconds. It fixes itself.

I suggest filing 3, 7, 8 and 14 as members of epic moai-wcy8. The help-text scope list is already moai-msw7.

## Code review (max, --fix): `moai show --removed`, moai-7dmq (`git diff develop...HEAD`)

I found 15 problems (list below). Ten finders ran, then six verifiers and one gap sweep. Twelve problems are fixed in the working tree. Three are reported only: #4 and #15 (partly) need a person's call, and #9 got a help-text fix instead of the full restructure. **Nothing is committed.**

Checks after the fixes:
- `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo test --locked` passes: 1518 unit tests and 591 CLI tests.
- `docs/cli.md` was regenerated with `MOAI=target/debug/moai scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh`.
- I broke the code three ways on purpose and the new tests caught each one: dropping the `\u` fallback, turning a JSON parse failure into `break`, and putting the unsanitized `short_stamp` back.

1. src/view.rs:2290 — view::removed printed the journal ts raw (short_stamp returns an unreadable ts unchanged); id, title and by went through one_line, the ts did not. Scenario: a journal line with ts "\u001b]0;pwned\u0007" retitles the terminal, and \u001b[2J clears it, on every `moai show --removed`. A ts containing \n splits one removal into two rows. Reproduced by 5 finders.
2. README.md:245 — README said 'the list above says whether it lives now', but `--since` misses exactly the rows that come back with an older stamp. Scenario: the id is restored via git checkout of issues.jsonl, or `rm` removed one of two lines sharing an id. `show --since T` gives [] and `show --removed --since T` lists the id, so a mirror following the recipe deletes a live row.
3. README.md:241 — the docs present `--removed --since` as the complement of `--since`, but it keys on the rm line's own ts, and the older-stamp caveat given for rows was missing (also src/cli.rs:976). Scenario: branch B runs `rm X` on 09-10; the consumer's cursor is 09-12; B is merged on 09-13. Both halves of the recipe return [] and the mirror keeps X forever. Same when the rm stamp is taken before a 5s lock wait (rm.rs:42), or when the journal append failed.
4. src/store.rs:1057 — `--removed` silently skips rm lines that fail to parse, with exit 0 and nothing on stderr. The leniency's rationale ('the journal builds no state') does not hold here, because the journal is the whole answer. Scenario: a torn journal tail (no trailing \n) followed by `moai rm B`: the rm line is glued onto the torn line. B is gone from the snapshot, yet `show --removed --json` prints [] with exit 0. NOT FIXED — needs a decision.
5. src/store.rs:1019 — journal_of_kind's prefilter `contains("\"rm\"")` dropped rm lines whose kind is written with a \u escape. The sibling prefilters model::may_hold_note/may_hold_work let \u lines through on purpose. Scenario: a line with "kind":"rm" plus a title is drawn as 'removed' in `moai show <id>` history but is absent from `show --removed`.
6. src/view.rs:2290 — the list used short_stamp (MM-DD, no year) on an all-time list. Scenario: removals on 2025-12-31 23:30 and 2026-12-31 23:30 both print as `12-31 23:30`.
7. src/cmd/show.rs:432 — removed() re-parsed --filter items by hand, duplicating query::desugar, next to given() with a literal 17 and name-string exclusions. Scenario: `--removed --filter since` (no `=`) and `--filter bogus=1` were refused as '`--filter` cannot be used', while the list gives desugar's own errors.
8. src/cmd/show.rs:448 — one refusal reason ('nothing to pick them by' / 'only --since narrows it') was used for every refused flag. Scenario: `-n 1`, `--sort`, `--reverse`, `--after`, `--worktree`, `--tree`, `--raw`, `--as-plan` got a filtering reason that is false for them.
9. src/cli.rs:1015 — `--removed` sits on the shared ShowArgs, so `moai issue|epic|milestone|idea show --help` advertise it, yet it is always refused there, naming the namespace word as if it were a flag.
10. src/cmd/show.rs:439 — the refusal lists were hand-kept with no compile-time or test guard; the new test tried 9 of 25 refused inputs.
11. src/cli.rs:977 — help and README said '--json gives the journal lines as they are', but JournalEntry has no flatten catch-all. An rm line with an extra key comes out without it.
12. tests/cli.rs:7132 — the `--removed` entry added to every_list_only_filter_is_refused_on_a_single_issue was vacuous: the refusal template always contains `--removed`. The same weakness hit the new test's `-s` check, because the how-line always contains `--since`.
13. src/store.rs:2578 — the store unit test's 'broken line' had no "rm", so the prefilter dropped it before the parser. No test reached each_entry's parse-failure `continue`.
14. CHANGELOG.md:11 — [Unreleased] had no entry for `--removed`.
15. src/store.rs:2567 — new doc comments broke docs/korean-terms.md: `판` in the 회차 sense, and the Korean-first gloss '그 갈래(`kind`)' / '만듦' for `create`.

Fixed (working tree): #1, #6 (stamp sanitized and carries the year; new unit test a_removed_row_is_one_clean_line_with_its_year); #5 (prefilter passes `\u`; shared in_ts_order); #13, #15 (test lines, terms); #7 (ShowArgs destructured exhaustively, --filter through query::desugar now pub, given() gone); #10 (exhaustive destructuring makes a new field a compile error); #8 (refusal reason en/ko); #2, #3, #9, #11 (help paragraph, README, docs/cli.md regenerated; sync recipe backs the cursor off a few seconds); #12 (tests cover all 25 refused inputs, flag in its slot); #14 (CHANGELOG entry).

Skipped or noted:
- #4 needs a design decision: either `--removed` counts rm-looking lines that fail to parse and warns with note_partial, or the journal append restores a missing `\n` (write path, outside this diff).
- #9 deeper fix (top-level-only arg struct) not done; the restriction is documented.
- `query::removed` takes `&[JournalEntry]` while CLAUDE.md says report and query are pure functions over `&[Issue]` — a wording mismatch that needs a person's decision.
- Efficiency: each_entry validates UTF-8 on every line before the prefilter, about 40–50% of `show --removed` time on the real 5.9MB journal. Predates this diff.
- Pre-existing, outside the diff: view::history (src/view.rs ~2218) has the same unsanitized-ts gap; single-letter entries in every_list_only_filter_is_refused_on_a_single_issue can pass on a random id alone (argos-n7tw contains -n).

text:
Review text — /code-review max --fix (agent-adee25d8194dfdcca), scope: moai-2htt branch diff + commit 670a530a

I ran the full max-effort pass: 10 finder angles, one verifier per candidate, and a gap sweep. 15 findings survived. I fixed 13 of them in the working tree, plus four smaller items that fell below the cut. Nothing is committed, and `.moai/` is untouched.

1. src/query.rs:802 — Since 670a530a, a range with one bare-day end and one `…Z` end is never checked for running backwards, so a range reversed by months is accepted and answers nothing. `moai show --created 2026-12-01..2026-01-01T00:00:00Z --json` (or `2026-12-01T00:00:00Z..2026-01-01`) prints `[]` and exits 0; the same-kind form is refused as bad_filter. The check `if let (Some(End::At(f)), Some(End::At(t))) | (Some(End::Wall(f)), Some(End::Wall(t))) = (from, to) && f > t` never matches a mixed pair, and before 670a530a every pair was compared. Reproduced with the dev binary.
2. src/cmd/mod.rs:368 — A bare-day filter now resolves the timezone before `show` can fail. `cmd::run` prints the zone-trouble line even when a `--json` run fails, so stderr is no longer the single JSON error object that main.rs promises. `TZ=Mars/Olympus` (or `TZ=KST-9`, or a musl build with no zoneinfo): `moai show --since 2026-06-01 --after <removed id> --json` puts `moai: this machine does not know the timezone …` on stderr ahead of `{"code":"not_found",…}`. A paging loop that parses stderr for `code` hits a parse error. With a `…Z` filter the stderr is clean. Reproduced.
3. src/tui/zones.rs:169 — `set_zone` (`SPC o t`) swaps `self.zone` but never re-applies the active filter, although 670a530a made `site.keep` depend on that zone. Explorer on Seoul time; `SPC f created=2026-10-01` keeps a row created 2026-09-30T20:00Z. Switch to UTC: the detail now prints 09-30 20:00, but the row stays listed under the `created=2026-10-01` badge until the next re-read (up to 60s) or a file change. Rows then flip without a keypress.
4. src/tz.rs:325 — The zone-file parser ignores the POSIX rule at the end of the file, assuming the file lists decades of future transitions. That only holds for 'fat' zone files; 670a530a makes the same wrong offset decide which rows a day filter keeps. With zone files built by `zic -b slim` (zic's default since 2020b), New York's last transition is 2007 into EDT. A row created 2026-01-15T04:30Z shows as `2026-01-15 00:30` (true local time is 01-14 23:30), is missing from `--created 2026-01-14` and appears under `--created 2026-01-15`. No warning is printed. Reproduced with a slim zone-file directory via `TZDIR`. The display offset was already wrong before this branch.
5. src/tui/mod.rs:2541 — The zone wiring had no test that fails when it is removed: the explorer's `wh.zone = Some(&self.zone)`, `show --removed`'s `timed.needs_zone().then(|| ctx.zone())` (show.rs:508), and the `done` part of `Filter::needs_zone`. Deleting any of the three left the whole suite green. No TUI test types `since=`/`created=`/`done=`, every CLI `--removed` test runs under TZ=UTC, and the `needs_zone` asserts cover `--since` only. Each would silently fall back to UTC days.
6. src/cmd/show.rs:507 — Two of the four new language mappings were not pinned: the `--removed` time-parse refusal, and the explorer refusal, which was only checked in English (the default). Replacing `ctx.lang()` with `Lang::Ko` at show.rs:507, or `self.site.lang` with `Lang::En` at tui/mod.rs:2567, stayed green. The only `--removed` case (`--filter since`) fails earlier, inside `desugar`.
7. src/view.rs:3047 — The view test pinned the retype command only for `-s` and `-a`. Swapping the i18n keys of two `Once` arms, or a wrong `Once::flag`, went unnoticed. Changing `Once::Parent => "--parent"` to `"-p"` stayed green. `moai show --parent a --parent b` would then advise `-p a,b`, which is a priority filter and gets refused in turn.
8. src/query.rs:789 — A single `…Z` value given to `--created` or `--done` means exactly that one second, which the help, README and CHANGELOG never say ('a range from..to … or a single day'). `moai show --done 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z --json` answers `[]` with exit 0 unless something closed in that exact second, while the same value on `--since` means 'at or after'. An agent reads it as 'nothing closed'.
9. src/view.rs:3057 — The shared refusal text suggests CLI syntax (`-s todo,review`, `-s review,done`), and it now also appears under the explorer's `SPC f` prompt, where typing that advice is refused. `SPC f status=todo status=review` → 'to find either one, `-s todo,review`'. Typing that into the prompt → '`-s todo,review` is not `key=value`'. Present before this branch too; the CHANGELOG entry lists the explorer prompt next to that example.
10. src/tui/mod.rs:2539 — The comment (and 670a530a's commit message) says the explorer's `since=<day>` means the same day as the CLI's `--since`. That is false whenever a `[tui] timezone` is picked, because `Ctx::zone` ignores it. `[tui] timezone = "Asia/Seoul"` on a UTC machine: `SPC f created=2026-10-01` keeps a row created 2026-09-30T20:00Z; `moai show --created 2026-10-01` does not.
11. src/cmd/mod.rs:117 — Stale docs after 670a530a. `Ctx::clock` says the `show` list never reads the timezone data or prints the zone-trouble line, and tz.rs:1-6 says the zone only changes text people read. `moai show --since 2026-09-30` now calls `ctx.zone()` (show.rs:312) and can print the trouble line. The zone now decides which rows `show --created <day> --json` returns.
12. src/cli.rs:438 — The explorer help says Options change 'how this screen draws what stands, not which rows stand', but `SPC o t` now changes which rows a bare-day `SPC f` filter keeps. With `SPC f created=2026-10-01` applied, picking another zone moves rows in or out of the list, which the help says Options never do.
13. src/query.rs:1725 — The test's doc heading still states the rule 670a530a reversed: '날은 UTC 의 하루다' (a day is the UTC day). The heading sits over a body that now measures with no zone attached (`span.holds(t(s), t(s))`), while `instant`'s doc says a bare day is the reader's day. A reader takes the old rule as current.
14. CHANGELOG.md:89 — The new [Unreleased] 'Fixed' entry says the time-filter and `show --removed` refusals used to be Korean, but those flags are new in the same [Unreleased] 'Added' section. After `bump-version.sh`, one release's notes would list both 'Added: --since/--created/--done/--removed' and 'Fixed: their refusals were Korean'.
15. src/cmd/show.rs:260 — `.map_err(|e| Fail::coded(view::bad_filter(ctx.lang(), &e), super::code::BAD_FILTER))` is copied at three sites instead of a `Fail::bad_filter` constructor like `Fail::no_actor`, and show.rs:176/201 spell the same code as a literal. A fourth caller has to copy the text-and-code pairing by hand, and a slip sends the same refusal out under a different `--json` `code`.

## What I changed (working tree only)

- Backwards ranges: a mixed day/instant range is now refused when it runs backwards by more than a day. Timezone offsets are all under a day, so no range that some zone could satisfy gets refused. A mix within a day is still accepted, and tests pin both.
- JSON stderr: `cmd::run` skips the zone-trouble line when a `--json` run fails. A new CLI check runs under `TZ=Mars/Olympus` and uses the existing `one_json_value` helper.
- Explorer zone switch: `set_zone` now re-applies the active filter and re-grips the cursor. The new test `a_filtered_day_is_the_screens_day_and_follows_a_new_zone` covers this and also pins the `wh.zone` wiring.
- Test gaps: `a_bare_day_is_the_readers_day` now also checks `show --removed --since <day>` in Seoul and the one-JSON-value failure. The `needs_zone` asserts now cover `created` and `done`. The language test gains a `--removed --since yesterday` case. The explorer refusal is checked in both English and Korean. The view test pins the noun and flag for all six `Once` variants.
- Docs and comments: updated the explorer comment, `Ctx::clock`, the tz.rs header, the test heading, the `SPC o t` help line, the lone-instant sentence in the `show` help (with `docs/cli.md` regenerated from the dev binary), and the CHANGELOG entry.
- Cleanups: new `Fail::bad_filter` used at all three sites, and the literal codes replaced with `code::BAD_FILTER`.
- Below the cut, also fixed: `spans_hold` now converts to wall-clock time once per row, and the explorer attaches the zone only when a bare-day end exists. `Zone::shift` now calls `Zone::local`, so the formula lives in one place. `命令 층` became `명령 레이어(`cmd`)`, per `docs/korean-terms.md`. The `NotAKind` doc now explains why `stale=` differs from `--stale`. Two assertions that only checked constants were replaced with a test that every listed filter key is accepted. The Seoul guard in `a_bare_day_is_the_readers_day` now reads `TZDIR` the way the binary does.

Checks: `cargo test` passes (1527 unit, 592 CLI), and `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. For each fix, I reverted it with a scripted edit and confirmed its test goes red.

- CLI syntax in the explorer prompt (view.rs:3057): older than this branch. It needs a refusal line that knows which surface it is on, which is a wording decision.

The in-flight read race was reproduced with the real binary, and the two weak tests were confirmed by mutation. The merge 8c2d84fa `src/store.rs` test-conflict resolution is clean: both sides' tests survived.

1. src/store.rs:1056 — journal_of_kind uses the parse prefilter ("rm" / \u) to decide which unparseable lines may hold a removal, so it errs both ways.
   Failure: An rm line cut before "rm" closes (e.g. `…"kind":"r`, 20–45% of cut points) is dropped: `show --removed` prints [] with exit 0 and nothing on stderr. A cut note containing \u001b is named as a possible removal and exits 1 on every run.
2. src/cmd/show.rs:508 — Unreadable lines are named whatever --since says, and nothing in the tool can clear them.
   Failure: A line cut on 09-05 makes `show --removed --since 2099-01-01 --json` print [] and exit 1. The README's incremental sync recipe fails on every pass, forever.

   Failure: With the journal file at mode 0200, `moai note` fails with Permission denied, and `moai mv` changes the snapshot but prints 'history could not be kept'.
4. src/store.rs:1101 — A whole line that an older binary glued onto a cut tail is never recovered.
   Failure: A cut note followed by a full old-binary rm line: `--removed` leaves the rm out and exits 1, and `show -g`, history and `work` drop a glued note silently with exit 0.
5. src/store.rs:1077 — An unlocked reader can see another session's multi-page append half-written, and it is reported as a broken line.
   Failure: The real binary under stress gave exit 1 in 2 of 38,193 `show --removed` runs on a healthy journal, because ext4 exposes a buffered write one page at a time.
6. src/view.rs:126 — stamp and short_stamp return a stamp they cannot read unchanged; only history and --removed cleaned it.
   Failure: A hand-edited `created_at` of `\u001b[2J\u001b[H…` makes the Created line of `moai show <id>` send clear-screen and cursor-home to a terminal (confirmed under a pty). Updated, Started and Finished lines have the same gap.
7. src/view.rs:2267 — history's entry() keeps newlines in by, from/to and unknown kind, not just in notes.
   Failure: A journal line with `"to":"in_progress\n09-30 09:00   done → todo"` draws a history line that was never written.
8. src/cmd/show.rs:529 — name_garbled prints with eprintln!, which panics when stderr's reader has gone.
   Failure: With stderr on a closed pipe, `show --removed --json > out` exits 101 and writes 0 bytes of stdout.
9. README.md:255 — The new stderr report and non-zero exit are not documented anywhere (README, --removed help, CHANGELOG, docs/recovery.md), and stderr gives no fix.
   Failure: A script following the documented recipe gets exit 1 with a valid array and no stated meaning; the only fix, editing the journal by hand, is not written down.
10. src/store.rs:1848 — The heal doc (and commit 7d645e2f) says readers skip the cut line.
    Failure: Since e73ea3c2 that is false for `--removed`, which names such a line and exits 1.
11. src/store.rs:2715 — The new unit test does not check that text with broken bytes is never parsed.
    Failure: Parsing the lossy text instead left every test green (confirmed by mutation), yet a complete rm line with one bad byte would then be listed with a '�' title.
12. src/cmd/init.rs:1702 — The dotfile test checks only a prefix and the final newline.
    Failure: Writing the block twice, dropping block lines, or adding a trailing blank line all stay green (confirmed by mutation).
13. src/cmd/show.rs:530 — name_garbled copies name_load_errors's 'first 5 then N more' logic, and it both prints and sets the failure flag.
    Failure: The literal 5 now lives in six places across two files. In cmd/mod.rs a `name_*` function only prints, so a future caller trusting the name gets an unexpected non-zero exit.
14. src/store.rs:1095 — journal_by_id silently throws away the Vec<Garbled>, and it lossily decodes invalid-UTF-8 lines it never parses.
    Failure: On a legacy journal re-saved as CP949, `journal_of` and `-g` get about 4x slower; the dropped result also compiles silently for any future caller.

What changed (working tree only):
- src/store.rs: Unreadable pieces are judged by the kind the piece names itself (`may_be`), and cut lines the prefilter skips are checked too (`cut`). Glued lines are split at `{"ts":"` and the whole piece is read back, for every journal reader. `Garbled` now carries the piece's `ts`. An unterminated last line that fails to parse causes the file to be re-read, up to 3 times; re-running the stress test gave 0 false alarms in 29,416 reads. `append_inside` falls back to a plain append (no heal) when the file cannot be read.

**Fixed** (all uncommitted in the worktree: `src/tz.rs`, `src/view.rs`, `i18n/en.json`, `i18n/ko.json`, `i18n/README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `Cargo.toml`):
- **Ojinaga week:** after the last stored transition, `offset_at` now keeps that offset until the rule's first change after it, which is how tzcode reads these files. Added a test built like the Ojinaga file.
- **Year window:** the rule now looks at years y-2..y+1, with a test for the long-transition case.
- **Korean text on the English screen:** there is a new `Trouble::NotTzif { name }` with a `tz.not_tzif` message in en and ko, plus a test. `TZ=leapseconds` now prints English on an English screen.
- **Unquoted CLI fix:** `Surface::Flags` now runs the value through `text::quoted`. Plain values like `-s todo,review` come out exactly as before; a value with spaces or brackets is single-quoted. Test added.
- **Weak test:** added the 2006-11-01 assert to the slim test.
- **`done=`:** added a test that feeds the explorer's `done=` back through `desugar`.
- **Docs:** fixed `CHANGELOG.md` (the stale sentence, plus new entries for the slim-tzdata fix and the `TZ=leapseconds` message), the doc comments in `tz.rs`, the `Cargo.toml` list (now all ten measured files), and `i18n/README.md`.
- **Cleanups:** `Posix::num` now takes a range and `hms` uses `eat`. `is_utc` now makes the same choice `offset_at` makes, so it didn't make the list, but it is applied. The verifier for these cleanups was stopped before it gave a verdict, but its parity runs found no difference between the old and new parser on 25M+ inputs.

**Not fixed:**
- **Explorer never shows the fix:** making it visible means choosing a layout. Either give the prompt two rows when the error has two lines, as the name/email prompt already does, or put the fix first on one line; the test should then check the drawn row. `draw.rs` isn't in this diff, and CLAUDE.md says to stop and ask on design calls. The explorer showing the suggested fix was what moai-tckz promised, so by the repo's rules this should be a new member of moai-efoc, not an idea.
- **DST lasting a year or longer:** only hand-built footers do this, and matching tzcode would need its special "permanent DST" rule.
- **`Twice` dropping repeats:** this existed before the diff, and fixing it changes the refusal wording.

**Worth recording in the tracker:**
- `TZ=JST-9`-style values are still treated as unknown zone names, although `Rule::parse` could read them now (idea).
- The explorer never resolves `assignee=me`.
- `Head::size` could overflow on 32-bit targets; nothing shipped is 32-bit.
- Commit `2dfc72ee` blames Ojinaga's slim/fat difference on differing tzdata versions; the real cause was the inconsistent footer, now handled.

Review of 98ae6925 (moai-p9mq) is done. The fold of linked journal files is in the right place, but the commit fails the CI format check, its tests missed two of the rules it documents, and choosing the first spelling as the kept name has some consequences worth a decision. I applied the safe fixes to `src/store.rs`. They are uncommitted, so they can go in a separate `fix:` commit.

On your questions:
- **Order of same-`ts` lines:** still deterministic, because `retain` keeps list order. But an alias whose name sorts early now moves its target's lines ahead of other files (finding 4).
- **Keeping unresolvable paths:** this is the right behaviour and it matters (finding 2). No test covered it until now.
- **`journal_marks`:** misses a change in only one contrived setup (finding 9).
- **Cost:** negligible. It is one `realpath` per file per journal read, about 30µs, and it never runs on the explorer tick.
- **Five checks:** no doc block was taken over. No other code builds the journal file list except a CLI test helper (finding 11). `canonicalize` never opens the file, checked on glibc and musl; macOS was not tested.

**Fixed in the working tree (`src/store.rs` only):**
- **Formatting:** the test is now rustfmt-clean.
- **Test coverage:** the link test now runs in two phases, links inside `journal/` first and then the legacy link. It also checks that an absent legacy file stays in the marks with no stamp. A new test, `an_old_journal_that_cannot_be_resolved_is_still_told`, checks that a self-looping legacy link still shows up as an unread journal.
- **Mutations now caught:** all four mutations above (dropping unresolvable paths, no fold, a different kept name, first-entry-only) now fail. Before, only "no fold" failed.
- **Fold:** it now calls `crate::path::real` instead of its own `canonicalize` branch.
- **Docs:** '위의' is now '아래의'. The unresolvable-path sentence now names `path::real` and says why those paths are kept. The hard-link paragraph now states what happens in this checkout and in clones. '판' is now '경우'.
- **Checks:** fmt clean, clippy with `-D warnings` clean, `cargo test` passes (1540 unit, 594 CLI).

**Skipped, for you or the issue owner to decide:**
- **Kept-name choice (finding 4):** changing which name survives or what the messages print reverses a rule the commit documents and tests. Two options: print the resolved file in `Garbled.at`, or keep the non-link name when its target is also listed.
- **Read race (finding 5):** fixing it means reading the resolved path while stamping the kept name, which changes the reader's internals.
- **`(dev, ino)` key (finding 7):** it would fold local hard links, but a false inode match would silently drop a journal, while the current key errs toward reading twice. I fixed the doc only.
- **Stale marks (finding 9):** fixing it means stamping every name before the fold. The setup is contrived and the explorer re-reads within 60 s anyway.
- **pagemap OOM and Emacs lock files (findings 3 and 8):** both predate this diff and should be filed. I did not write to `.moai/`.
- **CLI test helper (finding 11):** harmless today and outside this diff.
- **Commit message (finding 14):** fixing it means rewording the commit, and CLAUDE.md asks for review fixes in separate commits.
- **CHANGELOG:** `[Unreleased]` has no Fixed line for this change yet. It may just be pending.

I found no correctness bug in epic moai-lpzj. I made 7 cleanups and test fixes in the working tree; they are not committed. `cargo test` (dev) passes, 1551 + 594, and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` are clean.

**Your three questions:**
- **Re-applying the filter:** `Hung` sets back the same value on every path. Reapply goes through `Hung::mode`. Esc restores the whole `Hung` from `grep_was` and reapplies it. Moving between the layer and a project clears it in `leave_project`. The timezone change reapplies it when something is hung.
- **`searching` vs `grep_query`:** all three `grep_query` callers in draw.rs (list-row paint, `about`, `fill_note_hits`) paint and nothing else. Everything that decides which rows show still uses `searching()`, so `grep=` gets the paint but leaves the view alone.
- **Badge re-readers:** none are left. `GrepIn::name` is gone and nothing strips `/` or the scope name back out of the badge. zh/ja/es show the English scope names, which is the intended fallback.

**Your five checks:**
- **Doc blocks:** nothing inserted takes over the doc block of the item below it.
- **No new file opens, FIFOs or locks:** `f grep=` already read notes before this epic. The new painting only reads what is already in memory.
- **Tests that stayed green on regression:** two of them could, and I fixed both (findings 3 and 4). I checked each fix by breaking the code on purpose: both go red, and I reverted the breakage.

Findings:

1. src/tui/mod.rs:143 — `Hung::query` always gives GrepIn::All for a `grep=` filter instead of the scope the built Filter decided (`filter.grep_in`), so the scope is decided in a second place with a default. Failure: if `f` ever gets a scope key, matching uses the Filter's grep_in while painting and the notes decision use All: rows caught by one field get paint in fields that didn't catch them, and note lines are drawn for a scope that doesn't read notes.
2. src/tui/mod.rs:2309 — `sees_notes()` re-parses the text and builds a whole Filter on every reload, while painting reads the same fact from `Hung::query`: two readers of whether notes are needed. Failure: if the two drift apart, the reload thread skips the journal while the detail tries to draw note hits (or the other way round). It also wastes a filter parse on every write and on the 1-minute tick.
3. src/tui/draw.rs:7895 — The test for 'grep= leaves the view alone' only checks `!a.searching()`, and `every()` uses a view that hides nothing, so the claim is never measured on the list. Failure: changing `visible()` to use `grep_query().is_some()` makes `f grep=` bring back rows the view hides, and every test stays green.
4. src/tui/mod.rs:4546 — The rewritten Esc path (restoring `grep_was`) had no test for a narrowed-scope search; the Tab test covered reapply only. Failure: dropping the scope when restoring on Esc turns `/태그:pars` into `/pars`. The rows are the same, so every existing test stays green.
5. src/tui/draw.rs:2396 — The comment "`f` 의 `grep=` 도 검색이다" contradicts `App::searching`, which says only `/` is a search. Failure: the next reader trusts the comment and routes view logic through `grep_query`, which is exactly the regression in finding 3.
6. src/tui/draw.rs:1040 — In `crumbs()`, `let badge = … badge(h, lang)` shadows the new `fn badge` inside its own initializer and for the rest of the function. Failure: it reads like recursion, and any later `badge(..)` call in `crumbs` hits the Option<String> local and fails to compile, or tempts someone into a workaround.
7. src/tui/layer.rs:1901 — The layer tests rebuild the rendered badge string inline (twice) instead of comparing the `Hung` the refactor added, repeating the `badge` helper from mod.rs. Failure: the layer tests assert on screen text, so a change in wording or language would break them even when the filter data is correct.

What I changed:
1. Findings 1 and 2: `Hung::Filter.grep` is now `Option<(GrepIn, String)>`, filled in `apply` from `filter.grep` and `filter.grep_in`. `query()` returns that pair. `sees_notes()` is now `self.grep_query().is_some_and(|(g, _)| g.sees_notes())`, which gives the same answer as `Filter::sees_notes`. Painting and the reload now read one value, and the docs say the stored text is the lowercased form.
2. Finding 3: the `grep=` test now hides done and checks `hit_count()`: `f grep=멤버` gives 1 and `/멤버` gives 2.
3. Finding 4: `tab_turns_what_slash_searches_and_a_reread_keeps_it` now reopens `/`, types, presses Esc, and checks that `(GrepIn::Tag, "pars")` comes back.
4. Finding 5: I reworded the comment in `about()` so it says `grep=` gets the note lines like `/`, but only `/` lifts the view.
5. Finding 6: I renamed the local in `crumbs()` to `hung`.
6. Finding 7: the layer tests now compare `a.hung` with `Hung::Filter { text: "status=in_progress", grep: None }`.

I skipped nothing.

/code-review medium --fix develop...worktree-moai-o4jt — reviewer's report (agent a174ecbefb8131e54)

I found no real bugs in `develop...worktree-moai-o4jt`, so there was nothing for `--fix` to apply and the working tree is unchanged.

What I checked:
- The new filter in src/store.rs, in `journal_names`: names starting with `.` are skipped after the `.jsonl` check and before `metadata`. This drops the broken Emacs lock link (`.#<name>.jsonl`) and the macOS AppleDouble files (`._<name>.jsonl`) without counting them as unread journals.
- No real journal is lost. `journal_file` turns every character outside `[a-z0-9_-]` (including `.` and `@`) into `_`, so the tool can never write a journal name that starts with `.`. The old single file (`journal_path`) is added separately and is not filtered.
- Other readers are covered. `journal_files` and `journal_marks` both go through `journal_names`, so they get the filter too. Nothing else in `src/` filters on the `.jsonl` extension, and the writer (`append_journal`) only writes names that `journal_file` builds.
- Tests: `store::tests::a_hidden_name_beside_the_journal_is_not_a_journal` and `an_editor_lock_beside_the_journal_does_not_fail_the_run` in tests/cli.rs both pass (dev profile).

One small comment nit, not counted as a finding: the source comment says the email's local part can't start with `.`. That doesn't matter here, because `journal_file` turns `.` into `_` anyway.

Findings: none.

/code-review high --fix develop...worktree-moai-xd7b — reviewer's report (agent ad93600fe1d96030f)

I found 7 problems and fixed the main one (working tree only, not committed).

Fixed (findings 1 and 2): the header already resolves who you are and caches the result, but it kept only the display string. Now it also keeps the reason when it can't tell. `me_for_filter` reads that cached answer and only calls `identify` itself when the cache has no answer for this user and project. This stops the per-frame git calls and means the filter and the header always name the same person. Both edits in src/tui/mod.rs. Extended `me_in_the_filter_without_a_person_is_refused_like_the_cli`: the header caches "unknown", then `identify` is swapped for one that panics, and typing `assignee=me` must show the refusal without calling it. cargo test passes (1554 + 598); clippy and fmt clean.

Skipped: 3 (shared drawing code in draw.rs; changing the separator would change existing refusals — better fixed in `view::no_actor` or the prompt's join later), 4 (refusal text matching the CLI was deliberate), 5 (CHANGELOG — add after pulling develop), 6 and 7 (cleanups; moving `resolve_me` into `query` would break the purity rule).

1. src/tui/mod.rs:2636 — When site.me is None, me_for_filter calls identify (two `git config` processes) on every input_error, and the filter prompt redraws every frame.
   Failure: no git identity; typing `assignee=me` shows the refusal, and every keypress and 120ms spinner frame starts two `git config` processes (~33ms) between term.draw and event::poll. The header_user cache was built to stop exactly this (moai-ropk).
2. src/tui/mod.rs:2636 — The fallback can find a person while the header and [NEW] still say unknown, so one screen names two different people.
   Failure: start without git identity (header `—`), set git config in another shell, type `assignee=me` → filter finds the new person while header still shows `—`. Contradicts the 2026-09-21 decision that git config changed while the screen is open stays invisible until the next read.
3. src/tui/draw.rs:229 — The multi-line no_actor refusal is squeezed into the filter prompt's single upper line, so the two `git config` commands and the `--user` hint run together.
   Failure: one line with single-space joins, cut at terminal width; the commands can't be copied as written.
4. src/tui/mod.rs:2614 — The refusal reused from the CLI tells the explorer user to pass `--user`, which can't be done while the explorer is running.
5. CHANGELOG.md:13 — This user-visible fix has no entry under [Unreleased] → Fixed.
6. src/cmd/mod.rs:936 — resolve_me is a filter-term helper that sits in `cmd`, so `tui` calls into `crate::cmd` (maintenance coupling only; tui already calls `crate::cmd::unknown_column`).
7. src/cmd/show.rs:245 — `model::label(&a.name, Some(&a.email), Naming::Full)` for 'this person as `Name (email)`' is repeated in five places.

text: 리뷰 moai-karj.8zm 1번이 같은 것을 짚었다. `Config::load`(src/config.rs:332)도 `.moai/config.toml` 을 같은 꼴로 읽는다. 스냅샷과 설정을 "체크아웃 안에서만, 크기는 연 손잡이까지" 로 읽는 자 하나로 모으자는 제안이다

/code-review high --fix develop...worktree-moai-karj — reviewer's report (agent a190f569136abf51f)

I found five problems in the diff and fixed two of them (uncommitted in src/store.rs). After the fixes, cargo test passes in full (1553 + 598), clippy reports nothing and fmt is clean.

The core fix is correct: `journal_files` now skips journal links that resolve outside the checkout, before it de-duplicates, and still leaves names it couldn't resolve to the reader. A checkout opened through a symlinked root is handled correctly. The original 53 store tests passed before I changed anything.

1. src/store.rs:1574 — The same OOM still happens through .moai/issues.jsonl and .moai/config.toml: read_snapshot (fs::read_to_string) and Config::load (src/config.rs:332) follow any link with no checkout or regular-file check.
   Failure: a cloned repo commits `.moai/issues.jsonl -> /proc/self/pagemap` or `-> /dev/zero`; plain `moai status` tries to read ~256GiB or zeros forever and is OOM-killed. Worse than the journal case, because every command reads the snapshot. A FIFO there hangs every command.
2. src/store.rs:1211 — The guard checks the path by name in journal_files, but journal_bytes reopens the file by name with fs::read, up to 4 times with REREADS. If the name is replaced with a procfs link in between, the unbounded read happens again.
   Failure: the TUI runs `read_notes` in a loop while `git pull`/checkout replaces `.moai/journal/x.jsonl` with a committed link to `/proc/self/pagemap`; fs::read follows the new link and runs out of memory. Root cause: fs::read keeps reading past what fstat reported (size 0).
3. src/store.rs:676 — The read-side check does not refuse links into .git/, although the doc says reads use 'the same ruler' as target_of, and target_of does refuse them.
   Failure: `.moai/journal/x.jsonl -> ../../.git/objects/pack/pack-*.pack` passes; every history read, -g, --removed and TUI note pass loads a multi-GiB pack, and `.git/config` content turns into garbled journal pieces.
4. src/store.rs:683 — The outside-link case is reported as kind 'failed', so the machine-readable kind can't tell 'remove this link' from an I/O failure, and the new test matches on `said`, which the Unread doc says not to do.
5. src/store.rs:677 — The Unread doc defines `said` as untranslated OS text, but this path puts an English sentence moai wrote itself into it, outside the i18n catalogue. Under MOAI_LANG=ko a Korean prefix is followed by a full English explanation.

Fixed 2: `journal_bytes` opens the file once, checks its size with fstat on that handle, refuses anything that isn't a regular file, and reads no more than that size. New test `a_journal_is_read_no_further_than_the_size_its_handle_gives` (Linux only, `/proc/self/status`).
Fixed 3: `journal_files` also refuses a link that resolves into `.git/` inside the checkout and reports it; case added to `a_journal_link_out_of_the_checkout_is_not_read_but_told`.
Skipped 1 (outside this diff; should become its own tracker issue), 4 and 5 (new `Unread.kind` value changes the `--json` contract — a deliberate decision, not a review fix).

판단: 2·3번은 리뷰가 고친 그대로 받았다. 크기를 연 손잡이까지로 자르면 잰 뒤 덧붙은 줄은 이번 읽기에서 빠지지만, 다음 명령이 읽고 쓰기 쪽 손실도 아니라서 받는다. 1번은 idea moai-sxwq 에 Config::load 까지 더해 두었다. 4·5번은 idea moai-wd0o 로 넘겼다. 새 kind 값은 --json 계약이 바뀌는 일이라 patch 판(v0.1.6)에 싣지 않는다

text:
/code-review high --fix (agent a2905ec0c6ea8a844, 139,696 tokens) — reviewer's own words

I applied 4 fixes to the working tree and skipped 3 findings. Nothing is committed. The full `cargo test --test cli` run passes (602 tests), and `shellcheck` reports nothing on either script. I also ran the updated `bump-version.sh 9.9.0` on a scratch copy of the real repo: `Cargo.lock` changed by exactly one line (`moai` 0.1.6 → 9.9.0) and the tag hint printed. The main fix in this branch, calling `cargo update --workspace` and then re-reading the lock file, works on the real lock.

```json
[
  {"file": "scripts/bump-version.sh", "line": 173, "summary": "lock_version re-implements the [package]-table name reader inside bump-version.sh, which the file's own comment (lines 112-114) forbids: only check-version.sh may read that table.", "failure_scenario": "If someone fixes table detection in check-version.sh (e.g. for `[package]` with a trailing comment), lock_version keeps the old regex. It then misses its own lock line and wrongly says '자기 줄이 없다', holding back the tag hint."},
  {"file": "scripts/bump-version.sh", "line": 218, "summary": "With no Cargo.lock, `cargo update --workspace` creates one and resolves the whole dependency graph, possibly fetching the index online. The script then reports success and prints `git commit -- … Cargo.lock` for a file git does not track.", "failure_scenario": "Library repo without a committed lock: an untracked Cargo.lock appears, and the printed commit command fails with \"pathspec 'Cargo.lock' did not match\"."},
  {"file": "scripts/bump-version.sh", "line": 177, "summary": "The value reader strips only double quotes, so a TOML literal string `name = 'moai'` is read as `'moai'`.", "failure_scenario": "A manifest using single quotes never matches the lock's `\"moai\"`, so a lock that did move is reported as '자기 줄이 없다' and the tag hint is held back."},
  {"file": "tests/cli.rs", "line": 20204, "summary": "bump_crate overwrites isolated()'s filtered PATH with the test process's raw PATH.", "failure_scenario": "The installed `moai` directory that isolated() deliberately removes (moai-bq6w) comes back into the script's PATH for the fake-cargo test."},
  {"file": "tests/cli.rs", "line": 18762, "summary": "A stale comment still says the script calls `cargo metadata`.", "failure_scenario": "A reader looks for the wrong cargo call when the offline setting misbehaves."},
  {"file": "tests/cli.rs", "line": 20180, "summary": "bump_crate copies the scratch setup that bump_with and bumping_moves_the_manifest_… already repeat (create scripts/ dir, copy two scripts), and its loop variable `name` shadows the function's `name` parameter.", "failure_scenario": "Three copies of the same setup; adding a third script means editing three places."}
]
```

**Fixed:**
- **Reader duplication (finding 1):** `scripts/check-version.sh` now reads any `[package]` key through one function (`manifest_key`). A new `--print-name` flag prints the crate name, and `--print` and the existing error message are unchanged. `lock_version` in `scripts/bump-version.sh` gets the name from `"$check" --print-name` and only parses `Cargo.lock`. Its value reader no longer strips a `#…` tail, which used to cut `git+…#sha` source URLs. A new test, `the_version_check_prints_the_crate_name_for_the_lock_reader`, covers the flag.
- **PATH (finding 4):** `bump_crate` now puts the shim in front of `path_without_moai()` instead of the raw PATH.
- **Stale comment (finding 5):** it now says `cargo update`.
- **Duplicated setup (finding 6):** a new `release_scratch(name)` helper does the setup, and all three call sites use it. The shadowed variable went away with it.

**Skipped:**
- **Finding 2 (no Cargo.lock):** this repo always commits `Cargo.lock`. The commit line naming an untracked lock file was already wrong before this change, and whether to skip cargo or create the lock is a design call.
- **Finding 3 (single quotes):** the version reader in `check-version.sh` has the same limitation. Changing quote handling there would change how the pre-push check reads versions, so it belongs in its own issue.

Changed files:
- scripts/bump-version.sh
- scripts/check-version.sh
- tests/cli.rs

받은 것: 1·4·5·6번은 리뷰의 고침을 그대로 받았다. `manifest_key` 위 주석의 첫 줄이 아직 "첫 `version` 만" 이라 코드에 맞춰 고쳤고, 같은 fix 커밋에 담았다.
안 받은 것: 2번. 이 저장소는 Cargo.lock 을 커밋하고 릴리스를 `--locked` 로 지어서 잠금 파일 없는 판이 서지 않는다. 고치기 전에도 커밋 줄은 Cargo.lock 을 댔다.
넘긴 것: 3번은 idea moai-i9x7 로 담았다. check-version.sh 의 판 읽기도 같은 한계라, 고치면 pre-push 동작이 같이 바뀐다. 이 에픽이 내건 것(맞추지 못한 Cargo.lock 을 맞췄다고 말하지 않기)은 그것 없이도 선다.

text:
/code-review xhigh --fix — reviewer's report (agent a099dbd85254489ef)

I found 8 issues and fixed 7 in the working tree (`src/tz.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`). None is a serious bug, and nothing is committed. Most are comment and test gaps; the one real code fix is in `Zone::load`. Unit tests (16) and the timezone CLI tests (5, including the new one) pass, and `cargo fmt --check` and clippy are clean. I confirmed the new CLI test fails against the old `Zone::load`.

1. src/tz.rs:121 — Zone::load tried the POSIX rule only when the tzdb answered NoTzdb or Unknown; other failures (Unreadable, NotTzif) never reached the rule, while glibc reads the rule whenever the file cannot be loaded.
   Failure: TZDIR exists but cannot be read (a sandbox with no permission on /usr/share/zoneinfo), or a non-TZif file named `JST-9` sits in TZDIR → TZ=JST-9 gives Unreadable/NotTzif → screen falls back to UTC with a warning on every command, instead of UTC+9.
2. src/tui/zones.rs:52 — When the current zone came from a rule (TZ=JST-9), the SPC o t list does not contain it, so the cursor lands on row 0 and no row is marked as current.
   Failure: TZ=JST-9 → SPC o t → Enter without typing → the zone silently becomes the first tzdb name (e.g. Africa/Abidjan) and is saved to config.
3. src/tz.rs:557 — The last_change doc and the `spanning` test comment say glibc reads `J1/0,J365/26` as permanent daylight time. glibc actually draws standard time from 00:00 UTC on Jan 1 until that year's start; the code follows tzcode.
   Failure: Under glibc, TZ=AAA3BBB,J1/0,J365/26 gives -3 at 2026-01-01T02:59:59Z (checked with Python time.localtime), but the test asserts -2 and says glibc agrees. A reader trying to match glibc would 'fix' correct code.
4. tests/cli.rs:7848 — No end-to-end test that a rule in TZ works without a tzdb, which is the main claim of 1gk for the static musl build.
   Failure: A filter on TZ reintroduced somewhere on the path from environment to Zone::load would silently send TZ=<+09>-9 back to UTC on machines without zoneinfo, and every test would still pass.
5. src/tz.rs:808 — The Zone::load test only used rules with no `/`; rules with `/` (`M4.1.0/3`) take the multi-part path lookup in safe_join and from_tzdb, and nothing covered that.
   Failure: A change to safe_join, or to how that lookup's errors are mapped, could make `AEST-10AEDT,M10.1.0,M4.1.0/3` fail while every test stays green.
6. src/tz.rs:445 — block(raw, at, h, time) took `at` (always h.after) and `time` (passed to head separately) even though both belong to the header, so the two could drift apart.
   Failure: A caller passing head(…, 4) with block(…, 8) would read past the range head checked against the file length, undoing the protection the xia fix adds.
7. src/tz.rs:431 — The head doc said only version 1 files are rejected when their trailing sections are cut, but the new size check also rejects version 2 data cut after the ttinfo records, which used to be read with the footer missing.
   Failure: A truncated version 2 file that used to load now reports NotTzif. This matches tzcode and glibc, but the comment did not say so.
8. src/tz.rs:35 — The doc on Trouble::Unknown did not mention that the name also failed to read as a POSIX rule.
   Failure: A reader of the enum cannot tell that Unknown now also means 'not a valid rule either'.

Fixed:
- Zone::load: it now reads the rule after any tzdb failure: `Zone::from_tzdb(name).or_else(|why| Zone::from_rule(name).ok_or(why))`. If the rule doesn't parse either, the tzdb's own error still comes back.
- glibc comments: the doc comment and the test comment now say what glibc really does and why the code follows tzcode.
- New CLI test: `a_posix_rule_in_tz_needs_no_tzdb` with `TZDIR` pointing nowhere checks that `<+09>-9`, `JST-9` and `:JST-9` show 13:12 with nothing on stderr, and that `Asia/Seoul` still falls back to UTC with one warning line. It also checks that a non-TZif file named `JST-9` still opens as a rule.
- Unit test row: `Zone::load("AEST-10AEDT,M10.1.0,M4.1.0/3")` added to the existing test.
- Head/block: `Head` now carries `time`, and `block(raw, &Head)` takes everything from the header.
- Docs: the `head` and `Trouble::Unknown` comments are corrected.

Skipped:
- SPC o t cursor (#2): the user decided on 2026-10-01 that the list holds tzdb names only. Fixing it would change that design.

Checked, no problem found:
- 49f: the new rule keeps the existing answers for the Sydney (southern), 167-hour, `J365/25` and leap-year `n` cases. For realistic rules it matches tzcode. It also fits with `Zone::offset_at`'s rule of following the footer only from its first change after the last listed transition.
- xia: the size arithmetic in `head`, `block`, `parse` and `footer` stays inside the file length on 32-bit machines.
- Removing the `TZ` filter: `safe_join` still blocks `..` and absolute paths. A `TZ` value that is neither a name nor a valid rule used to fall back to `/etc/localtime` silently; it now shows UTC with one warning line. That is the same answer glibc gives.

The `CHANGELOG.md` entry is not written yet. The review issue already plans it for step 7-3.
