text:
/code-review max --fix develop...worktree-moai-1hka — reviewer's report (agent a7b985d2cf1210ed7)

Fifteen findings, most severe first. Thirteen fixed in the worktree (one only partly), two left alone; all fixes uncommitted. Each angle and every candidate got its own verifier: everything listed came back confirmed except #12, which is plausible only. Line numbers refer to HEAD.

1. src/cmd/stats.rs:17 — Ask.kind is read from the raw --type flag before Filter::build desugars `--filter type=…`, so the rows are picked as one kind and counted as another.
   Failure: `moai stats --filter type=idea --json` returns {"kind":"issue","rows":0,…} while `--type idea` gives rows 1; the TUI uses the built filter.kind, so CLI and explorer disagree. Five finders hit this independently.
2. src/tui/draw.rs:556 — stat_bars sets aside the label plus 8 bar cells before the number column gets room, then cuts the number mid-digit with no ellipsis.
   Failure: at 80 columns AI-work rows read `… (47` (real 471); at 50 columns `61,983,609` shows as `61,983`; a 22+ char column name makes its count disappear. Confirmed in a pty.
3. src/tui/stats.rs:88 — count() calls read_notes, which parks the full note text plus a folded copy in the Ground; the layer-place branch also anchors the flow at a stale site.now (line 164).
   Failure: on a layer project notes are never re-read, so a later journal-only `model:` note is missing from every following SPC p s while the CLI counts it; ~9MB stays resident (leave_project avoids this); each open decodes and folds 4,946 journal lines on the UI thread; an idle expanded project's flow ends on the day it was last read.
4. src/report/stats.rs:438 — spans and flow have no far_ahead (future_timestamp) guard; the board's flow excludes such rows.
   Failure: one done row stamped 2099 pushes lead-time p90 to 38,044,800 minutes (~72 years) and shifts the median, while `moai status` flags the row and leaves it out; a stamp 1–6 days ahead lands in the current week bucket.
5. src/cmd/stats.rs:39 — Human `--by` output still reads and decodes the journal for work it never prints; the comment claims a decode saving that does not happen.
   Failure: with one unreadable journal (chmod 000), `moai stats --by status` prints a complete screen but adds 'this history could not be read…' and exits 1; plain `moai show` exits 0.
6. src/tui/draw.rs:842 — The narrow text fallback and chart-mode text lines use Paragraph with no wrap and the window cannot scroll sideways.
   Failure: below 50 columns `✓ done 2` and `· 1 unknown` are never visible; at 50–56 the legend loses `✓ done`. Confirmed in a pty.
7. src/report/stats.rs:357 — The epic and milestone axes count eclipsed, lost and folded rows under (none), but `-e none`, `--milestone none` and no_epic exclude them.
   Failure: with a duplicate-id issue/epic pair, `stats --by epic` gives (none) 2 while `stats -e none` gives 1 (same class as moai-mibi.ndh).
8. src/report/stats.rs:355 — The assignee axis groups by the exact (name, email) pair, so one person splits when the email differs only in case.
   Failure: `Kim (Kim@Example.com)` and `Kim (kim@example.com)` become two entries while `-a kim@example.com` matches both; with naming=name the screen prints identical `Kim 1` lines.
9. src/view.rs:2123 — In human output `--by` returns before the flow, so `--bucket` and `--last` are accepted and silently ignored.
10. src/view.rs:2317 — A group's cycle time is always unknown by design, but the screen explains it as missing data ('not measured - none of the 1 done carry a start').
11. src/tui/stats.rs:172 — SPC p s on a never-read layer project goes through open_place, which marks the row, never stamps asked_install and throws the synchronous read away.
   Failure: a read already running is dropped and queued again; one read-only keypress cost 3 full reads plus 3 summary reads (measured with a pty and an open() shim).
12. src/tui/stats.rs:87 — (Plausible) The TUI shows AI-work and review totals with no sign that a journal could not be read; the CLI reports journal_error and exits 1.
13. src/tui/stats.rs:128 — The 'with sibling worktrees' title flag uses origin.labels(), which lists every overlaid sibling including ones that contributed no rows.
14. src/guide.rs:862 — The agent docs compare stats with `moai show <epic>`'s 'Spent', which only milestones have, and leave out that the two spans end at different stamps (Spent at done_at, stats at the time the row entered done).
15. src/view.rs:2277 — `stats --by epic` draws a dangling epic id with a blank title instead of the shared view::gone_epic label.

Fixed: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 13, 14, 15. Partly fixed: 11 (opens with projects::open_shallow, falls back to open_place; stamps asked_install; keeping the read as the project's site would need follow_site's Site-building pulled out). Not fixed: 7 (how lost rows appear in by.epic/by.milestone is a --json contract change), 12 (the `/` note search has the same gap — one decision for the whole TUI).
Also fixed below the cap: the flow chart showed one bucket fewer than fits at some widths and sized bars from off-screen buckets; stats wording duplicated between view.rs and draw.rs had drifted — both now use shared helpers in view.rs.
Below the cap, not touched: `b` shifts the scroll position (day view's flow is taller); cleanups — the window counting everything twice, the -g/work_by_id copy, closed_at repeating the --done rule, board and tag-notation copies, value_at repeating object_at's scanner, the JSON contract written twice, the Korean-terms rule in new doc comments, the open_form duplicate.
Tests: added for each fix except 11, 13, 15. cargo test passes (1,579 unit, 610 CLI); clippy and fmt clean.

text:
사용자 결정(2026-10-01, 일꾼 창에서 물었다)
- 마우스 잡기는 기본으로 켠다. `SPC o m` 으로 끄고 켜며, 고른 값은 `[tui] mouse` 에 남아 다음 실행으로 이어진다
- 끌어서 바꾼 목록·상세 몫은 `[tui]` 에 남긴다. 끌기를 놓을 때 한 번만 적고, 가로(좌우)와 세로(위아래) 몫을 따로 둔다
- 덮는 창: 통계 창(`SPC p s`)만 휠로 굴린다. 폼·묻는 칸·고르는 창(프로젝트·시간대)·지우기 확인·SPC 메뉴가 떠 있으면 마우스는 아무것도 안 한다. 한눈 보기(`0`)는 같은 목록·상세 칸이라 그대로 받는다
- 목록 줄을 누르면 커서가 그 줄로 가고 포커스는 목록으로 간다. 두 번 누르기는 안 받는다 — 들어가기는 지금처럼 Enter·l 이다

The max-effort review of `f35597d7..HEAD` (the `moai-irrj` mouse support) found 15 issues worth reporting. I fixed 12 of them in the working tree and left 3 unfixed (#6, #8, and the behaviour side of #5). Nothing is committed.

## What I fixed
- **#1 lost release:** any mouse event other than a left drag, and any key, now ends the drag and saves it (`App::key` calls `drop_line`).
- **#2 formatting:** ran `cargo fmt`.
- **#3 absolute drag:** drags are now relative to where the line was grabbed, and moving only along the other axis leaves the share untouched.
- **#4 unseen share:** new `draw::share_for` limits the stored share to what the layout can actually draw.
- **#5 and #11/#12 docs:** help, `docs/cli.md`, README and CHANGELOG now mention mouse paste, Option in iTerm2, and "while the menu is up". I also added a `### Changed` entry for capture being on by default.
- **#7 bursts:** consecutive wheel and drag events are now handled together before drawing, capped at 50ms (`rolls`, `BURST`); clicks and keys still get one frame each.
- **#9:** events at 65535 are ignored. **#10:** doc corrected; the one-cell gap itself can't be removed with whole percents.
- **#13:** the field is renamed `mouse_on`. **#14, #15:** test and comment fixed.
- **Cleanups the verifiers confirmed:** the off sequence now uses `DisableMouseCapture`, and turning on clears 1003/1015 first; the on/off pairs are folded into `modes_on`/`modes_off`; the wheel uses a new `scroll::cursor_by`, so it no longer builds `rows()` when moving up; `Drawn` now has a single writer; `LIST_MIN_H = DETAIL_MIN_H`, with a doc note on its 20-column limit; the stats window gets its own `Window::roll`; `pane_at`/`grab_at` replace the duplicated hit tests; two test fixtures were cleaned up; the `판` wording was changed per `docs/korean-terms.md`; the `Look` doc example now lists the new keys.

I added 5 regression tests. Two of them fail if their fixes are removed, and the others failed against the old code.

**Checks:** fmt clean, clippy `-D warnings` clean, 1595 unit and 610 integration tests pass.

## Not fixed — these need a decision
- **#6 queued input:** a reliable drain needs a terminal round trip (a DA1 query), and draining can swallow the user's type-ahead.
- **#8 banner shift:** clearing the notice on a click is the intended "a click counts as a keypress" behaviour.
- **Middle-click paste (#5):** releasing capture outside Browse/Stats would bring paste back into forms, but it changes the documented decision.
- **Wheel over pickers:** the user decided pickers ignore the mouse, but the cost was never put to them: before this change the wheel scrolled those pickers through the terminal's alternate-scroll.
- **Other efficiency ideas:** skipping redraws when nothing changed, or enabling mode 1002 only while dragging, would mean wider loop or design changes.
- **`acted()`/`paste` duplication:** marginal; the repo's style is a per-entry clear.

note: Took in 12 of 15 findings in the review fix commit. Took in #5 and the picker wheel too, after asking the person: the explorer lets the mouse go while a form, a prompt or a picker is up (App::wants_mouse), so middle-click paste and alternate-scroll work there as before. Handed on #6 (drain queued mouse reports before leaving raw mode) as idea moai-fpxd, outside the release. Kept #8 as it is: a click counts as a keypress, so it clears the notice.

I found no correctness bugs in this diff, only three minor cleanups. I fixed two of them in the working tree and did not commit.

The fix itself is sound: it adds `.padding(Padding::horizontal(left_gutter()))` to the statistics window's block, which is the same mechanism the detail pane uses. Because the margin lives on the block, `inner` now feeds the chart-or-text cutoff (`STATS_CHART_W`), the side-by-side cutoff, the bar measuring (`stat_bars`) and the line folding. The things that work off the outer rect (the scroll marker, the mouse wheel, the scroll height) are not affected by a horizontal margin. All 27 stats tests pass under `cargo test stats`, including the new `the_stats_window_keeps_the_detail_panes_gutter`.

title: mosh 아래에서는 DA1 답이 먼저 와 마우스 보고가 샌다

text:
/code-review xhigh --fix — reviewer's own words (agent a5870a9dd3c0cf3e1)

Found 7 issues, fixed 4 in the working tree (not committed). Clippy (`--all-targets -D warnings`), `cargo fmt --check`, and full `cargo test` (1599 + 610) all pass. Also exercised the debug binary in a private tmux server (`-L`): `SPC q` with and without injected wheel reports — tmux log shows mouse-off sequences, then `ESC[c`, then the reply `ESC[?1;2;4c` consumed; quit takes 60–90 ms and the shell prompt is clean.

Diff reviewed: `a5588c16..HEAD` touched `src/cmd/tui.rs` and `CHANGELOG.md` (before fixes). No CLAUDE.md violations found.

1. src/cmd/tui.rs:1022 — `caught` was never refreshed after `resume(term, app.wants_mouse())` in loop_until_quit, so it could claim the mouse was on when the terminal had it off.
   Failure: mouse on, SPC n, editor returns but the save fails or a who-are-you prompt opens (Mode::Idea/Ask), so resume does not turn the mouse on and `caught` stays true. If the first event closes the form (Esc), wants_mouse() is true again, equals the stale `caught`, and the mouse is never turned back on: it stays dead until SPC o m is pressed twice. The next suspend(caught) also runs a needless DA1 drain.

2. src/cmd/tui.rs:581 — drain_reports sent the DA1 query without checking that poll could read the fd, so wherever poll fails at once (POLLNVAL/POLLHUP/POLLERR) the answer is sure to reach the shell.
   Failure: poll returns POLLNVAL on the fd (likely macOS /dev/tty when stdin is piped; not tested) or the tty is hung up. drain_until_answer returns false at once, and the terminal's `ESC[?1;2c` then lands at the prompt on every quit. Strictly worse than not asking.

3. src/cmd/tui.rs:350 — the drain in screen() is not protected by the EDITING gate (only suspend holds it), so a reload-thread panic during the drain can turn raw mode off in the middle of it.
   Failure: a reload thread panics during the quit round trip. The hook runs modes_off and ratatui's restore, and the tty goes back to line mode. The answer then sits unread in the line buffer: the drain waits the full 1 s, and the answer is echoed and handed to the shell with the next line.

4. src/cmd/tui.rs:350 — screen() decides whether to drain from app.wants_mouse(), not from the mouse state the loop actually set, and its comment says the two always match, which is not quite true on error exits.
   Failure: if enable_raw_mode succeeds in resume but EnterAlternateScreen fails, modes_on never runs and the terminal is not capturing, yet wants_mouse() is true, so the drain does a needless round trip (or a 1 s wait). Costs time only, never leaks.

5. src/cmd/tui.rs:649 — Answer/Heard (and their test) were compiled on every platform, but their only reader, drain_until_answer, is unix-only.
   Failure: on Windows the non-test build warns about dead code for Answer, Heard and Answer::push. CI builds no Windows target, so it never shows, but `cargo clippy -D warnings` there would fail.

6. src/cmd/tui.rs:562 — the DA1 check assumes the terminal that answers is also where the mouse reports come from. A middle layer that answers DA1 itself but passes upstream input through unfiltered (mosh-server) breaks that.
   Failure: under mosh, the server answers `ESC[c` locally right away while the client's wheel reports are still crossing the network. The drain stops at that early answer, and the late reports still land at the prompt. tmux and screen are fine because they drop mouse input for a pane that has turned the mouse off.

7. CHANGELOG.md:45 — the entry did not say that quitting or opening the editor can now pause for up to ANSWER_WAIT (1 s).
   Failure: someone on a terminal that does not answer DA1 sees a 1-second freeze on every quit and every SPC n while the mouse is on, and the release notes give no reason.

Fixed:
- 1: `caught = app.wants_mouse();` is now set before `resume(term, caught)`, and the comment above `let mut caught`, which claimed the two could not drift apart, is corrected.
- 2: a zero-timeout `poll` now runs before `ESC[c` is written. If it errors or reports POLLNVAL/POLLHUP/POLLERR, the query is not sent.
- 5: `#[cfg(unix)]` on `Answer`, `Heard`, `impl Answer`, `answered_at`, `only_a_da1_reply_ends_the_drain`.
- 7: CHANGELOG adds "A terminal that never answers is waited on for one second at most."

Skipped:
- 3: gating the drain in screen() with EDITING. The race is one round trip wide and needs a panic somewhere else. Holding the gate would change when panic hooks run: the hook's second `LeaveAlternateScreen` (`?1049l`, which also moves the cursor back) would then always come after restore. That is a trade-off for the owner, not a review fix.
- 4: with fix 1 they agree on every normal exit, and on error exits a mismatch only costs a needless round trip.
- 6: this is a limit of the DA1 approach the user chose, not a code bug.

text:
Person's answers (2026-10-02, worker window, AskUserQuestion) — all four were the recommended option:
- `ready --json` `others`: same Row shape as `ready`, plus an always-present `owner` key — `"theirs"` or `"unowned"`
- human `moai ready`: a separate block under the list (`?` glyph, id · p · title · owner label); the header count is mine only; `-n` cuts that block too
- `moai prime`: `picked` also drops rows that are not mine (same judge as the hook focus); its `ready` splits like `ready` and carries `others`
- hook focus: an unowned row already in a started column leaves the focus too ("unowned is not mine" holds there as well); the way back is `moai mv <id> <col> --take`, which only changes the assignee when the row already stands there
Defaults taken without asking: `--take` on a row that is already mine writes nothing extra; `--take` also takes a row that already stands in the target column; the stderr line without `--take` stands only for a move into a started column; the hook's actor honours a `--user` on that same `moai` call

text:
Fable design notes for the board (2026-10-02, read-only planner; the person chose every recommendation — see the epic body)

Fit
- Layout of the list, not a window: `App::layout: view::Layout {List, Board}`, persisted as `[tui] layout = "board"` (`user_config::Look`, `look_now`/`apply_look`/`Doc::merge_look`). Toggle `SPC v b` — stateful like `d`/`w`/`r`, the menu stays open and shows `[목록/보드]` (`Browse::state`). `Pane::Explorer`'s word becomes "보드" on the key bar.
- Same cursor, same rows: `App::cursor` stays an index into `App::rows()`; in Board layout `rows()`/`rows_in()` return the current directory fully unfolded (the `open` closure of `nav::Index::entries_tree` returns true) and keep only cards — rows with `e.at()` and `!report::is_group` (work + ideas). Group rows and baskets are not cards.
- Placement is a new pure component `src/tui/board.rs`: `board::column_of(kind, shelved, status)` (Idea → idea column; `Index::shelved_at(at).is_some()` → 미룸; else `Site::column(at)`), `board::Plan::of(rows, facts, width, card_h)` → lane/column/rect per row, `board::step(plan, cursor, Move/Side)`. No I/O, tested without a terminal; `report`/`query` untouched.
- List↔board keeps the selected row: on toggle take `anchor_of(current)`, rebuild rows, `row_of`. Cursor on an epic row → first card under `Seg::Epic(id)`, else 0. Board→list uses `land(id)`.
- Visibility is the list's: `View::shows(column, deferred, known)` — `SPC v 1..n` hides a status column, `SPC v l` the 미룸 column; done hidden by default; the badge names what is hidden.
- Lanes at the root: `Seg::Milestone(Some(id))` directories plus the `(마일스톤 없음)` basket, in the list's order; a card's lane is `nav::Index::home_of(at)[0]`. Lane header drawn like the milestone's list row (glyph from `Site::column`, spinner when `Site::spins`, tally). Inside a milestone or epic: one lane, no header.
- Keys: `j/k/↑/↓` next/prev card in the column, `h/l/←/→` neighbouring column (nearest card by height) — `Browse::Expand/Collapse` re-aimed in Board layout via `keys::Ctx.board`; `gg/G`, `Ctrl-d/u/f/b` within the column; `Tab` disabled on the board; `Enter`/`Bksp`, `r`, `SPC n`, `SPC m g`, `SPC s *`, `/`, `f` unchanged.
- Mouse (v0.2.0 rules): `mouse::Drawn` gains `cards: Vec<(Rect, usize)>` and `columns: Vec<(Rect, usize)>`; click on a card → `move_to(n)` + focus; wheel over a column moves the cursor within that column; divider drag untouched.
- Scrolling: one vertical `Scroll` over a whole-board canvas drawn like `stats_window`; lane height = its tallest column; `Scroll::reveal_span(top, h)` for 2–3-line cards; only cards inside the window are built (moai-wt4n).
- Narrow: columns split the inner width evenly with `CARD_MIN = 18`; columns that do not fit are named in the frame title with counts (`+1 칸 ? review 0`); the column holding the cursor is always drawn. 16-colour style table only; selection = REVERSED head + `>`.

Card A (chosen), 120 columns, detail at the bottom, 5 columns of 22:

    ┃◇ idea 1               ‖ 미룸 1               · todo 9               ▸ in_progress 10       ? review 0   ┃
    ┃── moai-jvfe ⠼▸ v0.3.0 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 0/21 ──┃
    ┃                         moai-qrnl   · p2       moai-psyu.0t3 · p3   > moai-0zjo.r13 ⠼▸ p1               ┃
    ┃                         말묶음 키가 있는지…    [NEW] created·updat…   [NEW] mv --take 가 …              ┃

Members — files and difficulty
- board 모듈: new src/tui/board.rs, src/tui/mod.rs (`mod board`) — medium
- SPC v b 토글: src/tui/keys.rs (`Browse::Board`, `state`, `stateful`, `Ctx.board`, `enabled`), src/tui/view.rs (`Layout`), src/tui/mod.rs (`App::layout`, `rows()` board branch, toggle, `step` dispatch, `Pane::word`), src/user_config.rs (`Look.layout`, `merge_look`), i18n — high
- 보드 그리기: src/tui/draw.rs (`board()` beside `list()`, column header, lane headers, card lines following `App::fields`, `CARD_MIN`, off-screen columns in the title, `Drawn` fill), src/tui/scroll.rs (`reveal_span`) — high
- 마우스: src/tui/mouse.rs (`Drawn.cards/columns`, press/wheel on the board) — medium
- 에픽 열: src/tui/view.rs (`Field::Epic`, `ALL`, `drop_rank`), src/tui/keys.rs (`SPC c e`), src/tui/draw.rs (list right cell with `EPIC_REF`, card foot) — medium
- 문서: src/cli.rs (tui --help), README.md, CHANGELOG.md `[Unreleased] ### Added` — low; keep out of src/guide.rs

text:
The review found 20 real problems in epic moai-0zjo; I fixed 15 of them in the working tree. Everything is uncommitted, nothing under `.moai/` was touched, and `cargo test` (1610 + 622), `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.

For every fix that adds a test, I reverted the fix and confirmed its test fails without it. Line numbers below refer to HEAD.

A review row under my own in-progress work that is unowned or assigned to someone else stopped being guarded.","failure_scenario":"I hold P; review P.r is `-a none` or someone else's. `moai mv P.r done` without -m passes (v0.1.6 refused it), Stop no longer lists P.r, and /code-review refuses as if P had no review, asking for a duplicate review row. What I fixed, besides the direct fixes above:
- Who you are is now looked up only where a rule needs it. A new lazy `hook::Person` asks git on first use, so plain Bash calls, read-only `moai show`/`note`, writes to `/dev/null` or `/tmp`, and `mv X done` without a review spawn no git; the `moai show` case was confirmed by timing. `asks_owner` and the `Who` struct are gone; the hook uses the same lookup as `ready` (`cmd::me_of`).
- Rule 3's `theirs()` is back to "which worktree holds it". Ownership now applies only to the focus and to the idle review suggestion. A re-run of the rule-3 reproduction now matches v0.1.6.
- Rule 5 follows the person `mv` will run as. It reads a `MOAI_ACTOR=` prefix, carries `--user` into the line it hands back, and treats `MOAI_ACTOR` set elsewhere on the line (`export …;`, `bash -c`) as unknown, so it passes.
- Hint lines run as given. `mv`'s stderr line quotes the column and keeps `-C` and an explicit `--user`. The `?` hint gains `-m '<who said yes>'`. A new `guide::TAKE_YES` tail is shared by the refusal and both hints, and a test ties TAKE_OVER to it.
- Blank assignees. `-a none` and `report::owner` now use the same rule, so a blank assignee counts as nobody's in both.
- Docs and generated files. CHANGELOG wording corrected and the `mv` next change added; "five rules" in skill.rs and en/ko; comments in config.rs, i18n/README.md and hook.rs updated; plugin tree regenerated with `MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in`. AGENTS.md is unchanged.

## What I fixed (uncommitted, in `.claude/worktrees/moai-itsu`)

- **One way to resolve the root.** `held::Home` is now the only way to get a resolved root, and `place`, `check`, `read_inside` and the new `open_inside` all take it. `Repo::rooted` resolves the root once for both config and snapshot.
- **Links are always measured.** `place` now measures every path. A link it can't fully resolve is followed the way `target_of` does it: to the directory it lands in, or to the deepest ancestor that exists for an absolute link.
- **held::read changes:**
  - a socket is now "not a regular file" instead of an OS error;
  - the buffer is sized from fstat up front (14 reads became 2 on a 147 KB snapshot);
  - opening retries on EWOULDBLOCK for up to 45 s, the same wait a blocking open had under a lease.
- **Refusals carry data, rendered in the chosen language.** `read_snapshot(root)` now returns a typed `Unsnapped`, and siblings report it through a new `worktree::Trouble::Unheld`. Snapshot and config refusals now read the same way, `<at>: <why>`. I dropped the `held.refused` key and added "socket" to `held.not_a_file`.
- **Journal changes:**
  - links to non-regular or unresolvable targets are reported as `outside`;
  - when two names fold together, the first one is re-checked so a reused inode can't drop a live file;
  - `Lock::holds` now uses the same `file_id` check;
  - journal file names are sanitized before display.
- **Other code fixes:**
  - the explorer clears the Tab intent when a project can't be opened;
  - `config::Trouble::code` now lists every variant (the repo rule against `_` wildcards).
- **Tests:**
  - added: dangling and `.git` rows in the snapshot/config test, a root opened through a link, journal links to `/dev/null` and to a missing target, the journal_bytes refusal branch, the sanitized name, a socket, and a failed-open Tab test;
  - the sibling test now goes through both the cheap check and the full read;
  - the FIFO tests now fail by name after 60 s instead of hanging CI.
- **Docs:**
  - CHANGELOG: new Changed entry, corrected Fixed entry, plus two Fixed entries (journal names, Tab);
  - docs/recovery.md: new `broken` section;
  - stale doc comments corrected;
  - `판`/`층` wording fixed per docs/korean-terms.md.

**Verification**
- `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` are clean.
- Unit tests: 1612 pass.
- CLI tests: 611 of 612 pass. The one failure, `bumping_moves_the_lock_line_with_the_manifest`, runs the release script with a real cargo under an isolated HOME. It touches nothing I changed, and two verifiers saw it fail on unmodified copies.
- I reverted each fix in turn and confirmed its new test goes red.
- A smoke run confirmed that `-C <symlink>`, links inside the checkout and a linked worktree redirected to the main checkout still read fine, and that nothing hangs on a FIFO.

## Left for you to file

These are outside the epic's diff or promise, so per CLAUDE.md they should be written down rather than fixed here:
- **AGENTS.md and the other unbounded reads (#1):** a p1 bug, or a member of moai-itsu.
- **The lock link (#2):** p1. It causes silent loss and is on the write path, so it deserves its own max-level review.
- **prime (#5).**

Also worth filing:
- The outside-repo overview's `--json` drops the `broken` code.
- `init` plants `.gitattributes`/`.gitignore` rules for `.git/` paths.
- The write side (`target_of`) still prints English with code `error`, e.g. a Korean line with an English middle from `MOAI_LANG=ko moai mv`.
- A human decision is needed on whether a monorepo sub-tracker's shared config link should be supported. For now it is documented under Changed.

The hook falling back to the worktree's own snapshot when the root snapshot is refused turned out to be the intended design, so I didn't change it.

One side effect: a finder agent accidentally ran an uncapped `moai init` on a scratch repo with `CLAUDE.md -> /dev/zero`. The container killed those two scratch processes for running out of memory (`oom_kill=2`); no sessions were affected.

text:
Review text (/code-review high --fix, opus, forked; range merge-base develop..HEAD of worktree-moai-3hxc)

I applied five of the seven findings to the working tree. Nothing is committed: the repo convention is to commit review fixes as a separate `fix:` commit. The full `cargo test` run passed (1622 + 630, 0 failed) and `cargo clippy --all-targets` showed no warnings.

1. src/cmd/add.rs:326 — On the plan path, the new --body notice suggests `--body - < <file>`, which conflicts with `--from -` and is refused.
   Failure: `moai add --from - --body plan.md` (the exact 2026-10-01 case behind moai-3hxc.58k) prints 'To use the file's contents, `--body - < plan.md`'. Running that gives `moai add --from - --body - < plan.md`, which is refused with refuse.plan_body_stdin, so the suggested way out is a dead end.
2. src/cmd/rm.rs:70 — The new `cut` set only asks whether any line with the id is left, but status's dangling_epic asks whether that line is an epic. If the twin left behind is an issue, rm now stays quiet about members that status flags.
   Failure: The file holds X as an epic, X as an issue, and a member with epic X. `moai rm X` removes the epic line. Before the diff, the member was reported as dangling. Now `dangling` is `[]`, while `moai status` warns dangling_epic for that member.
3. i18n/en.json:720 — add.body_names_a_file says the text 'went into the body' (ko: '본문에 … 적었다'), but the notice prints before the write, so the claim can be false.
   Failure: `moai add --from p.md --body plan.md --dry-run` writes nothing, and `moai add t -b plan.md -s nope` is refused afterwards. Both still print that the body was written.
4. src/cmd/add.rs:433 — The single-add path checks and reports the milestone from argv (`args.milestone`), while `bulk` reads it from the row it made (`stood_on(&made)`), whose comment warns the two will drift once writes normalise the field.
   Failure: Once the field is normalised on write, the single path would report a different id than the one stored, and bulk and single add would disagree on the same input.
5. src/cmd/add.rs:135 — `{text}` goes to stderr unsanitised. `names_a_file` only excludes \n and \r, so ESC and tab pass through.
   Failure: A file in the working directory whose name contains an ESC sequence, given as `--body`, writes raw terminal escapes to stderr. Everywhere else, moai cleans such text with `text::one_line` before drawing it.
6. src/cmd/rm.rs:72 — rm never counts `milestone` references, so removing a milestone leaves its members dangling_milestone with no notice from rm (this predates the diff, but sits in the function it touched).
   Failure: `moai rm <milestone>` with issues carrying `milestone: <that id>` reports `dangling: []`, then `moai status` shows a dangling_milestone warning for them.
7. src/cmd/rm.rs:65 — rm re-derives 'dangling' by hand in cmd/ instead of reusing report's predicates, which is why it drifted on twin kinds and on milestones.
   Failure: Each new reference rule in report (kinds, twins, milestones) has to be copied into rm by hand, or rm and status disagree again. CLAUDE.md says: '`cmd/*.rs` 안에 이슈의 뜻을 판단하는 `if` 를 두지 않는다'.

Fixed:
1. Plan path advice: a new `read_body_told(arg, ctx, plan_on_stdin)` sits behind `read_body_said`. The `--from` path passes `reads_stdin(from)`, and when the plan already holds stdin it uses a new key, `add.body_names_a_file_plan_on_stdin` (en and ko). That message tells you to move the plan into a file: `moai add --from <plan file> --body - < plan.md`. The existing test now asserts this line.
2. rm with a twin of a different kind: the epic-reference check now uses `report::kinds_of` over the removed ids. A member counts as dangling unless the line left behind is an epic, which matches dangling_epic. Parent and blocker checks keep using `cut`. Added the test `rm_calls_a_member_dangling_when_the_twin_left_is_not_an_epic`.
3. Notice wording: en and ko now state what the body is ("the body is the words `{text}`, not the file by that name") rather than claiming it was written.
4. Milestone source: `known` and `say_no_such_milestone` on the single-add path now read `issue.milestone` and `made.milestone`.
5. Unsanitised text: `{text}` now goes through `text::one_line`; the shell-quoted `{path}` is unchanged.

Skipped:

## What was fixed (uncommitted in the worktree)

I fixed 1–6, 10–15, plus a few smaller items:

- Zone picker: aim only when the filter text actually changes. The footer leaves 20 cells for the scroll mark, and the strings now put "Enter alone keeps it" first. The list keeps its gutter (`HighlightSpacing::Always`). A filter with no match shows a new `tui.tz.no_match` line.
- Header row: it gets the width left before the project numbers. Paths are shortened in the middle by a new `journal_at`, so the root name and file name both survive.
- Banner: `tell_journals` waits while a text field has focus, names the first newly unreadable journal, and reuses `cmd::journal_errors`. The "does the header stand" check is computed once.
- mosh drain: the gate is extracted into `drain_answered` and tested through a pipe. The last-wheel time moved from the process-global `ROLLED` onto `App::rolled_at`.
- Small items: `user_root` has its doc block back; stale header docs are fixed; Korean doc comments now use 때/비용 where they had 판/값 for "case" and "cost", per `docs/korean-terms.md`; the comment claiming GNU screen drops these reports is corrected (screen's source shows it passes them through); en.json uses `—`, matching the person's decision text; the CHANGELOG wording is corrected.

Every new or changed test was checked to fail when its fix is reverted (12 reverts, all red). `cargo test`: 1631 passed, 3 ignored, plus 624 CLI tests. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` are clean.

## Decisions for the person

- 7 (header row never clears): meeting the decision needs `src/store.rs`, which belongs to another epic, or a new re-check on the `follow` tick. The docs and CHANGELOG now say "until you quit".
- 8 (half-eaten keys): the decision says "that one byte". Eating the rest of an escape sequence the drain has already started into would stop the leftovers, but it changes what was decided.
- 9 (UTC rewrite): this is pre-existing. Fixing it means deciding which name is "in use" when the configured zone won't load.
- 300ms wait after a wheel: every quit or editor launch within a second of scrolling now waits 300ms, even where reports can't trail (tmux, a local terminal, plain ssh). That is the accepted trade-off. A `TMUX`/`STY` skip would be wrong: GNU screen and iTerm2 `-CC` need the drain.
- Typing then clearing the filter: row 0 stays highlighted and the footer is gone, so Enter picks it. The highlight is visible, so this is a design question rather than a silent pick.

Not done: sharing the near-identical poll/read loops of `drain_trailing` and `drain_until_answer` (unsafe I/O code whose timeout handling deliberately differs), testing the production branch of `App::journals`, and a few minor cleanups.

- Left as they are: the 300ms wait after a recent wheel (the person's accepted trade-off); a typed-then-cleared filter keeps row 0 highlighted (visible, not a silent pick); sharing the two poll loops (drain_trailing now reads through `next_byte`; drain_until_answer keeps its own timeout handling); testing the production branch of `App::journals` (it is the global `store::journal_unread`, which other tests fill).

I found no bugs in `434f6f12..HEAD` (commits 876f303b and 924027ef), so I changed nothing. The ReportFindings tool isn't available in this session, so this reply is the whole report.

Answers to the questions in the brief:

- **The fixed flag test goes red when the message loses the flag.** It now looks for the exact text `자리에는 \`<flag>\` 를 쓸 수 없다`. That matches the `{flag}` slot in `i18n/ko.json:735` (`refuse.show_filter_on_one`). The old check could pass for one-letter flags because the issue id also appears in the message, and that loophole is closed. `-a` and `--deferred` are refused under those same names by `first_given` in `src/cmd/show.rs`. That function now has a test row for every field.
- **Each script test goes red on a revert.** I put each script back to its `434f6f12` version on its own, ran the two new tests, then restored the script with `git checkout HEAD --`:
  - Reverting `check-version.sh` failed both `the_version_check_reads_a_single_quoted_manifest` and `a_single_quoted_manifest_is_read_and_bumped`.
  - Reverting `bump-version.sh` failed `a_single_quoted_manifest_is_read_and_bumped`, because `Cargo.toml` was left at `'0.1.5'`.
  - The worktree is clean again afterwards.
- **The bump keeps the quote style.** It tries the double-quote substitution first and only falls back to the single-quote one if that fails. Both patterns need the quote right after `=`, so a quote inside a trailing comment cannot trigger the wrong one. The test checks the result is `version = '0.2.0'`.
- **Leaving `lock_version` double-quote-only is sound.** It runs only after `cargo update --workspace` succeeds, and cargo always writes `Cargo.lock` with double quotes. The part that could go wrong with a single-quoted manifest is the crate name, and that now comes from `--print-name`, which strips both quote kinds.
- **The comments say what the code does.** The note that `\047` is a single quote, the reason for keeping each line's own quote, and the `argos-n7tw` example of a one-letter flag hiding inside an id are all accurate.

In the dev profile, the six tests in scope all pass: the two new ones, the flag test, and three existing bump tests.

**One thing I left alone:** if neither substitution matches the `version` line, the bump still prints `Cargo.toml <old> → <new>` without having changed anything. This could only happen with a malformed or exotic `version` line; I couldn't find a valid TOML form that `check-version.sh` reads but the bump fails to rewrite. It also existed before these commits, so I didn't treat it as a finding.

10. src/cmd/add.rs:943 — `is_milestone` (documented as the same check status uses, and newly relied on by edit) returns true if ANY line with the id is a milestone; status uses the LAST line.
   Failure: argos-m009=[milestone line, issue line] → `add --from plan --milestone argos-m009 --dry-run` says the epic stands on it, while status counts rows on argos-m009 as dangling_milestone.
11. src/cmd/edit.rs:27 — The `known_milestone` field doc says it checks the id typed on the command line; the code and the comment beside it check the edited row's value.
   Failure: A maintainer trusting the doc 'simplifies' the check to read argv, the very divergence the comment guards against.
12. src/cmd/rm.rs:3 — The module doc ('rows that stood on the removed milestone') is narrower than what the code names: any row that status newly counts as dangling.
   Failure: `rm A`, where A shadowed child A.b's broken milestone field, names grandchild A.b.c, which fits none of the documented categories.
13. src/report.rs:3788 — `dangling_milestones` builds a full Soil but reads only `kinds` and `lost`; rm calls it twice while holding the write lock, even when every id is missing.
   Failure: Measured (opt-level 3 dev build, no LTO): rm holds the lock 137 ms longer at 10k rows and 15 ms longer on the 2.2k-row tracker; 53–70% of each call is never read.
14. tests/cli.rs:3692 — The new rm test reads `--json` by splitting the string to the end of stdout instead of using the existing `list_in` helper.
   Failure: If a key is ever added after `dangling`, the positive checks can pass on the wrong array and the negative ones fail falsely.
15. CHANGELOG.md:119 — PLAUSIBLE: neither commit adds an [Unreleased] line for the edit notice or for the wider rm `dangling` list.
   Failure: If the branch merges without the step 7-3 `docs(changelog)` commit, the v0.3.0 notes omit both changes.

Fixed:
- rm (the epic gap, the twin case, the lock cost, the module doc): rm now compares, row by row and on both the epic and milestone axes, what `status` counts before and after the removal. The comparison comes from a new `report::dangling_lines`, which shares its per-row check with the function `status` uses. `report::dangling_milestones` is gone. The new function builds only the type map and the epic inheritance (`Ties::epics_only`) instead of a full Soil, and rm skips the work when nothing is removed.
- Kept-milestone hint: when the typed id is not a milestone, the hint shows a placeholder instead of that id. This needed a `known` parameter on `milestone_kept_line` and a new i18n key `edit.any_milestone` in en.json and ko.json. Both edit and add use it.
- `is_milestone`: now uses `report::kinds_of`, so it reads the last line like `status` does.
- Docs and comments: reworded the two guide.rs sentences, then regenerated the plugin (`MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in`) and AGENTS.md (throwaway `moai init`; new hash `c3424ccd`). Corrected the `known_milestone` field doc and the false part of the edit.rs comment, and changed `판` to `경우` in edit.rs and add.rs.
- Edit closures: made the three closures plain values computed once. A verifier checked this against HEAD on 32 scenarios with identical output.
- Tests: the rm test now uses `list_in` with an exact match. Four new integration tests and one random-pile unit test were added (checks `dangling_lines` against `status` on 3,000 piles). Three of the new integration tests fail when the fix is reverted; the fourth, for the placeholder hint, fails against the HEAD behaviour the sweep reproduced.

Not fixed, needs your call:
- Notice wording with an unusable epic: the text is shared with add and predates this range, so I only corrected the comment. Fixing it means choosing new wording or a second i18n key.
- Opposite rules in rm's `dangling` list: making them agree would break one of two existing tests, which pin opposite rules, so it is a design decision.
- Epic notice in edit (printed before the write lands, existence-only, silent on repeats): older code; fixing it changes when an existing notice fires, and add has the same pattern.
- CHANGELOG: worker-brief step 7-3 writes it after pulling develop, whose CHANGELOG has moved 31 lines, so adding it now would conflict. Your draft in the scratchpad (`changelog-draft.md`) should also mention epic-inherited rows and the hint fix.

Outside this range:
- The validation loop in src/store.rs line 946 is O(n²) and makes up most of every write's lock time (about 600 of 850 ms at 10k rows). In a debug build at 10k rows the lock is held past the 5 s lock timeout. Worth parking as an idea.

Review text — /code-review high --fix over 303f6311..HEAD (moai-q5zs), agent adda5103a92df74b7

I found 7 problems in the moai-q5zs diff (`303f6311..HEAD`) and fixed 5 of them in the working tree. The main one: a group row (an epic or milestone row) given `-e <real epic>` got no notice, even though `moai status` counts it as `dangling_epic`. After the fixes, `cargo test` passes (1634 unit and 641 CLI tests), and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` are clean.

1. src/cmd/add.rs:954 — is_epic does not match report::broken_at for group rows: it only checks the kind of the epic id, but broken_at counts any group row that has an `epic` field as dangling_epic (moai-fg0t). Its doc comment says it is the same check as status, which is wrong. Failure: `moai epic add X -e <real epic>`, `moai milestone add M -e <real epic>` and `moai edit <epic> -e <real epic>` all exit 0 with no notice, but `moai status` lists all three under dangling_epic. Reproduced with the dev binary.
2. src/cmd/add.rs:958 — The is_epic/is_a kind check lives in cmd/*.rs, which the project rules forbid. CLAUDE.md says "`cmd/*.rs` 안에 이슈의 뜻을 판단하는 `if` 를 두지 않는다". The new check was a second copy of report's rule kept in cmd, and that copy is exactly where it drifted on group rows.
3. i18n/en.json:191 — The notice texts no longer fit the cases that now trigger them. `edit.no_such_epic` says "left as it was" although the field is written, and `add.no_such_epic_yet` says "no epic X yet" when X is an existing issue that will never become an epic. Failure: `moai edit A -e <issue id>` writes the field, then says "no epic … left as it was".
4. src/cmd/edit.rs:351 — add and edit each had their own copy of the same eprintln block, using two i18n keys that mean the same thing. The milestone side already shares one helper (say_no_such_milestone) and one key.
5. src/cmd/edit.rs:259 — known_epic worked out again from args.epic which values mean "clear the field", and add carried a redundant `issue.epic.is_none() ||` check that the print site already covers. Neither matched the milestone side (`wrote_milestone`) exactly.
6. src/cmd/add.rs:434 — is_milestone and the epic check each call kinds_of, so the issue list is scanned twice while the write lock is held. Two O(n) passes over 10k rows per add; small.
7. src/cmd/edit.rs:344 — When `-e` points at a bad epic and `--milestone` at a bad milestone, the milestone notice still says status counts the row as dangling_milestone. Status counts it only as dangling_epic. Older than this diff; the existing code comment already says so.

Fixed:
- 1 and 2: `report::epic_held_wrong(all, row) -> Option<HeldEpic>` (`NotAnEpic`, `Group`) is the epic half of `broken_at`. `is_epic`/`is_a` gone, `is_milestone` back to its one-liner.
- 4 and 5: add and edit both measure the written row with `epic_held_wrong` and print through `add::say_held_epic`; epic line before milestone line, under `--json`, only after a successful write.
- 3: the two keys are now one, `add.no_such_epic`, worded like the milestone notice; `add.group_in_epic` for group rows, en and ko.
- New test `a_group_row_given_an_epic_is_told` (epic add -e, milestone add -e --json, edit <epic> -e, status agrees).

Skipped: 6 (negligible), 7 (older than this diff, documented in edit.rs).

Notes: could not check out pre-diff add.rs/edit.rs to prove red (auto-mode classifier blocked it); from reading, every assertion in the two new tests fails on the old code, including the refused-write cases. Twins: none on the write path. Id-derived members: `Handing::at` reads the written epic first, so the check matches `misplace_of`. Edit policy matches `--milestone`. Nothing new fires on a path that was silent before.

text:
Reviewer (/code-review high --fix, agent a884fd2c4f7162971) over 60c1f69f..HEAD, own words:

Two real gaps turned up, both in the tests, and I fixed both. The code under review needed no changes. The fixes are in `tests/cli.rs` and are not committed. Only the three affected tests were run, and all pass. Each new check fails when I temporarily undo the code it protects, and passes again once restored.

1. tests/cli.rs:7815 — No test catches it if the `*a != "-"` check in `add::say_if_body_names_a_file` is removed: the stdin case passes either way because no file named `-` exists in the test directory.
   Failure: someone drops `*a != "-" &&` from the helper and the suite stays green. Later, in a directory with a file named `-`, `moai add t -b - < x` reads stdin and also wrongly says "the body is the words `-`".
2. tests/cli.rs:16772 — The required 'note -b - with empty stdin says one line, not two' had no test: the empty-note test only checked that the message contains the "empty" word, and its whitespace-only input never triggers the extra 'stdin was empty' line anyway.
   Failure: switching `note` to `read_body_said` (an obvious-looking cleanup) prints two lines (the stdin-empty notice, then the empty-memo refusal), and the old test still passed. Confirmed by temporarily making that switch.
3. src/cmd/note.rs:26 — The file-name notice prints before the id lookup and actor check, so a refused note still gets the hint first.
   Failure: `moai note nope-zz -b plan.md` prints the `--body takes the text itself…` hint and then `nope-zz not found`, exit 1. That is two lines when nothing was written. add and edit behave the same way.
4. src/cmd/add.rs:153 — The helper does not skip the other spellings of stdin that `reads_stdin` already recognises, so `-b /dev/stdin` gets a circular suggestion.
   Failure: `moai note <id> -b /dev/stdin < plan.md` saves the note as the text `/dev/stdin` and suggests `--body - < /dev/stdin`. The suggestion does work, but it reads oddly. This was already true for add.
5. i18n/en.json:724 — Shown for `note -b`, the message says 'the body is the words `plan.md`', but a note has no body.
   Failure: `moai note <id> -b plan.md` tells the user about 'the body' when the text actually became a note. It is a wording mismatch only, and the advice to use `--body - < plan.md` is still correct.

Fixed
- Check for `-`: `a_body_that_is_not_a_lone_file_name_stays_quiet` now creates a file named `-` before the stdin case, so removing the check fails the test.
- One line on empty stdin: `an_empty_note_is_told_apart_from_a_missing_one` now also runs `note -b -` with completely empty stdin. It asserts exactly one line on stderr.

Skipped
- Hint before refusal (3): add and edit print it in the same place. Moving it only for `note` would break the "same message from the same place" rule this change set out to keep.
- `/dev/stdin` (4): a small, harmless oddity that predates this change and is out of scope.
- 'body' wording (5): fixing it means new message keys in all five languages, and the flag is named `--body` anyway.

The other things you asked me to check all hold. No inserted item took over a doc block. There is one shared helper, `add::say_if_body_names_a_file`, called from `read_body_told` and `note.rs`, not a copy. The notice uses `Path::is_file`, a stat only. The `note` help line matches the `edit` one and `docs/cli.md`, as `the_cli_reference_matches_the_help` confirms. And taking out the `note.rs` call fails `a_one_line_body_naming_a_file_is_said_and_kept`.

The `note`-only parts of the CHANGELOG entry hold too: the help really does say "Text, not a path", and the note text is kept, apart from the trim it already had.

My call on the findings:
- 1, 2 taken in as committed test fixes (fix commit on worktree-moai-18so). Both checked green after the change; reviewer checked each goes red on revert.
- 3 not taken: the hint is still true for a refused call, and add/edit print it at the same point; moving it for note alone splits the one place this epic set out to keep.
- 4 not taken and not handed on: the notice is truthful there. `read_body` treats only `-` as stdin, so `-b /dev/stdin` really stores the words `/dev/stdin`; saying so is the point of the notice.
- 5 handed on as idea moai-4oii (no epic, no milestone): wording only, the advice is right and the flag is `--body`.

2026-10-02 사용자 결정 — 락 자리의 링크는 안을 가리켜도 다 거절한다(`O_NOFOLLOW`). `.moai/lock -> issues.jsonl` 이면 쓰기마다 rename 으로 갈리는 아이노드를 잠가서 두 쓰는 쪽이 서로 다른 파일을 잡는다. 거절 코드는 스냅샷 거절(moai-itsu)과 같은 `broken` 이다. `locked` 로 내면 기다려도 안 풀리는데 재시도 고리가 그 코드를 보고 끝없이 돈다. 규칙은 모든 락에 건다. 사용자 설정·읽음 표시·`moai-held.lock` 의 락도 `Lock::acquire` 한 자리에서 `held.rs` 를 지난다.

범위를 고쳤다(2026-10-02 사용자 결정) — 링크를 거절하는 것은 저장소 락뿐이다. `.moai/lock` 과 링크 너머 `issues.jsonl` 곁의 락(`Repo::far_lock`)이 그것이다. 앞 노트의 "모든 락" 은 틀린 전제 위에 섰다. `user_config::a_linked_lock_file_is_locked_once`(moai-2l74)가 stow·rcm 이 건 `config.toml.lock` 을 일부러 살려 둔다. 사용자 설정·읽음 표시의 락은 사용자 자신의 파일이고, `.git/moai-held.lock` 은 git 이 커밋하지 않는 자리라 지금대로 둔다.

text:
Review text — /code-review max --fix, 217f65a04e322e18be51d7ea6cfc7a2d1cff2866..HEAD (agent a787c90b6e0584cfe)

I found 15 problems, fixed all of them in the working tree, and committed nothing. The worst: three cases still lost writes silently, and I reproduced each one with the built binary. Two came in with this change; the snapshot-onto-lock case already existed before it.

**Verification:**
- Unit tests: 1635 passed.
- CLI tests: 639 passed; the only 3 failures are the known `target/`-symlink ones.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` are clean.
- Reverting each fix separately turns the extended store test red at the case meant to catch it. Before this pass, reverting only the far lock left every test green.

**Findings:** none.

**Checks against the three criteria:**
1. **The tests still go red when the product records the wrong path.** The product records `std::env::current_exe()`: in `src/cmd/skill.rs:36` for the hooks, and in `src/cmd/merge_driver.rs:1581` as the `--install` default. On Linux that value is fully resolved.
   - If the product recorded the unresolved spelling instead (argv[0] or the `CARGO_BIN_EXE_moai` spelling), the new comparison fails on this machine. In `skill_status_notices_a_vanished_hook_binary`, `.replace(recorded_bin(), …)` would replace nothing and the `/nowhere/moai` assertion would fail.
   - The planted wrapper script in `install_prefers_a_moai_on_path_when_it_is_the_same_build` is at `root/bin/moai`, which does not contain the resolved path, so a product that wrongly picked the wrapper still fails.
   - On a machine where `target/` is not a link (CI), the two spellings are identical, so a regression to the unresolved spelling can't be caught there. The test can't avoid that, and it was true before this change too.
2. **One helper, not three copies.** `recorded_bin()` is one function backed by a `OnceLock`, and the four call sites (in three tests) all use it. Calling the binary and passing `--as` still use `BIN`, which is correct.
3. **The comment says what the product records and why.** It names `current_exe` and `/proc/self/exe`, says the test is the side to change and why (`argv[0]` can't be trusted), and explains why it resolves only on Linux. That macOS claim is right: std's `current_exe` there returns the `_NSGetExecutablePath` spelling unresolved.

**Remaining uses of `BIN`:** none of them compare against a path the product recorded on its own.
- `--as BIN` passes the path in explicitly.
- The other uses run the binary or put its path inside test scripts.
- The `--as {BIN}` hint check around line 19624 echoes a driver line the test wrote itself.

I found 12 issues in the board epic. I fixed six of them and skipped six. The fixes were left in the working tree uncommitted. The full `cargo test` run passes (1659 + 642), clippy and `cargo fmt --check` are clean, and two new regression tests fail on the old code.

1. src/tui/mod.rs:2247 — land() moves into the written row's home folder even on the board, which already shows every card under the current folder as a card. Root board in a repo with milestones, park an idea with SPC n: land() sets the path to [Milestone(None)] and the board collapses from every milestone lane to the single (no milestone) lane. flip_layout avoids land for this exact reason, but the write path still calls it.
2. src/tui/board.rs:233 — window() always pins the cursor's column to the right edge instead of keeping the previous window, so the visible columns shift even when the target column is already on screen. Narrow board with columns 3 and 4 shown and the cursor on 4: rolling the wheel over column 3 crosses to it, the window slides to {2,3}, and the pointer is now over column 2; each further notch crosses one more column left until column 0. Pressing h also scrolls the board for a column that was already visible.
3. src/tui/mod.rs:5213 — On the board, leave() prefers 'first card under the folder' over the remembered cursor, so Enter followed by Bksp back to the root loses the card the user started from. Root board, Enter on issue X (which has children) under milestone M and epic E jumps three levels at once; three Bksp presses return to the root but land on the first card under M, not on X.
4. src/tui/draw.rs:2245 — card_foot re-implemented row_line's right-column cell text (assignee label, +MM-DD and ✎MM-DD dates, epic name) as a second copy of the same match. Changing the date or assignee format in one copy silently makes the board foot and the list column disagree.
5. src/tui/draw.rs:2803 — FOOT was a hand-indexed copy of RIGHT ([RIGHT[0].0 … RIGHT[4].0]) typed [Field; 5]. Adding a sixth right column still compiles, but the card foot and card_height silently leave it out.
6. src/tui/board.rs:204 — roll() duplicated step()'s in-column walk (find position in the column, saturating add, clamp to the end). Two copies of the clamp-at-end rule: changing one makes the wheel and j/k stop at different places.
7. src/tui/mod.rs:4186 — column_of() puts every idea in the Idea column regardless of status, so closed or promoted ideas mix with open ones. Show done with SPC v 3: every promoted (done) idea floods the Idea column next to live ideas, told apart only by the glyph.
8. src/tui/mod.rs:4215 — headed is true for any lane that is not None, including the (lost) lane in a repo without milestones. This contradicts the comment that lane headers stand only for milestone lanes, and Site::lane's 'one lane' doc. A repo with no milestones but some lost rows gets lanes [None, Lost]; the first lane's header draws as a bare '── ─────' rule with no name.
9. src/tui/mod.rs:4155 — cards_in walks the fully opened tree (sorting each folder), then sorts every card again, on every rows() call. rows() runs several times per key and on every spinner frame. At the root, the board builds the whole repo every time. The rows() doc measures that at ~9ms for ~1,700 rows and says this repo never draws that many at once; on the board that is now the default case.
10. src/tui/draw.rs:2168 — Cards that can be entered (issues with children) carry no folder marker; the list appends '/' for exactly this reason. With counts hidden (SPC c n), or when the children are all ideas, nothing on the card says Enter will open it.
11. src/tui/mod.rs:2214 — When the held card disappears (reload, search cleared), regrip and after_search fall back to the same flat row index, but board rows are ordered by lane and then priority. The card under the cursor moves to done and is hidden on reload; the cursor jumps to whatever card is next in the flat order, often in another column or lane.
12. src/tui/draw.rs:2045 — The board's scroll mark counts canvas lines, not cards, while the list's mark counts rows. '↓ 12' on the board means 12 terminal lines (4 three-line cards), which reads as 12 cards.

text:
## Review of `worktree-moai-oagj` (max effort, `--fix`)

I found 15 problems and fixed 14 of them in the working tree; nothing is committed. 11 of the 14 code findings were confirmed by a test that fails on the branch as written. After the fixes, the full suite passes (1676 unit tests, 9 of them new regression tests, plus 642 integration tests), and `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` are both clean.

1. src/tui/board.rs:279 — `roll` treats a cursor on a project header as being in another column and snaps it back to that project's nearest card, whichever way the wheel turns. Overview board, projects A and B open, cursor on B's first card in column c. Wheel up moves onto B's header; the next wheel-up moves back down to B's card, so the wheel can never reach A. Wheel down onto a header whose project has no card in c stays there for good. Test: roll(B header, up) returned 3 instead of 1; roll(C header, down) returned 4 instead of 6.
2. src/tui/draw.rs:2005 — `board()` returns early when the board has no columns, which also skips drawing the project headers. Config has hide_ideas = true, hide_deferred = true and layout = board. Run `moai tui` outside any project: nothing is unfolded yet, so there are no columns and the frame is empty — no headers, nothing to click, no title. Test: `one/` and `two/` were missing from the rendered screen.
3. src/tui/board.rs:257 — Half-page and page moves from a header jump along one column's path, skipping any project that has no card in that column. On a header, Ctrl-d jumps to the next project's header and skips every card of the project just unfolded. Test: Ctrl-d from header A landed on header B (7) instead of A's 5th card.
4. src/tui/mod.rs:4933 — `board_column` (the column `j` returns to from a header) stores a position in the column list, starts at 0 (the idea column), and only key moves update it. `k` from an in_progress card to the header, then `SPC v i`, then `j`: the list shifted, so the cursor lands on the todo card. On first use, `j` jumps down to an idea card in the last lane. Mouse moves, climbing back to the overview and layout flips leave it stale. Test: got `one 의 첫 줄` instead of `one 의 둘째 줄`.
5. src/tui/mod.rs:4351 — Switching list→board with `unwrap_or(0)` as the fallback lands on project 0's header in the overview. Overview list, cursor on an empty epic in project 2, `SPC v b`: the cursor jumps to the first project's header and you lose your place. Test: landed on Project(0) instead of Project(1).
6. src/tui/keys.rs:794 — In the overview, the view toggles turn themselves off once no card is left — exactly when un-hiding would be needed. The only unfolded project shows nothing but ideas; `SPC v i` hides them all, and then both `SPC v i` and `SPC v a` are disabled, so the overview can't undo it. Test: `SPC v i` could not bring the idea back.
7. src/tui/board.rs:280 — The per-project fence meant for h/l also restricts the wheel when the cursor is on a card. Overview board, cursor on project A's card, wheel over a column where only project B has cards: the cursor never moves. Test: roll returned 1 instead of 3.
8. src/tui/layer.rs:3046 — New test code is not rustfmt-formatted, so the CI fmt check fails. `cargo fmt --all --check` exits 1 at 7 places (board.rs:388, draw.rs:4511 and 4622, layer.rs:3043/3069/3084/3092), so the required ci-gate job goes red.
9. CHANGELOG.md:27 — [Unreleased] still says the overview stays a list and says nothing about `SPC v i`, `[tui] hide_ideas` or the not-yours card foot. Release notes are generated from this section, so they would contradict `moai tui --help` and the README.
10. src/tui/draw.rs:2281 — The `→ name` / `unowned` marker sits after Tags and Epic in the card foot, and the foot is cut to card width. With `SPC c e` on, a narrow card with a long epic name shows only the epic; the marker is cut off.
11. src/cli.rs:539 — The help text (and docs/cli.md:2097, and the `run()` doc comment) says `k` from the top card of a lane goes up to the header; that is only true for a project's first lane. Project with two milestone lanes, cursor on the top card of the second lane: `k` goes to the card above in the first lane, not to the header.
12. src/tui/mod.rs:4273 — `App::laid` clones a milestone id for every card just to build a lookup key, scans every lane per card, and repeats the find-or-push block twice. Runs every frame and every key; on a multi-project overview that is thousands of needless allocations and card × lane comparisons per build.
13. src/tui/mod.rs:4239 — `Site::whose` runs for every card on every layout build, even when a turned-on column already forces the third line. Each call allocates a fresh `Me` and re-parses `name (email)`, on every card, every frame and every key.
14. src/tui/board.rs:174 — `nearest` builds and sorts the whole column path (now including headers) only to strip the headers again; `off_banner` writes every step twice, once per direction, using a `usize::MAX - top` trick. Every h/l and wheel crossing allocates and sorts; the mirrored logic invites the two directions drifting apart.
15. src/tui/mod.rs:84 — A new doc comment uses `층` for the layer, which docs/korean-terms.md forbids in newly written doc comments. Offending line: '층 줄의 첨자다' — it is actually a `layer.places` index.

### What I fixed
- Wheel: a cursor on a header now walks the column path in the direction rolled. From a card it prefers the same project but falls back to any project's nearest card. h/l keep the per-project fence.
- Multi-step moves: half/page moves now repeat the single `j`/`k` step through a new `Plan::walk`.
- Return-to-column hint: stored as the column itself (`Option<board::Column>`), resolved to a position each time, and recorded by both the key path and the drawing (`App::note_board_column`). With no hint, `j` goes to the nearest card.
- Empty overview: the board only returns early when it has no height, so headers always draw.
- Layout flip: the fallback is now the cursor's own project header.
- View toggles: keys that would un-hide something stay enabled with no rows (`Browse::unhides`).
- Cleanups: `laid` uses a clone-free lane lookup; `card_height` only asks whose a card is when no turned-on column already gives it a third line; `nearest` is a single pass, and `off_banner` is written once for both directions (same results as before).
- Docs and process: corrected help text in `src/cli.rs` and `docs/cli.md`, plus the matching doc comments; updated the CHANGELOG; fixed the `층` term; ran `cargo fmt`.

### What I skipped
- Clipped owner marker (draw.rs:2281): fixing it means moving the marker out of the assignee's position in the foot, which was a user decision. That needs a person's call.
- Smaller cleanups: reusing `view::owner_label` and `ready.unowned` would change the visible wording to `(unowned)`; merging `tui.act.ideas` into `tui.board.idea` would change the English menu label; a shared helper for the selected-row style, the dead `Go::Side(Up/Down)` arms (a pattern that predates this branch), duplicated fields between `Placed` and `Slot`, and the doubled lane-header check.
- Outside this diff: `relayer` (layer.rs:1531) uses a project index as a row index, so after `SPC p a` the cursor can land on the wrong row. It predates this branch, in a function the diff doesn't touch; worth filing as an idea. `App::unveiled` reads the placeholder site, but search is disabled in the overview, so it can't trigger.
- Commit history: README lines for the `SPC v i` and not-yours-card members went in under the overview-board member's commit subject. That can't be fixed without rewriting history.

text:
/code-review max --fix on worktree-moai-ggxi (agent abd6d7f24db14c686). Line numbers refer to reviewed HEAD 2a3c2be6.

1. src/tui/draw.rs:1531 — The new Stale version line (63–67 cells) is never fitted to the width left for the project numbers, so at 80 columns in the project layer every `<n> name` cell disappears from the header. Scenario: 80 columns, a registered project, latest = Stale{Offline, v0.3.0, 2 days}: told_w=74, so the cells start at x=77; `<0> all` needs 84 and is skipped (numbered=false), for the whole 24h window. Before the change the longest line was 46 cells. Breaks the invariant pinned by the_journal_row_leaves_room_for_the_project_numbers and the_logo_yields_before_the_project_numbers_vanish; the new 80-column test renders without a layer.
2. src/latest.rs:550 — Held::answer builds Seen::Stale from the stored tag without the semver gate seen() applies, so a tag reported as 'odd tag' is later drawn as a release 'seen N days ago'. Day 1 tag_name "v0.1" reads 'latest not checked (odd tag)'; day 2 offline: '… v0.1 seen 1 day ago'.
3. src/latest.rs:597 — read() maps a `trouble` value that is present but unknown (or not a string) to None. Since `trouble` next to a tag now means 'stale', a reason kind written by a newer binary turns the stale tag back into a fresh answer.
4. src/latest.rs:549 — Released 0.1.2–0.3.0 binaries delete `trouble` whenever they write a line with a tag, including after their own failed ask. On a mixed-version machine a failed ask's old tag is still drawn as fresh. Pre-existing; the file is identical to an old binary's successful same-tag ask.
5. src/latest.rs:559 — Held::heard trusts any heard_at, but older binaries rewrite tag and asked_at while leaving heard_at behind. A newly heard tag is dated with an earlier tag's stamp (D1 hears v0.3.0, D5 old binary hears v0.4.0, D6 offline: 'v0.4.0 seen 5 days ago'), and the Err arm writes it back.
6. src/latest.rs:861 — The Err arm carries the line read before an ask that can block up to 5 s, so a failing process can overwrite a sibling's just-heard line. write()'s doc ('둘 다 같은 것을 적으므로 진 쪽도 잃는 것이 없다') is no longer true.
7. src/latest.rs:548 — v0.1.1 writes only asked_at and tag and keeps every other key, so its successful ask over this binary's failure line leaves `trouble` beside a freshly heard tag, drawn as Stale ('v0.4.0 seen today').
8. src/tui/draw.rs:1525 — days_since clamps a far-future heard_at to 0, so the line says 'seen today', and every failed ask carries that stamp forward. Held::fresh already distrusts such stamps.
9. src/latest.rs:1373 — No test tells carrying heard_at apart from carrying the previous asked_at across two failed days, and the Stale `said` re-attach arm is untested.
10. src/tui/draw.rs:1246 — The banner puts the upgrade notice last because 'the version line still says a new release is out' when clipped; for a Stale-but-newer answer the version line says 'latest not checked … vX seen N days ago' instead. README.md:85 makes the same claim.
11. src/tui/draw.rs:6721 — The 80-column test pins the tag to v0.3.0 with a 1-cell margin and hand-lists 7 of 9 Trouble kinds with no exhaustive guard.
12. src/tui/draw.rs:6585 — The new comment says App::new reads the user's language, but test Apps are pinned to Lang::Ko (moai-9it4). Pinning En removed the Korean coverage of 'the four answers are different text'.
13. src/latest.rs:33 — Several doc comments contradict the new model: the module doc, the_reason_stands_for_the_whole_window, pointers to a Seen::Newer promise that moved, '두 키', and a false history in a new test doc.
14. src/latest.rs:181 — Doc comments added by the diff break docs/korean-terms.md: 그물 for network (lines 181, 184, 198, 487, 837, 842, 1363), 판 in the 회차 sense, and the '못 물었다' gloss in place of variant names.
15. src/latest.rs:203 — Seen::newer re-implements seen()'s 'tag is newer than mine' step for Stale, so the version line's classification and the banner's live in two places. Nothing diverges today.

Fixed by the reviewer: 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 (partly), 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14.
- Held::answer: Stale only for a tag that parses as a version and has heard_at next to it; odd tag gives Unasked(reason); a reason without heard_at (v0.1.1 case) reads as a heard line.
- read(): a present but unknown/non-string `trouble` reads as NotAsked.
- Held::heard(): trusts heard_at only when trouble is set; otherwise asked_at.
- refresh(): after a failed ask it reads the file once more and follows a fresh line a sibling wrote meanwhile; write() doc corrected.
- version_said: heard_at more than FUTURE_SLACK_SECS ahead shows as "seen earlier"; FUTURE_SLACK_SECS doc lists its third user.
- Tests: 7 new in latest.rs plus draw.rs cases; 80-column loop uses v{mine} with an exhaustive Trouble guard; four-answers test checks En and Ko. Each fix reverted in turn: 7 of 7 new tests went red.
- Docs corrected, korean-terms violations in added lines fixed. fmt, clippy -D warnings clean; 1646 unit + 642 integration pass.

Left by the reviewer:
- 1: needs a decision — two-row version line (touches header()) or accept losing the labels.
- 4: no reader rule can tell the files apart; re-ask once when no trouble and heard_at != asked_at would relax "ask once a day" — design decision; documented on Held::trouble.
- 7 remaining part: v0.1.1 success over a failure line that already had a tag still reads as Stale; needs a new key; documented.
- 10: banner() and README outside the change's functions.
- 15: not worth churning.
- Cleanup not listed: hand-written `said` re-attach match in refresh; test scaffolding duplication.
- Commit 47c2893a puts two issues in one commit and uses 그물 in its message; needs a history rewrite, untouched.

Decision on the findings (worker window):
- Took in the reviewer's fixes for 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 (partly), 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14 as one fix: commit after checking them and re-running the suite.
- 1: asked the person, who chose the two-row fold. When the joined line would push out the project numbers, header() moves the last answer and age to the row under the version line; wide windows keep one row. The supervisor confirmed header() and told_of were free after moai-9nfw merged. Test: a_stale_version_line_folds_before_it_pushes_out_the_project_numbers.
- 10: fixed the banner comment. Left README.md:85 as it is: moai-oagj holds that file, and the sentence still holds because the header names the newer release.
- 4 and the remaining part of 7: handed on as idea moai-jh44, outside v0.4.0. They only happen on machines running mixed versions, and they break nothing already merged.
- 15: not taken. Nothing diverges today, and a shared helper would only move the same comparison.

## What I fixed
- **Stuck scroll on a header** (`board.rs`, `pull`): when the cursor is on a header and has not stood in any column yet, it is now pulled to the nearest visible row in any column, matching what `step`'s `j` does in that state. When two rows are equally close, the choice is now fixed by `(distance, top, column)` rather than by row order. I added two regression tests:
  - `a_header_with_no_column_yet_pulls_onto_the_nearest_row_on_screen` in `board.rs`
  - `the_overview_board_scrolls_right_after_unfolding_from_a_header` in `layer.rs`, which reproduces the real `l` then `Ctrl-d` flow
- **`Plan::next`**: put the `saturating_sub` / `get().copied().unwrap_or(cursor)` guard back.
- **`board_roll`**: returns early when the offset did not change, and only then builds the layout.
- **Shared setup**: moved into a new `App::board_hint(rows) -> (Laid, Option<usize>)`, now used by both `board_step` and `board_roll`.
- **`mouse.rs` tests**: one `id_at` helper now backs both `on_card` and `card_at`.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: rewrote the board's Added entry to describe scrolling. Your handover note planned this for after the review, so it is already done and only needs committing.

## Skipped
- **Unreachable arm in `board::step`**: harmless, and it documents what those moves do on the board.
- **Lane-header rule**: deliberate. `a_lane_first_card_counts_as_seen_only_with_its_lane_header` exists so the draw does not scroll back afterwards.
- **Stop rule**: this is the user's decision ("멈춤"). I'm listing it only so you know a short column blocks skimming a long one; whether to raise it again is yours.
- **Docs wording**: "pulled to the nearest card on screen in its column" leaves out that in the overview the cursor can land on a project header. It's minor, and changing it means editing `src/cli.rs` and `docs/cli.md` together, so I left both as they are.

I found 7 problems and fixed 4 of them in the working tree. I skipped 3 because each needs a decision from you or reaches well past this diff. The fixes are uncommitted. `cargo test` (dev profile: 1700 + 642 passed), `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass. I checked both new tests against the code before my fix and both fail there.

1. src/tui/mod.rs:2304 — When a card vanishes, the fallback for its lost position reuses the card's old row on the whole board, so when a lane above gets shorter the 'same height' points into a lower lane and the cursor jumps to another milestone.
   Failure: Milestone A holds 3 review cards and 1 todo card, milestone B holds one review card (the cursor, argos-0007) and one todo card (argos-0008), and the no-milestone lane holds one todo card (argos-0009). After `SPC v 3` hides review, the todo column is searched at the old row 8: lane A shrank, so that row now belongs to the no-milestone lane and the cursor lands on argos-0009 instead of argos-0008. Reproduced by the new test a_vanished_card_keeps_its_lane_when_the_lanes_above_shrink.
2. src/tui/mod.rs:2304 — In the overview (`0`), when a view toggle hides every card of the cursor's project, the cursor keeps only its old row number, which now belongs to the next project.
   Failure: Overview board where project `solo` has a single idea and project `other` follows. With the cursor on solo's idea, `SPC v i` leaves the rows [Project(0), Project(1)]; row 1 is now other's header, so the cursor leaves the project it was in. Reproduced by the new test hiding_every_card_of_a_project_on_the_overview_keeps_to_its_header (it landed on Project(1)).
3. src/tui/mod.rs:5284 — The fix only covers reload (`take`), view toggles (`look`), time zone change (`set_zone`) and clearing a search (`after_search`). Applying a filter, typing a search, cancelling a search, rebuilding the overview and reloading a project in the overview still put the cursor back by row number on the board.
   Failure: On the board with the cursor on an in_progress card, `f` then `status=todo` then Enter goes through `settle(held, self.cursor)`, which keeps the row number and ignores even a held card that is still visible. Because board rows are ordered lane first, then priority, the cursor lands in an unrelated column or lane, which is the bug moai-r1ly.dwb set out to fix. The same row-number fallback is in `live`, `Prompt::Cancel` (5172), `relayer` (layer.rs:1531) and `follow_site`, which re-reads a project in the overview and never re-places the cursor at all.
4. src/tui/mod.rs:2948 — The view filter still treats a closed idea as an idea (`report::is_idea`) while the board now puts it in done, so the `hide ideas` toggle (`SPC v i`) also empties closed ideas out of the done column.
   Failure: Done is shown and `SPC v i` is on: the idea column is hidden as intended, but promoted (done) ideas also disappear from the done column and its count drops. The board says a closed idea is not an idea, while the filter for that same toggle still counts it as one. CHANGELOG and help (src/cli.rs:517) say `SPC v i` hides 'the idea column on the board'.
5. src/tui/mod.rs:4336 — The test 'is this idea still open' was written out by hand as `is_idea(i) && !i.status.is_done()`; the same expression was already written out by hand at report.rs:5529, and report::is_idea's own doc warns against each screen re-deriving such a check.
   Failure: Two copies of one check: if the meaning of 'open' changes, the board's idea column and the idea-pile notice drift apart.
6. src/tui/mod.rs:2310 — `stand_near` built the identity of every row and searched for each old neighbour even when the card's column no longer exists, which is a case where none of them can be used.
   Failure: Wasted work: one identity per row (a string or path copy each) plus a linear search per neighbour, all thrown away because the column-exists check sat inside the predicate.
7. src/tui/mod.rs:2264 — `grip_of` lays out the whole board and records an identity for every card in the column on every reload and every view toggle (including `SPC s` sort, which can never hide a card), even though the result is thrown away whenever the cursor's card survives, which is the usual case.
   Failure: Every reload (each write from another session) and every toggle costs one extra board layout plus up to one string copy per card in the column. The work is linear in the board, but it is spent on every reload and toggle when it is only needed if the card disappears.

Fixed
1. Lane jump: `CardAt` now records the card's lane and its height within that lane. `stand_near` measures "nearest height" inside the same lane in the new layout, capped to the lane's height. It falls back to the old position on the whole board only when that lane is gone.
2. Overview fallback: when no card of the project is left, `stand_near` falls back to that project's header. This follows the same choice `flip_layout` already makes.
3. Shared check: added `report::is_open_idea`; the board and the idea-pile count at report.rs:5535 both use it now.
4. Wasted work in `stand_near`: the neighbour lookup only runs when the card's column still exists.

New tests are `a_vanished_card_keeps_its_lane_when_the_lanes_above_shrink` (src/tui/mod.rs) and `hiding_every_card_of_a_project_on_the_overview_keeps_to_its_header` (src/tui/layer.rs).

Skipped
- Finding 3 (other ways the cursor still jumps): fixing it changes how filtering and searching place the cursor, which is outside this diff. It looks like part of what moai-r1ly.dwb promised, so it should go on the tracker as a member of epic `moai-r1ly` (`-e moai-r1ly`) rather than as an idea.
- Finding 4 (`SPC v i` hiding closed ideas in done): whether that toggle should still hide closed ideas is a design question. The user's ruling for moai-r1ly.91p only covered which column a closed idea stands in, so it needs your call. It should also be written down on the tracker.
- Finding 7 (extra layout on every reload): the work has to happen before the issues are swapped out, so avoiding it would need `laid` restructured to work on a set of issues passed in. The cost is low; not worth it here.
