/code-review xhigh --fix 293bfea2..HEAD (agent a917dba973ca8e81f, 205621 tokens)

The commit `293bfea2..HEAD` (moai-r1ly.f2x) has one real bug next to the paths it fixed: pressing Esc to clear an `f` filter on the board still moves the cursor to whatever card is now at the old row number. I fixed it, added a test that failed before the fix (cursor landed on `argos-0007` instead of `argos-0006`), and made three small cleanups. The whole `tui::` test suite passes (648), and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --tests` are clean. The changes are in `src/tui/mod.rs` and are not committed; the repo convention puts review fixes in a separate `fix:` commit.

1. src/tui/mod.rs:4911 — Esc clearing an `f` filter (`B::ClearFilter`) only re-places the cursor when a search was active, so on the board it keeps the old row number, and nothing rewinds the detail pane when the card under the cursor changes. The new `regain` doc says the filter paths are covered, but this one was missed.
   Failure: Board view, apply `status=todo`, cursor on argos-0006, press Esc. The filtered-out cards come back above it and the cursor ends up on argos-0007, a different card the person never picked (confirmed by the new test `clearing_a_filter_on_the_board_keeps_to_the_card`).
2. src/tui/mod.rs:5236 — While typing a search on the board, `live` re-measures the card under the cursor on every keystroke. Once a typo filters out the card the person opened the search box on, fixing the typo brings that card back but the cursor stays on the neighbour it moved to.
   Failure: Cursor on X, type `fo`, typo `foz` (X drops out, cursor moves to neighbour Y), backspace to `fo` (X is back), press Enter: cursor lands on Y, a card the person never chose. Esc would have gone back to X. Where you end up depends on typing history, not on the final query.
3. src/tui/mod.rs:4126 — `follow_site` saved the cursor position and re-placed it on every finished project read, even when the person is inside a project, where reading another project's rows cannot change the list.
   Failure: Inside a large project in board view, every commit from another session triggers re-reads of the expanded projects. Each finished read counted the inside list twice and built the board layout again for nothing.
4. src/tui/mod.rs:4149 — `follow_site` copied the body of `regrip` line for line (rows, `regain`, `stand`) without calling it.
   Failure: Two copies of the cursor-restore code. A later fix to `regrip` would miss the overview re-read path.
5. src/tui/mod.rs:4891 — `B::Grep` called `self.rows()` again even though the key handler already had `rows` for the same state.
   Failure: Every `/` press counted the whole list one extra time (and laid out the board from it).
6. src/tui/layer.rs:1537 — When the project under the cursor is dropped, the fallback card position remembers the project by its index in the list (`Seat::Place(n)`). After the change, that index can name a project other than the one that moved up into the slot.
   Failure: One config write removes project B and adds project D that sorts into B's slot, or the launched project is re-spelled when it gets registered. The cursor jumps to a card in a project the person was not looking at. This is no worse than the old fallback by row number.
7. src/tui/layer.rs:1398 — `relayer_with` saves the cursor position (including the board layout) before the branches that return early with `Nothing`/`Lost`, where it is never used.
   Failure: Board view, config re-read fails or there is no repo: the board layout is built and thrown away on every settings-file change. Small cost, not on a hot path.
8. src/tui/mod.rs:2365 — Root-cause depth: each place that changes the rows has to save the cursor position before and call `regain`/`stand` after, by hand. `B::ClearFilter` was missed for exactly that reason.
   Failure: Any new path that changes rows (a new toggle or reload) silently falls back to the row number on the board. A single shared wrapper (save position, change rows, restore) would make it hard to forget.

Fixed:
- Finding 1: `B::ClearFilter` now saves the position with `grip_of(&rows)`. If `after_search` doesn't place the cursor, it calls `settle(grip, self.cursor)`, the same as Enter does. Added the test `clearing_a_filter_on_the_board_keeps_to_the_card` and updated the `regain` doc's list of paths.
- Finding 3: `follow_site` now saves the position only when `self.on_layer()` is true.
- Finding 4: `follow_site` now calls `self.regrip(held, stood)` instead of copying its body.
- Finding 5: `B::Grep` now reuses the `rows` it already has.

Skipped:
- Finding 2: changing it would change how board search behaves while typing (going back to the original card when it reappears). That's your call; I'd log it as an idea.
- Finding 6: about as good as the old row-number fallback, and the commit's comment says it is intended.
- Finding 7: small and only runs on config changes; fixing it means restructuring `relayer_with`.
- Finding 8: a refactor well outside this diff.

/code-review xhigh --fix 69efff6e..HEAD (agent a6871b76abc7b8fc0, 288361 tokens)

I found 12 issues in `69efff6e..HEAD`. Three of them are real bugs: after scrolling the board, leaving a folder, running a search or filter, or pressing `h`/`l` on a project header can leave the cursor off screen. I fixed those, added three tests that failed before the fix and pass after it, and fixed four out-of-date comments. Five lower findings are not fixed. All 1713 unit tests and clippy pass, `cargo fmt --check` is clean, nothing is committed, and the worktree's `.moai` is untouched.

1. src/tui/mod.rs:5140 — Leaving a folder (Bksp) after scrolling can land the cursor back on the scrolled-away card. The flag that stops the draw from bringing the cursor back stays set, while the scroll offset still belongs to the folder's board.
   Failure: In an epic's board, stand on its first card and press PageDown twice (offset 20), then Bksp. The root board puts the cursor on that same card, which is now at line 60. The flag still matches the card, so nothing scrolls to it: the cursor sits off screen even though the person never scrolled this board. The new test `leaving_a_rolled_folder_board_shows_the_card_it_lands_on` failed with offset 20.
2. src/tui/mod.rs:5140 — A search or filter rebuilds the board, but if the card the search was opened on still matches, the flag survives and the cursor's card stays hidden behind the old scroll offset.
   Failure: On a 30-card board, cursor on card 0001, press PageDown twice, then search for `argos` and Enter. The cursor stays on 0001 and the board keeps offset 20, so the chosen card is off screen. `a_search_on_a_rolled_board_shows_the_card` failed with offset 20.
3. src/tui/mod.rs:4862 — In the overview board, `h`, `l` and `Tab` on a project header go to `unfold`/`fold`, not `board_step`, so they never clear the flag. These are the header's cursor keys, but they act off screen.
   Failure: On an unfolded header, press Ctrl-d (offset 5), then `l`. Nothing visible changes, so the key looks dead; folding or unfolding a hidden header is equally invisible. The extended `the_overview_board_scrolls_right_after_unfolding_from_a_header` failed with 5 instead of 0.
4. src/tui/mod.rs:1284 — The `adrift` field doc says two places clear it, then names three (`board_step`, `rolled_off`, `flip_layout`).
   Failure: The doc says something the code does not do; a later reader trusts the count and misses a place that clears it.
5. src/tui/mod.rs:4470 — The `flip_layout` doc says, as if it were what happens, that the draw won't show the card on the rewound board. That is only what would happen if the flag were *not* cleared.
   Failure: It reads as the opposite of the code: the code clears the flag precisely so the draw does show the card.
6. src/tui/mod.rs:5117 — The `board_roll` comment says that when the board did not move, the visible cursor stays visible. That is false when an earlier scroll already pushed the cursor off screen; the flag is simply kept.
   Failure: Wheeling at the end of the board with the cursor already off screen: the comment promises a visible cursor that is not there.
7. src/tui/draw.rs:2062 — The comment justifies measuring visibility by the card alone with 'don't undo a one-line scroll that hid the header'. Scrolls are now protected by the flag; the rule only matters for cursor keys.
   Failure: The stated reason no longer matches the path where the rule actually applies.
8. src/tui/mod.rs:3856 — View toggles (`SPC v`), sort (`SPC s`) and card-field toggles (`SPC c`) relay the board but keep the flag, so the cursor's card can be pushed off screen and stay there.
   Failure: Scroll, then `SPC v d` to show done cards: lanes grow, the card moves below the screen, and the draw does not bring it back.
9. src/tui/mod.rs:5118 — A small scroll that leaves the card fully visible still sets the flag. A later reload, terminal resize or detail toggle that pushes the card off screen will not bring it back; clicking that same visible card does not clear it either.
   Failure: Wheel 3 lines (card still visible), open the detail pane so the board shrinks: the card is hidden and is not scrolled back into view.
10. src/tui/mod.rs:4894 — Switching projects with the number keys keeps the flag if the new project's landing card has the same id as the scrolled-away card. Both are matched by id alone and both roots have an empty path.
   Failure: Two registered projects share the `argos` prefix. Scroll in one with the cursor on argos-0001, press `2`, and land on the other project's argos-0001: its cursor is not brought into view.
11. src/tui/mouse.rs:248 — Every wheel event rebuilds the full row list even when the board cannot move (at its end, or it fits on screen), although only the cursor row is needed, and only when the offset changes.
   Failure: A trackpad burst at the end of a large overview board rebuilds the tree on every event in the burst.
12. src/tui/mouse.rs:467 — The wheel test's 'the draw undid a visible cursor' check can no longer fail for that reason: the scroll already set the flag, so the draw never scrolls anyway. The card-only visibility rule is now covered only by `draw::tests::a_visible_card_keeps_the_board_scrolled_past_its_lane_header`.
   Failure: Reverting the card-only visibility rule leaves this assertion green.

Fixed:
- Findings 1 and 2: `adrift` is now a small struct (`Adrift`) holding the cursor's card plus the folder path and the active filter or search at the moment of scrolling. `rolled_off` clears it when the card differs or when the folder or the filter or search has changed. Covers entering and leaving folders, search typing, Enter, clearing a filter, and the folder-popping in `after_search`, all checked in one place. A reload keeps the scrolled board, as decided, because a reload changes neither the folder nor the filter.
- Finding 3: `unfold` and `fold` now clear the flag, the same way `board_step` does for card keys.
- Findings 4–7: comments rewritten to match the code. The field doc now names all four places that clear the flag.
- New tests (each failed before the fix): `leaving_a_rolled_folder_board_shows_the_card_it_lands_on` and `a_search_on_a_rolled_board_shows_the_card` in `src/tui/mod.rs`; an extension of `the_overview_board_scrolls_right_after_unfolding_from_a_header` in `src/tui/layer.rs`.

Not fixed:
- Findings 8 and 9: "keep the scrolled board" is consistent with the reload rule, and pulling the view back on a column toggle could be just as surprising. This needs a decision from you.
- Finding 10: a rare edge. The fix would mean adding a project identity to `Adrift`.
- Finding 11: the cost was already there before this change, which in fact made each wheel event cheaper.
- Finding 12: coverage exists in the draw test.

I didn't change `CHANGELOG.md` or the `cli.rs` help: the rule they describe ("the next cursor key brings the board back") is still true.

## Code review of moai-vtfu (1ce056b5..HEAD, src/tui and .moai skipped), max effort, with fixes applied

The epic's main paths hold up. `uninstall` behaves as it did before it moved onto `retire()`. The lexer still numbers heredocs the same way and `relex` is unchanged. `counted()` is the old logic minus `_workspace`. No planted text (AGENTS block, SKILL.md, references, supervisor skill, worker brief) still mentions the removed section. The real problems are in how install now removes plugins on every run, plus test gaps and stale docs.

After the fixes, `cargo test` passes (1703 unit and 643 cli tests, 3 of them new), and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. Each new test was checked by reverting the behaviour it guards; all 8 reverts turned a test red. I committed nothing and wrote nothing to the tracker.

### What I fixed (working tree only, not committed)
- **`retire()`:** it now takes the moai scopes from its caller, so `uninstall` uses the same snapshot for its plan and for retire. Each step stores its own result (`Retire.ok`), replacing the parallel `Vec<bool>` matched by index. `kept_lines()` replaces three copies of the same expression. The JSON output is unchanged.
- **Docs made to match the code:** the install comment, the retire() doc, both helps plus `docs/cli.md`, the CHANGELOG (section placement and `kept` wording) and the `skill.retired` message in en/ko, which no longer claims an earlier moai installed the plugin.
- **Hook lexer:** `Lexer::docs` is now a counter and only unquoted heredoc bodies are collected. `Aim::Here` is folded into `Read`. The stale comments are fixed.
- **Tests added:**
  - `skill_install_measures_the_scopes_before_registering` (uses a fake that writes the ledger when moai registers)
  - `skill_retires_nothing_while_the_name_points_elsewhere`
  - `skill_uninstall_keeps_the_korean_plugins_while_moai_stays`
  - a `--scope project` dry-run check and a real other-repository case in the install retire test
  - the one-language test now runs with an empty and a seeded ledger, plus a fake that renders the removed and failed lines in English.

### Not fixed — these need your decision
- **Removal on every install (item 1):** this is the big one. One option that needs no new state: retire at a scope only while the installed moai copy there (its installPath) still has `korean-skills:` in `skills/moai/SKILL.md`. Every tag from v0.1.0 to v0.3.0 and commit 29c8a02b has that text; HEAD does not, so removal would happen once per scope. The costs: you must choose what to do when the copy has vanished, and a removal that failed is no longer retried once registration succeeds.
- **Source check, project-scope declarations, gating on registration (items 2–4):** each changes the scope rule recorded in moai-vtfu.dvk, so I left them.
- **CLAUDE.md:309:** I did not edit CLAUDE.md; the parenthetical needs rewording by you.
- **Commit split (last item):** fixing it means rewriting history.
- **Also left:** `aim_flag` now has a single caller; `hangul()` is a test-only helper living in `src/hook.rs`; `ledger_with` never uses its user-scope arm; by-hand commands omit the working directory (an older pattern); `other_user_moai` counts this repo's own stale registrations as another repository's (an older behaviour that errs toward keeping).

Separately, your memory note about the supervisor brief refers to step 4-4, which this epic removes.

I found 6 problems in the brief and its test. I fixed three of them and left them uncommitted in the worktree for you to commit as a `fix:` commit. The full `cargo test` (dev) passes: 1708 and 646 tests, 0 failed. I ran `MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in` again, so `SKILL.md` and `plugin.json` were regenerated, not edited by hand.

1. src/guide.rs:2300 — Step 7 quotes the English refusal text word for word, but in Korean moai prints a different sentence. The test only checks English.
   Failure: With MOAI_LANG=ko or lang="ko" in the user config, a repository with no `review` column refuses with "`review` 라는 칸이 없다. 있는 칸: …". The brief tells the worker to look for "`review` is not a column", so the worker cannot match the refusal and stops or works around it. The same goes for mv.stale, which reads "… 는 이미 review 다 — 안 옮겼다" in Korean. es, ja and zh fall back to English, so only Korean is affected.
2. src/guide.rs:2298 — The brief says `--from in_progress` passes over first-column members, but not what moai prints when it does: "already stands todo — not moved" and a non-zero exit.
   Failure: Step 2 taught the worker that a non-zero code means someone else took the member, so tell the supervisor. Step 7 only describes two answers (no column, already in `review`). A worker who sends a 4-3 member through the command sees exit 1 and "already stands todo", reads it as a lost pick-up, and sends the supervisor a false report.
3. src/guide.rs:3201 — The test builds the refusal from the raw i18n key, not the way `mv` actually builds it (`require_known` → `view::no_such_column`).
   Failure: If the target-column check in `mv` switched to the `refuse.no_column_nor_rows` message or a different key, the brief's quote would no longer match what moai prints, and the test would still pass.
4. src/guide.rs:2298 — Step 7 says members left by 7-1 are passed over, but 7-1 runs after 7. On a first pass those members do not exist yet.
   Failure: A worker on its first pass looks for 7-1 members in step 7 and finds none. The sentence is only true after coming back from 8, which makes the order of steps confusing.
5. src/guide.rs:2297 — Members in other started columns (such as `blocked` in a custom setup) are also refused by `--from in_progress`, and the brief does not mention it.
   Failure: With statuses `todo, blocked, in_progress, review, done`, a member standing `blocked` gets "already stands blocked — not moved" and exit 1. None of the answers the brief describes covers it.
6. src/guide.rs:2411 — Step 10's wording ("…from `in_progress` where there is no `review` column alike") is awkward to read, though what it claims is correct.
   Failure: `moai mv <member> done` has no `--from`, so it closes from any column; the statement is true. It is only harder to read than it needs to be.

Fixed (in src/guide.rs, then the generated SKILL.md and plugin.json rebuilt):
- Finding 1: step 7 now says moai answers in the screen's language (`MOAI_LANG` or `lang` in the user config) and tells the worker to read what it means, not the exact words. A refusal of `review` that lists the columns without it means the step does not exist. The English text stays only as "in English …". The test now checks that this line is in the brief.
- Finding 2: step 7 now says that a first-column member gets "already stands in the first column, moves nothing, non-zero code", and that this is the pass-over, not a lost pick-up as in step 2.
- Finding 3: the test now builds the refusal through `Config::parse` (with no `review` column), then `require_known("review")`, then `view::no_such_column(Lang::En, …)`, which is the same path `mv` uses.
- Finding 4: the wording now reads "by 4-3 (and by 7-1 when you came back from 8)".

Skipped:
- Finding 5: this only happens with custom columns. Listing every other started column would make the brief longer, and an earlier user decision chose to rely on the refusal rather than check the columns first.
- Finding 6: the statement is correct, so I left the wording alone.

Checked, nothing wrong:
- Five checks: the new constants and test sit between the existing doc blocks without taking any of them over; removing the step-7 command or its `--from in_progress` makes the test fail; the command is defined once, in `TO_REVIEW`; the comments match what the code does; nothing that was closed before is opened (rule 5 passes because the members are the worker's own, and `review` stays in the hook's focus).
- Step 10's "closes from both columns" is true, because `mv done` has no `--from`. The CHANGELOG Changed line matches the code.
- One side effect, not a bug: members sitting in `review` now count toward `stale_review` instead of `stale_progress`, so a merge left stuck for days will warn about the review instead.

- 설정 자리: 저장소 `.moai/config.toml` 의 평평한 키 `archive_days`. 0 이면 아카이브를 끈다
- `show`: `--all` 은 done 을 열되 아카이브는 숨긴다. `--archived` 가 아카이브까지 연다(옛 `--all` 과 같은 줄). 꼬리에 아카이브 숨김 수와 `--archived`. `-g` 와 `--done <폭>` 은 아카이브를 연다(찾거나 때를 콕 집은 물음). `-s done` 은 `--all` 처럼 아카이브를 숨긴다
- 탐색기: `SPC v o`(old)가 켜고 끈다. `SPC v a`(모두 보이기)는 `--all` 처럼 아카이브를 안 연다. `/` 검색은 보기를 걷으므로 아카이브도 찾는다
- 재는 시계: done 칸에 든 때 — `show --done` 과 같은 시계(`query::Where::since`). 본문의 "`done_at` 없으면 아카이브" 대신이다. mv 로 닫은 줄은 `done_at` 과 같은 값이고, `done_at` 없는 옛 줄은 그 칸에 든 때로 잰다
- `moai status` 보드의 마일스톤·에픽 목록에서도 아카이브된 묶음을 빼고 한 줄로 수를 댄다. `--json` 도 같이 빠진다 — 이 에픽의 멤버로 세운다

text:
사람이 정한 것(2026-10-03, AskUserQuestion). 그 전에 잰 것:

- claude 2.1.287 의 `plugin marketplace remove <이름> --scope project` 는 그 범위 설정의 선언만 지운다 — 단 저장소 뿌리에서 보이는 다른 범위(user·local)에 같은 이름의 선언이 없으면 기계 전체 장부(known_marketplaces.json)에서도 지우고, 다른 저장소의 local 설치까지 걷는다(스크래치 HOME 두 저장소로 확인). 그래서 claude 에 맡기는 길은 흔한 판(project 에만 선언)에서 마켓플레이스를 두고 간다는 결정(moai-vtfu.dvk)을 깬다

text:
사람이 정한 것(2026-10-03, AskUserQuestion): **다른 범위도 함께 올린다.**

그 전에 잰 것(claude 2.1.287, 스크래치 HOME, 로컬 디렉터리 마켓플레이스):
- project·user 두 범위에 같은 플러그인을 깔고 판을 올린 뒤 `plugin update --scope user` 를 부르면 user 줄만 새 판(cache/2)이 되고 project 줄은 옛 판(cache/1)에 남는다 — p22t 의 전제가 맞다. `teaches_retired` 는 그 줄의 installPath 를 읽어 project 를 계속 옛 판으로 본다
- `plugin update <id> --scope project -y` 는 장부의 그 줄만 새 판으로 올리고 커밋된 `.claude/settings.json` 은 바이트째 그대로 둔다
- claude 의 install 은 로컬 디렉터리 플러그인을 "loads in place from <source>" 라 말한다. 세션이 실제로 어느 사본을 읽는지는 로그인 세션 없이 못 쟀다

정한 것:
- install 이 이 저장소의 moai 가 선 범위 중 이번 `--scope` 밖의 범위도 `claude plugin update moai@<m> --scope <S> -y` 로 올린다. 새 상태 없음 — 장부가 그 표식이다
- 걷기는 올라간 범위만 — 이번 `--scope` 는 등록이 됐을 때, 다른 범위는 그 update 가 됐을 때. 올리기가 실패한 범위는 안 걷는다(옛 판이 그대로라 다음 install 이 다시 잰다)
- 앞선 두 결정(moai 가 선 범위마다 · 범위당 한 번)을 둘 다 지킨다. 대가: --scope 밖 범위의 장부 줄을 고치고 claude 호출이 범위 수만큼 는다
- uninstall 은 그대로

## Review of `worktree-moai-47mz` (the archive epic) — max effort, with fixes applied

I found 15 problems; 11 are fixed in the working tree and 4 need a decision. Ten finder angles ran, then single-vote verifiers on the findings I hadn't already reproduced. I reproduced the rest myself with the debug binary, a fixed `MOAI_NOW` and scratch repos. Two of the fixes matter most: as committed, the branch fails CI's clippy gate, and it silently drops the `no_milestone` warning.

After the fixes: `cargo test` passes (1714 unit, 647 CLI) and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean. `cargo fmt --check` still flags `src/guide.rs:3210`. That comes from develop (moai-vxld.iqe), not this branch, so I left it alone.

1. src/report.rs:5361 — The no_milestone gate `if !stones.is_empty()` runs after `stones` has had archived milestones removed (line 5305), so a repo whose milestones are all archived stops getting the warning.
   Failure: Reproduced: milestone closed 29 days ago, open issue outside any milestone. `moai status --json` gives warnings [] (with archive_days=0 it gives [no_milestone 1]). A new milestone brings the warning back, and the Stop hook reads that as warnings having grown and holds the session. The TUI warning counts move the same way.
2. src/projects.rs:57 — `Config.archive_days: i64` makes `Repo` 8 bytes bigger, which pushes `projects::State::Open` over clippy's `large_enum_variant` limit; CI runs clippy with `-D warnings`.
   Failure: `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` fails with 'largest variant 232 bytes, second-largest 24'. The ci-gate job goes red and the branch cannot merge.
3. README.md:308 — The 'complete copy' recipe (also in src/cli.rs:1072 and five places in docs/cli.md) pulls ideas with `moai idea show --all --json`, which now leaves out closed ideas past archive_days.
   Failure: Reproduced: ideas closed 29 days ago are missing from `idea show --all --json` (only `--archived` returns them). The README then says 'An id missing from the new pull was removed', so a sync script deletes ideas that still exist.
4. src/tui/mod.rs:5448 — After a search is cleared, the notice for a row the view hides always names `SPC v a`, which never opens the archive.
   Failure: `/` finds an archived row, Enter, Esc. The notice says 'hidden by the view · SPC v a shows all'. Pressing SPC v a leaves the row hidden; only SPC v o shows it.
5. src/query.rs:587 — `--stale` does not open the archive, so `-s done --stale N` with N >= archive_days can never return a row.
   Failure: Reproduced: `moai show -s done --stale 20 --json` returns [] (before this branch it listed the row). The human output says 'archive 1 hidden'; the JSON says nothing.
6. src/report.rs:2235 — A group's archive clock is the latest status_since of its counted members, so an epic closed today by deferring, removing or moving out its last open member is archived at once.
   Failure: Reproduced: epic with one member done 29 days ago and one todo; `moai defer` the todo. The epic leaves the `moai status` list at once (`archived.epics: 1`) and is hidden from `show --all`; the board's 'folded' note never shows.
7. src/tui/mod.rs:3045 — The `[archive N hidden]` count covers the whole project and ignores the active SPC f filter, the current folder, folder rows that show anyway, and board rows that can never be cards.
   Failure: With `SPC f status=todo` the badge still says 'archive 3 hidden' and SPC v o reveals nothing. On the board in this repo about 400 closed ideas and epics are counted that can never become cards. The CLI tail counts only rows that pass the filters.
8. src/guide.rs:750 — The AGENTS block tells agents to add up `work` with `moai show [filters] --json`; the usual `--all` now silently drops long-closed rows.
   Failure: `moai show -e E --all --json | jq` undercounts tokens for members closed more than 14 days ago, while `moai stats --json` counts them.
9. src/cli.rs:1047 — The help (and CHANGELOG) say '-g and asking by time find it anyway', but `moai show -g X` never lists an archived row without `--all`; the `--all` one-line help still says it includes done.
   Failure: Reproduced: `moai show -g thought` prints 'done 2 hidden — `--all`'; the archived rows appear only with `-g --all`.
10. CHANGELOG.md:64 — Behaviour changes are listed only under Added: the explorer's done/show-all toggles, the status board lists, and `idea show --all`.
   Failure: Breaks the CLAUDE.md release rule '동작 변경(Changed)도 minor 다'. Someone reading Changed doesn't learn that showing done no longer shows old work.
11. src/tui/view.rs:51 — Cleanup: the new `archived` parameter of `View::shows` is `false` at every production call; the real rule lives in `see_in`, so the unit test covered a branch that never runs.
   Failure: A change to the archive rule made in `shows` keeps the tests green while the screen follows the copy in `see_in`.
12. src/tui/mod.rs:4289 — `aged()` was inserted between `sites()`'s doc comment and `sites()`.
   Failure: rustdoc attaches the overview-filler warning to `aged()`, and `sites()` loses its doc.
13. src/cmd/show.rs:291 — The 'open every hidden row' filter is written by hand in show.rs and stats.rs, and the comment above it still lists only all·ideas.
   Failure: The next hidden axis has to be added in both places; `..filter.clone()` compiles even if one is missed.
14. tests/cli.rs:13126 — The new CLI test writes its own runner instead of using `ok_at`/`add_at`.
   Failure: On failure it prints only stderr, so a failing `--json`/`-q` call gives an empty message — the regression `ok_env` was written to prevent.
15. src/config.rs:389 — A misplaced `[archive] archive_days` reuses the thresholds error ('thresholds are written at the top'), and `[archive] days = 30` is ignored with no message.
   Failure: The error calls archive_days a threshold; the bare `days` key never takes effect.

Fixed (findings 1–4 and 8–14):
- 1: the archive is now removed from the board lists only after all warnings are counted. The existing test now also checks that the warnings are the same with the archive on and off.
- 2: I added `large_enum_variant = "allow"` to `Cargo.toml` with a reason. That follows the existing `result_large_err` entry for the same enum, rather than boxing it.
- 3, 9, 10: README, help text, CHANGELOG (Added and Changed) and the regenerated `docs/cli.md` are corrected. The `--all` help now reads "Include done and deferred, no archive", short enough for the 80-column test.
- 4: the notice now names `SPC v o`, or both keys when the row is also hidden for another reason. There are two new en/ko strings and a test that goes through Enter then Esc.
- 8: the guide text is updated, the `AGENTS.md` block is rewritten with its new hash, and the committed plugin was refreshed with `MOAI_BLESS=1`.
- 11–14: the dead parameter is gone and the badge borrows its names again; the doc comment is moved; `Filter::unhidden()` is shared; the test uses `ok_at`/`add_at`.

Not fixed — these need your call:
- 5, `--stale`: I'd let `--stale` open the archive the way `-g` does. It wasn't in your decision on which questions open the archive, so I didn't guess.
- 6, groups archived the moment they close: this follows from the clock you chose (same as `show --done`). Changing it means picking a different clock for groups.
- 7, the badge count: it should be counted where the list and board are laid out, which is a redesign.
- 15: low value.

Smaller items I didn't put in the 15:
- Overview projects judge the archive by the time they were last read, so it can lag the CLI by days.
- The TUI test constructors turn the archive off instead of fixing the clock.
- `now` is re-parsed for every done row.
- The CHANGELOG commit names the epic instead of member moai-47mz.97f, and one commit carries four member issues.

Still to do:

title: 등록하는 범위의 update 만 실패하면 옛 판인 채 걷힌다

text:
## Code review of moai-tl3k (2f8d9cea..HEAD), xhigh effort, with fixes applied

I reviewed `2f8d9cea..HEAD` (review issue `moai-tl3k.wx7`, grade xhigh) and found 9 problems; I fixed 6 and skipped 3 that need a decision from you. The fixes are uncommitted in the worktree, and all 31 `skill_` tests plus `the_cli_reference_matches_the_help` pass.

I checked a few things against the real `claude` 2.1.287 in a scratch HOME and repository:
- **Install on an already-installed scope** exits 0 and leaves the old version in place.
- **Update when already at the latest version** exits 0.
- **Update at a scope where the plugin isn't installed** exits 1.
- **Update at project scope** changes only the plugins ledger: `.claude/settings.json` stays byte-identical and the old cache directory stays.

What the review brief asked about, and what I found:
- **Doc blocks:** `Lift` was inserted above `Undeclare` without taking over its doc block.
- **One lift per scope:** `scopes_of` lifts each scope once, and the scope being registered is never lifted separately.
- **Dry run:** calls nothing.
- **Uninstall:** behaves as before (`retire(..., None)`).
- **Exit code:** a failed lift doesn't change it.
- **Forked marketplace source:** nothing new opens there.
- **Mutation checks:** removing the lift creation turns the new test red. Calling lifts after a failed registration left every test green, so I added coverage (finding 4).

```json
[
  {"file":"src/cmd/skill.rs","line":135,"summary":"The scope being registered counts as registered when `installed || updated`, but `plugin install` exits 0 on an existing install without raising its version, so if only `plugin update --scope <S>` fails, S stays on the old version and still has its plugins and declarations removed. The new `stuck` guard only covers the other scopes.","failure_scenario":"An old moai at local, `skill install` (local), and `claude plugin update moai@m --scope local -y` fails. Registration still counts as done, korean-skills and humanize-korean are removed at local, and local stays old. The next install removes again whatever a person reinstalled there, which is the bug this epic closes for the other scopes. The `retire` doc wrongly said every scope install removes from goes up."},
  {"file":"src/cmd/skill.rs","line":811,"summary":"Lifting a user scope where the plugins were only kept (another repository's moai also stands there) permanently gives up moai removing them later.","failure_scenario":"Repositories A and B both have an old moai at user scope next to korean-skills. A runs `skill install` (local): user is lifted and korean-skills is kept. B later uninstalls its moai. A's next install no longer sees user as old, so it never removes korean-skills there. Before this diff it would have removed it once B's moai was gone."},
  {"file":"src/cmd/skill.rs","line":42,"summary":"A lift copies the freshly planted tree, whose hooks call the binary that ran this install, into a scope the person did not name.","failure_scenario":"`skill install --scope local` is run from a worktree's `target/release/moai`, with an old moai at project scope. The project scope is lifted, and its hooks now call the worktree binary. Once that worktree is removed, hooks at project scope fail. Before, only the scope named by `--scope` was exposed."},
  {"file":"tests/cli.rs","line":17307,"summary":"No test failed if the lifts ran after a failed registration.","failure_scenario":"Mutation: call the lifts in an `else` branch of `if registered`. All 31 `skill_` tests stayed green."},
  {"file":"tests/cli.rs","line":17307,"summary":"The new test's dry run (which plans a lift) never checked that no `claude` call was made.","failure_scenario":"A regression that runs the lifts during `--dry-run` would change another scope's ledger entry, and the test would not catch it."},
  {"file":"src/cmd/skill.rs","line":713,"summary":"`Retired::call` copied the stuck scopes into a `Vec<String>` and used an early `return` to skip removing the declarations.","failure_scenario":"Any step added after the declarations loop would be skipped silently whenever project could not be lifted, and the copy adds an allocation for nothing."},
  {"file":"src/cmd/skill.rs","line":634,"summary":"`Lift::argv` repeated, by hand, the `plugin update` command that `register` builds.","failure_scenario":"Changing the flags in one place (for example `-y`) would update the registered scope and the lifted scopes with different commands."},
  {"file":"CHANGELOG.md","line":98,"summary":"The CHANGELOG said `--dry-run` lists only the removals, and that only removals are skipped when registration fails. A stray line ending in 'A' also broke the wrapping.","failure_scenario":"A reader isn't told that the dry run also lists the scopes it would bring up, or that nothing is brought up when registration fails."},
  {"file":"src/cli.rs","line":1602,"summary":"The `skill install` help (and `docs/cli.md`) said only 'Nothing is removed when moai's own registration fails'.","failure_scenario":"A reader could expect other scopes to be brought up even when moai's own registration fails, which the code does not do."}
]
```

**Fixed:**
- **Finding 1, comment only:** the `retire` doc comment now says what the code does: the registered scope is counted on "registration done", and that has a gap when only its `update` fails.
- **Findings 4 and 5:** `skill_install_brings_an_old_scope_up_before_retiring_it` now asserts the dry run makes no `claude` calls. It also covers a failed registration:
  - no `--scope project` call is made
  - `lifted` reports `ok: null`
  - the settings file is unchanged
  - the screen shows a "not called" line for the lift

  That mutation now turns the test red, and reverting either `stuck` filter still does.
- **Finding 6:** the copied list and early return are replaced by a `stuck` check applied as a filter to both loops.
- **Finding 7:** register and the lift now share one `update_argv` function.
- **Findings 8 and 9:** the CHANGELOG paragraph is reworded and rewrapped. The help text and `docs/cli.md` were edited identically to say "removed or brought up".

**Skipped, needs your decision:**
- **Finding 1, code change:** the user decision (`moai-tl3k.jvz`) literally says the scope being registered is cleared once registration succeeds. Holding it back would need a new screen line and a new `--json` shape.
- **Findings 2 and 3:** these follow directly from the decision to lift every old scope. Changing them changes intended behaviour.

I didn't touch `src/guide.rs` (its `cargo fmt` diff is `moai-3mig`'s) or the worktree's `.moai`, and I committed nothing.

title: 묶음의 닫힌 때가 멤버의 먼 미래 시각을 받는다

text:
리뷰 원문 (/code-review xhigh --fix, 5ef2f1b7..HEAD, 서브에이전트 a843bd173f8097805)

I found 9 issues in moai-23q4 (`5ef2f1b..HEAD`) and fixed 7 in the working tree. The fixes are tests, comments and docs plus one cheap early exit in the code. The full `cargo test` passes (1722 unit and 654 CLI tests), and so do `cargo fmt --check` and clippy. Nothing is committed.

Answers to the angle:
- `Stand::entered` vs `Stand::since`: they differ only for groups that read done, because of the `column == DONE` guard.
- Stale and blocked clocks: unchanged. `blocked_since` still reads `since`, and for groups not in done `entered == since`, so `--stale` gives the same answer there.
- How `left_at` dates members: it picks only members dropped from the count. It dates each by its earliest deferral that isn't the group's own, then takes the latest across those members.
- One clock: the archive, `show --done`, stats `closed_at`, the status board and TUI `Site::archived` all read `entered`.
- Help, CHANGELOG and comments: the stated limit (rm and `edit -e` leave no trace) was incomplete, and some text was wrong. Fixed (findings 1, 5 and 6).

Findings:
1. src/report.rs:2400 — left_at dates a row moved into an already-closed group by that row's deferral, so `edit -e` of a deferred row re-dates the group to a day its column never changed; the stated limit only covered rm and moving rows out.
   Failure: Epic E done since 08-01 (archived). Issue x deferred 09-25 elsewhere. On 09-30 `moai edit x -e E`: E comes back onto the status board, `show --done 2026-09-25 --type epic` lists E, and `--done 2026-08-01` no longer finds it. Reproduced with the dev binary.
2. src/report.rs:2262 — The `column == DONE` guard on entered was not pinned by any test.
   Failure: Dropping the guard would let deferring one member move an in-progress epic's `--stale` clock to today (the moai-cxk8 loophole), with every test still green.
3. src/report.rs:2399 — The latest-across-members choice in left_at and the exclusion of the group's own deferral were not pinned.
   Failure: Changing the outer max to min, or dropping the filter that excludes the group's own deferral, gave a wrong `entered` and every test stayed green.
4. src/tui/mod.rs:477 — The TUI's wiring to `entered` (Stood and Ground::here's since map, used by Site::archived) had no test.
   Failure: Putting `s.since` back compiles and passes, and the explorer hides an epic closed by deferring on the day it closed.
5. CHANGELOG.md:91 — The Changed entry left out that `--stale` on a done group now reads the deferral clock too.
   Failure: `moai show -s done --stale 10 --type epic` changes answers with no release note.
6. src/query.rs:50 — The Where.since field comment said it is not the staleness clock, but Where::since is exactly what `--stale` reads; the Stand doc named only one clock.
   Failure: The next reader picks the wrong clock for a staleness or blocked check.
7. src/report.rs:2262 — left_at ran for every done group whenever any row in the repo was deferred, even when no member dropped out of the count, including on ready and blocked paths that throw `entered` away.
   Failure: An extra `shelf.every(g)` walk and one set lookup per member, per done group, on every `ready`, `status` and hook call in a repo with deferred rows.
8. src/report.rs:2392 — left_at checks each off member against the whole counted list, and the check is redundant with the date filter that follows it.
   Failure: Large done groups with many deferred members pay off-members times counted pointer comparisons.
9. src/report/stats.rs:296 — A member's far-future deferred_at can become the group's closed time, and the far-future check in stats only looks at the group row's own timestamps.
   Failure: A member deferred with a clock typo of 2099 makes `moai stats --type epic` lead-time p90 span decades.

Fixed:
- 1: this can't be fixed in code, because the snapshot is identical to a real "deferred and closed the group" case. I wrote the limit into the `Stand::entered` doc, the `show` help (and regenerated `docs/cli.md`), and the CHANGELOG.
- 2 and 3: new test `entered_parts_from_since_only_when_a_group_reads_done` in `src/report.rs`.
- 4: new test `an_epic_closed_by_deferring_is_not_archived_the_same_day` in `src/tui/mod.rs`.
- 5 and 6: the CHANGELOG entry now names `--stale`. The `Where.since` and Stand doc comments and the Stood field doc are corrected.
- 7: `left_at` is now skipped when no member dropped out (`of.len() > counted.len()` is checked first). The result is the same either way.

I mutation-checked the new tests. Removing the DONE guard, swapping max for min, dropping the group's-own exclusion, and the TUI revert each turn them red, and restoring the code turns them green.

Skipped:
- 8: with fix 7 in place, the scan only runs for done groups that actually lost members. It also guards against the "who is dropped" rule drifting between `counted` and `left_at`, so I kept it.
- 9: the same thing already happens with a member's far-future `status_since`. Fixing it means changing how the far-future check treats groups, which is well outside this diff.

text:

**What I changed (uncommitted):**
- **`-C`:** a new `store::invoked_dir()` returns the cwd from before `-C`, and `invoked` joins argv[0] to it.
- **Unwritable spellings:** `spelled` now returns nothing for spellings that are not quotable, not UTF-8, or under `/proc` or `/dev`. Those cases fall back to the resolved path, which is what was written before the diff.
- **`exe_name` is pure again:** `place()` resolves `current_exe` once and passes it in, so `exe_name(spelling, resolved, on_path)` compares by text. A new pure unit test, using a link spelling, goes red if that is reverted to comparing the spelling.
- **`status`:** `same` is now `*hook == exe || matches!(…)`, which behaves the same.
- **Tests:** the unit tests compare text and gained an absolute `..` case. New cases cover unwritable and procfs spellings, `-C` with a relative argv[0], and argv[0] naming an existing different executable. The vanished-hook test reads the hook's spelling from `skill status --json` and now checks the 'another moai' line.
- **Comments:** the `recorded_bin` doc, the `exe_name` and `spelled` docs, the notice-key comments, and one line in `invoked` saying its cwd is the resolved one.

**Not fixed — this needs your decision:** the `status` silence (third finding). The new test `…same_binary_says_nothing` deliberately asserts silence, and fixing it means either a new en/ko message ("planting here rewrites the hooks to {exe}, same file") or changing your rule to "keep the already-installed spelling when it is the same file". Until then, `./moai skill install` at the root still dirties `plugin.json`.

**Also not done:**
- **Switching to `user_config::same_dir`:** I didn't swap the inline place comparisons over. The repo deliberately keeps inline `real()==real()` for files (merge_driver.rs:1592, review fix 12df6c0f), and `same_dir` is documented as the directory check.
- **Low-value cleanup:** test-fixture duplication, and `spelled` duplicating `hook::resolve_path`.
- **CHANGELOG:** the line is already planned after this review.

**Refuted, so excluded:**
- The merge driver keeping its own path policy: out of scope, and `.git/config` is not committed.
- `skill status --json` having no verdict field: nothing consumes it.
- Joining to the resolved cwd rather than `$PWD`: intended.
- On macOS, a symlinked install run by bare name now gets the name `moai` written: that is `exe_name`'s documented rule.
- An explicit path becoming the name `moai` when PATH has the same file: the same documented rule, and it predates this diff.

For the review note: the 27 review subagents used 5,452,578 tokens in total (from their completion reports). My own thread's count isn't known, so leave `tokens=` off for it.

title: 거르개 입력 칸이 쓸 키와 값을 보인다
SPC f 입력 칸에 쓸 수 있는 키와 예제를 보인다
user=·tag=·milestone= 뒤에 고를 수 있는 값 목록을 띄운다
탐색기 도움말과 README 에 거르개 입력 칸을 싣는다
거르개가 user 여럿과 날짜·시각 범위를 받는다
user= 가 이름이나 메일을 받고, 여러 번 쓰면 또는으로 고른다
created·updated·started·ended 가 날짜·시각과 ~ 범위를 받는다
거르개 글이 따옴표로 묶은 값을 한 값으로 읽는다
--filter 도움말·docs/cli.md·CHANGELOG 에 새 문법을 싣는다

text:
사용자 결정(2026-10-03, 일꾼 창에서 물음)

- 자리: 입력 칸 위의 패널이다. SPC 메뉴처럼 목록을 밀어 올리고 덮지 않는다. 커서가 값 자리(`user=`·`tag=`·`milestone=`)에 서면 값 목록, 아니면 쓸 수 있는 키와 예제
- 고르기: 위·아래 화살표로 옮기고 Enter 가 넣는다. 값 목록이 열린 동안 Enter 는 값을 넣고, 닫힌 때만 거름망을 건다
- 사람: 목록에는 `이름 (메일)`, 넣는 값은 메일이다. 메일이 없는 사람은 이름을 넣는다
- 좁히기: 친 값의 부분 일치로 좁힌다. 대소문자는 가리지 않는다. 사람은 이름·메일, 태그는 이름, 마일스톤은 id·제목에서 찾는다

문법 확정(2026-10-03, 사람이 AskUserQuestion 으로 정했다) — 입력 칸의 예제(moai-h2rh)는 이 꼴을 따른다.

요청의 `user=` 와 `created·updated·started·ended` 는 이름이 바뀌었다.

- **`user=` 는 더하지 않는다.** 담당 키는 `assignee=` 하나다("assignee 로 통일")
  - 값: 이름만·메일만·`이름 (메일)`·`none`·`me` — `-a` 로 맡길 때와 같은 판정
  - **되풀이하면 또는이다** — `assignee=a assignee=b`. CLI 의 `-a a -a b` 도 또는이다(지금까지는 두 번 쓰면 거절했다).
    쉼표도 또는이다. 담당 하나짜리 줄에서 "그리고" 는 늘 0건이었다
- **새 시각 키는 `--json` 의 필드 이름이다**: `created_at`·`updated_at`·`started_at`·`done_at`
  - 넷 다 **줄 자신의 그 필드**만 본다. 묶음(에픽·마일스톤)도 제 필드만 본다 — 멤버로 재지 않는다
  - 필드가 없으면(모른다) 어느 폭에도 안 든다
  - `done_at=` 은 마지막으로 done 에 든 때다. 되돌린 줄도 걸린다. 지금 닫힌 것만 보려면 `status=done` 을 함께 준다
- **옛 키는 뜻 그대로 남는다**: `since=`(updated_at 의 그때부터, 한 끝만), `created=`, `done=`(지금 done 칸에 선 줄이 그 칸에 든 때, 묶음은 멤버로)
  - 옛 키도 아래의 새 때 꼴과 `~` 를 받는다
- **때 꼴** — 셋이다
  - `YYYY-MM-DD` — 그날 하루 전체. 읽는 사람의 시계다(CLI 는 시스템 시간대, 탐색기는 `SPC o t` 로 고른 시간대) — 지금 `created=` 와 같다
  - `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` — **그 1분**(`HH:MM:00`~`HH:MM:59`). 읽는 사람의 시계다
  - `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` — UTC 의 한 순간(그 1초). 시간대가 안 옮긴다 — 지금 그대로
- **범위**: `A~B`. 옛 `A..B` 도 받는다. 한쪽을 비워도 된다(`A~`·`~B`). 두 끝 다 든다 — 끝은 그 꼴의 마지막 초까지(`~2026-10-05 23:59` 는 23:59:59 까지)
  - 쉼표는 폭 사이의 또는, 같은 키를 되풀이하면 그리고(지금과 같다)
- **따옴표**(탐색기 입력 칸): `=` 바로 뒤의 `"…"` 또는 `'…'` 는 한 값이다. 따옴표는 벗겨진다
  - 다른 자리의 따옴표는 글자 그대로다 — `grep=don't` 는 그대로 찾는다
  - 닫지 않은 따옴표는 줄 끝까지다(치는 동안 거절하지 않는다)
  - 따옴표 없이도 `항목=` 이 없는 낱말은 앞 값에 빈칸 하나로 붙는다(지금 그대로) — `done_at=2026-10-10 10:10` 도 통한다

사람이 든 예를 이 문법으로 옮기면:

    assignee=raven@buzzni.com assignee=joshep@buzzni.com tag=bug done_at="2026-10-03 00:00~2026-10-05 23:59"
    done_at=2026-10-02
    done_at="2026-10-10 10:10"

리뷰어 원문(/code-review xhigh --fix, agent-a9048aff522072c60)

I found 15 problems in the `moai-h2rh` diff and fixed 12 of them in the working tree; nothing is committed. Three are left: two need moai-97tn merged first and one is in commit history. The full test suite and clippy pass, and fmt is clean.

The most serious one: `every_example_is_a_filter_the_explorer_takes` will fail in CI. The `assignee=me` example needs to know who you are, and CI sets no git identity or `MOAI_ACTOR`. I confirmed this by running the test with an unusable identity. I also confirmed the four new behaviour tests go red when their fix is reverted.

1. src/tui/hint.rs:546 — every_example_is_a_filter_the_explorer_takes depends on the machine's identity: the `assignee=me` example is refused when nobody can be resolved. CI (ubuntu-latest, no git user.name, no MOAI_ACTOR) or MOAI_ACTOR set to a malformed value: input_error returns the no-actor refusal and the test panics. On machines that do have an identity, the test starts git config processes.
2. src/tui/draw.rs:166 — On a short window the hint panel gets 0 rows, so the value list is never drawn, but offered() still returns Some and Enter puts a value nobody can see. Terminal 7 rows high, SPC f, type `tag=`, press Enter: the field becomes `tag=bug ` instead of applying the filter. Up/Down also move the hidden aim.
3. src/tui/hint.rs:84 — `first` is true for the first comma segment inside an already-open quote, so quoted() wraps the pick in a second pair of quotes. `assignee="Ki|,bob"`, pick `Kim Lee`: the field becomes `assignee=""Kim Lee",bob"`.
4. src/tui/hint.rs:88 — With an unclosed quote, the replace span runs from the opening quote to the end of the line, deleting items typed after the cursor. `assignee="Ki| tag=bug`, pick Kim Lee: `tag=bug` is gone.
5. src/tui/hint.rs:181 — Aim is keyed only on (text, cursor), so an old aimed row comes back when the same text recurs after reopening the field or after typing and deleting a character. Type `tag=`, Down, Down, Esc, SPC f, type `tag=`, Enter: puts `ui` instead of `bug`.
6. src/tui/hint.rs:162 — Quoted inserts and slot()'s quote-reading follow moai-97tn's split_items, but this branch still splits with tui::split_filter, which keeps quotes as literal characters. If h2rh merges before 97tn: pick `Kim Lee` (no email), the field gets `assignee="Kim Lee"`, the filter value includes the quote characters, and is_assignee matches nothing. The module doc's 'follows the query splitter' is also untrue on this branch.
7. src/tui/hint.rs:162 — quoted() leaves a value that starts with a quote character bare, so the grammar reads that character as an opening quote and strips it. Separately, quoting a value with a comma does not keep it as one value, because the comma split happens after unquoting.
8. src/tui/hint.rs:263 — People without an email are deduped by lowercased name, but query::is_assignee compares names case-sensitively. `Anna` and `anna` show as one entry.
9. src/tui/hint.rs:277 — Tag offers are collected raw, but reading does not normalize tags while the filter does. `Bug` and `#bug` list as separate choices; an all-blank tag shows as an empty row.
10. src/tui/draw.rs:4237 — The `n/m` count sits on the second row's label, so with only one visible row the truncation says nothing.
11. src/tui/draw.rs:300 — offered() builds the whole value list twice per frame (panel and prompt help), and sort_by_key lowercases the label on every comparison.
12. src/tui/hint.rs:104 — items() re-implements the split_items tokenizer by hand, so there are two grammars to keep in sync, and they already differ on text after a closing quote (`grep="a b"c`).
13. src/tui/draw.rs:4208 — hint_lines defines a local pad closure that duplicates draw::pad.
14. README.md:142 — README lists assignee=, tag= and milestone= but leaves out no-tag=.
15. src/tui/hint.rs:1 — Commit 70b9e707 carries two issues (moai-h2rh.5zb and moai-h2rh.pjs) in one commit. CLAUDE.md '## 커밋': "한 커밋은 한 가지 일이다."

Fixed: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14 (5 regression tests added, 3 extended; fixture gained a "Kim Lee" assignee with no email).

Not fixed:
- 6 (quotes on this branch): quoting only works once moai-97tn is in, so 97tn should merge first, or h2rh should take develop after 97tn lands before it merges.
- 12 (duplicate tokenizer): removing `items()` needs 97tn's `split_items` to return byte positions so the hint can reuse it.
- 15 (two issues in one commit): fixing it means rewriting history.
리뷰 moai-h2rh.koh 12번이 같은 것을 짚었다. 이미 갈린 자리가 하나 있다 — `grep="a b"c` 에서 split_items 는 낱말을 c 까지 잇고 hint::items 는 닫는 따옴표에서 항목을 끝낸다. 커서 자리 읽기에는 해가 없다(닫는 따옴표 뒤는 값 자리가 아니다)

리뷰를 받고 정한 것

- 받은 것: 1·2·3·4·5·7·8·9·10·11·13·14 — 리뷰가 고친 그대로 fix: 커밋 하나에 실었다(시험·clippy·fmt 를 다시 돌려 확인)
- 6(이 가지는 따옴표를 글자로 읽는다): 이 에픽 안에서 푼다 — moai-97tn 이 머지된 뒤 develop 을 받아 시험을 다시 돌리고 나서 머지한다. 예(`hint::EXAMPLES`)도 그때 새 문법으로 바꾼다
- 12(쪼개는 자가 둘): idea moai-e0qk 로 넘겼다. 리팩터라 릴리스 막대(회귀만) 밖이다 — 에픽과 마일스톤에서 뺐다
- 15(커밋 하나에 멤버 둘): 안 고친다. 두 멤버의 코드가 같은 함수들에 섞여 있어 가르려면 역사를 다시 쓰고 나눠 지어야 한다. 값어치에 비해 비싸다

text:
The review ran all ten finder angles, verification and the gap sweep. 15 findings survived, and I applied 12 of them as fixes in the working tree; three are skipped and noted below. None of the four settled decisions is broken in code; the problems are untested decision paths, misleading user-facing text, and stale docs. Nothing is committed, so you can make the `fix:` commit.

```json

It is `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`', so the user believes minutes are not accepted. Following that advice with `…T09:05:00Z` asks for one UTC second, 9h off in Seoul. `done_at=~` is told to give a side of `from..to`. The SPC f prompt shows the same text on every keystroke."},

In that state, `moai show --filter updated_at=<day> --json` silently drops done/deferred/idea/archived rows changed that day."},
  {"file": "src/query.rs", "line": 1030, "summary": "`desugar` trims the value, so a quoted SPC f value loses its leading and trailing spaces, although the `split_items` doc and the CHANGELOG said 'one value with its spaces'.", "failure_scenario": "In SPC f, `grep=\" fix\"` becomes `fix` and also matches 'prefix', while `-g ' fix'` keeps the space."},

Pasting the example as `--filter 'done_at=\"2026-10-03 00:00~…\"'` is also refused, because on the CLI the quotes reach `desugar` literally."},
  {"file": "src/cli.rs", "line": 1055, "summary": "The help offers `~` ranges with either side open but does not warn that a word-initial `~2026-10-05` is a shell tilde-prefix.", "failure_scenario": "In zsh (the macOS default), `moai show --done ~2026-10-05` fails with 'zsh: no such user or named directory' before moai runs."},

A maintainer 'fixing' code to match these comments would reopen the `timed`/`needs_zone` gaps."},
  {"file": "src/query.rs", "line": 942, "summary": "`wall_minute` re-implemented `parse_instant`'s strict clock check, and its sign guard was not pinned by any test.", "failure_scenario": "Tidying `two` to length-plus-parse would accept `2026-10-10 +1:30` / `-1:30`, since `\"-1\".parse::<i64>()` succeeds, and no test would go red."}

```

**Fixed:**
- **Refusal texts:** the three messages in en and ko now name all three time forms and both range separators. A new view test pins this.
- **One list of time fields:** a new `Filter::times()` (exhaustive destructure) is now read by both the hide-opening in `build` and `needs_zone`. A new test takes the time keys from `KEYS` and checks that each one opens hidden rows and asks for the zone, while an instant does not.
- **New tests for decisions nobody pinned:**
  - an explorer test typing a quoted value (including the zone re-apply);
  - `done_at=` + `status=todo` being accepted;
  - a hand-moved group matching by its own fields;
  - signed-clock cases added to the bad-input list.
- **Revert checks:** I confirmed the new tests go red on the reverts they guard: the old splitter, a `times()` missing a list, and `*_at=` skipping groups.
- **CHANGELOG:** range wording corrected, the example uses the CLI-safe form, the edge-trim and zsh notes are added, and "means or" replaces "is not and". I kept the quoted-value trimming behaviour and documented it instead, because changing `desugar` would change the CLI `--filter` as well.
- **Help:** one zsh sentence added to the Time paragraph, and `docs/cli.md` regenerated from the dev binary.
- **Stale docs:** the `spell` doc, the query.rs internal docs and the `FilterArgs` doc are corrected.
- **Cleanup:** `wall_minute` now delegates to `parse_instant` (the `instant()` doc already claimed it did). As an extra cleanup outside the 15, the grep/notes scan in `matches` now runs after the cheap time checks; the result is unchanged.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the full `cargo test` pass: 1731 unit tests and 658 cli tests, the docs test included.

**Skipped, for you to place:**
- **guide.rs "repeated = and":** outside the diff. Fixing it means regenerating the AGENTS block, and running `moai init` from the worktree could write the root checkout's AGENTS.md. Worth its own issue.
- **DST fall-back:** fixing it would change the wall-clock comparison model decided in moai-efoc, and the impact is low. Worth an idea.
- **Hint clipping:** draw.rs is held by moai-h2rh, and its new panel lists `KEYS` wrapped, which supersedes the clipped line.

**Hand on:**
- README time paragraph (README.md:257) and `moai tui --help` (cli.rs:471): no minutes, `~` or quoting. Both are held by moai-h2rh.
- moai-h2rh's `hint::items` re-implements the quote rules, which breaks "one splitter" once the two epics merge.
- `--filter grep=` silently overrides `-g` (existing behaviour): worth an idea.

Changed files, all in `/home/coder/workspace/moa-issue/.claude/worktrees/moai-97tn/`: `src/query.rs`, `src/view.rs`, `src/tui/mod.rs` (one test only), `src/cli.rs`, `i18n/en.json`, `i18n/ko.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/cli.md`. `.moai` is untouched.

For the review issue's `model:` line: anthropic/opus-5.5. The eleven subagents used 3,186,396 tokens between them, but my own count is unknown, so the total is unknown and `tokens=` should be left out.

판단(리뷰 원문과 따로 적는다)

- 받은 것 12건: 리뷰가 작업 트리에 고친 그대로 읽고 받았다. fmt·clippy(-D warnings)·cargo test(1731·658) 를 다시 돌려 확인하고 `fix(query): 에픽 끝 리뷰를 반영한다` 한 커밋으로 남겼다

text:
## Code review: epic moai-m1za (`mv -m -` / `defer -m -` read stdin)

/code-review max --fix, range c435e507..HEAD. agent ad2c6575b3d982283 (opus).

**Result:** 14 findings survived verification. 9 fixed in the working tree, 5 skipped (need a decision or sit outside the epic). Full suite passes (1752 unit + 661 integration), `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Revert checks: a plain `trim()` fails the `work` assert and the BOM inputs; going back to `Fail::new` fails the code assert; moving `read_msg` inside the lock fails the new lock test with a `locked` refusal; treating BOM as non-blank fails the `"\n\u{feff}\n"` input.

Refuted (dropped): size check for oversized stdin before the lock; duplicate refusal texts; repeated comments; padded `-m ' -'`. Real but pre-existing, left out: a large `-m -` text is copied once per id.

1. src/cmd/mv.rs:139 — Blank text on the command line is still written as a closing line: read_msg returns non-`-` text untouched, mv has no empty check, and hook rule 3 sees `-m "$OUT"` as the literal word `$OUT`. `moai mv <review> done -m "$OUT"` with OUT empty, or `-m "$(cat missing.md)"`, closes the review with `"note":""`; `mv X review -m ''` on a row already in review writes an empty note line. Pre-existing. NOT FIXED: needs a decision.
2. src/cmd/add.rs:122 — read_msg's `trim()` removed the first line's indentation, so an indented `model:` example got counted as work (argv text is stored as given, so stdin and argv disagreed). FIXED: blank_lines_trimmed keeps the first line's indentation.
3. src/cmd/mv.rs:139 — read_msg runs before the in-lock checks (`--from` typo, group with `--from`, missing ids); empty stdin answers bad_input ahead of a `--from` typo, and the comment wrongly said a wrong call never waits on stdin. FIXED: comments and a test assert pin the order.
4. src/cmd/add.rs:122 — `str::trim` keeps U+FEFF, so BOM-only stdin (or blank line + BOM) got past the empty-stdin refusal. FIXED: leading BOM stripped, U+FEFF counts as blank.
5. tests/cli.rs:8017 — No test checked that `-m -` is read before `.moai/lock`. FIXED: a_message_waiting_on_stdin_holds_no_lock.
6. src/cmd/defer.rs:38 — defer refused an empty argv reason with code `error` but an empty `-m -` with `bad_input`; note uses bad_input. FIXED: BAD_INPUT, CHANGELOG Changed line, test assert.
7. src/cmd/mod.rs:550 — A lone `-` is still literal text in note's text argument, the add title and edit --title (`moai note <id> - < close.md` writes `-`). Pre-existing, outside the diff. NOT FIXED.
8. src/cmd/add.rs:119 — read_msg skips the "this is a file name" notice every `-b` path prints (`-m closing.md`). Pre-existing; needs a new `-m` message. NOT FIXED.
9. CHANGELOG.md:229 — Entry only under Fixed though it turns exit-0 calls into exit 1 and starts reading stdin. FIXED: split into Fixed and Changed.
10. src/cmd/add.rs:112 — read_msg's doc contrasted its refusal with `-b -` passing silently, but `note -b -` refuses — that is the rule the decision names. FIXED: doc wording.
11. i18n/en.json:158 — refuse.msg_stdin_empty said "nothing came" even when stdin held only blank space. FIXED in en and ko.
12. src/cmd/add.rs:100 — Non-UTF-8 stdin is refused with code `error` and an English-only message (read_body, shared with note/add/edit). Pre-existing. NOT FIXED.
13. tests/cli.rs:8028 — Negative asserts `!contains("note":"-")` / `!contains("text":"-")` could never fail once the positive assert passed. FIXED: mv's moved first, defer's removed.
14. src/cmd/add.rs:116 — The out-of-scope gap (`mv -m ''` writes empty notes) was recorded only in a doc comment and a commit body. Needs a tracker record.

Suggested follow-ups: idea for #1 (`mv -m 의 빈 argv 글이 빈 닫는 줄로 리뷰를 닫는다`), idea for #8, idea for #7, idea for #12, and `note -b -` trimming (first-line indentation, BOM) — one shared helper would fix both.

text: 갈림길(밤사이 정함): 이 버그는 idea 를 담은 뒤 moai-r1ly.f2x(6c2a3b77)가 이미 고쳤다 — relayer 의 landed 가 rows 안의 Row::Project(n) 자리를 찾는다. 코드는 다시 안 쓰고, f2x 의 시험이 안 잰 보드 보기와 실제 키 길(SPC p a → a → Esc)을 시험 하나로 더했다(725b62ff). 고침을 Some(n) 으로 되돌리면 이 시험과 f2x 의 시험이 함께 붉어지는 것을 보았다. 안 고른 것: 시험 없이 바로 닫기 — idea 가 "카드나 줄" 이라 적은 보드 쪽을 아무도 안 쟀다.

밤사이 정한 갈림(사람이 아침에 볼 것):

- 정한 것: 안 읽기로 한 AGENTS.md(밖·.git 으로 가는 링크, FIFO·장치·디렉터리)는 권한·UTF-8 로 못 읽는 AGENTS.md 와 같은 자리에서 멈춘다. `init` 은 아무것도 심기 전에 서고 `--no-agents` 를 대며, `init --check` 는 1 로 끝나고, `status` 의 알림은 입을 다문다
- 안 고른 것: 건너뛰고 나머지(.moai·딸린 파일)를 심은 뒤 AGENTS.md 를 untouched 로 대는 길
- 까닭: 디렉터리인 AGENTS.md 가 이미 멈추는 자리라, 이어 가면 같은 "보통 파일이 아니다" 가 둘로 갈린다. 그 자리는 쓰기도 이미 거절해(`store::target_of`) 블록을 심을 길이 원래 없다. 앞 판은 밖의 링크를 읽고 "못 썼다" 로 이어 가, `status`·`--check` 가 남의 파일의 블록 상태를 댔다
- 값: `AGENTS.md -> <체크아웃 밖>` 을 둔 저장소의 첫 `moai init` 이 이제 0 이 아니라 1 로 끝난다. 그 사람은 `--no-agents` 를 붙인다. 되돌리려면 `read_agents` 의 `Err(Fell::Unheld)` 를 `run` 에서 untouched 로 돌린다

덧붙여 정한 것: 못 읽는 CLAUDE.md 에는 `@AGENTS.md` 가리킴을 더하라고 안 한다(앞 판은 빈 글로 쳐서 권했다). `dotfile_gaps` 의 "무엇이 들었는지 모르니 빠졌다고 할 수 없다" 와 같은 자다.

(3) 프로젝트 다시 읽기에만 묶기 — 층에서는 다시 읽기가 안 돌아 그 줄이 끝까지 선다. 걷은 것이 있으면 프로젝트를 다시 읽게 했다(노트가 모자란 채 헤더만 걷히지 않게). 설정은 부르는 쪽 것을 빌린다(cmd::show::at_home 과 같은 꼴) — 뿌리마다 config.toml 을 새로 읽으면 연 적 없는 옆 워크트리의 파일을 연다.

밤사이 정한 갈림을 뒤집었다(리뷰 moai-x0o7.52k 5번, 사람이 아침에 볼 것):

- 새로 정한 것: 안 읽기로 한 AGENTS.md(밖·.git 으로 가는 링크, FIFO·장치·디렉터리)를 `init` 은 멈추지 않고 그 파일만 못 건드린 자리로 대고 나머지(.moai·딸린 파일·드라이버)를 심는다. `--json` 은 `untouched["AGENTS.md"].kind = "unreadable"`, 고칠 말은 "그 자리에 보통 파일을 두거나 `--no-agents`". `init --check` 는 그대로 1 로 끝나고 `status` 의 블록 알림은 입을 다문다. 권한·UTF-8 로 못 읽은 AGENTS.md 는 전처럼 아무것도 심기 전에 멈춘다
- 앞의 결정(멈춘다)을 버린 까닭: 리뷰가 하위 트래커의 `svc/AGENTS.md -> ../AGENTS.md`(dotfiles 저장소의 링크도 같다)에서 `moai init` 이 늘 1 로 끝나는 것을 보였다. 그러면 보드가 딸린 파일 규칙을 고치라며 대는 `moai init` 이 막다른 길이 되고, develop 은 0 으로 딸린 파일을 맞췄으니 회귀다. 그 자리는 쓰기도 거절해(`store::target_of`) 지킬 산문이 없다 — 멈춤은 산문을 지키려고 선 것이다
- 남는 값: 디렉터리인 AGENTS.md 가 이제 멈추지 않고 건너뛰어진다(develop 은 `Is a directory` 로 멈췄다). `init --check` 는 그 저장소에서 늘 0 이 아니다 — `--check` 의 계약("파일을 못 읽을 때만 0 이 아니다")대로이고, 권한으로 못 읽는 AGENTS.md 도 develop 에서 같았다
- 되돌리려면: `run` 의 `Err(Fell::Unheld(why))` 갈래를 `Err(fell)` 갈래와 합친다

I reviewed the three member commits in four steps:
- Ten finder angles ran in parallel. I ran some experiments myself as well.
- Each surviving candidate got one verifier, in nine verifier runs (three single checks and three batches).
- One gap sweep ran after that.
- I built and tested the fixes in a scratch copy, then copied them into the worktree.

**Verification after the fixes:** `cargo fmt --check` passes. Tests pass: 1755 unit and 663 CLI. `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -D warnings` passes. I also ran end-to-end checks with the fixed binary in scratch.

**Nothing is committed.** Six files are changed in the worktree: `src/store.rs`, `src/cmd/init.rs`, `src/held.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `i18n/en.json` and `i18n/ko.json`. Per CLAUDE.md, review fixes go in as a separate `fix:` commit.

### What I changed
- **`on_lock` (store.rs)**
  - It compares file identity using `file_id`: `stat` on the target and `lstat` on the lock places. A lock that is a link is never held, so following it would misread `.moai/lock -> ../AGENTS.md`.
  - It no longer checks the name first. For a target that does not exist yet it falls back to the canonical directory plus the name.
  - It also covers a lock inside any `.moai` and a lock next to any `issues.jsonl`, so nested trackers' own locks and far locks are protected.
  - It still opens nothing: only canonicalize, readlink, stat and lstat.
  - Side effect: a hard link to the lock is refused too. That is over-strict but harmless.
- **`target_of`**: the refusal text is now true for both the replace and append paths and ends with "replace the link with a regular file". The 34-line refusal doc moved onto `resolve`, its false "only caller" line was fixed, and the rustdoc link was fixed.
- **`far_lock`**: the fallback now compares the two lock places.
- **`held::into_git`**: new shared predicate, matching whole components case-insensitively. git itself refuses such paths in trees. place, resolve and inside all use it, and it has a unit test.
- **init.rs**
  - `read_held` now holds the "only NotFound means absent" rule once (the verifier confirmed the cleanup).
  - `agents_state` returns `(BlockState, String)`, so each caller reads once.
  - New key `refuse.init_agents_unheld` (en and ko) for Unheld refusals; Io refusals keep the old wording.
  - Fixed the two stale docs.
- **Tests**
  - store: nested own lock, nested far lock, hard-link stand-in for the case alias, and "a lock that is a link is not a lock". I checked that they go red against the old `on_lock`.
  - init: final-name `.git` case; the outside test now uses a stale block.
  - cli: assertions for the new advice; a fresh-repo FIFO init must leave no `.moai`; `status --json` must show no `*_rules` for refused dotfiles.

### Not changed (verifier refuted these)
- An extra `plant` outside-link test: `init_never_swaps_the_lock_through_agents_md` already pins the bounded writer.
- Routing `agents_unread` through `held::refused`: it doesn't fit, because the I/O-error case needs rendering too.

### Your five questions
1. No inserted item took over a neighbour's doc. The split did leave the refusal doc on the wrapper; that is finding 12, now fixed.
2. Each test's main claim goes red against develop's behaviour (FIFO hangs, outside read, lock swap, .git rules). Four assertions did not; finding 11, now strengthened.
3. Lock paths are spelled only in `lock_at` and `far_lock_at` apart from the far_lock fallback, now fixed. The `.git` rule now lives in one place.
4. Doc mismatches are findings 12 and 14. on_lock's premise that "the name rename replaces is `lock`" was also wrong; I rewrote it with the fix.
5. Nothing newly opens a path. plant's pre-open still runs after the read, but a FIFO swapped in between hangs it; that predates this diff and is parked as moai-2sbt.

**SnapshotOnLock** still fires on unix, because far_lock calls resolve and compares identity first; tests assert `broken`. On non-unix `holds()` returns None, so it can't fire and you get `error` instead. No release target is non-unix.

**Stopping init on a refused AGENTS.md** is sound for FIFOs and devices. For links pointing outside or into .git it is not sound as is (finding 5), and that needs your decision.

### Tracker and follow-ups
- New ideas in the root tracker, all `-e moai-x0o7`: moai-8q6b, moai-9irl, moai-2sbt, moai-9j25. Commit `.moai/` from the root.
- Fork 1 promotion candidates (they fall under the epic's promise that init does not trust links inside the checkout): moai-279k, moai-8q6b, moai-9j25.

  - The claim that `moai init` no longer waits on any of the four files should be narrowed for git repos (moai-279k).
  - Optionally, note the new advice line.
- Left unaddressed:
  - On non-unix the snapshot-on-lock case returns `error` instead of `broken` (no shipped platform affected).

The epic's own fixes hold up: reverting the f2x landing fix turns the new board test red, and the original ncj tests catch reverts of their core lines. But the ncj change introduced two user-visible regressions.

**Fixed (uncommitted):**
- **Exit report:** the unread list is split in two. `store::UNREAD` grows only again and is what the exit report and the CLI read, as before the epic. A new prunable `UNREAD_NOW` (`store::journal_unread_now`) feeds the header.
- **Stats window:** the reopen check skips while it is open; the next step after it closes re-checks.
- **Matching:** reopen compares `tried` by resolved path (`crate::path::real`).
- **Re-reads:** the flag only forces a project re-read while notes are held, and `leave_project` clears it.
- **Docs:** all of the above corrected, including `hint.rs` and the `input.rs` exemption reason.
- **Cleanups:** the three above.
- **Tests:** new or extended tests for every fix and test gap, each confirmed red when its fix is reverted (20 repeated runs of the new tests, all green).
- **Checks:** fmt, `clippy -D warnings`, and `cargo test` (1760 unit, 661 CLI) all pass.
- **Files:** `src/store.rs`, `src/query.rs`, and in `src/tui/`: `mod.rs`, `draw.rs`, `hint.rs`, `layer.rs`, `input.rs`.

**Not fixed:**
- **CHANGELOG:** parked as idea `moai-2wmh`. The hook asked whether the epic can deliver without it; if you count release notes as part of the epic, promote it to a member with `moai idea promote moai-2wmh -e moai-mkyg --from -`.
- **Loop-thread I/O:** only documented. The real fix belongs in `src/held.rs` (moai-x0o7's), so it's parked as idea `moai-sjtw`.
- **Both ideas** were written to the root's `.moai` and aren't committed yet.

**Left as is:**
- A stats window opened in the ~1s before a triggered re-read lands. This is the same window the epic's own comment accepts for `/`.
- A re-spelled entry re-appends under its new name (now documented).
- The hard-link variant would need an inode id stored on each entry.
- Duplicated test fixtures.

**Refuted:** replacing the thread-local `CAUGHT` (it would change the documented order) and "reopen adds newly broken names" (documented, honest). The production fn-pointer line needs no test: clippy's dead-code check already catches a revert.

**Your five checks:**
1. No inserted item captured another item's doc block, in the epic or in the fixes.
2. The tea, store, draw and TUI tests go red on revert; the four gaps above are now pinned.

밤사이 정한 갈래(사람이 아침에 볼 것): (1) 못 연 트래커는 --json 에 새 키 `tracker_error:{code,said}` 로 낸다 — `no_tracker` 에 값을 더하거나 최상위에 `error`/`code` 를 다는 길은 안 골랐다. 최상위 `{error,code}` 는 main 의 거절 꼴과 같아 0 으로 끝난 판을 실패로 읽게 하고, 객체 하나는 `commits_error` 와 같은 꼴이다. 낱말은 `kind` 가 아니라 `code` — 값이 거절의 code(broken·error)와 한 어휘다. (2) `no_tracker` 는 못 연 트래커에서 빠진다 — 문서("트래커가 없을 때만")대로 좁힌 것이라 뜻을 바꾼 것으로 보지 않았다. (3) 못 연 까닭은 판(stdout)에 싣고 stderr 의 같은 줄은 걷었다 — 세션 시작 훅은 stdout 만 맥락에 싣고, 터미널에서는 두 번 선다.

밤사이 정한 갈래(사람이 아침에 볼 것): 코드를 `status`·`ready` 의 한눈 보기에만이 아니라 같은 상태 낱말을 쓰는 `tui --json`(밖)·`project ls --json`·`project add --json` 에도 달았다. 고친 자리가 그 넷이 함께 읽는 `projects::State::Unreadable` 하나라, 한 표면만 달면 "넷이 다 같다" 는 `cmd/tui.rs` 의 글이 깨진다. unreadable 줄에는 `code` 가 늘 서고, `project add` 는 `error` 와 함께 서고 함께 빠진다(읽히는 저장소에 키를 달면 전부터 내던 줄이 바뀐다). 등록한 자리가 디렉터리가 아니면 code 는 `error` 다 — 고칠 것이 그 저장소의 파일이 아니라 등록이다.

Full pipeline: 10 finders, 27 merged candidates, one verifier each (none refuted), plus a gap sweep that added the climbed-tracker case. Fixes are uncommitted in the worktree; `cargo test` (1764 unit, 668 CLI) and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

Fixed:
- Findings 1-3: the file-name notice is deferred via a new `cmd::tell_after` and printed by `cmd::run` with the EPIPE-safe `tell` only when the command succeeds. This restores "a failed `--json` stderr is one object" for mv/defer/note/add/edit. `read_msg` no longer prints; `mv` and `defer` raise the notice after the write, and only when the message was actually journaled. `cmd::gather` now uses `tell`.
- `-C` measurement: `names_a_file` checks the invoked directory (`store::invoked_dir`) first; if the file exists only in the `-C` directory, the hint gives an absolute path.
- Deleted cwd: `Repo::find` wraps the error with the existing `refuse.no_cwd` wording, which also improves every other command there.
- The reason is no longer trimmed. `tracker_error.said` goes through `one_line`.
- `-m` long help on mv/defer says "text, not a path"; docs/cli.md regenerated.
- Docs: broken-code wording, init wording, stale test docs, project.rs State doc, recovery.md, the note.rs stat comment, and the laziness doc (takes `ctx` again).
- New tests: one JSON object on failing `--json`; no notice when nothing was journaled; `-C` from a sibling dir; `/dev/full` (Linux) not aborting the write; the `gather` arm via a non-UTF-8 snapshot; deleted cwd; a `prime_bare` unit test for the untrimmed reason. Each fix was reverted temporarily to confirm its test goes red, then restored.
- Cleanups: `project add` builds `error`/`code` in one `unzip`; tests use `field()`/`object_at`; the two new tests carry `#[cfg(unix)]`.

Not fixed (parked as ideas with `-e moai-yivo`):
- moai-94vn: climbed tracker (the climb doc warns against advising init there; wording needs your call)
- moai-t73s: prime advising init in a linked worktree outside main
- moai-on5b: a `.moai` that is a file or dangling link reads as "no tracker"
- moai-gy1v: prime's other troubles are stderr-only
- moai-ctpj: overview `problems` lose the user-config trouble code
- moai-17bp: one shared `{error, code}` type instead of hand-splitting Fail in several places
- Skipped: the `said` vs `error` key naming (the 6je note leaves it to the person); the automount stat risk (negligible).

Your questions:
- Narrowing `no_tracker` is a contract change: since v0.1.0, an unreadable tracker gave `no_tracker:true` with the reason on stderr; now it gives `tracker_error` and nothing on stderr. CHANGELOG still needs a Changed line (narrowed `no_tracker`, the reason moving to the page) and Added lines (`tracker_error`; `code` on the overview, project ls, project add and the outside tui --json; the `-m` notice).
- `tracker_error.code` matched the other commands in every case probed: both go through the same `Repo::find` and `gather`.
- JSON keys: `code` always stands on unreadable entries, project add carries `code` exactly when it carries `error`, and `tracker_error` and `no_tracker` are legitimately absent keys.

Incident: an early probe's `chmod` through a symlink briefly broke the shared scratchpad directory's mode; it was restored to 700 immediately and no files were lost.

## Review of moai-z46r (105fa41e..HEAD), xhigh, with --fix applied

The core feature works. I found no bug in screen selection, the closing paths or the layout handling: picking a screen never toggles, `SPC g l`/`b` close the stats window before switching layout, and the wheel does nothing while the menu is open. I also checked how the current screen is worked out (`Ctx::screen()` reads `mode` and `layout`), how the `layout` saved in config is restored at startup (`apply_look`), and the background reread paths. Mode only changes through keys, so none of those leaves a stale screen. The findings are a missing CHANGELOG entry, one gap in notice carry-over, gaps in test coverage, and some comments that no longer match the code.

Full `cargo test` (dev) passes after the fixes: 1773 unit and 670 integration tests. `scripts/bump-version.sh --next` still picks 0.5.0. Nothing is committed. The working tree has changes in `CHANGELOG.md`, `src/tui/menu.rs`, `src/tui/mod.rs` and `src/tui/stats.rs`. I did not touch `.moai/`.

- **CHANGELOG.md**: added a `### Changed` entry under [Unreleased]. It covers the new `SPC g l/b/s`, the removal of `SPC v b` and `SPC p s` with no alias, that choosing is not a toggle, the root menu showing `+screen [board]`, and the `SPC` menu over the stats window.
- **`src/tui/stats.rs` stats_key**:
  - When the window's own table leaves a key waiting, it now returns `w.chord.held().is_empty()`, so the window's waiting `g` keeps the notice the way browse does.
  - Rewrote the doc to say what the return value means: whether this key clears the notice.
  - Fixed the doc of `a_move_key_closes_the_menu_over_the_window_and_scrolls_it`.
- **`src/tui/stats.rs` tests**:
  - Extended `a_move_key_closes_the_menu_over_the_window_and_scrolls_it`. It now checks that opening the menu throws away a waiting `g` (pressing g, SPC, Esc, g does not reach the top), and that Bksp goes `SPC g` → `SPC` → closes the menu while the window stays.
  - Added `the_menu_over_the_window_keeps_the_notice_until_a_key_acts`. These keys keep the notice: SPC, g, Bksp, Esc, `SPC j`, and the window's waiting g. These clear it: the window's gg, and `SPC g s`.
- **`src/tui/mod.rs`**:
  - Moved the stats intercept above the text-input comment, so each block has its own comment again.
  - Rewrote the `B::Go` comment for all three screens.
  - Extended the Mode::Stats doc to say `SPC g l` and `SPC g b` also close the window.
- **`src/tui/menu.rs`**:
  - The root-layer branch of `a_move_key_closes_the_menu_and_moves` now asserts that `g` goes down into `SPC g`, and the gg comment sits above the gg code again.
  - Added `SPC o` to the `waits` doc.

### Skipped
- **#12, Key::any vs Key::bare**: not fixed, because fixing it inside stats_key just trades one inconsistency for another. If the menu path is made to use the window's bare table, a Ctrl-Down over the menu closes it and does nothing. That breaks the rule that a move which does nothing leaves the menu open ('조용히 꺼진 이동도 메뉴를 안 닫는다'). The proper fix is to switch the arrow and page rows in the STATS table to Key::any, which is outside this diff. It is low severity.
- **keys.rs "SPC 밑 묶음은 넷이다"** lists seven groups, but it reads as "the four from moai-en4u, plus p, g and o". I counted it as a false positive.

### What decides the outcome
- The window's `g` notice change touches behaviour the epic did not set out to change. Before, routing through `typing()` dropped the notice by accident. I aligned it with the documented browse rule. If the worker wants a strictly minimal scope, revert the `None => return w.chord.held().is_empty()` arm and the last `"g"` in the new test's loop.
