Fable design notes for the project wiki (2026-10-04, read-only planner; the person took every recommendation — 자리 docs/, 마크다운만, 탐색기는 읽기만, 7-4 + 부르면 훑기, 페이지는 영어)

## 요약
- 위키는 저장소 안의 마크다운 파일 묶음이다. 자리는 `.moai/config.toml` 의 평평한 키 `wiki_dir`(기본 `docs`), 페이지 = `<wiki_dir>/**/*.md` 하나, 슬러그 = 확장자 뗀 상대 경로, 제목 = 첫 `# ` 줄(없으면 파일 이름). 색인은 파일에서 읽는다 — `issues.jsonl` 에는 한 글자도 안 들어간다
- 위키 파일은 문서라 가지를 탄다. 트래커의 워크트리→루트 옮김(`store::Repo::redirect`)을 받지 않고 `Repo::here()` 밑에서 읽는다. 그래서 `.moai/` 밖에 둔다. 병합은 git 기본 3-way, 충돌 표시가 든 페이지는 원문으로 보이고 `conflict` 알림 하나가 선다
- 형식은 마크다운만. `pulldown-cmark` 0.13.4 가 이미 의존성이라 비용 0. org 는 유일한 러스트 파서 `orgize` 가 2024-06 알파에 멈춰 있고, `TODO`/`DONE` 헤드라인 키워드가 moai 칸 낱말과 부딪혀 둘째 어휘가 된다. 문은 열어 둔다 — 로더가 확장자로 가르고, 그리는 쪽은 표면 중립 `markdown::Block` 만 받는다
- 탐색기는 `SPC g w` 로 위키 창(통계 창 `Mode::Stats` 와 같은 덮는 창)을 연다. 왼쪽 목록, 오른쪽 본문(`body_lines`), `Enter` 로 링크·이슈 id 고르기, id 는 창을 닫고 `App::land(id)`. 읽기만 한다
- CLI 는 `moai wiki ls`·`moai wiki show <slug>`(둘 다 `--json`). 쓰는 명령은 없다
- 자동 매뉴얼은 일꾼 브리프 7-4(7-3 CHANGELOG 의 형제)가 맡고, 그 걸음이 가리키는 글이 셋째 스킬 `moai-wiki` 다. 레퍼런스(`docs/cli.md`)는 지금처럼 `--help` 에서 생성·시험되고, 스킬은 베끼지 말고 가리키라 한다. 아무것도 막지 않는다
- v0.6.0 = 에픽 넷(저장·CLI / 탐색기 창 / 스킬·브리프 / 첫 페이지). org·`$EDITOR` 편집·`moai show` 의 Pages 절은 뒤로

## A. 저장 — 근거
- `.moai/wiki/` 를 안 고른 까닭: `.moai` 는 `tracker_root`(`worktree.rs:1246`)가 루트로 옮기는 자리라 한 디렉터리에 두 규칙이 선다. 또 훅 규칙 2 의 `SKIP`(`hook.rs:8155`)에 들어 위키 편집이 집은 일 없이 지나간다 — 매뉴얼은 에픽의 diff 에 들어야 한다
- 루트 `wiki/` 는 관례가 아니다. 이 저장소의 `docs/cli.md`(생성)·`docs/recovery.md`(손글)가 이미 매뉴얼의 시작이다
- `[[위키링크]]`: `pulldown-cmark` 의 `ENABLE_WIKILINKS` 로 공짜지만 GitHub 이 안 그린다. 한 어휘만 둔다
- 머지 드라이버·`merge=union` 은 산문을 겹쳐 쌓는다. 기본 3-way 가 맞다
- 근거 자리: `hook.rs:8153-8178`, `store.rs:111-160`·`:397-476`, `worktree.rs:1246-1249`·`:1446-1461`, `held.rs:75-160`, `config.rs:317-339`(`archive_days` 선례), `.gitattributes:17-21`, `id.rs:79 is_valid`

## B. 형식 — 잰 것
- 지금 그리는 길: `markdown::parse`(`markdown.rs:112-117`, `ENABLE_TABLES` 만)→`Block`→`layout`. 탐색기 상세는 `draw.rs:3660-3680 body_lines`, CLI 는 `view.rs:2616-2622`. 링크 주소는 `trail_url`(`markdown.rs:220-225`)이 뒤에 붙인다 — 위키 창의 `(글, 대상)` 목록은 `wiki.rs` 가 `Tag::Link{dest_url}` 을 한 번 더 훑어 모은다
- 바이너리 9,285,640바이트(15MB 의 59%). 위키 모듈·창은 +50~120KB 어림(못 쟀다)
- org 후보 `orgize`: 최신 0.10.0-alpha.10(2024-06-11), 의존 `rowan`·`nom 7`·`jetscii`·`bytecount`·`cfg-if`·`memchr`. 크기 +0.4~0.9MB 어림. org 를 고르면 첫 멤버는 `Cargo.toml:35-45` 의 `ureq` 표처럼 재는 일이다. 사내 부분집합 파서(300줄 안팎, 의존 0)가 먼저다

## C. 탐색기 — 안 고른 것
- 위키를 목록의 셋째 배치로: 페이지는 이슈가 아니라 커서·거름망·보기를 공유할 것이 없다
- 상세 칸 안에 페이지를 끼우기: 한 칸을 다투고 `/` 의 뜻이 갈린다
- 링크를 `Tab` 으로 본문 안에서 돌기: 펴진 줄에는 주소가 표식으로만 남아 다시 세야 한다. 고르기 창이 싸고 id 도 같은 창에 선다

## D. CLI — 안 고른 것
- `moai wiki new <slug>`: 스킬의 틀 한 줄로 충분
- `moai wiki put`: `with_write` 곁에 둘째 쓰기 경로가 선다. 합치는 자는 git 이다
- `moai show <id>` 의 Pages 절: 표면을 가로지르니 다음 판 idea

## E. 자동 매뉴얼 — 누가·언제
- 일꾼 창, 브리프 7-4. 워크트리에서 `docs(wiki):` 커밋으로 머지에 태운다(리뷰 가능 = 머지 diff)
- 사람이 부르는 훑기: 지난 릴리스 뒤 닫힌 에픽(`moai show --type epic -s done --done <폭> --json`)을 돌며 같은 물음을 묻고, 고칠 페이지 목록을 한 번 보인 뒤 `moai add '위키: …' -t docs` 로 집고 쓴다
- 릴리스: CONTRIBUTING "Releasing" 의 `bump-version.sh auto` 앞에 "스킬의 훑기를 한 번" 한 줄(선택, 게이트 아님)
- 감독은 안 쓴다. 일꾼 보고(11)에 "고친 페이지, 없으면 없다" 한 줄
- 읽는 것: `moai show <epic> --json`, 7-3 의 CHANGELOG 줄, `moai <명령> --help`, `moai wiki ls --json`

## F. 뒤로 미룬 것
- org(부분집합 파서 또는 크레이트 + 크기 측정), 탐색기 `e`→`$EDITOR`, `moai show <id>` 의 Pages 절, 한눈 보기 전체 위키 검색, 프런트매터·틀 명령, 위키 머지 드라이버, 감독의 확인, git 시각 대 `done_at` 으로 낡음 재기

## 일정
- 먼저: 저장·CLI 에픽과 스킬·브리프 에픽을 두 워크트리에서 나란히. 겹칠 자리는 CHANGELOG 이웃 줄과 `docs/cli.md` 재생성(받은 쪽이 `scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh` 를 한 번 더 돌린다)
- 그 뒤: 탐색기 창 에픽은 저장 에픽 머지 뒤. 첫 페이지 에픽은 저장·스킬 머지 뒤, 탐색기 창과 나란히
- `report`·`query`·`store::with_write`·`hook.rs`·`issues.jsonl` 은 네 에픽 어디서도 안 바뀐다

## 위험과 못 잰 것
- 바이너리·빌드 시간 증분은 어림이다(빌드 금지)
- 탐색기 실물을 못 봤다 — 따로 띄운 tmux 서버에서 SPC 가 리더로 안 들었다. 창 꼴은 `draw.rs:565-600` 코드로 잰 것이다
- `docs/` 기본값은 Sphinx·mkdocs 트리를 든 저장소에서 페이지가 많이 선다. 큰 생성 페이지(`docs/cli.md` 128KB)는 폭·페이지별로 한 번 펴서 들어야 한다
- 부름 받은 훑기가 `docs/` 를 고치면 집은 일이 있어야 한다 — 스킬이 `moai add -t docs` 를 먼저 시킨다
- 충돌 표시 판정은 git 을 설명하는 페이지에서 거짓 양성이 날 수 있다(알림이라 해롭지 않다)
- 슬러그의 대소문자·비ASCII 파일 이름·`wiki_dir` 가 링크인 경우·윈도 경로 구분자는 시험으로 못박는다
- 7-4 가 브리프를 늘린다 — 짧게 두고 본문은 스킬에 둔다

text:
2026-10-04 사람이 정했다(AskUserQuestion 한 번, 넷 다 권장안).

- `links`: 페이지 링크만 싣는다 — 상대 경로이고 `.md` 로 끝나며 위키 안에 떨어지는 링크. `to` 는 페이지 폴더 기준으로 푼 대상 슬러그(`../x.md` → `x`), `resolved` 는 그 페이지가 있는가(bool). 외부 URL·`#앵커`·`.md` 아닌 파일·위키 밖으로 나가는 링크는 안 싣는다
- `no_dir` 는 종료 코드 0 — 위키를 아직 시작 안 한 것은 상태다. `outside`·`not_a_dir` 는 설정이 틀린 것이라 비영
- `issues`: 본문과 인라인 코드의 id 는 세고, 울타리·들여쓴 코드 블록 안은 예시로 읽어 안 센다(work 줄 규칙과 같다). 저장소 접두어(`prefix`)가 맞는 낱말만 id 다 — `worktree-moai-xxxx` 같은 가지 이름은 id 가 아니다
- **`--json` 꼴에 선택 키 하나가 는다**: 못 읽은 페이지(1MB 초과·밖 링크·FIFO·UTF-8 아님)는 목록에 서고(제목은 파일 줄기) 그 쪽에만 `error:{"kind":"too_large|refused|failed","said":"…"}` 가 선다. 없으면 다 읽은 것 — `commits_error`·`journal_error` 와 같은 약속. moai-bl3x 에 알린다

text:
Fable design notes for multi-agent support (2026-10-04, read-only planner with web research). The person's answers: .agents/skills 공용, .moai/mail 파일, moai mcp 를 손으로 짠 stdio 로 넣는다(Fable 의 권장은 v0.8 로 미루기였다), 벤더의 길로 깨우기, 모델 열은 비우고 창의 모델, Codex 훅은 저장소 .codex/hooks.json

## 요약
1. 항상 읽히는 글은 이미 벤더 중립이다. `moai init` 의 AGENTS.md 블록을 Codex 는 1순위로, Antigravity(IDE·CLI `agy`)는 AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md 로, Claude Code 는 2.1.277 부터 직접(이 저장소는 CLAUDE.md 가 `@AGENTS.md` 로) 읽는다
2. 스킬 본문도 한 벌이다. 세 벤더 모두 Agent Skills 공개 표준(SKILL.md + name/description, agentskills.io)을 채택했다. Codex 와 Antigravity 는 같은 `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` 를 읽는다. 출처는 `src/guide.rs` 하나, 벤더별 렌더링은 글 안의 낱말표 한 칸
3. 훅은 Codex 에 거의 그대로 걸린다(stdin·stdout 꼴이 Claude 와 같다, 셸 도구 이름 `Bash`). 다른 것은 `apply_patch` 와 심는 자리(`.codex/hooks.json` + 신뢰). Antigravity 훅은 꼴이 달라 `cmd/hook.rs` 에 어댑터만 둔다. 판정(`hook.rs`)은 안 바뀐다
4. 통신은 `.moai/mail/` 우편함 + 훅이 배달 + 벤더별 깨우기. `moai send/inbox/agents/hello`. `issues.jsonl`·저널에는 안 든다
5. moai 는 다리(서버·프록시)가 되지 않는다. 데몬·소켓·HTTP 는 CLAUDE.md 의 새 축이고, 감독 프로토콜은 파일 + 훅 + 벤더의 깨우기 명령으로 선다
6. 역할·출석은 `.moai/agents/<name>.json`. 감독의 `~/.claude/sessions/*.json`(비문서) 읽기는 `moai agents --json` 으로 바뀐다
7. 리뷰·묻기·창 비우기는 낱말표의 열이다

## 조사 결과
| 무엇 | 날짜·성숙도 | 출처 | moai 판단 |
|---|---|---|---|

## Review of epic moai-ihu4 (wiki), xhigh, `--fix`

I found 14 issues and fixed 12. The full suite passes (1784 unit, 678 cli), and `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy --all-targets` are clean. Nothing is committed; the changes are in the worktree's working tree.

1. src/wiki.rs:411 — A page that starts with a UTF-8 BOM loses its title: `# Title` is no longer read as a heading. A page saved by a Windows editor, `﻿# Bom title`, lists with title `bom` (the file name), and `show` draws the heading as plain text.
2. src/wiki.rs:404 — A page that opens but is not UTF-8 reports `bytes: 0`, although the docs say 0 means the page could not be opened. `docs/latin.md` (11 bytes, Latin-1) → `"bytes":0,"error":{"kind":"failed"}`.
3. src/view/wiki.rs:499 — The 'not read' mark suggests `moai wiki show <slug>` without quoting the slug. Slug `out side` → it suggests `moai wiki show out side`, which clap rejects as two arguments.
4. src/wiki.rs:707 — `notices` lists the same broken link once for every link that points to it. `[gone](gone.md) [again](gone.md)` → `Links leading to no page 2  README → gone, README → gone`.
5. tests/cli.rs:23407 — A test assertion can never fail: it checks for no conflict notice on README, which has no conflict. Reverting `Notices { conflict: Vec::new(), .. }` in `view::wiki::page` leaves the test green.
6. src/cmd/wiki.rs:60 — Nothing tests that ids on unreadable tracker lines count as existing. Removing `.chain(reserved)` leaves every test green.
7. CHANGELOG.md:13 — `[Unreleased]` was empty, although member moai-ihu4.083 promised a CHANGELOG entry. `bump-version.sh --next` stops on an empty `[Unreleased]`.
8. src/cmd/wiki.rs:228 — `ls --json` does not include the entries the walk skipped (directory links, non-UTF-8 names, unreadable directories). The exit code is 1 and `pages` looks complete; the reason is only in human-readable stderr.
9. src/cli.rs:820 — The `wiki ls` help never says that an unreadable page (other than one over 1 MB) or a skipped entry makes the exit code non-zero. The `show --json` help omits the `{dir,error}` output shape.

I found six problems in the three wiki pages and fixed all six in the working tree; none were skipped. The fixes are uncommitted. I couldn't submit them through ReportFindings because that tool isn't available in this session, so the list below is the only record.

After the fixes, `./target/release/moai wiki ls --json` shows no conflict, no unresolved links and no unknown ids on any page.

**Findings**
1. `docs/workflow.md:66` (medium): the page says other sessions see a pick-up "only once it is committed" in the main checkout. That has been wrong since moai-y7go. A `moai` run in any worktree reads the main checkout's tracker file directly (`src/store.rs`), so a pick-up shows to every session on the clone as soon as it is written; committing only matters for other clones. The rule also comes from this repository's `CLAUDE.md` but sits in the generic part of the page. I rewrote it to "Pick up first, then make the worktree", with the correct reason.
2. `docs/workflow.md:69` (low): it says only a worktree at `.claude/worktrees/<id>` or on branch `worktree-<id>` counts. The code (`worktree::names`/`from_label` in `src/worktree.rs`) also counts any worktree directory named `<id>` and a branch named plain `<id>`. A reader using another layout would wrongly expect a "stranded" warning. I listed all three.
3. `docs/workflow.md:73` (low): it hard-codes `docs/` as where wiki pages live. The directory can be changed with `wiki_dir` in `.moai/config.toml`, and this part of the page is meant to hold in any repository. I named the key.
4. `docs/explorer.md:17` (low): it describes the `--path lost` basket as rows "whose epic cannot be found". The code (`misplace_of` in `src/report.rs`, `src/nav.rs`) also puts there epics whose milestone is missing and rows under a parent whose id appears twice with conflicting lines. I widened the wording.
5. `docs/agents.md:81` (low): the rule 1 sentence "…which this rule never stops, and so is a whole plan through `moai add --from`" doesn't parse, and reads as if a plan were "something for later". It now reads "…nor does it stop a whole plan created with `moai add --from`".
6. `docs/agents.md:136` (low): it says the two hand-run `claude plugin` lines mean `claude` is not on `PATH`. `src/cmd/skill.rs` prints them whenever registration fails, so other causes would be misdiagnosed. It now says "the registration did not go through — most often `claude` is not on PATH".

Finding 1 also touches the repository's `CLAUDE.md`: its line "집기는 develop 에서 커밋한다" (commit the pick-up on develop) gives the same visibility reason, which no longer holds. I didn't change `CLAUDE.md` because it is outside this review's scope.

text:
I found 9 problems in the moai-m6ni diff and fixed all of them in the working tree. One is a real bug: clicking the `…` at the end of a cut-off menu line ran an item the user couldn't see. Nothing is committed.

```json
[
  {"file":"src/tui/draw.rs","line":4238,"summary":"`span_at` trims a menu cell's click area at `room`, but when a line overflows `fit` puts `…` in the last column, so an item whose key falls on that column is clickable while only `…` shows.","failure_scenario":"At 15x6 the menu folds onto one line and `f` sits under the `…` at column 14. Clicking the `…` opens the filter prompt, an item the user cannot see. Confirmed with a test that sweeps widths."},
  {"file":"src/tui/mouse.rs","line":131,"summary":"No test checks that only a left click on a menu cell presses its key; changing the button check to `Down(_)` kept every test green.","failure_scenario":"A right or middle click on `/ : search` would open the search prompt without any test failing. This was meant to do nothing."},
  {"file":"src/tui/mouse.rs","line":136,"summary":"Only right-click is tested outside the menu; release, middle click, drag and plain movement outside it are not.","failure_scenario":"Changing the check to `!Down(Right)` stayed green. A mouse button release outside the menu would then close it, even though release, drag and right-click with the menu open must do nothing new."},
  {"file":"src/tui/draw.rs","line":370,"summary":"Click areas on the bottom line over the stats window were untested.","failure_scenario":"Dropping `menu_keys.extend(...)` in the stats branch stayed green. `Bksp` on the bottom line over the stats window would silently stop responding to clicks."},
  {"file":"src/tui/draw.rs","line":4209,"summary":"`menu_panel` works out where cells are clicked (`at.x+1`, `at.y+1`, `width-2`) by hand instead of asking the box it paints with, so painting and clicking come from two separate calculations.","failure_scenario":"Changing the box's padding or border would shift every click area away from the painted cell with no compile error. Rows taller than the box would also get click areas."},
  {"file":"src/cli.rs","line":524,"summary":"`tui --help` says 'a click or a roll anywhere else closes the menu', but empty space inside the menu and the wheel over it do nothing.","failure_scenario":"A user clicks the divider line or a gap between columns expecting the menu to close, and nothing happens. The same text is in the generated `docs/cli.md`."},
  {"file":"README.md","line":135,"summary":"The README says 'a click anywhere else closes the menu', which is wrong for empty space inside the menu, and 'to run it', which does not fit groups (they go down a level).","failure_scenario":"It describes behaviour the code does not have."},
  {"file":"src/tui/mouse.rs","line":11,"summary":"The module's head comment never says that clicking a menu cell presses its key, and 'the stats window hears only the wheel' is no longer true.","failure_scenario":"Someone reading it thinks the stats window ignores clicks, but clicks on its menu now work. Focus item 4 asked for exactly this check."},
  {"file":"src/tui/draw.rs","line":4383,"summary":"`menu_line` splits the exit list into two vectors and then joins them back together just to measure the width.","failure_scenario":"Extra code to read and keep in sync; a single sum over the pairs does the same job."}
]
```

**Fixed**
- **The `…` bug:** `span_at` is replaced by `cells_at`, which trims click areas the same way `fit` trims the line: if the line overflows, one column fewer is visible. Both `menu_panel` and `menu_line` collect their cells first and place them once the line is built.
- **One calculation:** `menu_panel` now takes the clickable area from the box it paints with (`block.inner(at)`), and rows taller than the box get no click areas.
- **New test `a_menu_cell_takes_clicks_only_where_its_key_shows`:** it sweeps widths 8–120 for the folded line and the grid, at the top level and `SPC v`, and checks that every click area shows its own key on the rendered screen. It fails on the old code (15x6, `f` under `…`).
- **Stronger existing tests:** right/middle click on a cell does nothing; right, middle, release, drag and plain movement outside the menu keep it open and don't move the list; `Bksp` on the bottom line over the stats window goes up one level. I re-ran all three mutations from above, and each now fails a test.
- **Docs:** `tui --help` now says "outside the menu", `docs/cli.md` is regenerated from it, the README is reworded, and the `mouse.rs` head comment is updated.
- **Simplification:** removed the split-and-rejoin in `menu_line`.

`cargo fmt --check` passes, `cargo clippy --all-targets` shows no warnings, and `cargo test` passes in full (1792 + 678).

**Checked and left alone**
- On review questions 1, 3 and 5:

  - **One place sets it up:** `Drawn` is written only in `draw::screen`, and click areas are recorded on all three draw paths.
  - **Menu closed:** mouse handling behaves exactly as before.
- **Divider drag with the menu open:** with the detail pane below the list, clicking the divider closes the menu and the layout grows, so on the first drag step the line jumps back under the pointer. I read that as the line following the hand, not a defect.
- **Release notes:** `CHANGELOG.md` has no line for this epic yet. The worker brief puts that step (7-3) after the review, so I didn't count it as a finding, but it's still owed before the merge.

I found nine issues in `7775a617..HEAD` and fixed eight. The ninth, the most serious, can't be fixed in code without changing a design you decided, so I documented it instead. Everything is uncommitted in the moai-p3r9 worktree. `cargo test` passes (1798 + 678), clippy is clean, and the new test fails when its fix is reverted.

**What I fixed:**
- **Finding 2 (code):** `refresh` now keeps the re-read line (`again`). On a failed ask it carries that line's tag and heard time, and falls back to the first read only when the re-read has no tag. New test `a_failed_ask_carries_the_tag_a_lower_sibling_heard_meanwhile`; with the old line put back it fails with `v0.0.1` instead of `v0.0.2`.
- **Finding 4:** corrected the doc, and the 0.1.1 test now also checks the no-`asked_by` case. That case must give `Stale{NotAsked, …}`, so the arm order you asked about is now pinned.
- **Findings 3 and 5–9:** text, doc and test-helper corrections as listed in the table.

**Not fixed in code — finding 1 needs your decision.** A version number can't tell a source build from a release of the same version. Fixing it means recording something besides the version, or shortening the window for answers already marked outdated, and either one changes the "re-ask once" decision from 2026-10-04. I wrote the limitation into the `outdated` doc. It matters here because the bump-then-build-before-the-tag flow in CONTRIBUTING.md is exactly the case that triggers it. Do you want to reopen that decision, or accept a one-day "ahead" after a release on machines that ran a build from the bump commit?

**Your specific questions:**
- **Network on `--json` or piped runs:** none. `gate` and `asking_from` are unchanged, and `held()` never asks.
- **Asking on every start:** only when the config directory is read-only, and that was already true and documented. An offline machine asks once, because a failed ask counts (tested). Binaries of different versions used alternately stay within one extra ask per lower-version ask.
- **Older binaries rewriting `tag` but leaving `asked_by`:** their tag comes from the same URL and is heard later, so reading it that way holds. The exceptions are the pre-moai-dael mirror case already documented, and the case in finding 1.
- **Odd tags:** they never count as outdated, so they still come out as `OddTag`.
- **Doc blocks:** no Rust doc comment got attached to the wrong item. The only takeover was prose (finding 5).
- **Tests failing on revert:** each part of the change has a test that fails when it is reverted. I actually reverted only the carry fix; the rest I traced by hand.

원인을 찾았다 — 바깥 터미널(Ghostty)이 넓은 글자의 고아 반쪽을 펜 바탕으로 지운다

- 사람의 바깥 터미널: `tmux list-clients` 의 `client_termtype` 이 `ghostty 1.3.1` 이었다(pane 0 은 120x69)
- 꼴: 다 읽은 카드의 제목이 넓은 글자로 열리고(`커밋된 …`) 그 위에 안 읽은 카드가 새로 서면, 새 카드의 `[NEW]` 가
  옛 제목이 섰던 줄에 내려앉아 `]` 가 셋째 글자(`된`)의 머리 칸을 덮는다
  - Ghostty 는 넓은 글자의 머리에 좁은 글자가 앉으면 꼬리 칸을 `Screen::clearCells` 로 지우고, 그 값은
    `blankCell()` — 커서 스타일의 바탕, 곧 그 순간의 노랑이다(Ghostty 소스 `Terminal.zig` printCell, `Screen.zig`)
  - ratatui 는 그 칸을 다시 안 낸다. 앞 프레임에서도 넓은 글자 뒤의 숨은 빈칸(`Cell::EMPTY`)이었고 새 프레임도
    `[NEW]` 뒤 빈칸이라 같다고 본다. ratatui-core 0.1.2 의 차이 셈은 **옛 글자의 바탕이 보일 때만** 꼬리를
    다시 낸다(`diff.rs` 의 `previous.bg != Color::Reset`) — 새 펜의 바탕은 안 본다
  - 그래서 `[NEW]` 바로 뒤 한 칸이 노랗게 남고, 그 칸을 바꿀 일이 없는 한 안 지워진다
- tmux 의 화면에 안 남는 까닭: tmux 는 고아 칸을 기본 칸으로 지우고(`screen_write_overwrite`) 바깥 터미널에는 새
  글자만 보낸다. 감독의 `capture-pane -e` 열두 장이 깨끗했던 것과 맞는다
- 잰 것
  - 내 tmux 서버(`-L c6go-r7k`)에 긁기 저장소로 보드를 열고 `script` 로 탐색기가 쓴 바이트를 떴다. 다 읽은 뒤 새
    이슈를 더하고 20 장을 `capture-pane -e` 로 떴다 — tmux 화면은 노란 칸 0
  - 같은 바이트를 작은 VT 재생기로 두 규칙에 돌렸다: 고아를 기본 바탕으로 지우면(tmux) 17 프레임 중 0, 펜
    바탕으로 지우면(Ghostty) 마지막 프레임까지 `[NEW]` 뒤 (51,13) 한 칸이 노랗게 남았다
- 고침: `tui::paint::Painter` 가 앞 프레임을 들고, 넓은 글자가 섰던 자리를 다른 것이 덮으면 그 꼬리 칸을
  `CellDiffOption::AlwaysUpdate` 로 적어 늘 내보낸다. 탐색기 루프의 그림은 모두 여기를 지난다

고친 뒤 잰 것 — 앞 노트의 `tui::paint::Painter` 는 `tui::draw::Painter` 로 섰다

- 새 파일(`src/tui/paint.rs`)로 두면 조각 훑기(`input.rs` 의 `NOT_COMPONENTS`)에 올려야 하는데 그 줄(배열 길이 8→9)을
  moai-o3cb 가 쥐고 있어서 draw.rs 에 두었다. draw.rs 의 헌크는 o3cb 의 것(148~379·1000~1290)과 안 겹친다
- 긁기 저장소, 모든 제목이 넓은 글자 셋으로 열리게 세우고 다 읽은 뒤 새 이슈를 더했다. 고치기 전 바이너리(루트의 develop
  빌드)와 고친 바이너리를 같은 판에 돌렸다 — Ghostty 규칙으로 재생한 마지막 프레임의 `[NEW]` 밖 노란 칸
  - 보드: 고치기 전 1칸(`[NEW]` 바로 뒤), 고친 뒤 0
  - 목록(커서를 맨 아래로 옮긴 판): 고치기 전 1칸, 고친 뒤 0
  - tmux 규칙으로는 네 판 다 0 — tmux 화면에는 안 남는다
- 목록에서 커서가 `[NEW]` 가 내려앉는 줄에 서 있으면 고치기 전에도 안 남았다. 그 줄은 반전이라 ratatui 가 제 규칙(옛 글자의
  `REVERSED` 가 빈칸에 보인다)으로 이미 꼬리를 다시 냈다 — 사람이 보드에서 본 것과 맞는다(카드의 몸줄은 반전이 아니다)
- 시험: `draw::tests::painting::a_new_card_leaves_no_yellow_cell_where_a_wide_glyph_stood` — Ghostty 의 지우기를 흉내 낸
  터미널(`Glass`)에 `Painter` 로 두 프레임을 그린다. `mend` 를 빼면 (48,5) 한 칸으로 붉어진다

**Fixed (findings 1–12):**
- **1:** the chooser now keeps its own chord, and a waiting `g` keeps the notice and shows the next keys in the bar.
- **2:** `wiki_pointer` now ignores mouse events whenever the mouse is released.
- **3:** the notice now names only what hid the row (filter, view, or both); the view part comes from `veiled_row`, so archived rows get the archive key. `tui.wiki.hidden` is replaced by `tui.wiki.veiled_filter` in en and ko.
- **4:** while typing, the cursor goes back to the page you were on when you pressed `/`.
- **5:** the pane is measured before lines are cut, the same order the detail uses.
- **6:** page text is lowercased once when the window opens.
- **7:** the explorer wiki page now has an SPC g w entry and the wheel line covers the wiki panes.
- **8:** the empty-wiki notice now adds the skipped count.
- **9:** a line break inside link text becomes a space.
- **10–11:** both comments corrected.
- **12:** the border code is shared through one helper, `pane_frame`.

**Skipped:**
- **13:** too minor to change behaviour for.
- **14:** the statistics window behaves the same way on a failed re-open, so I left it consistent.

**Your five checks:**
1. **Doc blocks:** no inserted item takes over a neighbour's doc. Each new item has its own `///`.
2. **Tests going red:** each fix above has a test that fails when the fix is reverted.
3. **One setup path:** all three ways of opening the window go through `show_wiki`. Every way of closing it leaves nothing behind except `drawn.wiki`, which lasts until the next frame and is harmless because mouse handling checks the mode first.
4. **Docs vs code:** the four user decisions are implemented as documented. The help text's `gg` in the chooser was untrue until fix 1.
5. **Nothing new on old paths:** the wiki is read only on SPC g w. `App::follow` and `draw::screen` don't touch it when the window is closed.

**Committing:** this splits into `fix:` commits for the code and a `docs(wiki):` commit for the explorer page. Use `git add -- docs` before that commit.

text:
The fix holds up. `mend` matches ratatui-core 0.1.2's diff and the explorer test goes red when `mend` is removed. I found no correctness bug that reaches the screen. I added two tests that were missing and a small cleanup, and left them uncommitted in `src/tui/draw.rs`. fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`) and the full `cargo test` all pass.

**Your checks (a)–(e):**
- **(a) Same cells as the diff:** yes. `mend` steps through `prev` glyph by glyph, using the same `CellWidth` as the diff. It catches both ways a head gets covered: a cell written at the head, or a new wide glyph whose tail lands on it. A marked tail that sits under a new wide glyph is skipped by the diff, so nothing extra goes out. The VS16 and old-glyph-bg paths in the diff also handle a marked cell correctly.
- **(b) `last` equals ratatui's previous buffer:** yes.
  - `done.buffer` is the buffer just drawn, after the swap.
  - On autoresize, ratatui resets its previous buffer, and `mend` returns early because the sizes differ.
  - After `resume()` both ratatui buffers are empty, and `forget()` matches that.
  - On the first frame `last` is `None`.
  - If `draw` fails, `last` stays `None` and the loop exits anyway.
- **(c) Leftover `AlwaysUpdate`:** one extra emit per marked cell, as expected. Cell equality includes `diff_option`, so the next frame re-emits that cell once, and the frame after compares equal.
- **(d) Glass model and red-on-revert:** Glass matches Ghostty's three clearing cases (narrow print on a head, any print on a tail, a new glyph's tail landing on a head). With the `mend` call stubbed out, the `[NEW]` test fails with a stray yellow cell at `(48, 5)`.
- **(e) Clone cost:** about 12k cells (~0.5 MB) per frame on a 200×60 screen. That is a few percent of a frame. It was also a fresh allocation every frame, which is now reused (finding 3).

**The five:**
1. No inserted item took over a doc block below it.
2. Before this review, reverting the size check or the straddle case turned nothing red. Both do now.
3. The only real terminal loop draws through `Painter`. The tests that call `term.draw` directly use `TestBackend`, which extra emits don't affect.
4. Comments, docs and the CHANGELOG entry (under `### Fixed`) match the code.
5. Nothing new opens on any path.

The other worktree's lines were not touched. I read `banner()` there (1210–1290) and it was only relevant to finding 6.

Findings:

1. src/tui/draw.rs:4715 — The size check in mend is what keeps it from crashing, but no test exercised it; removing it panics with an index outside the buffer once the terminal grows, and no test went red.
   Failure: Frame N at 80x14; the user enlarges the window; frame N+1 at 100x20 makes mend read prev[(80,0)], ratatui panics, and the explorer exits through catch_unwind. Confirmed: with the check removed, the new test a_frame_of_another_size_is_not_mended_against_the_old_one panics in ratatui-core buffer.rs:251.
2. src/tui/draw.rs:4724 — The second path mend's doc names (a new wide glyph whose tail lands on an old head) had no test, and Glass's rule for a wide glyph's tail landing on a head was never exercised.
   Failure: If mend were narrowed to narrow cells covering a head, prev "a가bc" -> next "나" (yellow) would leave column 2 yellow in Ghostty with every test still green. The new test a_wide_glyph_straddling_onto_a_head_leaves_no_colour_behind fails with mend stubbed out.
3. src/tui/draw.rs:4694 — Painter::draw allocated a new screen-sized Buffer every frame (done.buffer.clone()) and dropped the old one.
   Failure: About 0.5 MB allocated and freed per frame at up to ~8 fps while a spinner runs; derived Buffer::clone_from also rebuilds from scratch, so the allocation only gets reused by cloning into `content`.
4. src/tui/draw.rs:4724 — mend's `!=` uses Cell's PartialEq, which includes diff_option, so an AlwaysUpdate mark it left on a new wide glyph's head makes that unchanged glyph count as covered on the next frame.
   Failure: prev "가" at 0 -> next "a나": mend marks 나's head (col 1). Next frame 나 is unchanged, but prev[1] carries AlwaysUpdate, so mend marks col 2, which is 나's hidden tail. Nothing visible: ratatui skips the tail and re-emits 나 once anyway. The doc says 'covered by something else'; the code means 'differs in any field'.
5. src/tui/draw.rs:4722 — Latent: mend ignores CellDiffOption::Skip. It treats a Skip head in prev as drawn, and forces tails out even when next's head cell is Skip and is never emitted.
   Failure: A widget that marks a wide cell Skip (image or link passthrough): ratatui does not emit the head, mend forces the tail, and the terminal blanks the head it still shows with the pen's bg. This is the orphan mend exists to prevent. The explorer uses no Skip cells today.
6. src/tui/draw.rs:10578 — stray_yellow flags every LightYellow cell outside "[NEW]" except on rows that open with '!', but the explorer draws other LightYellow text that does not open with '!'.
   Failure: A banner of only soft notices (draw.rs:212, no '!' lead), the hung badge (draw.rs:1806) or the ask line (draw.rs:343) appearing on the test board would turn a_new_card_leaves_no_yellow_cell_where_a_wide_glyph_stood red with mend working. Checking only cells that were wide-glyph tails in `before` would avoid that.

**Fixed:**
- **Findings 1 and 2:** `Painter::draw` now calls a private `paint(term, render)`, so tests can draw arbitrary frames through Glass without an `App`. I added `a_wide_glyph_straddling_onto_a_head_leaves_no_colour_behind` and `a_frame_of_another_size_is_not_mended_against_the_old_one`. Each goes red on the revert it guards: the first with `mend` stubbed out, the second with the size check removed.
- **Finding 3:** `paint` keeps the old buffer and copies into it (`keep.content.clone_from(...)`) instead of allocating a new one each frame.

**Skipped:**
- **Finding 4:** nothing visible changes. The extra mark only lands on a hidden tail, and ratatui would re-emit that head anyway.
- **Finding 5:** nothing in the codebase uses Skip, so guarding it would be code for a case that doesn't exist.
- **Finding 6:** narrowing the check would change what the test is meant to catch (any stray yellow on the screen). It passes here, so I left it.

Something to consider passing upstream: ratatui-core's diff doesn't handle the case where a new wide glyph's tail lands on an old head at all, even when the old glyph's background is visible. `mend` covers it here.

Review (code-review xhigh --fix, agent-a6d8df18d7c9b6762) — reviewer's own words

I found 15 issues in the moai-fyul epic and fixed 13 of them in the worktree. Nothing is committed. The full test suite passes (1830 and 678 tests), as do clippy and `cargo fmt --check`. Each new or extended test failed when I temporarily took its fix back out, and failed for the right reason.

On your five checks:
1. **Doc comments on the wrong item:** none. One old comment was left describing code it no longer matched (finding 9).
2. **Tests going red when their fix is reverted:** mostly yes. Two gaps were in the key-level reset: `h` and `Tab` were never tested, and neither was the `SPC v w` toggle (findings 3 and 4).
3. **One place sets it up:** two gaps. The `SPC v w` toggle didn't reset the scrolled list, and `unfold`/`fold` reset it a second time alongside `App::key`.
4. **Docs match code:** several small mismatches, all fixed.
5. **Nothing newly opened:** `roll` had been widened to `pub(super)`. I made it private again.

The one real bug: the wheel now moves the scroll position straight away, but the event loop takes a burst of wheel events plus the click that follows before it redraws. A click right after the wheel therefore picked a row offset by however far the wheel had scrolled, both in the explorer list and in the wiki page list. Clicks are now matched against the position the last frame was drawn with.

Findings:
1. src/tui/mouse.rs:287 — A click on the list is matched using the live scroll position, which the wheel now changes before any redraw, so a click that arrives with a wheel burst picks the wrong row. Scenario: 40 rows; two wheel notches (position 0→6, not drawn yet); the same batch delivers a click on the third row on screen (argos-0003) → the cursor lands on argos-0009, six rows below what was clicked.
2. src/tui/mouse.rs:241 — The wiki page-list click has the same mismatch: it uses the live scroll position of the list the wheel just moved. Scenario: README plus 30 pages; one wheel notch over the list (position 0→3); a click on the second row on screen (p01) in the same batch → p04 opens instead.
3. src/tui/mod.rs:164 — The saved scrolled-list state ignores the worktree overlay, so `SPC v w` leaves the list scrolled away from the cursor. This contradicts the 2026-10-03 rule that `SPC v` toggles show the cursor again, and the CHANGELOG's 'a view toggle … shows the cursor's row again'. Scenario: scroll the list with PageDown twice (cursor off screen), press `SPC v w`; the list is re-read with sibling-worktree rows but stays scrolled and the cursor's row stays hidden.
4. src/tui/mod.rs:6923 — The key-level reset covers `l`, `h` and `Tab`, but the test only pressed `l`. Scenario: narrowing that check to `l` alone keeps every test green while `h`/`Tab` on an off-screen group row no longer scroll back to it.
5. src/tui/mod.rs:4861 — `unfold`/`fold` still reset the scrolled state themselves, though their only caller `App::key` now resets it before dispatching. Two places own one reset, against the 'one place sets it up' rule. Scenario: changing the reset rule in one place leaves the other behind and the two disagree.
6. src/tui/mod.rs:5354 — `roll` (formerly the private `board_roll`) became `pub(super)`, which opens it to the whole crate although only the child module `mouse` calls it. Scenario: code outside `tui` (e.g. cmd::tui) can now scroll the explorer and detach it, a path that never existed before.
7. src/tui/mod.rs:1331 — The `App::adrift` doc says seven places reset the scrolled state but lists eight. Scenario: a reader auditing the reset paths trusts a count that doesn't match the code.
8. src/tui/mouse.rs:38 — The docs for `Drawn::rows` and `WikiAt::rows` say on-screen row n is the current scroll position plus n, which is no longer true between frames. Scenario: the doc points readers at exactly the mapping that produces finding 1.
9. src/tui/draw.rs:2348 — A comment says the cursor was already revealed above so the widget won't move it, which is false while the list is scrolled away. Scenario: the comment hides why the off-screen-cursor filter just below it is needed.
10. src/cli.rs:453 — The `moai tui --help` text 'and so does the wheel' reads as if the wheel scrolls half or whole pages; it scrolls three rows. Scenario: a user expects one notch to move half a page.
11. src/tui/layer.rs:1274 — The `leave_project` comment and the `flip_layout` doc (mod.rs:4677) still describe the reset as board-only. Scenario: they say board-only while the same reset also covers the list.
12. src/tui/draw.rs:155 — The menu-layout comment says the list always reveals the cursor at the reduced height, which no longer holds for a scrolled list. Scenario: the comment misstates behaviour when the SPC menu opens over a scrolled list.
13. docs/explorer.md:62 — The wiki section lists only the wheel and Ctrl-d/Ctrl-u as scrolling the page list; Ctrl-f/Ctrl-b do too (the CLI help says so). Scenario: the two manuals disagree.
14. src/tui/zones.rs:214 — Changing the timezone with a date filter active re-applies the filter, so the list can change, but the saved scrolled-list state doesn't track the timezone. Scenario: a filter such as `created=2026-10-01` is active and the list is scrolled away; `SPC o t` changes which rows match, but the list stays scrolled with the cursor hidden.
15. src/tui/mod.rs:6851 — The test checks 'scrolled to the end' with `below()==0`, which cannot detect overshoot because `above()` clamps. Scenario: if the scroll stopped clamping at the end, this assertion would still pass; only the mouse test's post-render check would catch it.

Fixed (findings 1–13):
- Findings 1–2: added a `top` field (the scroll position the last frame was drawn with) to `Drawn` and `WikiAt`, filled in `draw::screen` / `wiki_window`, and both clicks now use it. New tests: `a_click_right_after_the_wheel_takes_the_row_on_screen` (mouse.rs) and `a_click_right_after_the_wheel_takes_the_page_on_screen` (wiki.rs).
- Finding 3: `worktree` is now part of the saved scrolled-list state, and `SPC v w` was added to `rebuilding_a_rolled_list_shows_the_row`.
- Finding 4: `the_next_cursor_key_brings_the_rolled_list_back_to_the_row` now also presses `h` and `Tab`.
- Finding 5: removed the extra resets from `unfold`/`fold`, so `App::key` is the only place; the board header tests still pass. After this, the "seven" in finding 7 is accurate, and that doc was reworded to match.
- Findings 6–13: `roll` is private again, and the comments, docs and help text are corrected. Regenerated `docs/cli.md` with `scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh` from a dev build; only the one help line changed.

Skipped:
- Finding 14: a timezone change behaves like a re-read today. Making it reset the scroll changes intended behaviour, so it needs a call.
- Finding 15: low value, and the mouse test already catches overshoot.

## Review of moai-8zz4 (wiki walk counts what it cannot read), high, `--fix`

I found 5 issues in the change. None of them breaks behaviour. I fixed 3 of them in the working tree and left 2 alone. The fixes are not committed yet; per the repo rules they should go in as a separate `fix:` commit. After the edits, all 1,841 unit tests in `cargo test --bin moai` pass, and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` are clean.

1. src/wiki.rs:492 — A file_type failure is reported as `unreadable` even when the error is NotFound, which means the entry was deleted while the walk was running. The new test's own doc comment names that deletion race as the usual cause. Failure: on a filesystem that gives no entry type (DT_UNKNOWN), `docs/scratch.txt` is deleted between listing the directory and checking it. The walk reports `docs/scratch.txt: could not be read — No such file or directory`, `moai wiki ls` exits non-zero, and `show --json` sets `linked_from_partial: true`, although no page was missed.
2. src/wiki.rs:351 — The doc comment on `load` still said that only directories it could not open and unreadable pages get recorded. It now also records directories it could not list to the end and names whose type it could not read. Failure: a reader trusting the doc assumes errors while listing a directory are still dropped silently, which is the exact behaviour this change removed.
3. src/cmd/wiki.rs:8 — The module doc on exit codes listed only directories and pages it could not open as reasons for a non-zero exit. The new skip kinds also cause one. Failure: someone reading why `wiki ls` exits non-zero finds no mention of a directory it could only list partly, or a name whose type it could not read.
4. src/wiki.rs:481 — The new code builds the directory's path for its `unreadable` row with a third copy of the same path-joining chain, already written out in the `path_of` closure and in `page_at`. Failure: there were three copies of the code that builds a page or skip row's path. If one changes alone, for example how `.` or an empty `wiki_dir` is handled, a page's `path` and a skip row's `path` drift apart.
5. src/wiki.rs:1344 — The test `what_the_walk_could_not_read_is_left_out_by_name` creates a real scratch directory, but the fake entries never touch the disk. Failure: the test creates a directory on disk it never needs. A plain path would do the same job.

### Fixed
- Duplicated path joining (finding 4): I added one helper, `place(shown, rel, last)`, in `src/wiki.rs` right after `slug_of`, with its own doc comment so it doesn't take over the doc block below it. The `path_of` closure, the directory's `unreadable` row and `page_at` all use it now.
- Stale doc on `load` (finding 2): updated to list all the skip cases.
- Stale module doc in `src/cmd/wiki.rs` (finding 3): updated the same way.

### Not fixed
- Deleted file counts as unreadable (finding 1): the change deliberately reports any type failure, `.md` or not, because the entry might have been a directory. Ignoring NotFound would change that intended behaviour, so it's your call.
- Scratch directory in the test (finding 5): harmless, so I left it.

### Your five checks
1. Doc comments on the wrong item: none. The new `Entry` trait and `Lost` test struct each have their own doc comment, and the comments below them are still in place.
2. Does a test go red on a revert: yes. Undoing either of the two drop sites fails the new test, and so does undoing the one-row-per-directory rule, the `.` path for the wiki root, or the hidden-name skip. Restoring the old `ReadDir`-only signature doesn't compile.
3. One place counts skips: yes. `Wiki::uncounted` and `fell_short` read `skipped`, and several listing errors in one directory collapse into one row. The TUI reads `skipped.len()` directly, but that code predates this change.
4. Comments and docs match the code: yes, apart from the two stale doc comments above. The claim that std's `ReadDir` stops after an error holds for Linux and macOS; I checked the std source.
5. Nothing newly opened: confirmed. A type failure returns before any `metadata` or `read_dir` call, and hidden names are skipped before their type is checked.

- SessionStart 는 늘 출석을 적고, 편지는 접힌 뒤(`compact`)에만 싣는다 — 붙는 것을 잰 자리는 거기뿐이다. startup·clear·resume 에서는 첫 UserPromptSubmit·Stop 이 싣는다
- 훅이 적는 Claude 세션의 이름은 `~/.claude/sessions/<claude pid>.json` 의 `name`(비문서 파일) — ListAgents·SendMessage 가 쓰는 그 이름이다. 못 읽으면 `claude-<세션 id 앞 8자>`. `moai hello --name` 이 늘 이긴다
- `any-idle-worker` 편지는 보낸 이와 역할이 `supervisor` 인 에이전트를 뺀 누구나 가진다 — `moai hello` 를 안 친 훅 등록 세션도 받는다

내가 정한 것(묻지 않았다)
- `SessionEnd` 훅은 안 건다 — 그 이벤트 목록은 `src/skill.rs` 의 `HOOKS` 이고 옆 에픽(moai-xs2h)이 쥔 파일이다. 끝난 세션은 `moai agents` 가 죽은 pid 로 걷는다(시작 시각으로 재사용을 가른다)
- 편지 id 는 파일 이름이다. 파일에는 안 적는다 — 파생값을 저장하지 않는다
- 새 편지는 temp 를 쓰고 `hard_link` 로 들인다 — `rename` 은 같은 이름을 말없이 덮는다. 들인 뒤 temp 를 지운다

실제 에이전트 실행 조건(2026-10-04, 사람이 이 기계에서 깔고 로그인하고 정했다)
- Codex 0.160.0: 이 컨테이너는 AppArmor(`cri-containerd.apparmor.d`)가 마운트를 막아 bwrap 샌드박스가 안 선다. 사람 결정으로 moai 일에서만 `codex -p moai` 를 쓴다 — `~/.codex/moai.config.toml` 의 `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`, 그 실행은 `approval: never` 다. 사람이 `codex -p moai exec` 로 셸 실행을 확인했다
- Antigravity CLI(agy) 1.2.16: 머리 없는 실행은 권한을 못 물어 명령이 막힌다. CLI 의 권한 규칙은 전역 `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` 하나뿐이라, 사람 결정으로 moai 일에서만 `agy --dangerously-skip-permissions` 를 붙여 부른다. 전역 설정은 안 바꾼다
- 그래서 두 벤더의 일꾼은 사람의 확인 없이 명령을 돌린다 — moai 훅(moai-u5wr 의 Codex·Antigravity 방언)이 그 일꾼을 지키는 유일한 장치다. 실제 Codex·agy 일꾼 시험은 u5wr 머지 뒤에 한다
- 감독 세션(Claude)에서 샌드박스 없이 `codex exec` 를 띄우는 것은 Claude 의 auto mode classifier 가 거절했다. 실제 에이전트 시험은 사람이 띄우거나 Claude 권한 규칙을 더해야 한다
- 헤드리스 예제(moai-b6cw)와 감독·브리프(moai-snyk)의 벤더 열은 이 두 부름 꼴(`codex -p moai`, `agy --dangerously-skip-permissions`)을 쓴다

- moai 의 감독은 claude·agy·codex 를 결코 직접 실행하지 않는다. 모두 같은 프로젝트에서 사람이 띄워 둔 대화형 세션과 통신한다. 일꾼도 리뷰나 확인을 위해 새 에이전트 프로세스를 띄우지 않는다

- Codex 는 샌드박스가 없어도 된다 — `codex -p moai`(`~/.codex/moai.config.toml` 의 `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`)로 띄우고, 확인은 대화형 기본대로 사람에게 묻는다
- 그래서 moai-b6cw 는 헤드리스 예제에서 "세 벤더의 세션을 프로젝트에 열어 두는 안내" 로, moai-snyk 의 리뷰는 "자기 세션 안의 기능" 으로, moai-u5wr 의 훅 입력 기록은 "사람이 띄운 대화형 세션에서" 로 고쳤다

Review of the whole epic diff (`64ac4d68..HEAD`, 21 files), `/code-review xhigh --fix`. Fixed 6 of the 10 findings. The full `cargo test` run passed after the fixes (1854 unit, 685 cli, 0 failed). The fixes are in the working tree and not committed.

1. src/cmd/skill.rs:160 — write_shared calls create_dir_all before any inside-the-checkout check, so a committed `.agents -> <outside>` link gets skills/moai/references/ built outside the checkout. Failure: a received repo commits `.agents -> ~/somewhere`. `moai skill install --agent codex` creates ~/somewhere/skills/{moai,moai-supervise,moai-wiki}/... and only then write_atomic_inside refuses the file. The 'links are followed only inside the checkout' rule (moai-4oab) holds for the file but not for the directories.
2. src/cmd/skill.rs:628 — uninstall lists `.agents/skills/<name>` through symlink_metadata without checking where `.agents` or `.agents/skills` lands, so the printed `rm -r` can delete a directory outside the checkout. Failure: `.agents -> /home/u/data` and /home/u/data/skills/moai exists. `skill uninstall --agent codex` prints `rm -r /repo/.agents/skills/moai`. Running it deletes /home/u/data/skills/moai, which moai never planted.
3. src/cmd/skill.rs:147 — found_line is shared by install and uninstall, but the auto_none text says 'planting for claude' / 'claude 로 심는다'. Failure: `moai skill uninstall --agent auto` on a machine with none of claude, codex or agy on PATH says 'planting for claude' while it removes.
4. src/skill.rs:1205 — every_skill_meets_the_agent_skills_frontmatter checks length and name shape but not that the unquoted description is valid single-line YAML. Failure: a future description containing ': ' or ' #', or starting with a quote or '-', still passes the test. Claude reads it leniently; an agent with a strict YAML parser (Codex) fails to load the skill.
5. CHANGELOG.md:30 — the rule-3 rewording, a change to text `moai init` already writes, is filed under Added. Failure: CLAUDE.md, release section: 'judge which section each CHANGELOG line goes in'; 'a behaviour change (Changed) is minor too'. Rewording output that already shipped is Changed, not Added.
6. src/cmd/skill.rs:176 — skill::skills(), which builds all four guide texts, is rebuilt several times per command. Failure: install builds it twice (place→plant, then agents_tree). status builds it 2+n times (place, once per hook, Shared::read). The same strings are formatted repeatedly for no gain.
7. src/hook.rs:8155 — hook rule 2's SKIP list exempts `.claude` (tool config) but not `.agents`, which is the same kind of generated tool tree. Failure: a Claude session hand-fixing .claude/moai-plugin/skills/moai/SKILL.md passes rule 2, but the identical .agents/skills/moai/SKILL.md is refused until work is picked up.
8. src/cmd/skill.rs:570 — skill status marks '.agents not planted', 'codex not on PATH' and 'agy not on PATH' with '!', even for a Claude-only user who never chose those agents. Failure: a repo whose Claude install is fully current now shows three '!' rows. The advice nudges the user to plant and commit a .agents/ directory they never asked for.
9. src/guide.rs:955 — rule 3 in the AGENTS block sends non-Claude agents to the 'Words per agent' table in the `moai` skill, but that table is not in AGENTS.md itself. Failure: a Codex user who reads AGENTS.md natively but never ran `--agent codex` is pointed at a table that does not exist in their checkout.
10. .agents/skills/moai-supervise/SKILL.md:3 — the supervisor description still says 'to the Claude sessions idling on it', though it is now planted for Codex and Antigravity too. Failure: in Codex or Antigravity the trigger text names only Claude sessions, which can blur when the skill is picked.

Fixed:
- #1: `write_shared` now runs a new `outside()` check (it resolves the deepest existing ancestor and rejects anything outside the checkout or inside `.git/`) before `create_dir_all`. It refuses with a message naming the link and where it lands.
- #2: `uninstall` lists nothing when `.agents/skills` lands outside the checkout. A new cli test, `skill_install_for_codex_builds_nothing_through_a_link_outside`, covers both #1 and #2.
- #3: the `skill.auto_none` text is now neutral in en and ko ("taking claude" / "claude 를 고른다"), so it reads right for install and uninstall.
- #4: the frontmatter test now also checks for `: `, ` #`, a leading YAML indicator character and a trailing `:`. All three current descriptions pass.
- #5: the rule-3 sentence moved into a new `### Changed` section under `[Unreleased]`. The release is still minor.
- #6: `Place` now carries one `skills` list that `plant`, `install`, `status` and `Shared::read` all reuse.

Skipped, with reasons:
- #7: adding `.agents` to `SKIP` changes hook rule 2 and the path list the rule documents. That is a design call for the person.
- #8: the `!` glyph on those rows mirrors the existing `claude` row and follows the user decision to show the rows. Changing it changes intended behaviour.
- #9 and #10: both are supervisor and AGENTS-block wording. The source says moving the supervisor and brief text onto the table belongs to the epic `moai-snyk`.

- moai 는 에이전트 실행 파일을 실행하지 않는다. `wake` 의 `codex queue --thread` 길을 걷는다(moai 가 `codex` 를 실행하는 길이다)

**What I fixed (uncommitted)**
- **Hooks (src/cmd/hook.rs, src/hook.rs):**
  - Letters stay within the 10,000-character cap: the board is counted, a letter too long on its own is cut with a pointer to `moai inbox --all`, and letters are picked by their exact rendered size.
  - At most one `any-idle-worker` letter per load.
  - After a turn held by letters, the next Stop still runs the closing check once.
  - Stop does not hold for letters the agent sent itself.
  - A card found by session id is moved to the live process if its pid is dead.
  - Compact keeps the existing busy or idle state.
  - The card is written before letters are taken, without fsync.
- **Mailbox and names (src/mail.rs):**
  - The id is minted at link time, and the directory is fsynced after the link.
  - `name_from` refuses names with no letters or digits and strips leading dashes; a new `name_with` keeps the collision suffix within 64 characters.
  - A tmux wake now needs the socket.
  - `alive()` only treats "process not found" as dead.
  - Unread mailbox files with bad JSON are cleaned up when a write fails, and an empty `.gitignore` is rewritten.
  - Read letters are filtered by the reader's name before opening.
  - The Claude config directory must be an absolute path.
- **Commands (src/cmd/mail.rs, src/cmd/agents.rs):**
  - `inbox --json` drops a letter's own `id`/`read` keys, and `--wait` no longer panics on huge values.
  - Subjects are capped at 200 characters.
  - A garbled letter only makes `inbox` exit non-zero when it could be yours.
  - `hello` trims `--role`/`--vendor`, treats names that differ only in case as the same, and removes the old card only after writing the new one.
  - Times are shown in the viewer's timezone.
- **Cleanups:**
  - One helper each for "same process", "gone", the card path and the any-idle-worker rule, replacing three to five hand copies.
  - `git::waited` is reused, and the duplicate test helper `letter_ids` is replaced by `ids_in`.
- **Init (src/cmd/init.rs):** the two self-ignoring lines are still written but no longer reported as missing.
- **Docs:** I updated the mailbox wording in the AGENTS block, docs/agents.md, the glossary, the CHANGELOG and the help texts, including the `hook --help` event lines. AGENTS.md and docs/cli.md were regenerated from the new binary.
- **Tests:** added 5 integration tests and 3 unit tests, and strengthened 7 existing ones. The 5 new hook tests go red when their fixes are reverted. The tmux test now shuts down its own `-L` server even when it fails, and the forever-wait case has a deadline.

**What I did not fix.** These need a design decision; each is parked as an idea in epic moai-h8tn:
- moai-a2y1: `--wake` cannot reach Codex or Antigravity (item 5 above). The epic promised this, so it may need `moai idea promote moai-a2y1 -e moai-h8tn --from -`, or it may be solved by moai-u5wr.
- moai-509k: letters are bound only to names, so a recycled or renamed name inherits or strands unread letters.
- moai-tocf: subagents act as the parent session's card.
- moai-t9ar: `MOAI_AGENT` gives a different identity from the one the hook uses.
- moai-3u8n: the recipient is only inside the letter file, so every hook opens the whole mailbox. This should be decided before the file shape ships.
- moai-w8z8: the supervise skill never runs `moai hello --role supervisor`.
- moai-dkkh: an interrupted turn leaves the session busy.
- moai-zyrv: the hook tests depend on which process runs `cargo test`.

The remaining minor cleanups (the `Woke.done` field, reusing id.rs helpers) I left alone.

**Your five priorities and the extra questions**
1. No inserted item took over another item's `///` doc block in the original diff. I made that mistake once in `init.rs` while fixing and corrected it before porting.
2. The race tests are covered above. The other suspicious tests are now fixed.
3. Path and name building now each go through one helper.
4. Several docs said things the code did not do; all are corrected (see Docs above).
5. `status`, `ready`, `show` and PreToolUse never open the mailbox or the presence files; I confirmed this.
- **Letter id reuse and `take` overwriting a read letter:** yes, it could happen (item 7); minting at link time narrows it, but a clock stepping back can still repeat an id.
- **Pid reuse in the sweep:** on Linux the start time catches it; on macOS a reused pid still looks alive, and the docs now say "on Linux".
- **Stop under stop_hook_active:** items 3 and 14.
- **Can `--wake` type into a person's tmux pane:** it could (item 8); it now refuses without a socket.

One verifier's wrapper script inherited `BASH_ENV`, which put `~/.local/bin` back on PATH, so the real `codex queue --thread thread-123 --message 'moai inbox'` ran twice under a scratch HOME. It failed with no such thread and changed nothing else. No tmux server outside the tests' own `-L` servers was touched, and no stray test processes are left. The 2.8 GB scratch build copy has been deleted.

The worktree changes still need a separate `fix:` commit. Moving review issue moai-h8tn.x4l is also yours; I touched the tracker only to park the 8 ideas.

Codex
- stdin 은 Claude 와 같은 키다: `session_id`·`turn_id`·`transcript_path`·`cwd`·`hook_event_name`·`model`(글)·`permission_mode`, 도구는 `tool_name: "Bash"`·`tool_input.command`·`tool_use_id`. Stop 은 `stop_hook_active`·`last_assistant_message`
- 나가는 꼴도 같다 — `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: deny` 가 막고 까닭을 모델이 그대로 댔다. Stop 의 `{"decision":"block"}` 이 한 번 붙들었고 다음 Stop 은 `stop_hook_active: true` 였다
- UserPromptSubmit 의 `additionalContext` 7,786자가 잘리지 않고 developer 메시지로 섰다. 문서는 `additionalContextLimit` 기본이 2,500 토큰 언저리라 하니 심을 때 그 값을 넉넉히 준다
- Esc 에는 Stop 이 안 오고 `Interrupt` 가 온다(`turn_id` 있음). /exit 에는 `SessionEnd`(`reason: other`)
- `apply_patch` 는 두 번 다 안 불렸다(모델이 셸 `printf`·`sed -i` 로 고쳤다). 꼴은 문서대로 `tool_input.command` 가 패치 글이다 — 시험 자료는 문서의 꼴로 짓는다
- **훅의 부모는 공용 `codex app-server --managed-daemon` 이다** — 환경이 그 데몬의 것이라 `TMUX_PANE`·`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` 가 엉뚱하다(moai-sile)

Antigravity (agy)
- stdin 은 camelCase: `conversationId`·`workspacePaths`·`transcriptPath`·`artifactDirectoryPath`·`modelName`. PreToolUse 는 `stepIdx`·`toolCall{name,args}`
- 도구 이름과 인자: `run_command{CommandLine,Cwd}`·`write_to_file{TargetFile,CodeContent,Overwrite}`·`replace_file_content{TargetFile,TargetContent,ReplacementContent,StartLine,EndLine}`·`view_file{AbsolutePath}`
- **빈 출력은 지나간다** — 남이 적은 "fail-closed" 는 이 판에서 아니었다. `{"decision":"deny","reason":…}` 이 막고 까닭이 모델에 섰다
- PreInvocation 은 모델 부름마다 오고 턴의 첫 부름이 `invocationNum: 0` 이다. `{"injectSteps":[{"ephemeralMessage":…}]}` 를 모델이 같은 턴 안에서 읽었다
- Stop 은 `terminationReason`·`executionNum`·`fullyIdle`. `{"decision":"continue","reason":…}` 가 한 번 붙들고(까닭이 SYSTEM_MESSAGE 로 섰다) 다음 Stop 은 `executionNum: 1` 이다. 빈 출력은 그대로 끝난다
- Esc 로 끊은 턴에는 Stop 도 PostInvocation 도 안 온다
- 훅은 `sh -c <명령>` 으로 돌고 부모가 `agy` 프로세스다. cwd 는 hooks.json 이 놓인 디렉터리다(작업 자리가 아니다). 환경에 `ANTIGRAVITY_CONVERSATION_ID` 가 선다
- agy 는 전역 hooks.json 을 다시 쓰며 `"SessionStart": null` 을 넣었다 — 그 이벤트를 아는 것 같지만 재지 않았다

사람 결정(2026-10-04): 끝 이벤트를 건다 — 오래된 `busy` 를 모름으로 읽지 않는다.
- Claude 는 `StopFailure`(API 오류)·`SessionEnd`, Codex 는 `Interrupt`(Esc, 실측)·`SessionEnd`, agy 는 늘 Stop 이다. 셋 다 출석을 `idle` 로 적기만 한다
- Claude 와 agy 의 Esc 는 훅이 하나도 안 온다(Claude 문서, agy 실측) — 그 장은 다음 프롬프트까지 `busy` 다
- 그래서 `send --wake` 의 busy 한 줄이 "그 턴의 끝" 을 약속하지 않고 언제부터 일하는 중인지를 댄다

I found 15 issues and fixed 13 of them in the working tree; the other two need a design decision or your hands. I ran ten finder angles, verified each candidate once and did a gap sweep. All 1873 unit tests and 689 integration tests pass, and clippy and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. Nothing is committed.

1. src/guide.rs:1990 — The supervisor skill says `--wake` types `moai inbox` into a window 5-1 just cleared, but `mail::wake` never types into a Claude pane (it returns ask_sender). 5-1 clears only Claude panes, and the `<after>` rule ignores the supervisor's own vendor.
   Failure: A Codex supervisor on tmux sends `end the turn` to a Claude worker, clears it with 5-1, then runs `send --wake`. Nothing is typed, and Codex has no SendMessage. The cleared window never loads the letter, and the supervisor waits forever for the report.
2. src/guide.rs:2247 — 5-1 treats `idle` as 'the turn is over', but `moai inbox --wait` now writes idle while a turn's shell command is still running.
   Failure: An `end the turn` worker gets a question letter as its turn ends, answers it, and waits again. Its row reads idle, both idle checks pass, and 5-1 erases the box and types `/clear`+Enter into a running turn (the idle-passing part was reproduced).
3. src/guide.rs:2247 — 5-1 can wait 240×0.5 s plus a `moai agents` spawn each time, then erase, then poll for 15 s. That is about 125–145 s, past Claude Code's 2-minute default for a shell call. The copy of the person's draft is printed into a block-buffered pipe.
   Failure: The worker goes idle at around 115 s. The call is moved to the background or stopped while erasing, and the person's half-typed text is erased with no copy left (the buffered copy is lost on SIGTERM; verified).
4. src/cmd/mail.rs:178 — `inbox --ack` takes every queued any-idle-worker letter in one call. The hooks take one per load, and moai-work makes `inbox --ack --wait` every worker's main path.
   Failure: Three open letters are queued. The first worker to wait takes all three (reproduced), the rest get nothing, and the extra jobs are hidden in that worker's read letters.
5. src/cmd/mail.rs:158 — `busy` is written as soon as a letter is seen, before `--ack` tries to take it. `idle` is written before the first scan.
   Failure: Workers that lose an any-idle-worker race end `busy` with no letter (reproduced). `--wait 0` turns a busy row idle. A letter already waiting causes an idle-then-busy double write that resets `since`.
6. src/guide.rs:1886 — `--role worker --status idle` also lists windows whose turn ended without waiting again: Stop, /clear, or an interrupted wait whose idle is never reset.
   Failure: A person interrupts a worker's wait to talk to it. The row still reads idle, the supervisor sends the next idea without waking it, and the letter sits until someone types there (reproduced).
7. src/guide.rs:1781 — Step 0's check ('if a worker in 2 is busy, it may be that one') can never fire, because step 2 only lists idle workers.
   Failure: A person's own session works a row in the root for over an hour. The row reads stranded, the supervisor hands it to a worker, and the work is done twice.
8. src/guide.rs:2554 — The worker and supervisor are told Claude Code's shell limit 'is ten minutes'. The Bash tool's default is 2 minutes; ten is only the maximum you can ask for with `timeout`.
   Failure: `moai inbox --ack --wait 540`, run as written, is moved to the background at 120 s. If the agent then follows 'run it again', two `--ack` waiters run at once.
9. src/mail.rs:665 — `wake()` only refuses `busy` rows. A Codex or Antigravity worker waiting inside its turn now reads `idle`, so it gets typed into.
   Failure: `send any-idle-worker … --wake` picks the waiting Codex worker and types `moai inbox`+Enter into its pane while its turn is running.
10. src/guide.rs:1886 — The rule 'hand work only to a session in the root' was dropped, and the worker skill never says to go to the root before steps 1–3, which use relative paths.
   Failure: A worker window opened in `<root>/src` creates `src/.worktrees/<epic>`. The anchored `/.worktrees/` rule does not cover it, so `git add -A` embeds it (reproduced).
11. src/guide.rs:2588 — `Person: away` only exempts design questions. Model-change requests and rule-5 take-over requests still block, and the letter has no place for 'who said yes'.
   Failure: Overnight, a worker on the wrong model asks the person to switch and blocks until morning.
12. src/guide.rs:2772 — Step 7 tells every worker to switch to sonnet or opus for the review, with no exception for Codex or Antigravity.
   Failure: A Codex worker reviewing a high-grade epic stops to ask for an opus switch that Codex cannot make.
13. src/guide.rs:2470 — The documented way to test 5-1 cannot get past the new tmux-socket check, and a test agent is never registered in `moai agents`.
   Failure: A tester following the instructions always gets 'not clearing — that pane is on another tmux server' and is pushed towards the person's real tmux server.
14. src/guide.rs:1949 — The send line puts the free-text title inside single quotes, with no warning about apostrophes, and `moai send` refuses subjects over 200 characters.
   Failure: 8 of the 617 ideas here would be refused for length, and a title with an apostrophe breaks the shell quoting (reproduced).
15. CLAUDE.md:321 — CLAUDE.md still puts the changed wiki pages in the report as step 11, but the report is now step 12. Line 208 says `.worktrees/<id>` while the commands above it use `.worktrees/moai-<id>`. '막혔을 때' gives no exception for `Person: away`.
   Failure: A worker following CLAUDE.md puts the wiki page list in its `Next:` note instead of the report, so the supervisor never sees it.

What I changed
- Supervisor skill (src/guide.rs): `end the turn` is now only used when the supervisor is itself in Claude Code, and waking a cleared window is described as SendMessage carrying `moai inbox`. The 5-1 script takes a `<root>` argument and asks `moai agents` there. It flushes each line as printed, waits at most 60 s for idle, and refuses to clear when a `moai inbox --wait` is running under the worker (checked twice). I confirmed the scripts compile and smoke-tested the new skip paths. Step 0 now checks every `moai agents` row, step 2 warns about `idle` windows that are not waiting, and the title quoting, 200-character subject, timeout and testing instructions are updated.
- Worker skill: covers the shell timeout, going to `Root:` first, the `MOAI_AGENT` name for hello, a model exception for Codex and Antigravity, what away mode does about model and take-over questions, a report that names unfinished work and is written outside the repo, and worktrees still in the old place. Rule 3 now says "agent program", so `AGENTS.md` was regenerated.
- Code: src/cmd/mail.rs: `idle` is written only once the call really waits; `busy` only when a letter was actually taken; one open letter per `--ack`; an empty `since` gets filled in. src/cmd/agents.rs: with no rows at all, a filtered `agents` call now gives the registration hint. New test `only_a_wait_that_took_a_letter_reads_busy`: it fails against the old src/cmd/mail.rs (I checked) and passed 5 times in a row.
- Docs: docs/agents.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, the `inbox` help text (and docs/cli.md regenerated from it), and the planted skill copies in .claude/moai-plugin/skills/ and .agents/skills/ (rebuilt with `MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in`).

Behaviour changes to confirm. `inbox --ack` now takes only one any-idle-worker letter per call, which is a change to existing behaviour. The `end the turn` rule now requires a Claude Code supervisor, which narrows the "any vendor" decision of 2026-10-04 because nothing else can wake a cleared Claude window.

Not fixed
- Wake into a waiting non-Claude pane (#9), and `idle` meaning both "waiting" and "turn ended": the proper fix is a separate waiting state derived from a live wait process. That is a design choice against the decision that the wait writes `idle`.
- CLAUDE.md (#15): I did not edit it; the three lines above need you or the user.
- Dropped as refuted: the 9-1 "filled in by the supervisor" wording — the letter's `Model:` line really does supply those values.
- Other leftovers: Nothing links a worktree back to its worker, so a freshly cleared supervisor cannot spot an orphaned worktree. The worker steps in the moai-work SKILL.md render badly as Markdown on GitHub; agents reading the raw text are unaffected. The monorepo paragraph is duplicated in the worker skill. Test-helper tidy-ups. Cost points: a 540 s wait outlives the 5-minute prompt cache, and Codex polling costs extra turns. Matching rule 2's exemptions by directory name rather than by "this path is another worktree".

### What was fixed (in the working tree, not committed)

The full suite passes: 1873 unit and 700 integration tests (5 new). clippy and fmt are clean. I reverted each fix temporarily and confirmed its new or strengthened test fails on its own assertion.

- **Finding 1, `patched` (`src/cmd/hook.rs`):** shell-form `apply_patch` / `applypatch` (with an optional `cd`) is now expanded into one Edit per file, plus the shell line itself. Headers are matched after trimming leading whitespace.
- **Finding 2, card names:** the disambiguated name is re-checked, falling back to the full session id.
- **Finding 4, `skill status`:** the hook files are now judged against the binary the file calls (new `skill::planted_exe`). Files are also compared by meaning, ignoring formatting and null keys (new `skill::same_hooks`).
- **Finding 7:** an agy Stop that ended on an error is now treated as StopFailure; `arrived` returns the event as well.
- **Finding 8:** Antigravity ownership now requires the group to be enabled and every handler in it to be moai's.
- **Finding 10:** a prompt now restarts `since`.
- **Finding 11:** the baseline is written at the start of a turn for every dialect.
- **Finding 14:** the Codex notice puts the path in double quotes. Claude's hook line is unchanged byte for byte; `plugin.json` only changed its version hash because the skill text changed.
- **Finding 15:** updated help/`Event` doc, CHANGELOG, docs/agents.md, glossary, README and guide.rs. The Codex SessionEnd status message now says "taking this session off moai's list".
- **Docs for findings 5, 6 and 12:** the Claude Code 2.1.78 minimum is now in CHANGELOG and docs/agents.md. docs/agents.md says a killed Codex session leaves its row behind. The AGENTS block now names input typed into a running command as unchecked.
- **Tests:** tightened the relink check, the vacuous `"state"` and `/hooks` assertions, `executionNum`, `*** Move to:`, and the cwd anchoring for both Codex and agy.
- **Cleanups:**
  - `rest()` no longer rewrites a card that is already idle.
  - End events are classified with an exhaustive match.
  - The `decision` field is now a `Verdict` enum, so `allow` cannot be written.
  - `plugin_json` uses the shared `TIMEOUT` constant.
  - Stale comments are fixed.
- **Regenerated files:**
  - AGENTS.md via `init --print` (`init --check` reports it current).
  - The skill trees and `.codex/hooks.json` via `MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in`. Codex users have to trust `.codex/hooks.json` again, but it is unreleased.
  - `docs/cli.md` via `scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh`.

### What was skipped, and why

- **Finding 3 (Codex identity) and finding 6 (cards that are never swept):** fixing these needs a design choice. Either tell the session its card name and let `hello` adopt it, or record a liveness anchor or expiry for pid-0 cards.
- **Finding 5:** hooking `StopFailure` was your decision (moai-u5wr.f29), so I only documented the minimum version.
- **Finding 9:** extend `calls_review`, or document the gap? moai-5kk1 is already changing those review commands.
- **Finding 12:** treating typed input as a shell line could refuse harmless keystrokes, so this needs a decision.
- **Finding 13:** it needs a token measurement in agy, or a switch to `userMessage`.
- **Also skipped:**
  - A 10-file Codex patch reruns the full check per file, about 45 ms each in release; avoiding that is a refactor, not a fix.
  - Commit granularity: f8feaa01 carries six issues, and it fails its own tests without 9a5cb01d. Fixing that means rewriting history.

The changes are mostly in `src/cmd/hook.rs`, `src/skill.rs`, `src/cmd/skill.rs` and `tests/cli.rs`, all under `/home/coder/workspace/moa-issue/.claude/worktrees/moai-u5wr/`. They are left for separate `fix:` commits.

text:
## Review of moai-t6hl (Codex hook file values) — /code-review max --fix, agent-a14641716df8a5512

The code change itself is correct: the Codex hooks file now sets each value only on the events that accept it. The real problem was the CHANGELOG entry. I applied three fixes to the working tree and did not commit. The full test suite, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` all pass, and the committed `.codex/hooks.json` is unchanged byte for byte.

1. CHANGELOG.md:182 — The new `### Fixed` entry describes a fix to `.codex/hooks.json`, a file no release has ever planted. The same [Unreleased] `### Added` entry at line 98 is what introduces it, and v0.6.0 has no `codex_hooks`. Failure: when `bump-version.sh auto` cuts 0.7.0, the notes tell 0.6.0 users that a /hooks warning they never saw is fixed, and to re-run `moai skill install --agent codex`, a flag their binary doesn't have. This goes against the repo's practice (commits 2e792a75 and 0f199cc1) of folding fixes to unreleased features into the Added entry.
2. src/cmd/hook.rs:446 — (Was already there.) Codex Stop delivers letters in the `decision: block` reason, capped by CONTEXT_CAP at 10,000 UTF-16 units. Codex holds that reason to its default of about 2,500 tokens, which it counts as UTF-8 bytes divided by 4; `additionalContextLimit` cannot raise it. The docs say: 'continuation prompts keep the default limit'. Failure: a Codex worker gets a Korean letter of about 3,400 characters (about 10.2 KB). moai marks it read and sends block. Codex saves it to <tmp>/hook_outputs/… and the model sees only the head, the tail and a file path, so the middle of the letter never reaches it. The removed Stop limit never covered this case.
3. src/skill.rs:176 — Each Codex event's values were split between the `CODEX` rows and two separate name lists, `CODEX_CONTEXT` and `CODEX_SHORT`, joined with `.contains(at)`. A row added without updating the lists quietly got 15 s and no limit. Failure: adding `PostToolUse` without touching `CODEX_CONTEXT` plants it with no limit. Codex then falls back to about 2,500 tokens and moves the board and letters into a file. Only the test's unknown-event panic would catch it.
4. src/skill.rs:163 — The `TIMEOUT` doc said Claude's manifest uses 15 and named only Codex as cutting it short. But Claude gives all SessionEnd hooks one shared 1.5 s budget, and plugin hook timeouts do not raise it (Claude Code hooks doc). Failure: a maintainer plans about 15 s of Claude SessionEnd work based on the doc. Claude cancels the plugin hook at 1.5 s and the work is left half done.
5. src/cmd/hook.rs:513 — (Latent.) `answer()` sends additionalContext for any Codex event. The list of Codex events that can carry it now exists only in the planted file. Failure: if a future change returns Context on Stop, Interrupt or SessionEnd, Codex receives context it cannot carry, and no test ties what the hook sends to the planted list.
6. src/skill.rs:182 — `CODEX_SHORT_TIMEOUT` had no doc of its own: the `///` block above it belonged to `CODEX_SHORT`. Failure: following `TIMEOUT`'s link shows a bare 3, with the reason sitting on a different item. Cosmetic.
7. src/skill.rs:2238 — Nothing checks the generated file against Codex's own validation. The test restates the docs by hand, and tests/hooks/ holds only stdin captures. Failure: the next Codex config rule will again be found only by a person opening /hooks, and every such fix makes Codex users re-trust the changed handlers.
8. .codex/hooks.json:4 — Changing the Stop, Interrupt and SessionEnd entries resets Codex's per-handler trust. `moai skill status` cannot see trust. docs/agents.md:155 ('Codex runs none of them') is wrong when only some handlers changed. Failure: a session that trusted the old file keeps running three hooks but skips Stop, Interrupt and SessionEnd until re-trusted, so its presence stays busy. This can't happen on this machine today: the project file was never trusted here.
9. .codex/hooks.json:1 — The root release binary predates this change. Failure: after the merge, its `skill status` calls the new file stale. Running `skill install --agent codex` with it puts the old shape and its warnings back. Rebuild the root binary right after merging.
10. src/cmd/hook.rs:178 — (Was already there.) Interrupt and SessionEnd build a full Repo, including parsing the root config, before `rest()`, which needs only the agents directory. Failure: if the root config.toml has conflict markers, the fallback opens the worktree's own .moai. A Codex SessionEnd then removes no root card and Interrupt marks nothing idle.
11. src/cmd/hook.rs:1253 — (Was already there; tracked by moai-j3n5.) A Codex SessionEnd killed at 3 s leaves its pid-0 presence card in place for good. Failure: `moai send any-idle-worker --wake` keeps picking the dead card. The fix is on the unmerged worktree-moai-ew4o branch.
12. src/mail.rs:420 — (Was already there.) Temporary files from `write_presence` in .moai/agents are never cleaned up. Failure: a hook killed between the write and the rename during an I/O stall leaves a dotfile there permanently.

Fixed:
- CHANGELOG: removed the `### Fixed` section and folded one sentence into the Added entry "The hooks stand in Codex and Antigravity too". The version pick is still minor, 0.7.0.
- Codex table: each `CODEX` row now carries its own timeout and limit, as `(&str, &str, &str, u64, Option<usize>)`. `CODEX_CONTEXT`, `CODEX_SHORT` and both `contains` lookups are gone, and `CODEX_SHORT_TIMEOUT` has its own doc.
- `TIMEOUT` doc: now names both short budgets, Codex's 1–3 s and Claude's 1.5 s SessionEnd, and says why 15 stays.

Skipped: the other nine.
- The Stop letter spill needs a per-agent budget in `cmd/hook.rs`, outside this diff. I recommend filing it.
- The `answer()` filter (latent) and the validation-check gap are outside this diff; worth recording as follow-ups.
- Trust reset and the stale root binary: notes for whoever merges.
- The last three were already there before this change and are outside the diff; one is already tracked.

Two candidates were refuted: the first sentence of the `TIMEOUT` doc (only a wording nit), and commit 0809a438 having no body (most changelog commits here have none).

Before or after merging: run `cargo build --release` at the root, then re-trust the three changed handlers in Codex's `/hooks`.

Side effect: one finder agent broke its read-only instruction. It ran `moai hook stop` and `moai hook session-end --dialect codex`, which created `.moai/agents/codex-reviewpr.json` and a `/tmp` marker, then removed both. I confirmed neither remains, and `issues.jsonl` and the mailbox were not touched.

Evidence the reviewer read from Codex's own logs: `/hooks` Issues showed "⚠ clamping SessionEnd hook timeout to 3s", and the codex binary carries "ignoring additionalContextLimit for … hook in …: this event cannot emit additionalContext".

### Fixed (11)
- Your own row is no longer "taken over": `take_over` gets a `keep` parameter. `hello` passes its own existing row, and the hook's rename passes the row being renamed.
- MOAI_AGENT: `who` checks the Codex session id before MOAI_AGENT. `hello` reads MOAI_AGENT only when registering its own process outside Codex (not with `--pid`/`--as`). An invalid MOAI_AGENT now errors, the same as in `who`. Help text (and the regenerated `docs/cli.md`), `docs/agents.md` and CHANGELOG are updated to match.
- Sweep and resume: before deleting a row, the sweep re-reads it and skips it if it changed. The resume cleanup no longer empties the box of the window's MOAI_AGENT row.
- Text fixes: the Codex refusal now recommends `--as <row>`, plus `--name` to rename it. Every command the hook's letters suggest carries `--as {me}`. The subagent refusal points `--as` at `inbox` and `send` only.
- Subagent guard: it now catches `env -C`, and lets `--help` and an `inbox` prefixed with `MOAI_AGENT=` through.
- Case: `Any-Idle-Worker` and other spellings are rejected as names and as recipients.
- Moving letters: the directory fsync happens once per destination box instead of once per letter. Moving falls back to a plain rename when hard links aren't available.
- Staleness: `stale()` uses the later of `seen` and `since`. `inbox --wait` also refreshes `seen` when it's due, even when the status doesn't change.
- Tests: a new `staged_under` helper runs the affected tests under a fake agent process. `hook_held` now checks the exit code. Regression tests were added for each fix.

### Not fixed: these need your decision (4)
- Cross-delivery, and what the 20-minute sweep throws away (first and third findings): moai-j3n5 chose to delete quiet Codex rows. Options are to hide those rows instead of deleting them, or to build Codex names from the random tail of the session id instead of its timestamp prefix. I did correct the `sweep` comment, which wrongly claimed letters come back on takeover.
- Returned-letter addressing and labelling: this needs either an explicit "returned" marker or place, or a rule that letters only go back to a sender who still holds the name.

### Outside the 15
- Possible issue: when the repo is shared across containers, `moai agents` can treat a live agent in another container as dead and now also returns its letters.
- Cleanups found, not applied: `inbox --wait` rereads every agent row every 500 ms, even for non-Codex agents. hello's Codex naming is a copy of the hook's and has already drifted. The anchor-stamping code is duplicated in four places.
- Commit hygiene: f264d26d bundles six issues in one commit, and 05e45e01 changes moai-ew4o.e1m behaviour without naming it. That can't be fixed in the working tree.
- Rejected: the non-Unix test build concern and the narrowed refused-send assertion.

I made no tracker changes. The findings and token count still need to go on review issue moai-ew4o.q9f.
