I reviewed commit 422b4dfc at max effort and verified every finding. Ten bugs and cleanups are fixed in the worktree (not committed); five findings need a decision from you or the person. `cargo test --locked` passes (1886 unit, 719 integration), `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean, and each new test fails when its fix is reverted.

The worst one: after a container restart, a session resumed with `claude --resume` keeps the old container's pid and machine on its row for good. From then on `moai inbox` and `moai send` in that session answer "Who are you?" unless `--as` or `MOAI_AGENT` is set. That is fixed.

Findings:

1. src/cmd/hook.rs:1236 — attendee reuses a row found by session id unchanged whenever !gone(); a row from another machine is never dead and its seen stays fresh, so a session resumed on a new machine never moves to its new process. Container restart then `claude --resume S` within 20 min: the row keeps the old pid and machine; every hook re-stamps seen; inbox/send without --as fail 'Who are you?'; hello refuses its own name; wake gives no_way; never dead after exit.
2. src/guide.rs:2329 — the supervisor's `<after>` rule and its 5-1 clear script trust a row's tmux_socket, pane and pid without checking machine, and `agents --json` gives no signal for whether a row is on this machine. Worker on container B, supervisor on A, shared `/tmp/tmux-1000/default`: B's row now survives as idle, supervisor picks `end the turn`, script runs local ps on B's pid and skips — worker never cleared or woken. If pids coincide it erases a local pane's draft and types /clear into an unrelated session. Skill text (guide.rs:1919, 1846) still says rows are 'swept as read'.
3. src/mail.rs:883 — a row from another machine that expires is swept without retire, so its mailbox stays; Claude names are about 256 per directory, so a later unrelated session that gets the same name receives those letters (after a container restart every earlier row reads as another machine's).
4. src/mail.rs:1140 — on non-Linux unix machine() was the hostname, which macOS changes with network/VPN (and collides across Macs): here() turns false for every live local row.
5. src/cmd/mail.rs:174 — after a reboot or container restart, a window with MOAI_AGENT=w1 cannot take its name back from its own dead pre-restart row, and its `inbox --wait` keeps re-stamping that row by name, so it never goes stale; the window stays split across two rows.
6. src/mail.rs:923 — take_over sends back the letters of a same-named row that is gone(); a row from another machine is gone after only 20 quiet minutes, so a live but idle agent there loses its letters, row and role when a local session takes its name. A remaining gap, not a regression.
7. src/cmd/hook.rs:1339 — due() lost its pid guard, so SessionEnd now rewrites an idle Claude row whose anchor is 60 s or older (puts back the write moai-u5wr.e74 removed; on exit turns a long-idle gone row back into idle for 20 min on another machine).
8. src/cmd/hook.rs:1237 — a row written before this field (no machine) for a session still running is never labelled (found-by-session branch writes it back with `..p.clone()`); on upgrade day another container sweeps it.
9. src/mail.rs:978 — idle_worker can pick another machine's worker, which wake() answers no_way, so a wakeable idle worker on this machine is never knocked.
10. src/mail.rs:945 — keep_alive's unlocked read-then-write now runs for every dialect, and subagent tool calls carry the parent's session_id: a stale busy copy can be written back over Stop's idle, or bring back the row under the old name inside a MOAI_AGENT rename.
11. src/mail.rs:784 — every session now rewrites its row on the RBD-backed repo once a minute from PreToolUse and inbox --wait, though on a single machine nothing reads that anchor. Plausible only: no stall longer than the 15 s hook timeout has been measured.
12. src/cmd/agents.rs:236 — hello's name-taken refusal prints another machine's pid as a bare number.
13. src/cmd/agents.rs:48 — every swept row is reported as 'its process is gone', including another machine's row swept after a day of quiet.
14. tests/cli.rs:24098 — the negative assertion matches the sleeper's pid as a substring of '4194400@box-b' (flaky when the pid is 400, 4400, 94400 or 194400).
15. src/cli.rs:484 — `send --help` promises a tmux knock or a SendMessage line, but an agent on another machine now silently gets no_way.

Fixed in the worktree: 1 (reuse a row found by session only if here() && !gone()), 8 (Presence::claimed labels a legacy row when its pid is alive here; attendee and keep_alive), 10 (keep_alive re-reads before writing), 7 (an idle row is not rewritten on SessionEnd), 4 (machine() is None off Linux; host only with machine), 9 (idle_worker prefers this machine), 12/13/15 (pid@host in the refusal, Swept struct and agents.swept_quiet, send help), 14, plus hello stamps through stamp(), a stale comment, a redundant test literal, and a doc note that VMs restored from one snapshot read as one machine. New tests: a_session_resumed_on_another_machine_moves_its_card_here, a_card_from_before_machines_is_labelled_by_its_live_session, a_closing_session_does_not_renew_its_anchor, the extended a_card_from_another_container_is_not_swept_by_its_pid, the_worker_to_wake_is_one_on_this_machine_first.

Not fixed — each changes decided behaviour or needs design: 2 (needs a per-row `here` key in agents --json, a script check and a reworded `<after>` rule — a contract change; make it a member of moai-dhxm), 3 (reverses the commit's accepted cost), 6 (already parked as idea moai-tezd), 5 (the simple guard would break `inbox --as` across machines; needs a design decision), 11 (intended; a longer cadence for rows with a known pid is the option). Also skipped: same hostname after a pod restart (label shows this host's own name, low impact), mixed-version rollout (heals at the next hook of the new binary), the `fresh` closure reshape (taste), the `unseen` helper reuse (the helper it would replace panics on that input).

text:
## Review of moai-o9tg (Codex hooks file against the /hooks captures) — /code-review high --fix, agent-a89a8300a2f4b6ba2

The review found 6 problems, all in the new test code that checks Codex hooks, and I fixed 5 of them. The hooks file moai plants is correct: it matches both of Codex's `/hooks` captures, and both capture JSONs are byte-for-byte the committed `.codex/hooks.json` from `db8de3c3^` and `db8de3c3`. The fixes are in the working tree only, not committed.

1. src/skill.rs:2431 — Matching a warning by its start was allowed for the last warning of every capture, not only the one capture that was cut off. Failure: a later complete capture whose mimicked last warning has extra text after Codex's real words (e.g. '… in <hooks.json> (was 15s)') still passes, because ours.starts_with(warning) is true. So a capture can't catch the mimic drifting on its last line.
2. src/skill.rs:2388 — codex_said returns an empty list whenever no line is exactly 'Issues', including captures pasted with their line breaks collapsed. Failure: after-moai-t6hl.txt is already one collapsed line. A collapsed capture that held 'Issues ⚠ clamping …' would read as 'Codex said nothing', and the test would only check that the mimic is also silent, so real Codex warnings pass unseen.
3. src/skill.rs:2389 — Every non-blank line after the warnings is joined onto the last warning, so anything Codex prints below the Issues block gets glued on. Failure: a capture that includes the event table or a footer after Issues turns the last warning into '… additionalContext Event Installed Active …'. That never matches and the test fails, wrongly blaming the mimic.
4. src/skill.rs:2389 — strip_prefix("⚠ ") doesn't allow leading indentation, and the TUI does indent (the after capture starts with '  Hooks'). Failure: an indented '  ⚠ clamping …' line is read as a continuation: it panics with 'Issues 밑 첫 줄이 ⚠ 로 서지 않는다' or merges two warnings into one, which then fails to match.
5. src/skill.rs:2333 — The timeout-cap lookup in CODEX_TIMEOUT_CAP was written out twice (in codex_issues and in the final assertion loop). Failure: two copies of the same find/map can drift apart, e.g. one changed to a default and the other not. One helper keeps the rule in one place.
6. src/skill.rs:2457 — The `sent` closure silently drops a stdin capture that fails to parse, so its event disappears from `known`. Failure: a damaged tests/hooks/codex/interrupt.json makes codex_shape report 'Interrupt: Codex 가 보내 온 적이 없는 이벤트', which points the reader at the hooks table instead of the broken capture.

What I fixed:
1. Cut-capture matching: a new `CODEX_CUT` list names the captures whose last warning was cut off (only `before-moai-t6hl`). Only those get start-of-text matching. I checked it: with the list emptied, the test fails on exactly that warning.
2. Collapsed captures: `codex_said` now stops with an assertion when "Issues" appears in the text but not on its own line.
3. Text after the warnings: a blank line after the first warning now ends the Issues block.
4. Indentation: lines are trimmed of leading spaces before looking for `⚠ `.
5. Duplicate lookup: both places now call one helper, `codex_timeout_cap(event)`.
6. README: `tests/hooks/README.md` now explains `CODEX_CUT` and says to restore line breaks in a collapsed capture.

What I skipped: the last finding. The test already fails loudly on a damaged capture; the only problem is a misleading message, and it isn't a correctness bug.

Checks: `cargo test --bin moai codex` passes (4 tests), `cargo fmt --check` is clean, and clippy gives no warnings in `src/skill.rs`.

I found 15 issues and fixed 11 of them. The fixes are uncommitted in `/home/coder/workspace/moa-issue/.worktrees/moai-jzym`. Before the fixes, CI would have failed on formatting, and attendance broke when the root `config.toml` was unreadable. After the fixes, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` pass, and `cargo test` passes (1888 unit tests, 726 CLI tests).

1. src/cmd/hook.rs:190 — The end events now find attendance at the tracker root, but SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and PreToolUse keep_alive still read and write attendance and mail through the rules-only `find_here` fallback (203-206). A broken root config therefore splits one session's card across two agents dirs.
   Failure: The root config.toml has `<<<<<<< HEAD` before a Codex session opens in `.worktrees/feat`. Its card is written only to `<wt>/.moai/agents`. Interrupt and SessionEnd look only at the root, so that card stays busy and is never removed; the pre-diff code idled and removed it, so this is a regression. For a session opened before the break, the first prompt during the break creates a second card in the worktree, the root card goes stale, and letters already in the root mailbox are not delivered. Reproduced with the HEAD binary.
2. src/cmd/hook.rs:247 — `cargo fmt --all --check` fails on the two new `let letters = …waiting(…)` bindings (247-250 and 312-315).
   Failure: The required `ci-gate` job runs fmt first, so the branch goes red before clippy and the tests run.
3. src/cmd/hook.rs:533 — The hold_room doc calls the measured 21KB text the largest text the slot can produce. The slot is counted in UTF-16 units, so all-Hangul text fills it at about 29.5KB, and the 21-30KB range was never measured. The new test sent 27KB.
   Failure: If agy limits by bytes or tokens somewhere between 21KB and 30KB, a dense Korean letter is cut or spilled to a file after moai has already marked it read: the moai-rxro loss again. The test asserted a size nobody has observed.
4. tests/cli.rs:25162 — The `ulimit -f 0` test depends on SIGXFSZ having its default action. `!status.success()` also does not check why the hook died.
   Failure: Confirmed: run under Python `os.system` (CPython ignores SIGXFSZ, and POSIX sh cannot un-ignore it), the write only fails with EFBIG, the hook delivers the letter and exits 0, and the test goes red with '시험이 헛돈다'.
5. src/cmd/mail.rs:244 — Outside the diff, same bug class as flj: `moai inbox --ack --wait` moves letters to read/ and then writes the attendance card before anything is printed.
   Failure: Reproduced by the verifier with `ulimit -f 0`: exit 153, nothing on stdout, the letter sits in read/, and the next `inbox --ack` says there are no letters. This affects the worker and supervisor wait loops (`moai inbox --ack --wait`).
6. src/cmd/hook.rs:1453 — `deliver` moves picked letters one rename at a time, so a stall after the first move still loses a delivery. flj narrowed this window but did not close it.
   Failure: Two letters pending; rename 1 completes and rename 2 stalls on RBD past the 15s timeout. `decision: block` is dropped and both letters end up read but unseen. This predates the diff.
7. src/cmd/hook.rs:500 — The `letters` session marker is still written to TMPDIR after letters are moved. The ulimit test cannot see it because it is a zero-byte write.
   Failure: If TMPDIR sits on stalling storage (here it is local /tmp), the hold is lost after the move.
8. src/store.rs:492 — The new `Repo::tracker_root_from` is identical to the existing `store::tracker_in_use` (`look` + `opened_root`), and both docs claim to be the single rule.
   Failure: A later change to one copy would make `moai init --check` and the hook's attendance root disagree.
9. tests/cli.rs:25124 — The uxa test never asserts that the broken config actually breaks `moai`.
   Failure: If config parsing ever tolerated the marker line, the old code would also reach the root and the test would stay green on revert.
10. src/cmd/hook.rs:486 — The Stop comment names only the `any-idle-worker` race as the cause of the second card write.
   Failure: Any take that is lost (another `inbox --ack`, a sweep) or fails (EACCES, a non-directory `read/`) causes it too. With a persistent take error, every Stop writes the card twice.
11. src/cmd/hook.rs:1212 — The `attendee` doc still says status is written by the attend that runs after the decision.
   Failure: After flj every status write that matters comes before letters move; someone 'restoring' the documented order would bring the lost-letter bug back.
12. src/hook.rs:284 — The letters_room doc says agy carried the slot whole, but only ~21KB was measured in bytes.
   Failure: Same unmeasured byte range as the hold_room doc (C4).
13. src/cmd/hook.rs:1458 — `deliver` now owns `mine` but still deep-copies every taken letter and repeats the empty check that `hook::letters` already does.
   Failure: One extra copy of each delivered letter (up to 64KB) on every delivering hook.
14. src/cmd/hook.rs:491 — `early: Option<&str>` is really a bool, and `repo.agents_dir()` is rebuilt at every call.
   Failure: Readability only: the reader has to work out which write is skipped.
15. src/cmd/hook.rs:203 — `Repo::find` reads the working directory again, and on `Ok(None)` the code still climbs a second time through `find_here`, which can only return None too.
   Failure: A redundant walk to `/` on every hook call made outside any tracker.

Fixed (11):
- 1 (attendance at the root): every event now writes attendance and mail at the tracker root. That is `repo.root` when the tracker opens normally, and `store::tracker_in_use(cwd)` when the rules fall back to the worktree. `attendee`, `waiting` and `deliver` now take that root path, and `keep_alive` uses it too. New test `a_hook_past_a_broken_root_config_keeps_attendance_and_letters_at_the_root` covers both scenarios and fails against HEAD.
- 2: ran `cargo fmt`.
- 3, 12: the docs now say only what was measured. The agy test letter is now 19.5KB, which is inside the measured bytes and still over Codex's line. Renamed that test `an_antigravity_stop_holds_whole_a_letter_codex_would_cut`.
- 4: the test now resets SIGXFSZ before exec (`pre_exec`) and asserts the hook died by SIGXFSZ or 153. Under `os.system` the HEAD version fails and the fixed version passes.
- 8: removed `Repo::tracker_root_from` and repointed its doc links to `tracker_in_use`.
- 9: a new `break_root_config` helper asserts the premise; `main_and_worktree` and `codex_in` are shared by both worktree tests.
- 10, 11: comments corrected. The Stop comment now also says the window is not fully closed (5-7).
- 13-15: cleanups as described.
All three original tests were confirmed to go red when their own fix is reverted.

Not fixed:
- 5 is outside the diff. Fixing it would follow the flj pattern: write `busy` before taking letters.
- 6 and 7 can only be closed by moving letters after the shell has printed (two-phase delivery). That is a design change, so only documented in the Stop comment.
- A finding that the flj test hand-builds its hook process was refuted by its verifier, so left alone.
- Below the bar and left as is: a shared helper for the two turn-head/post-compact delivery sites, skipping the early write when nothing changed, deferring the snapshot read in Stop, and the crash-handler noise the SIGXFSZ test causes on this host.

What to do: commit the fixes as separate fix: commits; add fix 1 to the planned CHANGELOG line; put finding 5 on the tracker; measure again with an all-Hangul letter of about 29KB — agy is now 1.2.17 and its binary has byte-based truncation messages, so the 21-30KB range is a real open question.

2026-10-05 리뷰 moai-jzym.a9k 3번의 틈을 쟀다 — 사람이 새로 띄운 agy 1.2.17 창(대화 2b6dfbe9, antigravity-2b6dfbe9)에 한글로만 채운 편지 둘(moai 가 낸 글 9,770 단위·28.1KB, 자르지 않음). 턴 머리 EPHEMERAL_MESSAGE 9,822 단위·28,184 바이트, Stop 의 decision: continue SYSTEM_MESSAGE 10,024 단위·28,382 바이트, 둘 다 표지 스물이 다 섰고 경로도 자른 표도 없다. 모델도 스물을 차례대로 댔다. 칸(UTF-16 1만)이 바이트로 가장 큰 꼴까지 agy 에 통째로 든다 — 자는 그대로 둔다

text:
Review (/code-review max --fix, opus) — reviewer's own words

I found no correctness bug in the made-name versus asked-name split itself; every contest uses the right check. The real problems were a misleading refusal message, docs that lead people straight back into the original letter loss, missing tests, and doc drift. I applied fixes for most of them; they are uncommitted in the worktree.

Checks after the fixes: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` are clean, and the full `cargo test` passes (1890 unit, 723 CLI). Each new assertion goes red under the mutation it guards, and putting `made_name` back on `!gone()` turns both the unit and CLI tests red.

1. src/cmd/agents.rs:256 — When `hello` makes up a name and another machine's quiet row holds it, the refusal reuses `refuse.agents_name_taken` ('already taken by a running agent'), although `moai agents` shows that row as `gone`. Failure: another container's `claude-1234` has been quiet for an hour. `moai hello --vendor claude` is refused with 'running agent (pid 4194400@box-b)' while the board says `gone`, and nothing mentions the one-day hold. The new test itself asserts the row reads `gone` and then expects this text.
2. docs/agents.md:511 — The new troubleshooting bullet ends with 'A name you ask for … is yours again once the old row reads gone', which reads as the fix for a suffixed or refused session. Following it reopens the exact moai-nas5 loss. Failure: the session came up as `moa-issue-25-1a2b3c4d`, so the person runs `moai hello --name moa-issue-25`. That counts as an asked name, measured by `!gone()`, so `take_over` sends the far session's unread letters back and its row is overwritten. The behaviour is the user's decision; the text should warn instead of inviting it.
3. src/cmd/hook.rs:1293 — Suffixed names stop matching the name Claude Code shows, which `SendMessage` uses. Before, that lasted at most 20 minutes; now it lasts up to a day, and after every container restart. Failure: after a restart, a worker whose Claude name is `moa-issue-3` is registered as `moa-issue-3-<8>`. `moai send … --wake` tells the sender to SendMessage that longer name, which Claude does not know. A letter sent to `moa-issue-3` lands silently in the dead row's mailbox until the day-later sweep. docs/agents.md:136 and :319 still promised the SendMessage name.
4. src/mail.rs:816 — Codex rows (pid 0, no machine) always count as this machine's, so they never get the day-long hold. The diff's `codex_name` change does nothing for any row Codex actually writes. Already true before this diff. Failure: two Codex sessions open within the same 65 s of session-id prefix. B ends and is resumed after A has rested 25 minutes. `codex_name` hands out A's name, and `take_over` returns A's letters. The unit test's `codex_name` assertion uses a Claude-shaped row named `codex-…` that no code path writes.
5. src/cmd/agents.rs:255 — The asked-name branch of hello's new check (`!made` means `!gone()`) had no test. Failure: changing `holds` to always use `holds_made_name()` kept every test green, while breaking the CHANGELOG promise that `moai hello --name` gets the name back once the old row reads `gone`.
6. src/mail.rs:2122 — The unit test had no row from this machine with a pid. Failure: keying `holds_made_name` on `pid == 0` instead of `here()` passed both new tests, yet a dead local Claude row would then hold its name forever, because process-measured rows never expire.
7. tests/cli.rs:24764 — The CLI test never checked that the far session's letter stays in the far session's own mailbox. Failure: moving that mailbox to the suffixed name would hand the far session's letter to the local session, and the test stayed green.
8. CHANGELOG.md:86 — The CHANGELOG and the docs bullet listed the made-up names wrongly, and both said `hello` refuses, which is false in Codex. The docs heading blamed only another machine's row. The CHANGELOG also described an unreleased intermediate bug in the past tense. Failure: the CHANGELOG said '`<vendor>-` and a number' and the docs said '`claude-` and eight characters'. The code also protects `<vendor>-<session prefix>`, `codex-<8>` and hello's `<vendor>-<pid>`. Codex `hello` appends a piece through `codex_name` instead of refusing, and a live row on this machine also causes the suffix.
9. docs/agents.md:526 — The page was edited by this epic, but its `Decided in:` line did not name moai-nas5, which the moai-wiki skill requires (src/guide.rs:1638: 'put this epic's id on it'). Failure: the wiki sweep and readers cannot trace the new bullet back to this decision.
10. src/cmd/hook.rs:1188 — Comments still said a name is split only when a live other row holds it. Failure: the same stale wording was at hook.rs:1188 and 1286, agents.rs:229 and mail.rs:1025. A made-up name is now also split for another machine's row that reads `gone`, so these comments describe the old rule.
11. src/cmd/hook.rs:1292 — Cleanup: the hook's `made_taken`/`free` copied `codex_name`'s suffix loop line for line. This diff had to edit both copies, in two commits. Failure: the next change to the rule made in only one copy would let Claude and Codex names drift apart again. Review moai-ew4o.q9f records an earlier drift of exactly this kind.
12. src/cmd/agents.rs:238 — Cleanup: the nested `(name, made)` match only tags which branch produced the name. Failure: the extra nesting and re-indented refusal arms made the diff harder to check against the original error paths.
13. src/mail.rs:716 — Rows with a pid but no `machine` (older binaries, non-Linux) are measured by this machine's /proc, so the day-long hold never applies to them. Already true before this diff. Failure: a live session in a container running a pre-moai-dhxm binary reads as dead here. Its made-up name is handed out at once and its letters go back to their senders.
14. src/cli.rs:546 — `moai agents --help` (and the comment at src/cmd/agents.rs:50-52) say another machine's swept row keeps its letters for that session, but `sweep_from` returns them to their senders. Already true before this diff. Failure: after a day-old sweep, `moai agents` prints 'its letters went back to their senders' while `--help` says the letters wait.
15. src/cmd/hook.rs:1342 — The made-up-name lookup can return None when the base name and both suffixed names are all held, so the session gets no row. The day-long hold widens that window. The same failure was possible before with live rows. Failure: a contrived resume across containers in which all three names are held by another machine's quiet rows. The session ends up with no row, and `moai inbox`/`send` stop with NO_ACTOR.

Fixed in the working tree:
- Refusal text: a new `refuse.agents_name_held` key in en and ko. It is chosen only when the holder is another machine's row (`!other.here() && other.gone()`), says the hold lasts a day, and warns that asking for that name itself takes the row over.
- Duplicated suffix rule: moved into one new `mail::made_name(all, base, session)`. `codex_name` and the hook both call it, and the hook's `whole`/`made_taken`/`free` and the `taken` alias are gone.
- hello: the nested match is flattened into `given` / `made = given.is_none()`.
- Tests added: CLI test — the far session's box keeps its letter and the new session's box stays empty, the refusal no longer says "running agent", and `hello --name w6` reclaims a far quiet row. Unit test — a live row on this machine keeps a made-up name, and a dead one lets it go.
- Docs: docs/agents.md bullet rewritten (correct list of made-up names, the Codex behaviour, the SendMessage caveat, a warning instead of the remedy line); the SendMessage caveat also went into lines 136 and 319; `Decided in:` now names moai-nas5. CHANGELOG: the made-up-name list, the Codex `hello` behaviour and the tense are corrected. Comments: the `STALE_AFTER`, `EXPIRE_AFTER` and `holds_made_name` comments now cover the Codex and machine-less cases.
- Introduced and fixed during the review: my first version of the refusal-text choice re-checked `gone()`, which could mislabel a row on this machine; the `!other.here()` guard closes that.

Skipped, for you to decide:
- Codex day-long hold (finding 4): giving Codex rows the hold would reverse the unit test's deliberate 20-minute assertion, so it needs the user's decision.
- SendMessage name for `--wake` (finding 3): fixing it in code means storing or looking up the Claude name when `wake` runs. That is a design change outside this diff, so only the docs changed.
- `--help` text (finding 14): this one is factually wrong for another machine's rows, but the fix means regenerating `docs/cli.md` (`MOAI=<bin> scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh`). Worth its own chore issue.
- Three older issues left as they are: an empty name lookup (finding 15), `hello` not finding its own row by session id after a resume in a new container without hooks, and `quiet()` having no slack for a row stamped in the future.

I reviewed the moai-dp35 range (5be40558..HEAD) and applied fixes for 9 of the 13 findings to the working tree; 3 are skipped and 1 got a doc line only. Nothing is committed.

The epic changes no behaviour on any path that runs today. Every (agent, event) pair gets the same room as before, and the slot table matches what each agent actually reads. The planted `.codex/hooks.json` is byte-for-byte unchanged (`the_checked_in_plugin_matches_the_guide` passes). No doc block ended up above the wrong item. The agy measurement doc sits on the `Carry::of` row it describes, and no path opens a new file or does new I/O.

What I found is three tests that couldn't go red, gaps that are not reachable today, and docs that say the wrong thing. On the epic's code, four reverts stayed green across the full unit and CLI suites: the `deliver` no-room guard, the Block filter in each of the two answer functions, and Antigravity's turn-head room.

**Fixed:**
- **Findings 4 and 10:**
  - New `Carry::wrap` lets the table pick the answer kind (Context for a Context slot, Block for a Hold slot). All three letter sites in `decide` use it.
  - New `Carry::admits` filters once in `answer`, before the agent split. It spells out every Decision × Carry combination, so a new variant forces a compile error.
  - `antigravity_answer` is back to a plain four-arm match.
- **Finding 5:** `letters_room` returns `None` when the earlier answer blocks.
- **New tests:**
  - `deliver_moves_no_letter_without_a_room` (finding 1) calls `deliver` with no room on a real mailbox.
  - `each_answer_lands_only_in_its_own_slot` (finding 2) has the expected slots written by hand.
  - CLI test `an_antigravity_turn_head_holds_whole_a_letter_codex_would_cut` (finding 3).
  - The test at hook.rs:14849 now asks `Carry::of` for the real room.
  - `letters_move_only…` now also checks that wrapped letters survive `answer` and that a blocking earlier answer leaves no room.
- **Docs (findings 6–9):** corrected, including cmd/hook.rs:182. For finding 12, one paragraph on `admits` says the refusal shape belongs to PreToolUse.

**Skipped:**
- Finding 11: the path can't be reached today, and the fix would move the guard back out to the callers.
- The structural change for finding 12: a "can refuse" flag per event would be over-engineering for a case nothing triggers.
- Finding 13: it is a separate design change, already parked as moai-yvev.
- The commit message of 41cbaa36 can't be amended. The fix commit should correct the `/hooks` claim.

**Checks on the fixed tree:** 1,895 unit tests pass (3 ignored), 728 CLI tests pass, and `clippy -D warnings` and `fmt --check` are clean. I re-ran 8 reverts against the fixed code and every one now fails at least one test, including the four that stayed green before. The scratch build copy is deleted.

  - `inbox` leaves unread `any-idle-worker` letters in place.
  - `send` and `inbox` print the blocked-dir line first, so a "who are you" error that follows makes sense.
- **Fenced `read/` (3):** `list` now checks each box together with its `read/`. A box whose `read/` points outside is reported once and its letters are not offered; they stay in the box.
- **Read time (4):** `take` writes the read time before the rename. On Linux it uses a path-based `utimensat` that doesn't follow links, and falls back to "now" when the reader isn't the owner. Other platforms open the file read-only.
- **Dangling links (5):** `place_dir` now follows a chain of dangling links to its end and refuses any link it cannot resolve.
- **Messages (6, 8):** `mail::refusal` returns code `broken` for a blocked dir. Blocked dirs are reported as `<dir>: <reason>` instead of "a letter that cannot be read".
- **Wait loop (7):** `inbox --wait` returns immediately when the whole mailbox is blocked.
- **`inbox --ack` error (9):** the `take` failure now goes through `mail::refusal`.
- **Tests (10):** extended `a_link_out_of_the_checkout_is_followed_nowhere`; added two unit tests and one CLI test (`a_fenced_roster_decides_nothing_and_a_box_whose_read_is_fenced_offers_nothing`); the CLI test now also checks the `broken` codes and the `--wait` early exit.
- **Smaller changes (11–13, plus one doc line):**
  - `sweep_read` skips letters whose id shows they were sent after the cutoff, so it stats far fewer files.
  - A shared `read_stem` parser replaces the two copies.
  - `Garbled` now carries a single `Why` enum instead of the duplicate fields.
  - `sweep` returns early on a blocked dir.
  - Corrected the agents temp-sweep doc comment (its reason was wrong) and added `mail_read_days` to the `ThresholdInTable` doc in `src/config.rs`.

**Skipped**
- **14:** fixing it means changing `cmd::skill`, which this diff doesn't touch. Worth an idea.
- **15:** left for your planned CHANGELOG and wiki steps. The exact lines are in the finding above; also mention `mail_read_days` in docs/agents.md.
- Also skipped:
  - Changing `relocate`'s return type (cosmetic).
  - Making `home_of`'s "two levels up" assumption explicit. Most older mail unit tests pass a bare scratch dir, so the fence is effectively off in them.
  - Sweeping read letters only from `moai agents`: that was the plan approved via moai-u3na.
  - Moving the read time into the file name: that changes the letter file format, so it needs your decision.
  - The small per-call path-resolution costs on the hook path: measured at about 0.1 ms per hook.

**Left as they are after the fixes**
- In a hook delivering several letters, letter k's read time is still written after letter k−1's rename.
- A link that can't be resolved but lexically points inside the checkout is refused with the "outside" message. Such a link could never be built through anyway.
- With the attendance dir blocked, hooks deliver nothing to that session until the link is fixed.

**Outside the working tree, for you to decide**
- The moai-work and moai-supervise skill texts say nothing about a non-zero `inbox` exit that names the mailbox. That now returns immediately, so a worker could re-run in a tight loop.
- Commit `db433d0d` cites "moai-ml0d.que 19번", but the epic body cites finding 10.

text: Next: /code-review max --fix 가 백그라운드에서 돈다(@code-review). 돌아오면 TaskStop·git status 로 트리를 보고, 고침을 fix: 커밋, 리뷰 원문을 노트로 남긴 뒤 7-1~7-4(CHANGELOG 는 Unreleased 의 Added 문안을 고치고 cq2 는 Changed 한 줄)와 머지로 간다

/code-review max --fix — moai-54yc 에픽 전체 (agent-ab4c50ca0f194b1a7)

The max-effort review is done and the fixes are applied, but nothing is committed. Tests pass (1905 unit, 733 integration), clippy is clean, `cargo fmt` is clean, and `moai init --check` reports the AGENTS block as current.

The review ran 10 finder angles, then verifiers, then a gap sweep. Four candidates were refuted and dropped.

1. src/cmd/mail.rs:376 — put_back reverts any busy row to the old idle/since, including a busy written by the same name that actually took the letter. A backgrounded `inbox --ack --wait` loses the letter to its own session's Stop hook, or to a second wait under the same MOAI_AGENT. The row goes back to idle while the session works the letter, and `send --wake` then picks the working session. Reproduced with an LD_PRELOAD shim (PLAUSIBLE: the documented foreground wait does not trigger it).
2. src/cmd/mail.rs:177 — `inbox <id>` lists both boxes with read/ included, so any unrelated unreadable letter makes the call exit non-zero, and every letter gets parsed. One corrupt file in w1/read/ makes `moai inbox <next> --ack` (the command the hook now suggests) move and print the letter, then exit 1. The code's own comment says a loop that sees non-zero after --ack drops the letter. It also costs 0.6 s at 5,000 read letters.
3. src/cmd/mail.rs:233 — `inbox <id>` says not_found ('someone else's, or swept') when it simply could not look. Reproduced in five states: `.moai/mail`, the box or read/ is a link out of the checkout; the roster is fenced; or the letter's own file is corrupt. In each case the code is `not_found` even though the letter is w1's and unread.
4. tests/cli.rs:24645 — The new die-on-write test lacks its sibling's SIGXFSZ->SIG_DFL reset and its check of why the process died. Reproduced: if the parent ignores SIGXFSZ (as CPython's os.system leaves it), the attendance write fails with EFBIG and the error is swallowed. The letter is moved, inbox exits 0, and the test fails on correct code.
5. tests/cli.rs:24923 — An assertion message slices Korean text by byte offset. In exactly the regression it guards (the tail line without the id), the offset lands inside '가'. The test then panics with 'not a char boundary' instead of showing its message (reproduced).
6. src/hook.rs:14936 — the_cut_names_the_letter_it_falls_in would still pass if `letters` simply named the last delivered letter. It uses two letters and the cut falls in the last one, so mutating `cut_in` to `delivered.last()` stays green.
7. tests/cli.rs:24695 — The bad-id test runs inside a repo, so it does not pin the documented 'refused before the repository is opened' order. Outside a repo, a malformed id gives bad_input and a valid id gives error. Moving the check after open_repo would leave the test green.
8. src/cmd/mail.rs:244 — Moving the attendance write earlier still leaves a window when one call takes several letters, and the new comment leaves out the caveat the Stop hook's comment has. Reproduced: two unread letters, a stall during letter 2's rename, then a kill. Letter 1 ends up read and never printed.
9. src/hook.rs:472 — `moai inbox <id>` has no paging, so the cut letters it exists to recover can be truncated again by the agent's own output cap. A letter over about 40 KB in Codex 0.160 (10k-token cap), or over 30,000 characters in Claude Code, loses its middle again; bodies may be up to 64 KB (PLAUSIBLE).
10. src/hook.rs:8536 — `.agents/` is now exempt from rule 2 but `.codex/` is not, and the SKIP comment wrongly implies Codex's hooks are exempt. Running the hook with nothing held: editing `.codex/hooks.json` is denied while editing `.agents/hooks.json` passes.
11. docs/agents.md:362 — The wiki still says a cut letter names `moai inbox --all`, never teaches `moai inbox <id>`, and its `Decided in:` line lacks moai-54yc. An agent following the manual dumps the whole mailbox, which is the output this epic replaced.
12. docs/agents.md:279 — The rule-2 'Not counted' list omits `.agents/`. The manual says an `.agents/` edit needs a held issue; the hook now lets it through.
13. CHANGELOG.md:112 — [Unreleased] lines 112 and 175 still say the cut names `moai inbox --all`, and the rule-2 `.agents/` change has no entry. The release notes would describe a cut line that no longer exists and omit a behaviour change.
14. src/guide.rs:1021 — The rule-2 prose is copied from SKIP by hand and no test ties them together. Editing only one side ships an AGENTS block and skills that teach a different rule 2 than the hook enforces, with every test green.
15. src/cmd/mail.rs:244 — `early: Option<Option<Was>>` plus a four-arm match: its late-busy arm can only fire without --ack. A flat form behaves the same in every combination; this was checked exhaustively. The current form costs readability only.

Fixed:
- put_back: when a take returns Lost, the new `mail::read_by` checks whether the same name took the letter; if so, put_back is skipped. A re-run of the shim experiments shows both the Stop-hook and two-wait cases now stay busy.
- `inbox <id>`: it now uses a new `mail::list_one`, which opens only that id's files. It says `not_found` only when nothing was in the way.
- Tests: new `dying_at_first_write` / `died_writing` helpers, shared by both die-on-write tests; both now pass under a SIGXFSZ-ignoring parent. The byte-slice message no longer panics. The cut test now has a third letter. The bad-id check also runs outside a repo. New pins for the no-`--ack` wait, an unrelated corrupt letter, the fenced mailbox, `list_one`, and rule-2 prose against SKIP.
- Cleanups and comments: `early` is flattened. The duplicated id refusal is now `bad_id`, with the i18n key renamed to `refuse.mail_id`. The multi-letter caveat is added to the comment. The SKIP comment is made precise. Stale frame numbers in two comments are corrected (586 of 600 now).
- Docs and changelog: `docs/agents.md` is updated. In `CHANGELOG.md`, the two false sentences are corrected and a Changed line for rule 2 is added. `--next` still picks 0.7.0.

Skipped:
- Needs a decision: paging for `inbox <id>` (an offset option, or cap the body size); whether to add `.codex` to SKIP; closing the multi-letter window in code (claim the letter before moving it, or take one letter per wait).
- Rare or negligible, left as is: a prompt hook writing busy inside the put_back gap still gets reverted (timestamps are whole seconds, so that write cannot be told apart; documented in put_back's comment). The same id can exist in two boxes, which needs a same-microsecond send; both letters print and nothing is lost. Losing workers now write the attendance row twice.
- Out of scope: the attendance rule exists in three copies, and refactoring it touches hook code outside this diff. Two low-severity points from the sweep: a lost `--ack <id>` exits 0 or not_found depending on timing; and `--ack <id>` cannot tell a fresh take from a letter shown again.

Subagent tokens: 5,265,654 in total (finders 3,124,710, verifiers 1,780,391, sweep 360,553), from the completion notices. The reviewer's own session tokens are unknown. Verifier reproduction scripts were left in its scratchpad under v1/, v2x/, v4a*.sh, v4b*, v5/.

text:
## Code review: `develop...HEAD` (moai-dj4j), max effort, with fixes applied

I found 15 problems and fixed 12 of them. The other 3 are performance or design follow-ups that I left alone. Nothing is committed: the changes are in five files in the worktree, ready for a separate `fix:` commit. `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and the full `cargo test --locked` all pass (1909 unit tests, 733 integration tests). I reverted each fix in turn and the new tests went red every time.

The two serious problems:
- **A tree that can't be built still got half-written.** If a directory slot in a tree holds a regular file or a dangling link, the up-front check passed it. `--dry-run` then exited 0, and the real run wrote the earlier trees before failing with `File exists`. I reproduced this with the real binary, and five finders found it independently.
- **Temp files could be created outside the checkout.** The `.moai` staging directory was never checked. In a linked worktree whose own `.moai` is a committed link pointing outside, `skill install` created its temp files in that outside directory. I confirmed it by watching the outside directory's mtime change.

The real run writes all of `.agents/skills/**`, then exits 1 with `.codex: File exists`. A dangling `.claude/moai-plugin -> /home/alice/...` does the same after `.agents` and the hooks are written. FIXED: new `unbuildable()` check in `measure`, plus a unit test and a CLI test."},
 {"file":"src/store.rs","line":2187,"summary":"`atomic` checks the target and the beside directories against the checkout, but never checks `stage`. The diff makes `<root>/.moai` the stage for every committed file.","failure_scenario":"In a linked worktree whose own `.moai` is a committed link to an outside directory or into `.git`, `skill install --agent codex` creates, fsyncs and renames every temp file through that directory. A crash leaves `*.tmp.*` outside the checkout. Reproduced. FIXED: `stage_inside`, so such a stage is skipped and the write happens beside the target. Test pins the outside directory's mtime."},
 {"file":"src/cmd/skill.rs","line":262,"summary":"Hook state is judged before the whole `.agents` tree is written and is not judged again before the overwrite. The race window grows from one fsync to the whole tree.","failure_scenario":"If a person adds their own hook to a stale moai `.agents/hooks.json` during that window, it is silently overwritten and `--json` says `was:stale`. The verifier reproduced this 3 out of 3 times. FIXED: each due hook is judged again right before it is written, and the report uses that state."},

NOT FIXED: it needs plan-level modelling and only crafted or broken repos hit it."},

FIXED: both beside places are blocked, so the write can only succeed through the stage."},

Removing the `.agents` part or the hooks part, or reverting `Undeclare` to `write_atomic_inside`, left every test green.","failure_scenario":"FIXED: the new CLI test covers the hooks part, `skill_install_for_codex_builds_nothing_through_a_link_outside` gained a `--dry-run` leg, and a new unit test covers `Undeclare` staging. Each goes red on revert."},
 {"file":"src/cmd/init.rs","line":998,"summary":"The rule for where a committed file's temp file goes was written twice: `init::tmp_dir` (with an `is_dir` probe that is now redundant) and `skill::write_one`.","failure_scenario":"The next caller could pick a different place. **Verifier verdicts that changed the plan:**
- **`write_committed`'s second measure is not redundant.** It catches cases where writing an earlier tree changes a later tree's verdict. I kept it and wrote down why in its doc comment.
- **The duplicated CLI fixture is not worth merging.** The two tests check different things.

**Before the merge (steps 7-3 and 7-4):**
- **CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` has no line yet.** The verifier suggests folding it into the existing Fixed entry for the plugin tree: every chosen tree is measured before the first write, `--dry-run` exits non-zero naming the place, and temp files go to `.moai/`.
- **Wiki:** `docs/agents.md:477-482` could add the new "is not a directory" refusal and say that `--dry-run` refuses the same way.

Review text — /code-review medium --fix (forked agent af28ed6d2e07cea30), scope 88e2c7fd (develop..HEAD)

I reviewed commit 88e2c7fd (the only commit on `develop..HEAD`) and found two problems in the guidance text. I fixed both in the working tree and did not commit. The ReportFindings tool wasn't available in this session, so the findings are only listed here.

**Findings**

1. `src/guide.rs:2067` (supervisor step 4; worker loop step 2 at about line 2729 has the same fault) — **medium.** If moai can't move a report into the read folder, the guidance says "the next wait shows the same letter again" but never says what to do next.
   - In `src/cmd/mail.rs`, when `mail::take` fails it calls `note_partial()` and leaves the letter unread (`reader` is still `None`).
   - The wait loop stops as soon as it sees an unread letter, so every later `moai inbox --ack --wait` comes back at once with that same letter and a non-zero code.
   - The new "stop" rule only covers the case with *no* letter. So a supervisor checks the same report over and over without pausing, which is the loop this commit was meant to remove. A worker would do the same work twice.
2. `src/guide.rs:2065` (worker at about line 2727) — **low.** The text says the link "points out of the checkout". But inbox gives up and returns at once for any fenced mailbox, and that includes a link that resolves into `.git`, where the message reads "inside git's own directory". The explanation was wrong for that case.

**What I fixed**
- **Finding 1:** the supervisor text now says "Check it once, then tell the person watching this window and stop rather than wait again". The worker text now says "Do it once, then tell the person … stop rather than wait again — waiting would hand you the same work twice".
- **Finding 2:** both paragraphs now say "points out of the checkout or into `.git`".
- **Tests:** I added assertions for the new sentences in `the_supervisor_and_the_workers_say_hello_and_trade_letters`. I also rewrapped the text so "do not run it again" stays on one line, because the existing `contains` check fails when a line break splits it.
- **Skill trees:** I regenerated them with `MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in`. This changed `.agents/skills/moai-{supervise,work}/SKILL.md`, `.claude/moai-plugin/skills/moai-{supervise,work}/SKILL.md` and `plugin.json`.
- **Tests run:** the full `cargo test` passes (1914 + 735 passed, 0 failed).

**Skipped:** nothing. The worker-side paragraph comes from an earlier commit (`moai-bkn4.yo1`), outside the reviewed diff. I fixed it anyway because it has the same fault and the two paragraphs are meant to say the same thing.

Review text — /code-review max --fix (agent a7eeee7930db79907), scope 0f8aeec6..worktree-moai-54yc

I applied 10 of the 15 findings to the working tree, uncommitted. Five are skipped and need a decision from you. The main thing the epic set out to do holds up: where a hook cuts a letter and where `moai inbox <id> --from <n>` resumes always line up. I fuzzed that against the debug binary, before and after the fixes, with about 1,000 hook cuts (Claude Stop and prompt-submit, Codex Stop) and paging runs, and got 0 failures. fmt, `clippy -D warnings` and the full `cargo test` pass (1917 + 736).

1. src/cmd/mail.rs:338 — Paging only covers `inbox <id>`. Without an id (`inbox --ack --wait`, which is how workers and the supervisor receive letters, plus `--ack` and `--all`) every letter is still printed whole, with no `--from` line, after `--ack` has already marked it read. A worker waiting on `moai inbox --ack --wait 540` gets a 60 KB brief: 63–75 KB of output, no continuation line, and the letter is already moved to read/. Claude Code or Codex cuts it at its output cap, and nothing tells the agent to page it with `inbox <id>`. Reproduced by four agents.
2. src/cli.rs:1141 — `--from` is accepted with no id when `--wait` is also given. clap quietly drops `requires = "id"` here because `id` conflicts with `wait` (the same quirk is documented on RmArgs). `moai inbox --from 5 --wait 1 --as w1` exits 1 with an empty id ("Letter  has 3 characters…"). `--from 2 --wait 0 --ack` exits 0, ignores `--from`, prints the letters whole and marks them read. Reproduced.
3. i18n/en.json:1083 — The hook's cut line (`hook.letter_cut`) says the named `moai inbox <id> --from <n> --as <me>` "shows the rest" (Korean: 나머지는 … 가 보인다). That command shows one page of at most 24 KB. A 45K-character letter cut at 7524: the named command stops at 22736 and names another `--from`. An agent that takes "the rest" literally stops early on a letter that is already marked read.
4. src/view/mail.rs:123 — If a letter's header lines alone are larger than the page budget, `page()` moves forward one character per call and prints the whole header every time. The hook's fallback branch sends the agent straight there with `--from 0`. A hand-placed letter with a 30,000-character subject: every page is about 30 KB, over the 24 KB budget, and reading a 30,000-character body takes 30,000 calls. Reproduced. `send` caps subjects at 200 characters, so only hand-placed letters or old dev-build letters can trigger it.
5. tests/cli.rs:25797 — The two CLI hook tests used to check the full cut command including `--as <me>`. Now they only check the prefix `moai inbox {id} --from `. A ko.json edit that moves `{me}` out of the command (without the backtick) would pass all tests, and a Codex shell without CODEX_THREAD_ID could no longer run the printed line.
6. src/cmd/mail.rs:248 — `list_one` can return the same id from two boxes (your own and any-idle-worker). The refusal then fires on the shorter copy, and each copy gets its own 24 KB page. A 54 KB copy plus a 4-character copy under one id: about 24 KB of output whose `--from` line is not the last line; running it is refused. It needs a hand-placed file or ids colliding at about 200 sends per second, and the old code already printed both whole.
7. CHANGELOG.md:35 — The new docs (also the help text in src/cli.rs:519 / docs/cli.md, docs/agents.md:377 and comments) say Claude Code's 30,000-character Bash cap "cuts the middle out". The installed Claude Code 2.1.289 instead saves longer output to a file and shows a short preview. Docs only; the pages fit under the cap either way. It depends on the Claude Code version.
8. src/cmd/mail.rs:249 — The out-of-range refusal checks `from >= len`, but the body's final newline is never shown. Body "abc\n": `--from 3` exits 0 and shows a blank line that the whole-letter view does not have. No offset the tool itself prints lands there; only a hand-typed one does.
9. src/hook.rs:284 — `block_to` repeats the framing of `letter_block`. The cut search depends on the two being byte-identical, and nothing enforced that. If one copy's frame changes, the chosen cut point drifts, and the cut could name `--from <len>`, which `inbox` refuses.
10. src/view/mail.rs:73 — `letter()` builds the 8-bytes-per-character position table just to draw the whole letter. The hook calls this for every waiting letter. About 512 KB of extra allocation per 64 KB letter on every hook run that has mail.
11. src/hook.rs:496 — `letters()` builds a full `Body` for every delivered letter only to size the digits of `--from`, then builds the cut letter's `Body` again. The cut letter is sanitized and indexed four times in one hook run.
12. src/hook.rs:8571 — `SKIP` is a hand-copied list of the directories `skill install` writes into, and no test ties the two together. This same bug already happened twice in this epic (cq2 `.agents/`, kr16 `.codex/`). The next new install location would be counted by rule 2 again.
13. src/hook.rs:505 — `position(..).unwrap_or(0)` has a fallback that can never run but reads like a deliberate policy. If the invariant ever broke, it would quietly cut inside letter 0. A panic is not acceptable here because the letters are already marked read.
14. src/view/mail.rs:123 — `page()` folds two cases into one `max`/`min`/`unwrap_or` chain and always evaluates `from + 1`. Easy to edit wrongly; it would panic on overflow if `page()` were ever called with `usize::MAX`.
15. src/cmd/mail.rs:251 — `args.id.as_deref().unwrap_or_default()` in the refusal; finding 2 shows this fallback is reachable. A refusal message with an empty id.

What I applied (in src/cli.rs, src/cmd/mail.rs, src/view/mail.rs, src/hook.rs, tests/cli.rs, i18n/en.json, i18n/ko.json):
- `--from` with `--wait`: `--from` now also has `conflicts_with = "wait"`, and the refusal takes the id from the let-chain. A new assertion in `inbox_pages_one_long_letter` fails on the old code.
- Cut text: now says "shows the next part" in English and "다음 쪽은 … 가 보인다" in Korean.
- Tests: both CLI hook tests check the full `moai inbox <id> --from <at> --as <me>`. The page walkers `pages_of` and `walk` also check the full continuation command.
- One shared frame: `block()` is now used by both `letter_block` and `block_to`. In the view, a private `framed()` is shared by `letter()` and `part()`, so `letter()` no longer builds the table. A new test checks that `letter()` equals `part(0, len)`, including read, returned and reply-to letters.
- `letters()`: the digit width now comes from the raw body's character count (an upper bound; at worst the cut lands one or two characters earlier). The cut letter's `Body` is built once, and the space left after earlier letters is computed once. The impossible fallback is now guarded by a `debug_assert`, which fires only in tests and never panics a real hook.
- `page()`: the `to` choice is a `match` with `saturating_add`; a brute-force check showed the same output for every case.
- Rule 2: new test `rule_two_skips_every_place_skill_install_plants`.

What I skipped:
- Finding 1, inbox without an id: the worker who wrote m81b already parked this as idea `moai-sn1t`. Fixing it changes what `--ack` takes and how the list prints, so it needs your decision. Since it sits on the epic's main delivery path, you may want to make it a member of `moai-54yc` rather than an idea.
- Finding 4, oversized header: the one-character step is a deliberate guard. The real fix is shortening the subject when displaying it, which is a display decision.
- Findings 6 and 8 (duplicate ids, the trailing-newline offset): both are very hard to reach; a proper fix for duplicate ids needs a way to pick one letter or share one page budget.
- Finding 7, docs about Claude Code's cap: it depends on the Claude Code version, so check which behaviour you want to describe before rewording. The rewording also means regenerating `docs/cli.md`.
- Smaller cleanups left alone: capping the binary-search probes saves only a few ms in release; sharing `Body::reach` with the TUI's `flex_cap` would touch unrelated TUI code; merging the duplicated test helpers is low value; making `Body` carry its letter guards against a pairing mistake, but every current call site pairs correctly.
- Refuted: the race when two workers read an open letter page by page (that is how ownership is designed); spelling the resume command in two i18n templates (the neighbouring keys do the same); `--from` being ignored with `--json` (your 2026-10-05 decision).

The reproduction and fuzz scripts are in the scratchpad, under `me-fuzz/` (`hookfuzz.py`, `codexfuzz.py`, `fuzz.py`) and `me-clap.sh`. I deleted the 2.2 GB scratch build directory I made.

text:
Review (/code-review max --fix, opus) — reviewer's own words

The review found 15 issues, most of them real. I fixed 12 in the worktree and left 3 (one is a user decision, two are older behaviour or need a bigger change). Nothing is committed. After the fixes, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` are clean, and the full `cargo test --locked` passes (1921 unit, 740 CLI). I also broke each main fix on purpose; every one turned its guarding test red on the right assertion.

1. src/cmd/agents.rs:273 — hello's new session-id fallback took over a row that is live on this machine under another process; the hook's attendee only takes a session-found row that is on another machine or whose process is gone. Failure: Window 1 (live pid, row `sup`, session S) and window 2 (`claude --resume S`, no hooks): `moai hello` in window 2 moved `sup` to its own pid. Window 1's `moai inbox`/`send` then failed with no_actor, and once window 2 exited `moai agents` swept `sup` as dead and returned its letters. Reproduced with the branch binary; the pre-diff binary left `sup` alone.
2. src/mail.rs:1047 — Presence::due still used the signed difference while quiet now measures |now - at|, so a stamp in the future was never refreshed by keep_alive, the inbox wait or the hook's rest. Failure: A clock that ran 40 min fast is set back: a live Codex worker waiting in `moai inbox --ack --wait` keeps its future stamp, shows as gone (skipped by --status idle and --wake), and with a step over a day is swept and loses its role. Reproduced against the pre-diff binary.
3. src/cmd/agents.rs:357 — hello kept the row's old session id ahead of the current one, so in a Claude window without hooks the row stayed on its pre-/clear session and the new lookup by session id missed it. Failure: Hookless worker: hello in session S1, /clear (S2, same process), hello again kept S1. After a container restart, `claude --resume S2` plus hello found nothing and either stood a second row or was refused agents_name_held — the moai-keka.fpm failure after one clear. Checked on this machine: Claude's shell session id does follow /clear.
4. src/mail.rs:1585 — send_message_name refused Claude names over 64 characters (the row-name limit, which exists because names are file names), although Claude Code allows 200. Those are exactly the names that always differ from the row name. Failure: A session renamed to a 70-character title gets a 64-character row name; `send --wake` gave no send_message_to and told the sender to SendMessage the row name, which Claude does not know.
5. src/mail.rs:1583 — send_message_name trusted ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json without checking it belongs to the row's process. Claude leaves files of dead pids behind (26 of 31 on this machine), and the file's procStart equals the row's pid_start. Failure: A row whose live pid is not the Claude that wrote that file (hello --vendor claude from a plain shell or --pid, or a recipient under another config directory): `send --wake` named a dead or unrelated session.
6. src/guide.rs:2113 — The supervisor skill told a Claude supervisor to wake a waiting worker with SendMessage without going through `moai send --wake`, now the only place that prints the name Claude knows. Failure: A worker registered as `moa-issue-25-<8>`: the supervisor SendMessages the row name and reaches nobody; the letter waits until a person types in that window.
7. src/mail.rs:1567 — send_message_name looks up the session file through the sender's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/HOME, while the recipient's hook named the row from the recipient's own setting. Failure: A worker started with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-b`: the sender finds no file and the wake line names the row, which SendMessage does not reach.
8. src/cmd/agents.rs:271 — hello looks up its row by process first and session second; the hook does the reverse and also drops the process's other rows. Failure: Hookless window on row `w1` does an in-process `/resume` into a session whose row `sup` belonged to a now-dead window: hello keeps `w1`, and the next `moai agents` sweeps `sup` and returns its letters. This predates the diff.
9. src/mail.rs:1006 — The symmetric distance makes two live machines whose clocks are more than 20 min apart read each other's fresh rows as gone (over a day apart: as expired), whichever side is wrong. Failure: The same MOAI_AGENT on two live machines 30 min apart: each prompt hook takes the name back and returns the other side's letters. With a 25 h skew, every `moai agents` on the slow machine sweeps the other's live rows. This follows directly from the 2026-10-06 user decision.
10. src/mail.rs:2435 — The new assertion `!wild.holds_made_name()` checked a row from this machine against the real clock, so it passed even with the old signed quiet. Failure: Reverting quiet kept the test green. The case it claims to cover — another machine's row stamped over a day ahead letting go of its made-up name — had no test.
11. CHANGELOG.md:100 — CHANGELOG and docs/agents.md said a row stamped ahead 'reads gone at once' / 'is swept at once', but quiet takes whichever of seen and since is nearer to now, so a dead row reads alive again within 20 minutes of either stamp. Failure: A worker on a container 2 h fast dies: it shows gone at once, then idle again from 1h40m to 2h20m after its death, so a supervisor can hand it work.
12. src/cli.rs:563 — Neither `moai agents --help` nor `moai hello --help` (nor the generated docs/cli.md) mentioned the clock-ahead rule or hello's lookup by session id. Failure: A live worker on a fast clock is listed gone seconds after it wrote its row, or hello takes back a row from another machine, and the reference explains neither.
13. i18n/en.json:1047 — The new wake line inserted the raw Claude name with nothing around it, and those names can contain spaces and commas. Failure: A session named `fix auth, then deploy`: an agent reading the line can't tell where the name ends and may SendMessage `fix auth`.
14. src/mail.rs:976 — Doc comments contradicted the code: stale() still said 'the later of seen and since', and made_name said only an unusable base returns None, when in fact None never happens. Failure: Someone fixing a sweep bug from stale's doc brings back 'take the later stamp, then measure', which reads a live row with a fresh since next to a far-future seen as expired.
15. src/cmd/agents.rs:257 — Cleanup: the 'this hello is for my own window' check was written three times; the `nobody` Woke result was built by hand in a second file (src/cmd/mail.rs:117); claude_session_title was pub with only in-module callers. Failure: The next flag that points hello at another process must be added in three places, and the next Woke field in two files.

What I changed
- Live row on this machine: a new `Presence::resumable` rule (`!here() || gone()`) is now used by both hello and the hook's attendee. hello leaves a live local row to its own process. Covered by the new test `hello_leaves_a_live_card_of_the_same_session_to_its_process`.
- Stamps in the future: `due()` now measures the distance either way, matching quiet, with a new assertion.
- Hookless /clear: in a Claude window that is its own (no `--pid`/`--as`), hello now writes the shell's current session id first. Covered by the new test `hello_without_hooks_follows_the_session_a_clear_started`.
- Claude's session file: it is read once, through a private `claude_session_book`. A file whose `procStart` differs from the row's `pid_start` is ignored. The name limit is now `TITLE_MAX = 200`, Claude Code's own limit. The control-character refusal stays. The waking test now covers a 70-character name, a control character, and a matching and a mismatched procStart.
- Supervisor skill: step 5 now says to send the next letter with `--wake` and follow the line it prints. I regenerated the checked-in plugin tree with `MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in`; the test `the_checked_in_plugin_matches_the_guide` requires this.
- Wording: the help text plus a regenerated docs/cli.md, CHANGELOG, docs/agents.md, the stale/expired/due/made_name doc comments, and backticks around `{name}` in the en and ko wake line.
- Cleanups: `Woke::new`. I did not derive Default, because `cmd::add` documents a rule against it. Also a single `own_window` binding and a simpler candidate chain in made_name.

What I left, and why
- Clock skew between live machines (9): this is the literal effect of the 2026-10-06 rule. Changing it is the person's call.
- Another config directory (7): reading the recipient's setting would mean parsing `/proc/<pid>/environ`. I only added a caveat in docs/agents.md.
- Process-first lookup in hello (8): this is older than the diff. Making hello match the hook would mean porting its "one process, one row" sweep.
- Swept/held messages: the i18n reasons still say "nothing marked it alive for a day" even when a row was stamped ahead. This is low impact, so I left the text.
- Not worth doing: sharing `is_word`, since the two limits now differ on purpose; and the copied test fixtures.
- Refuted by verification: stricter Unicode filtering, since Claude already strips those characters; hello numbering made-up names, which is documented as intended; the shared future-slack constant; and the bundled commit, which is one tracker item.

The `due()` fix was already on the list as a writer-side extra (idea moai-ekz9); the review found it is needed, so it is in. The reviewer's model line should leave out `tokens=`, because the reviewer does not know its count.

**What changed in the working tree** (fmt and `clippy -D warnings` are clean; `cargo test` passes 1921 unit and 737 integration tests):
- `src/hook.rs`:
  - `closing` now collects `rows` and `reviews` separately.
  - The new `fit(head, rows, reviews, foot, room, lang)` gives open reviews the room first, then fits held rows from the top. The order on the page is unchanged, and the text is byte-identical to before when everything fits.
  - `Carry::room` doc corrected; the redundant `#[allow]` removed.
  - Unit test updated: the review now stays and "N more" counts rows only. New boundary test added.
- `src/cmd/hook.rs`: `closing_hold` uses an exhaustive match on `Carry`, and its doc is reworded.
- `tests/cli.rs`:
  - The id extraction now uses `ids_in`.
  - The assert message no longer cuts Korean mid-character.
  - Removed an unneeded `session-start` call; a Claude Stop holds without one.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Added-bullet wording fixed, and a new Changed bullet for Claude.
- `docs/agents.md`: wording fixed and `moai-084j` added to `Decided in:`.
- `i18n/ko.json` and `Cargo.toml`: as listed above.

**Two fixes go slightly past "intended behaviour", so check them before committing:**
- **Reviews kept first.** The new unit test previously asserted that the review was dropped. The 2026-10-06 decision note covers only held-row bundles and assumes `moai prime` recovers whatever is dropped; reviews break that assumption, which is why I changed it.
- **Cargo.toml note.** The list grew from two sites to seven, so it covers four stale entries from before this diff.

**Skipped, needing a decision or out of scope:**
- **V2 (the `moai prime` pointer).** Naming the dropped ids in the overflow line would fix it, but that extends the line the person specified.
- **V3 (epic-closing warnings).** Fitting rows that would close their epic first would fix it, but that changes "from the top" for rows. A broader alternative is for `moai defer` to warn when it leaves an epic done.
- **V4 (oversized block).** `continue` instead of `break` would keep the rows that fit, and is proven to stay inside the room, but it changes the documented prefix policy; the trigger needs a title of about 7.6 KB.
- **V14 (`carried`).** Worth a follow-up idea, since `fit` can be reused there as is.
- **Dead `if !wip.is_empty()` guard.** It is pre-existing, and removing it means re-indenting 61 lines.

**Refuted:**
- The test's hand-written measures are a deliberate independent check.
- Reusing `status.more` instead of the new key isn't required: hook keys put commands inside the text by design.
- Not re-asking dropped rows later in the session is the designed behaviour.

Per CLAUDE.md, the fixes should go in as separate `fix:` commits from the worktree. The wiki page under `docs/` needs `git add -- docs` first.

Review of `pr-20-trial` (develop…HEAD, 27 files, +2492/−108) by /code-review max (fork of this session, claude-fable-5-1). Method: 10 finder angles → dedup → one verifier per candidate (run against the PR's debug binary in scratch git repos; symlink, slow-git shim, pty/`script` emulations) → gap sweep. Full suite passes (1942 unit + 757 cli). All findings CONFIRMED by reproduction unless marked; most severe first.

1. src/cmd/init.rs:385 — tracking_within folds every git failure (exit 128: safe.directory, broken .git/config, `.moai` symlink, git missing from PATH) into Tracking::Commit, so a tracker kept out of git is re-read as committed and the re-run `moai init` that status/--check point at plants commit-mode files into it with no way back. Repro: `moai init --tracking exclude`; break git; `moai status` demands rules → `moai init` writes .gitattributes, .gitignore block, merge driver, 33 KB AGENTS.md block; `moai init --tracking exclude` then refused as 'already planted as commit'. Fix: treat non-empty stderr or spawn error as unknown (as the budgeted path already does) and never re-plant committed files when tracking is unknown.
2. src/cmd/init.rs:1610 — A first-run init never consults git or the standing AGENTS.md block: in a clone of a repo planted with --tracking gitignore --guide file (or any repo whose .gitignore / global excludes already ignore .moai/) the non-terminal defaults plant commit mode and replace the link block; the next run then flips tracking the other way. `again` is false in a clone so tracking_of/guide_of are skipped; the first run must ask them too, or record the choice in config.toml.
3. src/store.rs:343 — look() takes any committed .moai found inside the worktree before trying main_tracker_for, and the two walkers use different markers (`climb`: `.moai` dir; `main_tracker_for`: `.moai/config.toml` file), so a sibling worktree writes a different tracker than the same subdirectory in the main checkout. Repro: main/.moai committed, main/svc/.moai out of git; `cd side/svc && moai add x` → written into main/.moai with the top prefix. Pre-PR the out-of-git variant wrote nothing; the PR turns that into a silent write elsewhere.
4. src/store.rs:344 — The sideways jump bypasses Repo::redirect and never consults MOAI_HERE, and find_from builds the Repo by struct-update instead of from_found — `MOAI_HERE=1 moai add` in a side worktree lands in main/.moai while `MOAI_HERE=1 moai init --check` says it plants here; find_here (doc: '안 옮긴다') now moves too.
5. src/cmd/init.rs:290 — agents_state reads .moai/guide.md under repo.here() (the checkout) although the guide lives at the tracker root; a missing guide is folded into Stale which agents_notice reports as `agents_hand_edited`. With --guide file plus --tracking exclude|gitignore every linked worktree and every clone carries that false notice permanently and nothing clears it.
6. src/cmd/init.rs:331 — guide_of cannot represent Guide::Hook ('no block + tracked' → Block): a later plain `moai init` plants the full block into a committed tracker that chose hooks; `init --json` reports guide:"none" for a hook tracker; an unreadable AGENTS.md on a local tracker exits 0 'everything is already in line' while `init --check` exits 1.
7. src/cmd/init.rs:775 — dotfile_notice now depends on one or two git subprocesses under the shared 2 s PROBE_BUDGET and returns an EMPTY file list on timeout, so the gap notices AND the dotfile_linked notice (previously a pure is_symlink check) silently vanish from status, the board, the TUI and the overview while `init --check` still reports them. Measured: `moai status` 2→3 git spawns; overview 3N. Docs still say 'up to three subprocesses'.
8. src/tui/init_screen.rs:30 — on_terminal() only checks isatty, but the inline viewport needs the cursor-position answer (ESC[6n); on a pty that never answers (TERM=dumb: Emacs shell, IDE consoles, `script`) `moai init` hangs ~2 s and exits 1 with nothing planted where it used to plant. ratatui's panic hook emitting ESC[?1049l stays installed (PLAUSIBLE).
9. src/tui/init_screen.rs:75 — ratatui-core Terminal::clear() restores the cursor to the last repainted cell, so the init report starts 2–11 rows below where the box stood (blank rows). Fix: take the viewport origin before clearing and MoveTo(0, y).
10. src/cmd/status.rs:219 — Because look() now makes here() a linked worktree that has no .moai, install notices are measured against that worktree and hint `moai init`, which init refuses there; the old CLIMBED line is gone for reads.
11. src/cmd/init.rs:338 — LOCAL_IGNORE's `/.moai/` is directory-only and local_block() mirrors only lock/tmp/mail/agents for a linked `.moai`, so in the `.moai -> tracker` layout under --tracking exclude|gitignore neither link nor target is ignored and `git add -A` commits the tracker.
12. src/init_choice.rs:221 — An explicit --driver beside --tracking exclude|gitignore is silently overridden and reported as driver:"skipped" ('run again to plant') while `init --check` calls it "off"; conflict() refuses the analogous --guide hook/--no-skill pair but not this one.
13. src/cmd/init.rs:383 — tracking_within asks `git check-ignore` through run_within, which strips GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM, so moai's tracking answer diverges from what the person's git does when the excludesFile lives in global config. Ask through run_reading_user_config like merge_driver::planted_anywhere.
14. src/cmd/init.rs:1873 — Under --tracking exclude the --json key `gitignore` is true when the lines went to .git/info/exclude and .gitignore was never touched; the meaning changed undocumented.
15. src/cmd/init.rs:1604 — The screen is opened before AGENTS.md readability is checked (person answers every row, refused on Enter, choices lost) and the non-interactive path checks the prefix after the git/clash refusals, so an agent following the first refusal is refused again. One shared refusal function (prefix → git → clash → AGENTS.md read) for all three sites.

Cut by the 15 cap (CONFIRMED unless noted): bare-repo linked worktree refused with a message promising a main checkout that does not exist (init.rs:442); `.git/info/exclude` that is a symlink makes `--tracking exclude` impossible (init.rs:1236); rule_of (init.rs:412) takes the first `:<digits>:` so a path like `a:1:b` flips gitignore→exclude; local-mode ignore lines appended before `.moai` exists and never rolled back (init.rs:1722); `--guide block` on a file-mode tracker leaves an orphan `.moai/guide.md` (init.rs:1781); refuse.init_tracking_fixed wording (PLAUSIBLE). Cleanup: refusal logic triplicated; LOCAL_IGNORE hard-codes skill::DIR; Flags duplicates Choices; complete() duplicates locked_by(); the prefix field re-implements tui::Input (Ctrl-U/W dead) and bypasses the keys tables; guide_of double-reads AGENTS.md; string value_parser lists instead of clap::ValueEnum; take_partial dance; init::one_line vs text::one_line. Conventions: trial merge commit bf93802a carries no issue id; review note moai-n22o.3gk hands ideas on without naming moai-0tyw/ghg2/hdzy. Refuted: anchored()'s escaping.

Side note from the reviewer: its pty run of the interactive screen registered its scratch repo with `moai project add` and ran `claude plugin install` (the screen's defaults); both were reverted. Two other sessions' scratch repos (`…/df746dad…/scratchpad/plant`, `…/df02f8e4…/scratchpad/plugcheck`) are still registered in `~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json` / `installed_plugins.json` — not from this review, left untouched.

Self-review at max of develop...worktree-moai-j9nf, including PR 20, the n22o removal, and the 15 requested fixes. Read the whole diff and the init choice/state setup, hook board call sites, guide readers, held-file access, terminal cleanup, git subprocess boundaries, and documentation. No review agents or background writers were started.

Findings taken in:
1. src/view.rs:972 — tracking_unknown had a report value and localized text but no human rendering arm. JSON worked while a person saw the raw key; the unused-text test also caught the missing consumer. Add the rendering arm and a human English CLI assertion alongside JSON.
2. src/cmd/init.rs:374 — git_place still stripped the global config that tracking_within now honored. A repository permitted by global safe.directory could answer check-ignore correctly yet be refused by rev-parse. Use the same user-config reader; the global-excludes fixture forces different ownership and grants safe.directory in that config.
3. src/cmd/init.rs:397 — before .moai exists, git check-ignore can report a directory as ignored under a star allowlist even though creating it enables !*/ and !*.toml. Read the config path in the same bounded subprocess and distinguish records by exact path. The standing partly-ignored/reincluded CLI regression exposed this and verifies the fix.
4. src/cmd/init.rs:964 — guide-file read errors used the worktree path although the guide was read at the main tracker. Map that error to the actual root; the linked-worktree regression corrupts the main guide and checks the named file.
5. src/init_choice.rs:579 — the exhaustive choices test still expected only HookWithoutSkill after DriverWithoutTracking was added. Update the expected conflict matrix to measure both independent constraints.
6. src/cli.rs:1030 — the TERM=dumb help addition exceeded the repository 80-column contract. Wrap it and regenerate docs/cli.md.

Review checks beyond findings: newly opened AGENTS/guide/hook artifacts use held regular-file reads and do not open a FIFO or outside link. Probe deadlines bound initialization and warning reads; failures remain unknown instead of producing commit-mode gap advice. Screen preflight, Enter and noninteractive refusal share InitCheck. The inline terminal cleanup retains raw-mode/cursor restoration without alternate-screen cleanup. Explicit flags retain lock semantics; inferred hook reruns do not reinstall. Doc blocks remain attached to the intended items, including the git user-config reader. Regression fixtures assert files, errors and real git behavior rather than reproducing implementation counters. Wiki and help describe first-run discovery, root guide access, global config, truthful JSON and driver conflicts.

The five cap-cut edges and the held explorer comment are outside this epic by its explicit contract. Recorded as moai-gqna, moai-mtae, moai-rj44, moai-m7yu, moai-3s7p and moai-ftwt; none is required to deliver the assigned 15 findings. No unfinished member was hidden as an idea.
