text: Sent: moai-2a (Claude, 에픽 나머지 — pxui → rsl → p1p → zk3 → 2b6, 끝 리뷰 max·병합)

사람의 결정 (2026-10-12): 한 자로 간다 — picked 가 names 를 이기는 것을 막는 판정(규칙 1·2·3·Stop)의 한 초점(theirs)에 싣는다. 받아들인 대가 하나 더: 그 줄을 집은 세션은 워크트리가 선 동안에도 루트를 고칠 수 있다(지금 규칙 2 가 '빈손' 으로 막던 것은 이름이 낳은 부산물로 본다). 서브에이전트가 경로 접두를 빠뜨려도 지나간다. 일꾼 글의 '규칙 2 가 루트 편집을 막는다'(worker() 6, guide.rs 의 브리프 문서 주석)는 rsl·p1p 에서 고쳐 쓴다. 다른 길(규칙 2 만 이름으로 재고 새 거절문)은 초점이 두 벌이 되어 걷었다

실기 결과 — 2026-10-12, Codex CLI 0.162.1

- 대상은 이 Codex 세션과 사람이 허락해 연 시험 자리뿐이다. 보호 대상으로 받은 감독·다른 Codex·Claude 탭에는 입력하지 않았다.
- cmux 시험 surface: F6482DEF-47B9-4EAF-A9A2-9C7AB018088B, workspace: 535F73BD-3B78-4E20-B603-DD240CBBA067. 시험 탭은 닫지 않았다.
- 스크래치: /tmp/moai-uzhx-bjj.iR8PVP (실제 경로 /private/tmp/…), git init + moai init + moai skill install --agent codex. tmux는 모든 호출에 env -u TMUX tmux -L moai-uzhx-bjj를 썼고 시험 Codex 칸은 %1이었다.
- 처음 모델·effort는 GPT-6.1-Sol high. 질문 화면만 /plan으로 재면서 시험 세션이 스스로 medium으로 바뀌었다. 이 조사 본 세션의 모델은 바꾸지 않았다.
- 토큰 항목은 사람의 결정대로 제외했다. /status와 토큰 기록을 조사하지 않았다. 아래에는 7번이 없다.

1. 띄우기
사실:
- cmux --id-format both new-split right --surface A5F97593-6F02-4F38-A051-417A44BD23CD --command 'cd /tmp/moai-uzhx-bjj.iR8PVP && codex --model gpt-6.1-sol' --focus false가 새 시험 칸을 열고 Codex를 띄웠다. 반환된 UUID는 위 surface다.
- 전용 tmux 서버에서 split-window -h -t survey:0.0 -c /tmp/moai-uzhx-bjj.iR8PVP -P -F '#{pane_id}' 'cd /tmp/moai-uzhx-bjj.iR8PVP && codex --model gpt-6.1-sol'도 서며 %1을 돌려줬다.
- 설치된 codex --help의 플래그는 -m, --model <MODEL>이다. 화면 시작 글은 `>_ OpenAI Codex (v0.162.1)`이다.
못 잼:
- 다른 Codex 버전·운영체제·cmux 설치의 동작은 재지 않았다.

2. Codex 자리 찾기
사실:
- 감독이 먼저 잰 사실: 갓 뜬 Codex surface의 cmux_process_pids에 Codex PID가 서며 ps -p <pid> -o args=는 /Users/raven/.local/bin/codex --disable computer_use -c mcp_servers.cmux-cua.…로 시작했다. node가 아니었다. comm=은 경로라 잘린다.
- 이번 시험 surface의 top --all에서는 cmux_process_pids가 [35280, 61066, 88321]로 관측됐다. Codex 외 PID도 있으므로 배열을 Codex PID 하나로 가정할 수 없다.
- ps로 35280의 args가 /Users/raven/.local/bin/codex … --model gpt-6.1-sol임을 확인했다. 여러 열로 읽은 comm은 /Users/raven/.lo로 잘렸고, 61066은 codex-code-mode-host였다. 88321은 그 뒤 ps를 부를 때 이미 사라졌다.
- tmux list-panes의 시험 행은 `%1 codex /private/tmp/moai-uzhx-bjj.iR8PVP 37733 0`이었다(pane_id, pane_current_command, pane_current_path, pane_pid, pane_in_mode 순서). 그 PID의 args는 codex --model gpt-6.1-sol이었다.
- cmux에서는 각 PID의 args 첫 실행 파일을 확인해야 한다. 경로 포함 codex를 읽고 codex-code-mode-host 등과 구별한다. root/워크트리 cwd 제한은 그대로 필요하다. tmux에서는 이 설치의 pane_current_command=codex로 가를 수 있었다.
못 잼:
- Node 래퍼로 설치한 Codex의 부모·자식 트리는 재지 않았다. SESSIONS를 바꾸거나 Claude 기록에 Codex를 넣지 않았다.

3. 입력창·응답 중·권한 물음·질문
사실:
- cmux read-screen과 tmux capture-pane에서 빈 composer는 `› Ask Codex to do anything`이었다. 두 표면에서 앞 두 코드포인트를 확인했다: U+203A(›), U+0020(보통 공백). Claude의 ❯+NBSP가 아니다.
- 갓 뜬 cmux 화면의 실제 하단 글:
  `› Ask Codex to do anything`
  `GPT-6.1-Sol high · /private/tmp/moai-uzhx-bjj.…`
  `? for shortcuts                       ⚠ 2 · f2`
- 초안 화면은 `› BJJ_DRAFT_20261012`였다. tmux 여러 줄 초안은 › 다음 실제 문장이 나오고 다음 줄에 계속됐다. 자리글 문구는 초안으로 교체되지만 과거 사용자 메시지도 ›로 시작하므로 화면의 아무 › 행을 composer로 읽으면 안 된다.
- 응답 중 실제 글은 cmux에서 `• Working (2s • esc to interrupt)`, tmux에서 `◦ Working (2s • esc to interrupt)`였다. tmux 상태 줄 끝에 `⠧`도 관측했다. 그 아래에 빈 자리글 `› Ask Codex to do anything`이 함께 있었다. 완료 화면에는 `Worked for 3s • 2:34 AM` 같은 과거 소요시간이 남았다. 과거 Worked와 현재 Working을 구별해야 한다.
- tmux의 실제 권한 화면(ANSI를 걷은 글):
  `Would you like to run the following command?`
  `Environment: local`
  `Reason: BJJ permission survey: allow the harmless true command?`
  `$ /usr/bin/true`
  `› 1. Yes, proceed (y)`
  `2. Yes, and don't ask again for commands that start with`
  `   /usr/bin/true (p)` (화면에서는 실행 파일을 백틱으로 감쌌다)
  `3. No, and tell Codex what to do differently (esc)`
  `Press enter to confirm or esc to cancel`
- cmux에서도 같은 권한 제목·Reason·$ 명령·승인 선택지를 실제 해결 전에 읽었다. 좁은 높이에서는 일부 선택지가 read-screen에서 빠졌다. lines=40/50이 요청한 줄 수만큼의 전체 TUI를 보장하지 않았다.
- /plan의 request_user_input 질문 화면에서 실제 글:
  `Question 1/1 (1 unanswered)`
  `BJJ question fixture: choose A or B?`
  `› 1. A                  Choose fixture A.`
  `2. B                  Choose fixture B.`
  `3. None of the above  Optionally, add details in`
  `                      notes (tab)`
  `tab to add notes | enter to submit answer`
  `esc to interrupt`
- surface.input_state의 직접 관측(state / agent / lifecycle / waiting_on_human / blocks_typing):
  - 갓 뜬 빈 칸: empty / false / unknown / false / false (감독의 선행 측정과 같음).
  - 갓 뜬 칸의 제 초안: draft / false / unknown / false / false, draft_length=18.
  - 응답 중 자리글: empty / true / running / false / false.
  - 뒤의 제 초안: draft / true / running / false / true, draft_length=14. 이미 완료 응답이 보일 때도 lifecycle=running이 남았다.
  - /new 작업 디렉터리 선택 메뉴: draft / true / idle / false / true, draft_length=138. 실제 초안이 아닌 메뉴를 draft로 읽었다.
  - A/B 질문 메뉴: draft / true / running / false / true, draft_length=115. 실제 질문인데 waiting_on_human=false였다.
  - 해결 전 권한 물음: dialog / true / needsInput / true / true.
  - 권한 해결·BJJ_PERMISSION_DONE·빈 자리글이 보인 뒤: empty / true / needsInput / true / false. 이 값은 마지막 재조회에서도 남았다.
- 따라서 Codex에서 input_state가 늘 unknown이라는 전제는 틀렸다. 다만 state=empty만으로 응답 완료를 판정할 수 없으며, lifecycle/waiting 값도 화면과 어긋나거나 남을 수 있었다. 초안·메뉴는 부분적으로 잡는다.
- 화면 판정 규칙: 살아 있는 Codex PID를 먼저 확인하고 composer의 가장 아래 입력 영역을 읽는다. ›+자리글은 초안이 없다는 단서일 뿐이다. 현재 Working·스피너, 실행 승인 제목/선택지, Question … unanswered, 슬래시/작업 디렉터리 선택 메뉴, 실제 입력 문장이 하나라도 있으면 일을 보내지 않는다. 과거 사용자 ›·과거 Worked를 현재 입력창으로 읽지 않는다. 화면과 JSON이 어긋나거나 일부가 잘려 판별할 수 없으면 사람에게 맡긴다. 보고 완료 확인과 함께 판정해야 한다.
못 잼:
- 모든 스피너 프레임·테마·너비, 입력 상태의 지연/잔류가 생기는 내부 원인, 다른 버전의 안정된 API 계약은 재지 않았다. 이 표는 이 설치에서 관측한 값이다.

4. /new
사실:
- cmux send --surface <시험 surface> -- '/new\n'만 보내면 입력창에 `› /new`와 다음 빈 줄이 남고 대화는 비워지지 않았다. /hooks\n도 같았다. \n을 제출 Enter로 가정하면 안 된다.
- 그 뒤 별도의 cmux send-key --surface <시험 surface> enter 한 번은 /new를 실행했지만 새 대화로 바로 가지 않고 다음 메뉴를 열었다:
  `Where should the new conversation run?`
  `› 1. Use current Git worktree  Keep using the current`
  `                             working directory`
  `2. Create new Git worktree   Create a separate`
  `                            checkout of this`
  `                            repository in another`
  `                            directory`
  `enter select · esc back`
- 여기서 Use current Git worktree에 별도 Enter 한 번 더를 보내 새 대화 시작 화면과 빈 자리글을 확인했다. 새 워크트리는 만들지 않았다.
- tmux send-keys -t %1 /new Enter를 한 호출로 보냈을 때도 입력창에 /new가 남았고, 나중에 다시 읽어도 실행되지 않았다. 별도 호출의 Enter로 같은 작업 디렉터리 메뉴가 열렸고, 또 별도 Enter로 현재 디렉터리에서 새 대화를 열었다.
- /plan·/model·/quit를 텍스트만 넣고 화면을 읽은 뒤 별도 Enter를 보내면 해당 슬래시 메뉴/명령이 실행됐다. /model의 `Select Model and Effort` 화면도 실제로 열렸다. /quit는 정상 종료됐다.
- 비우기는 완료 보고·빈 입력창 확인 뒤, 명령 텍스트와 Enter를 분리하고 매 단계 화면을 읽어 선택 메뉴까지 처리해야 한다. Enter 횟수를 고정해 보이지 않는 선택지를 누르지 않는다.
못 잼:
- tmux의 한 호출에서 첫 Enter가 실행되지 않은 내부 원인이 빠른 입력의 붙여넣기 판정인지 슬래시 처리인지는 분리해 재지 못했다. 모든 /new 설정에서 같은 메뉴가 뜬다고 보장하지 않는다.

5. 여러 줄 붙여넣기·초안 가드
사실:
- 첫 사실: 이 조사를 보낸 원래 메시지는 여러 줄 전체를 한 덩이로 받았다. 중간 줄바꿈에 나뉘어 제출되지 않았다. 감독이 쓴 문법은 cmux paste --surface <이 창> --submit - < 파일이었다.
- 시험에서도 `cmux paste --surface <s> --submit - < 파일`은 설명+세 표식 줄을 한 번에 제출했고 Codex가 BJJ_LINE_A / BJJ_LINE_B / BJJ_LINE_C 세 줄을 한 응답으로 돌려줬다.
- 반면 이슈 본문에 쓰인 `cmux paste --surface <s> --submit -- - < 파일`은 파일을 읽지 않고 문자 `-` 하나를 제출했다. 시험 Codex 화면에 `› -`와 `Your message contained only “-”. What would you like me to do?`가 섰다. 이 설치에서는 stdin의 - 앞에 --를 넣지 않는다.
- tmux load-buffer -b bjj-multiline <파일>, paste-buffer -p -b bjj-multiline -t %1은 여러 줄을 제출하지 않고 composer에 유지했다. 별도 send-keys -t %1 Enter 한 번으로 한 메시지가 제출됐고 같은 세 표식 응답을 받았다.
- tmux의 제가 만든 초안 위 붙여넣기는 `› BJJ_TMUX_DRAFT_This is a controlled UI survey. …`처럼 이어졌다. 기존 초안은 보존된 채 앞에 붙어 하나의 입력이 됐다. 빈 칸 확인은 필수다.
- cmux 초안 가드는 조건부였다. 초기 agent=false, draft_length=18, blocks_typing=false일 때 제가 만든 초안에 cmux paste를 시도하자 막지 않고 `› BJJ_DRAFT_20261012BJJ_PASTE_SUFFIX`가 됐다.
- 뒤에 agent=true, draft_length=14, blocks_typing=true일 때 같은 제 초안 위 paste는 exit 1로 거절했고 아무것도 보내지 않았다:
  `Error: paste: the agent prompt in F6482DEF-47B9-4EAF-A9A2-9C7AB018088B holds text someone is typing, so nothing was sent.`
- 해결 전 권한 dialog에서는 send-key enter도 exit 1로 거절했다:
  `Error: send-key: F6482DEF-47B9-4EAF-A9A2-9C7AB018088B is waiting on a question or dialog, so nothing was sent.`
  사람이 시험 칸을 직접 처리했다. --force는 쓰지 않았다.
- “Codex에는 초안 가드가 안 선다”도 “항상 보호한다”도 이 설치의 사실이 아니다. 직접 화면을 읽고 초안·응답 중·질문·권한 물음에 입력하지 않는 규칙은 여전히 필요하다.
못 잼:
- 가드가 agent=false/true로 달라지는 내부 구현·설치 조건, 모든 줄 길이/붙여넣기 크기를 재지 않았다.

Review hooks`, `2. Trust all and continue`, `3. Continue without trusting (hooks won't run)`였다. 사람이 허락한 뒤 시험용 네 훅을 신뢰했다.

10. worker.md의 Claude 낱말을 이 Codex가 읽는 법
사실:

- EnterWorktree(path): 이 이름의 Codex tool은 없다. 각 shell 호출의 workdir를 절대 경로로 주거나 명령에서 그 절대 경로로 cd한다. 한 번의 exec에서 cd해도 다음 exec의 cwd가 바뀐다고 가정하지 않는다.
- ExitWorktree(keep): 이 이름의 tool은 없다. 하지만 “아무것도 안 함”이 아니다. 루트 tracker commit·HEAD 확인 전에 다음 호출의 workdir/cd를 Root: 절대 경로로 되돌린다. worktree 삭제는 그 밖에서 하고 실제 merge 확인 뒤에 한다.
- AskUserQuestion: Claude tool 이름 그대로 호출할 수 없다. 이 창에서는 request_user_input_async로 사람에게 묻고 계속 가능한 일을 했다. 질문에 의존하는 실행은 답을 기다렸다. 터미널 Codex의 Plan mode에는 request_user_input이 있어 위 A/B 질문 UI를 실제로 냈다. 도구가 없으면 이 대화에서 묻고 기다린다.
- /model: Codex에도 실제로 있다. 시험 tmux에서 /model Enter를 분리해 Select Model and Effort를 열고 GPT-6.1-Sol (current)를 확인한 뒤 Esc로 나왔다. “Codex에 /model 없음”은 틀리다. 모델 변경은 사람의 일이라는 worker 규칙을 유지한다. /plan은 이번 설치에서 시험 세션의 effort를 high에서 medium으로 자동 변경했다.
- /code-review <grade> --fix: Claude의 그 명령을 Codex에서 실행했다고 할 수 없다. Codex 자체 review 기능이 있다는 것과 감독이 정한 opus 리뷰의 절차는 다르다. 이 C 에픽의 지시대로 Codex는 멤버/시험/커밋 뒤 Review-ready:를 에픽 노트로 보고하고 멈추며, 감독의 review 결과 및 merge and close 지시를 기다려야 한다. 이번 멤버에서는 리뷰를 호출하지 않았다.
- TaskStop: 이 이름의 tool은 없다. 임의로 다른 세션/프로세스를 죽이는 것으로 번역하지 않는다. 제가 띄운 명령만 제공된 실행 세션 수단으로 정리하고, 감독이 돌린 review나 정리할 수 없는 작업은 보고에 이름을 남긴다.
- SendMessage(to: <supervisor>, …): Claude 세션 간 SendMessage를 이 도구 모음에서 실행할 수 없다. collaboration.send_message는 제가 spawn한 sub-agent 대상이고 cmux의 다른 실제 Codex/Claude 탭인 moai-8d와 같은 대상이 아니다. 이 배정에서는 보고를 늘 `moai note <epic> -b -`의 report:/Review-ready:/Decision needed: 머리로 남기고 루트에서 경로 지정 commit한 뒤 사람에게 위치를 알린다. 감독 탭에 입력하지 않는다.

- Claude tool과의 1:1 실행 호환성은 없다. 이 에픽의 나머지 코드·문서 멤버는 수행하지 않았다.

리뷰 원문 — `/code-review xhigh --fix milestone/moai-fmge` (opus, 감독 moai-8d 가 .worktrees/moai-uzhx 에서, 2026-10-12)

I reviewed `milestone/moai-fmge...HEAD`, the moai-uzhx epic (10 files). The two serious bugs are in the Codex steps file and the report watch. First, a Codex worker skips straight to the merge after the supervisor's review, so the review's fixes and the CHANGELOG and wiki steps are left out. Second, the supervisor can't watch for reports on a newly handed backlog, because the epic doesn't exist yet when the assignment is pasted.

I fixed 14 of the 15 findings in the working tree and committed nothing. The full test suite passes (2004 unit, 785 cli), including two new checks: one actually runs the report watch against a fake `moai`, the other parses the Python inside the cmux surface script. I regenerated the checked-in plugin copy with `MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in`. The changes touch `src/guide.rs`, `src/skill.rs`, `docs/agents.md` and the regenerated files under `.claude/moai-plugin/`.

1. src/guide.rs:4539 — worker_codex tells Codex to 'Resume 8–11' after the review. That skips the end of worker.md step 7 (taking in the review's fixes) and steps 7-1 to 7-4.
   Failure: The supervisor's reviewer leaves its fixes uncommitted in the worktree, as REVIEW_BRIEF says. Codex jumps to the merge in step 8, so the fixes are not in the merge and `git worktree remove` refuses or loses them. The CHANGELOG line (7-3), the wiki (7-4), the reclaim of parked backlog (7-1) and the release sort (7-2) never run.
2. src/guide.rs:3127 — The report watch must read `<epic>` before the paste, but a backlog sent `from step 1` has no epic yet; promote creates a new id later.
   Failure: For the most common assignment there is no epic id to give the watch, and `moai show <epic>` exits non-zero. No Monitor ever sees the Codex worker's `Review-ready:` or `report:`, so the person has to tell the supervisor again — the very problem this epic set out to fix.
3. src/guide.rs:2508 — The shared Codex rules told the supervisor to 'Finish the review issue' before 'merge and close', but worker.md step 10 has the worker close it. Nothing picked the review issue up, though rule 3 and REVIEW_BRIEF ('picked up already') require it.
   Failure: The supervisor closes the review before Codex has taken anything in, so the close message records nothing. Then Codex's step 10 tries to close an issue that is already done. Or the review runs on an issue still in todo.
4. src/guide.rs:3143 — The watch skipped every entry with `at <= since` after moving the cursor to the newest timestamp seen. Journal timestamps are whole seconds.
   Failure: A poll sees a `Next:` note at 12:00:05, then the `report:` lands in the same second. Every later poll skips the report, and re-arming from that cursor skips it again, so the report is never announced.
5. src/guide.rs:3138 — Only `report:` ended the watch, yet the text says to re-arm after pasting 'merge and close'.
   Failure: The first Monitor is still running when the second is armed. Two monitors watch one epic, and the final report fires twice.
6. src/guide.rs:2807 — The tmux and cmux paste steps reused the supervisor's Claude `Model:` suggestion, and worker-codex never said the Claude model ladder does not apply.
   Failure: Codex receives something like `Model: opus (high — …)`. Following worker.md, it asks the person to `/model opus` in Codex, and in 9-1 it is told to take an OpenAI name from that same `Model:` line.
7. src/guide.rs:3139 — Decision heads were matched with `startswith`, but CLAUDE.md's 'when blocked' format starts with the id: `<id> 진행 중 결정이 필요합니다.`
   Failure: A Codex worker in this repository that follows CLAUDE.md writes `moai-x 진행 중 결정이 필요합니다.`. The watch never reports it, and the worker sits blocked with nobody told.
8. src/guide.rs:2750 — The tmux text checked only one level of children and accepted a 'Codex CLI entry point'. The shared empty-box rule requires the first executable's basename to be `codex`.
   Failure: With an npm install, the pane's shell starts `node …/bin/codex`, which starts the native `codex` one level further down. The two rules contradict each other, so the supervisor either refuses a live worker or accepts a launcher the shared rule rejects.
9. src/guide.rs:3517 — The cmux surface script ran `git worktree list` in the current directory instead of the root it was given.
   Failure: Run from the scratchpad or anywhere outside the root, git fails or lists another repository's worktrees. The script then says 'check failed' or allows the wrong paths.
10. src/guide.rs:3538 — `shlex.split` was applied to `ps -o args=` output, which is not shell-quoted.
   Failure: Any Codex argument with an odd number of apostrophes (a `-c` value, a path) raises ValueError. That live Codex tab is then silently left off the candidate list.
11. src/guide.rs:6538 — The new tests only ran `bash -n`, which never reads the Python inside the heredocs, including the cmux script that goes through `format!` brace escaping.
   Failure: One misplaced `{{` or `}}`, or a wrong comparison in the watch, ships as broken Python while every test stays green.
12. src/skill.rs:1720 — The exemption for worker-codex.md asserted something always true (`worker_codex()` contains `worker.md`).
   Failure: If the tmux or cmux skill stops naming `references/worker-codex.md`, the planted file points nowhere and the test still passes.
13. src/guide.rs:2494 — The skill text names `moai models --json`, `[models] codex` and `REVIEW_BRIEF`, which do not exist on milestone/moai-fmge or this branch; they come from the unmerged moai-9tqo.
   Failure: If this epic merges into the milestone before moai-9tqo, the shipped skills tell the supervisor to run a command that does not exist and to use a brief that is nowhere.
14. src/guide.rs:4472 — worker-codex said to read `worker.md` 'at the absolute path supplied by the supervisor', but only worker-codex.md's own path is supplied (the docs said 'paths', plural).
   Failure: Codex looks in the assignment for a second path that is never there.
15. src/guide.rs:3600 — The cmux text said 'When the screen clearly selects `Use current Git worktree`, the person handles that menu', which reads as a condition; the tmux text says 'Even when'.
   Failure: A supervisor reads the cmux wording as permission to answer the menu itself whenever the selection is not clear, and may choose a new worktree.

What the fixes do:
- Codex steps file: after "merge and close", Codex finishes step 7 (commits the review's fixes as a separate `fix:` commit and notes what it hands on), then runs 7-1 to 11 and 12. A new "Step 1" has Codex write `moai -C <root> note <id> 'Unfolded: <epic>'` on the backlog right after unfolding. The `Model:` line now names the Codex model, and worker.md's Claude ladder is said not to apply.
- Report watch: a backlog is watched until its `Unfolded:` note, then the watch is re-armed on the new epic. It now ends on `Unfolded:`, `Review-ready:` or `report:`. Same-second notes are told apart by what has already been seen, and the Korean decision phrase is matched anywhere in the first line.
- Supervisor review steps: the supervisor picks the review issue up, waits for the reviewer's words, and leaves the issue open for Codex to close.
- Finding Codex processes: tmux now checks two levels below the pane's shell for npm installs, and the shared rule rejects the `node` launcher but accepts the native `codex` it starts. The cmux script uses `git -C <root>` and falls back to a plain split when `shlex` fails.
- Tests and docs: the skill test now checks that both the tmux and cmux skills name `references/worker-codex.md`. `docs/agents.md` describes `Unfolded:` and Codex taking the review's fixes in.

Not fixed: the missing `moai models` and `REVIEW_BRIEF`. They come from moai-9tqo, so the fix is to merge moai-9tqo into `milestone/moai-fmge` before this epic — the epic body already says that order is cleaner.

Open question: `Unfolded:` is a new note heading the worker writes, so it adds to the contract between worker and supervisor. Check that it matches what moai-9tqo's supervisor text expects before merging.

text:
Review text — /code-review xhigh --fix (agent a461371cd1d3c8351, the reviewer's final message as it came)

The review of `moai-9tqo` (merge-base `dd4ea02b..HEAD`, xhigh) found 15 problems. I fixed 10 in the working tree, left them uncommitted, and skipped 5 that need a decision or are out of this diff's scope.

The most serious ones are four protocol bugs in the new subagent worker steps. Each would make a real round fail or loop:

1. **The review issue is never picked up, so rule 3 refuses the review.** A subagent worker stands in the root, so the hook treats an unpicked review issue as belonging to `.worktrees/<epic>`. The refusal then tells the nested reviewer to create a second review issue. The review brief already says "picked up already". Step 7 now picks it up first.
2. **The model-raise loops forever.** After `Model: raise to complex`, the supervisor re-sent the same message, so the new worker still read `Model: <old>` as too light and handed the same line back. The `Model:` and `Effort:` lines are now changed before re-raising.
3. **The model notes come out as `anthropic/anthropic/<name>`.** The report's `Model ran:` value already has the vendor, and the templates added it again. The parser rejects that form, so the work count silently misses those lines. Both templates now say to copy the name after `anthropic/`.
4. **"Measure before you unfold" came after the unfold instructions.** A worker that raises after unfolding leaves the next worker an already-done backlog item. It is now at the head of step 1.

Test results:
- After the fixes: `cargo test` passed (2005 unit, 791 CLI). `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` are clean.
- Last full run: one test failed, `merge_driver::the_probe_calls_the_command_instead_of_reading_its_mode`. It passes alone, and the 3la report already notes it as flaky.
- Plugin files: I regenerated the planted ones with `MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in`.

Findings (file, line — summary — failure scenario):

1. src/guide.rs:4185 — Subagent step 7 never picks up the review issue, yet the review brief says 'picked up already'; from the root the hook treats an unpicked review issue as the sibling worktree's. — The nested review's code-review call is refused by rule 3, whose message says to create a new review issue under a member, so a duplicate review row is made or the review never runs.
2. src/guide.rs:2376 — After 'Model: raise to complex' the supervisor re-raised with the same message, so the Model: and Effort: lines were unchanged. — The new worker runs on the complex model but still reads the work as heavier than the old Model: line and hands back the same line, an endless raise loop.
3. src/guide.rs:2455 — The supervisor template 'model: anthropic/<model ran>' gets a value that already reads 'anthropic/<name>' (same in step 10 with <model it ran>). — The note reads 'model: anthropic/anthropic/opus-5.5'; the parser rejects a second '/', so work and stats silently drop those lines.
4. src/guide.rs:4059 — Step 1's 'measure before you unfold' line sat after the unfold and milestone instructions. — The subagent unfolds, then hands back the raise line; the next worker 'starts from step 1', finds the backlog done and stops, leaving an unfolded epic nobody holds.
5. src/cmd/hook.rs:784 — The pick record's 'mine' set includes uncertain ('?') picks; moai-pxui now uses it in blocking decisions, where it beats a sibling worktree's name. — A pick that may never have run (an '&&' chain, or one that lost the --from race) takes over a row another worktree holds; rule 1 then blocks and Stop holds, breaking moai-hze6 ('records only release').
6. src/guide.rs:1947 — The skill said a dead subagent worker's row 'comes back in 0 like any stalled work', but its worktree still stands, so it is never listed as stranded. — After a supervisor crash, step 0 shows a path instead of none and never hands the work on, so it is orphaned.
7. src/guide.rs:2191 — The [models] value is passed as-is to Agent(model:), which accepts only the names its model parameter lists, and the skill did not say what to do when it is refused. — A person writes develop = "opus-5.5" (the real-name form CLAUDE.md teaches for notes); every Agent call is refused and the supervisor has no rule, so it may swap in a model of its own choosing.
8. src/guide.rs:1920 — The supervisor text and the ROLES table point to a 'Codex workers' section in moai-cmux/moai-tmux that does not exist on this branch. — If this epic ships before moai-uzhx, the reference points nowhere.
9. docs/agents.md:433 — The wiki said the supervisor's turn end is 'held until they close'; Stop actually holds once a session. — Readers expect every turn end to be held while subagent rows stay open.
10. src/guide.rs:4348 — Worker step 10 said that while the worktree stands the hook 'reads this work as a sibling worktree's'; after moai-pxui that is false for rows this session picked. — The docs contradict the code: for a subagent's own review issue, the hook does refuse a close without -m.
11. src/cmd/hook.rs:777 — away_of now reads the picks directory (every session file) on every PreToolUse when worktree names and picked-up rows exist, including calls that always pass; blocked calls read it up to three times. — Extra disk I/O on every tool call; the files are tiny today (at most 8 per repo), so the cost is small.
12. CHANGELOG.md:61 — A stray blank line inside the [Unreleased] Changed list made it a loose list. — The released notes render that section with paragraph spacing, unlike the other sections.
13. src/user_config.rs:49 — The comment said MODELS_DEFAULT fixes the output order, but --json key order is BTreeMap alphabetical. — Misleads anyone relying on JSON key order.
14. src/view.rs:3434 — A role row is marked 'default' by its own key only, while its effort tail may be user-set (or the reverse). — 'develop  sonnet  (high)  default' when only effort was written.
15. src/guide.rs:150 — The 'plan' role is used by no supervisor step (workers unfold on their own model), and 'bulk' claims the 64KB summary, which the review subagent writes on the review model. — The person's table has keys that never take effect.

Fixed (1–4, 6–9, 12, 13):

1. install.ps1:237 — the refusal's re-run line writes `$env:MOAI_REPO=<bare repo>`, which PowerShell runs as a command, so the variable is never set. MOAI_REPO=fork/moai and a moai.exe that isn't ours: the printed line errors on `fork/moai`, then `powershell ... -File install.ps1 -Force` installs from buzzni/moai over it.
2. src/update.rs:270 — `Plan::line()` for PowerShell has the same unquoted `$env:MOAI_REPO=` (ps_quoted leaves `fork/moai` bare), though its doc comment says it is quoted. `moai update --dry-run` prints a line that does not set the variable when pasted.
3. tests/cli.rs:8166 — `served()` now includes Windows, so `every_command_still_speaks_json` runs `hoisted()`, which names the copy `moai`, not `moai.exe`; the JSON sweep goes red on Windows.
4. src/update.rs:181 — off unix, `writable()` treats a folder's read-only attribute as "cannot write", but Windows ignores that attribute on folders (Explorer sets it on customised folders). `moai update` refuses NotWritable where writing works.
5. install.ps1:362 — fallback names `moai.exe.<pid>.old` are never removed by later runs.
6. src/cmd/update.rs:148 — the temp script `moai-update-<pid>.ps1` has a predictable name and `fs::write` follows a file or link already there; a write failure is reported as "could not start powershell".
7. src/update.rs:251 — `ps_quoted` and install.ps1's `Quote` leave `,` and a leading `@` unquoted; in PowerShell `a,b` is an array and `@` splats.
8. src/update.rs:236 — `\\?\` was stripped only from `-Dir`; `Plan.dir` (`--json` dir, "running … over {dir}") and refusals still showed `\\?\C:\...`.
9. scripts/windows-dev.ps1:115 — `cargo test` stops at the first failing test binary, so the summary CONTRIBUTING asks to note comes out short.
10. install.ps1:378 — the rollback `Move-Item $old $dest` in the catch had no guard; if it throws, the user is not told where the old binary went.
11. src/update.rs:148 — the name check against `moai.exe` was case-sensitive; Windows file names are not.
12. install.ps1:269 — `if ($item.LinkType)` also refuses HardLink; install.sh only refuses symlinks.
13. CONTRIBUTING.md:91 — "Until the Windows work ships, it lives on milestone/moai-c12a — check that out" reaches develop only at release, when the branch is gone.
14. src/update.rs:198 — `Plan.program` stored separately though it follows from `runner`; flags matched again in `plan()`.
15. src/latest.rs:274 — the USERPROFILE fallback in `home_from` has no effect on Windows: `upgrade_line` rejects names other than `moai` before reading home.

title: review — moai-j9gv 에픽 끝 셋째 (6kbo, MSYS2 인자 싸기)
MSYS2 빌드의 저장소 도구에 -C 뿌리를 MSVC 꼴로 싸 넘겨 따옴표 든 뿌리에서 진다
셸 밖에서 띄운 MSYS2 편집기가 따옴표 든 임시 경로를 잃는다

text:
Reviewer's report — /code-review max --fix 0a0c43c7..4719e7ac (model anthropic/opus-5.5). Measured under wine with MinGit 2.56.0.2's real sh.exe: all 49 hand-picked words reach sh unchanged with the new quoting (same as a port of Git's quote_arg_msys2); the old Command::args quoting got 35 through, dropping the `'` in `C:\Users\o'brien\…` and halving `\\`. Full editor flow with a temp dir under `…\o'brien\Temp` and an EDITOR with `\\` works end to end. ~33,600 random words round-trip through msys-2.0.dll (only batches with an unquoted `[]` word crash the runtime itself; Git leaves those unquoted too). docs/windows.md and CHANGELOG still match.

Findings:
1. src/cmd/tui.rs:1113 — the other Windows branch (no Git Bash) still quotes the MSVC way; an MSYS2-runtime editor (Git's nano.exe picked by default in PowerShell with usr\bin on PATH) loses the `'` in the temp path and the jot is lost. Same bug as moai-6kbo, branch from 048ca16d.
2. src/cmd/tui.rs:1107 — the temp path always contains `\`, so it is always quoted and goes through MSYS2's glob step; under a legacy LANG (ja_JP.SJIS) with a character the charset lacks, sh receives it with quotes and doubled backslashes. The old unquoted path arrived correctly.
3. src/cmd/tui.rs:1009 — msys_sh() looked sh up through PATHEXT, so a sh.cmd/sh.bat could be picked; Rust runs those through cmd.exe and raw args skip the batch escaping (measured: `%` and `&` in EDITOR break). Git only picks sh.exe.
4. src/cmd/tui.rs:1106 — no test runs the Windows-only wiring (quote then raw_arg); changing raw_arg to arg passes all of CI and breaks every Git Bash launch.
5. src/git.rs:184 — outside the diff: with MSYS2's own git build, `-C <root>` is quoted the MSVC way, so a `'` in the repo root breaks every git call and writes stop with unknown actor.
6. src/tui/jotfile.rs:250 — the quoting test never checks `'`, `"` or a plain space alone; removing `'` or `"` from the set leaves it green.
7. src/tui/jotfile.rs:100 — is_ascii_whitespace counts \x0C, Git's isspace does not; not an exact port as the docs say.
8. src/tui/jotfile.rs:88 — with MSYS=noglob MSYS2 strips quotes without unescaping, so the -c script breaks; not a regression (old quoting and Git's break the same), but the doc presents the quoting as unconditional.
9. src/tui/jotfile.rs:5 — module header leaves out msys_quoted.

Fixed: 3 (sh.exe only per PATH dir), 4 (msys_command + Windows-only test the_git_bash_sh_gets_raw_msys2_words; red under wine on revert to args and on arg), 6 and 7 (trigger set exactly Git's, checked byte-identical over 1.18M inputs; each trigger tested alone), 8 and 2 (doc notes only), 9.
Not fixed: 1 and 2 code side (needs a decision: detect MSYS2-runtime editors, or pass the temp path as `C:/…`); 5 (outside, backlog); 8 (no quoting works in both modes without leaving Git's).
Checks: Linux cargo test 2025 unit + 798 cli (BASH_ENV unset), clippy/fmt clean; Windows-gnu clippy clean. Wine prefix removed; a ~/.wine dated 07:56 from an earlier pass was left.

The working directory is not part of the command line, so MSYS2 does not split it. This goes one step past the literal C:/ wording for that one case; flagged in the report.

text:
Reviewer's report — /code-review max --fix ba144f36..b13a7b5a (model anthropic/opus-5.5). Linux 2028 unit + 798 cli (BASH_ENV unset), Linux clippy/fmt and Windows-target clippy clean. Under wine the failing set is the same 151 as at HEAD, plus 4 new tests that pass.

Wine measurements with MinGit's real sh.exe: a word starting with `~` is rewritten to the home directory when that file exists (the earlier `~/x` passed only because it did not exist); a word starting with `@` is replaced by that file's contents; `]`, a lone `}`, `^` and a leading `-` arrive unchanged; `//server/share/…` reaches a native editor unchanged.

Findings:
1. src/cmd/tui.rs:1167 — bare-name fallback plus a UNC temp dir: cmd.exe cannot start a .cmd/.bat editor there and moves to %SystemRoot%, so the editor opens a different file (TEMP=\\fs\home$\John Smith\Temp, EDITOR='code --wait'; jot lost). Worked at ba144f36.
2. src/cmd/tui.rs:1075 — when the fallback fires, current_dir moves the whole editor process: directory-changing wrappers lose the jot, a relative Git Bash EDITOR exits 127, project-local editor config is not found. A relative .cmd program is unaffected (Rust resolves it first; measured).
3. src/cmd/tui.rs:1086 — PREDATES (moai-08af): write_in_editor deletes the temp file even when read_to_string fails (non-UTF-8 save), destroying what was typed.
4. src/cmd/tui.rs:1072 — no test covered the new wiring; dropping current_dir or editor_target stayed green on Linux and under wine.
5. src/tui/jotfile.rs:135 — msys_word passed an empty word, a leading ~ and a leading @, and msys_command passed such editor words raw.
6. src/tui/jotfile.rs:48 — PREDATES (moai-08af): parse does not strip a UTF-8 BOM, so the title gets U+FEFF.
7. src/cmd/tui.rs:1162 — UNC temp dir with no special characters: native editors now get //server/share/…; editors reading a leading / as a switch drop the file (plausible, not measured).
8. src/cmd/tui.rs:1837 — the C:/ assertion compared Paths; on Windows Path equality ignores / vs \.
9. src/cmd/tui.rs:1119 — doc headlines (msys_command, editor_command, jotfile header, 6kbo test doc) no longer said what the code does.
10. docs/windows.md:91 — wrong file name, missing share spelling, impossible characters listed; CHANGELOG silent on the new spelling and the working-directory change.
11. src/tui/jotfile.rs:307 — msys_word's fails table lacked \n and \r.
12. src/tui/jotfile.rs:142 — forward_slashed plus unverbatim re-implemented path::slashed in UTF-16.
13. src/cmd/tui.rs:1158 — editor_target's logic was Windows-only, never run in CI.
14. src/tui/jotfile.rs:109 — the two character sets were written out twice (nit).
15. src/cmd/tui.rs:1143 — Unix editor_target twin was a no-op, bare name and cwd built in separate functions, unreachable `_` arm, l3pp asserts appended to the 6kbo test (nits).

Fixed: 4, 5, 8-15 — editor_target and current_dir together in the Windows editor_command (Unix byte-identical to ba144f36), new Windows test the_editor_command_starts_where_the_bare_name_is (red under wine without current_dir), Linux test the_editor_spelling_is_slashed_unless_msys2_would_change_it, msys_word rejects empty/leading ~/leading @ and only the temp-path word goes unquoted, path::slashed_os replaces forward_slashed and backs slashed, one MSYS2_SPECIAL constant, docs/CHANGELOG/CONTRIBUTING real-machine line.
Not fixed: 1 and 7 (need a decision — suggested guard: keep the full path for a UNC temp dir, at the cost of Git's nano.exe outside Git Bash in that case); 2 in code (cost of the bare-name path; documented). Trailing-dot `\\?\` case ruled out (Windows tidies TEMP first; measured). 3 and 6 predate this epic: backlog candidates.

Review: /code-review max --fix (agent ad1a8f2ea7294ab04), scope merge-base 6af6aebb..a86b5fcd

The review found 15 issues. I fixed 10 in the working tree, partly fixed 1 (the wording; the signal itself is unchanged), and left 4 that need a decision from you or the person. Nothing is committed. After the fixes, all 794 integration tests pass, clippy and rustfmt are clean, and one unit test fails. That test is `guide::tests::codex_report_watch_skips_the_baseline_and_ends_on_a_report`. It also fails on HEAD, because it uses `/root` and gets permission denied, and it is not part of this diff.

1. src/hook.rs:5907 — In crowded mode, rows this session is actually working on become unknown whenever their pick record is missing or out of date, not only rows picked in a terminal or by a hookless session.
   Scenario: Another session recorded a pick in the last 12h. (a) A review is started with `moai mv "$R" in_progress` (the documented `claim=$(moai mv "$id" …)` loop), `moai add -s in_progress`, or the TUI. The narrowed close_in then drops it from `open`, so `moai mv <review> done` with no `-m` passes rule 3, and Stop never mentions the review. (b) In `cargo test && moai mv X review`, if the tests take over 60s, `fold`'s SLACK rule discards both records. X becomes unknown for its own picker: Stop and compaction release it, rule 1 stops scoping to it, and rule 3 says 'holding nothing'. Before the diff these rows stayed in the picker's focus. NOT FIXED: needs a decision.
2. src/hook.rs:8217 — vouch explained every started row whose id appeared anywhere in the text, not the focus the decision was judged on. It also used base `own`, `load.issues` and a fresh second read of the picks, and checked the worktree name before this session's own pick.
   Scenario: A held row's title names t-9, which another session picked. The refusal or hold then printed 't-9  another session picked it up last' under 'Why this session holds them:'. Stray reviews and other people's reviews got lines too. A row held only because `sure` beat a closer sibling name was labelled 'this worktree's name points at it'. FIXED.
3. src/hook.rs:5802 — `crowded` is keyed on session ids and pick records. The session before /clear counts as another session. Hookless peers, and hooked peers that never move rows (the supervisor), never count.
   Scenario: A solo user who runs /clear is crowded for 12h, so terminal picks are released. A worker beside hookless sessions is never crowded and keeps their rows. vouch said 'no other session is running here' while one was running. PARTLY FIXED: the reason now says 'no other session recorded a pick here in the last 12 hours', and the docs describe the /clear case. The signal itself is the user's decision and is unchanged.
4. src/hook.rs:5999 — Dropping `$R` words meant variable-only pickers wrote no record at all, so they never made other sessions crowded. The filter also used Unicode `is_alphanumeric` and let the empty word through.
   Scenario: A worker that uses only the documented `"$id"` loop is invisible, so its rows stay in everyone's focus. `moai mv '' …` recorded an empty id, and non-ASCII words risked a torn UTF-8 read that drops that session's whole file. FIXED: such words now record a `Picks::UNNAMED` marker that counts only toward crowded, using an ASCII id character test shared with `git::words`.
5. src/hook.rs:6000 — `--from "$col"` was treated as a lost race, so a literal-id pick that won was not recorded.
   Scenario: `moai mv moai-ab12 in_progress --from "$col"` succeeds, nothing is recorded, and in crowded mode the picker loses its own row. FIXED: the pick is recorded as maybe-ran (`?`).
6. src/hook.rs:8238 — vouch's header and reasons were hard-coded English, appended to the Stop hold, which is built from the i18n bundle.
   Scenario: With MOAI_LANG=ko, the turn-end hold was Korean with an English tail, and the new CLI test (which runs in Korean) asserted the English lines. FIXED: added `hook.vouch_*` keys in en and ko. Stop uses the session's language; rule 1/3 refusals stay English, like their bodies.
7. src/hook.rs:5688 — A row this worktree's own name points at directly is dropped when its non-group parent is crowded and unrecorded.
   Scenario: A worktree named after child t-1.f, after /clear, with t-1 started in a terminal: t-1 becomes unknown and `theirs` drops t-1.f too. NOT FIXED: the code doc says descendants are removed 'regardless of distance' and a test pins it.
8. src/hook.rs:5802 — `saturating_sub` counted future-dated records as live.
   Scenario: If the clock steps back, or a line holds a huge corrupt number, crowded stays true until the clock catches up, and prune never removes a file with a future mtime. FIXED: `abs_diff`, which still accepts appends made during the read.
9. src/cmd/hook.rs:332 — Rule 1/3 refusals from other trackers were never given reason lines.
   Scenario: `moai -C <other project> add` was refused without the block that the same refusal carries in this tracker. FIXED.
10. src/cmd/hook.rs:324 — `read_picks` ran eagerly on every blocking decision, re-reading what settle and releasing had just read.
   Scenario: Every rule 2/4/5 deny, and every warnings-only hold, re-scanned the whole picks directory and threw the result away. FIXED: the picks read once inside settle/releasing are passed on.
11. src/cmd/hook.rs:761 — Narrowing can swap a rule 1 refusal naming the session's own unrecorded row for a rule 2 'holding nothing' refusal or rule 3's empty-focus text, with no hint why.
   Scenario: In a crowded repo, `moai add x && echo y >> src/a.rs` now gets 'holding nothing' instead of a refusal naming X. NOT FIXED: it would need a new reason surface.
12. src/hook.rs:8239 — The room check is all or nothing, after `fit` has already filled the hold.
   Scenario: On Codex (8000-byte hold) with many held rows, every reason is dropped. NOT FIXED: this is the documented trade-off.
13. docs/glossary.md:70 — The Focus text was inaccurate, the page's `Decided in:` line lacked moai-pyi4, and some code doc comments were stale.
   Scenario: The text contradicted moai-pxui (a row this session surely picked stays its own under a sibling name), left out the own-name exception, claimed every refusal gets reasons, and said 'Working alone' where the code means 'within 12h'. FIXED, along with the `Picks` and `record_picks` doc comments.
14. src/hook.rs:8250 — Two dead or duplicate pieces: the `!report::is_group` checks, and `names_whole`.
   Scenario: `report::wip` only returns issue rows, so the group checks never filter anything, and their comments and test claimed coverage that did not exist. `names_whole` re-implemented `git::words` and disagreed with it (`t-1를`, `t-1..x`). FIXED.
15. tests/cli.rs:15810 — Some test assertions could not fail.
   Scenario: The unit tests passed with a plain `contains` and with an `Away::picked` override that does nothing. The CLI test never checked worker2's pick, so if it broke the test would pass about one run in three, by id order. FIXED: the boundary and picked-child assertions are tightened, and worker2's pick and the crowded worker's rule 1 refusal are now asserted.

What I changed:
- src/cmd/hook.rs: `settle` now returns a `Settled` value (decision plus the rows, `Away` and picks it judged with), and `vouch` reads those. The same applies to other trackers' refusals.
- src/hook.rs: `vouch` lists only rows in that focus, with three reasons, checked in this order: this session picked it, the worktree name points at it, nobody recorded it. The rest of the record-handling fixes are in the table above.
- Other files: `id_char` and `words` in `src/git.rs` are now shared. New keys in `i18n/en.json` and `i18n/ko.json`. `docs/glossary.md` updated. Tests updated in both suites.

Decisions for you or the person:
- Finding 1 is the most serious one left. It weakens rule 3's closing-line requirement and drops the picker's own work from its Stop hold. Two options:
  - A narrow one: don't treat unrecorded rows under this session's recorded pick as unknown.
  - A root-cause one: have `moai mv` record the pick itself after the write, using `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` (Codex sets a foreign value, moai-sile). Telling "another session" apart by process (`CLAUDE_PID`) would also stop a /clear'd predecessor from counting.
- Findings 7, 11 and 12, plus the crowded signal itself (finding 3), are left as they stand for the same reason.
- The glossary was committed before this review. Re-check the wiki step (7-4) after you take these fixes as `fix:` commits. I updated the page to match the fixed behaviour.

**Fixed:**
- **fmt:** ran `cargo fmt --all`.
- **`shelved_by`:** corrected the docs in `src/cli.rs` help, `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/json.md`. The code is unchanged because `show <id>` has always emitted `shelved_by` this way.
- **`--fields` normalization:** `Keys::of` now trims each key and keeps it once, in first-seen order.
- **Skipping expensive keys:** `one()` now takes the selected keys and skips the journal, `git::table`, the sibling-worktree scan, the `Where` build and the read-marks lookup when none of their keys are selected. The human screen and the no-`--fields` output are unchanged.
- **`show <id>` cost:** fixed only for `--fields` (see above).
- **`progress` docs:** corrected in help, CHANGELOG, json.md and the field comment.
- **Double refusal:** `tui` now finds the repo before refusing on screen, so outside a `.moai` both forms get the same message.
- **Time-filter pointer:** added a line to `tui --help` pointing at `moai show --help`.
- **Duplicate measuring:** `listing` now borrows the explorer's existing filter state through `Ground::here`, which I made `pub(crate)` in `src/tui/mod.rs`.
- **`keep`:** now just calls `filter.matches`.
- **Tests:** added `show_json_marks_a_moved_row_archived_with_the_clock_off` and confirmed it fails when the `stored` line is removed. Added a `--fields 'id, title,id'` check, plus `--reverse` and outside-refusal checks to the tui test.
- **`docs/cli.md`:** regenerated with `MOAI=target/debug/moai scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh`.

**Skipped:**
- **Key order under `--fields`:** fixing it needs a serde_json feature change (`raw_value` or `preserve_order`), which is a dependency change.
- **`naming()` in config.rs:** the fix is a `Naming` method in `src/config.rs`, outside the diff.
- **Default `show <id> --json` cost:** a cheaper path would mean adding a lighter query to `query`, so I left it.

One unrelated failure: `guide::tests::codex_report_watch_skips_the_baseline_and_ends_on_a_report` fails in this session's shell. `BASH_ENV=~/.bashrc` puts `~/.local/bin` (which holds a `moai`) ahead of the test's fake one. It passes with `env -u BASH_ENV cargo test`.

/code-review xhigh --fix (agent-adb6278ba3fd879bd) — reviewer's words

I found 13 problems in the diff and fixed 11. The fixes are in the working tree, uncommitted, for you to take in as a separate `fix:` commit. The diff is all instruction text plus its tests: the supervisor and worker step files in `src/guide.rs` and the plugin copies generated from them.

Tests: `cargo test --no-fail-fast` gives 2023 passed and 1 failed in the binary's tests, and 802 passed in `tests/cli.rs`. The one failure is `guide::tests::codex_report_watch_skips_the_baseline_and_ends_on_a_report`. It fails the same way before and after my edits, and outside the sandbox too: the test's fake `moai` is never used, the real binary runs instead and hits `/root: Permission denied`. That test covers `REPORT_WATCH`, which this diff doesn't touch. `cargo fmt --check` is clean.

I regenerated the plugin copies with `MOAI_BLESS=1 cargo test checked_in`, so `plugin.json` changed too.

1. src/guide.rs:2477 — The supervisor's 'member refused:' rule always says to unfold the parked backlog, but the worker's 4-3 lets the worker unfold it itself in 7-1 and say so in that same line. Scenario: the hook lets the worker's promote through in 7-1 and the report line says so. The supervisor still runs `backlog promote ... -e <epic>`, which also unfolds a closed backlog item, so the same member exists twice.
2. src/guide.rs:4829 — The work of a subagent worker's own subagents is never recorded: 9-1 asks for a line per subagent, but subagent workers skip 9-1, and the report and the supervisor's step 5 carry only one `Model ran:`. Scenario: a subagent worker hands write-path code to an opus subagent; the supervisor writes only the worker's own model, and the opus share disappears from `work` and `moai stats`.
3. src/guide.rs:4854 — The check for members without a `model:` line lists every member of the epic with an empty `work`, including ones earlier windows finished, and tells the current worker to write its own line on each (the supervisor's check at 2511 has the same gap). Scenario: an epic handed over at step 2 or as stalled work after another window closed members without lines; the new worker writes its own model on work it never did — a false line.
4. src/guide.rs:2383 — Codex workers get the same message, so `Subagents:` arrives filled with Claude models and worker.md tells them to call `Agent(...)`; the supervisor text allowed `none` only when the person says so.
5. src/guide.rs:2382 — The `Subagents:` list carries models but no effort, while the supervisor raises its own workers with each role's effort. Scenario: a write-path piece handed to the `complex` subagent runs at default effort instead of `effort_complex`.
6. src/guide.rs:380 — The tracker-out-of-git check was tied to 'the first tracker commit in 2'; a worker started from 'Carrying on stalled work' never runs step 2, so it never asks, and `git commit -- .moai/` fails with 'pathspec did not match'.
7. src/guide.rs:374 — The check used a path relative to the current directory. Scenario: the supervisor stands in `<root>/src`; `git ls-files --error-unmatch -- .moai/issues.jsonl` fails there, so a tracked tracker reads as outside git and every `Sent:` and `Report-checked:` commit is skipped.
8. src/guide.rs:4626 — 4-3 and 7 tell the worker to look for the English heading `Why this session holds them:`, but the hook writes that heading in the screen's language and leaves the lines out when the refusal would run too long.
9. src/guide.rs:4305 — In the subagent path, the review brief's hand-back never says the review was done by hand, so the worker cannot add `manual` to the review issue's model line.
10. src/guide.rs:8451 — The test's guard `include_str!("hook.rs").contains("Why this session holds them:")` matches a test assertion inside hook.rs, not the real text in `i18n/en.json` (`hook.vouch_head`).
11. src/guide.rs:4387 — The `Subagents:` instructions have no fallback for when `Agent` refuses a model name from the person's table.
12. src/guide.rs:2511 — The supervisor checks session workers' lines only after writing `Report-checked:`, and asks the worker by message right after the worker told its person the window can be cleared. Scenario: the supervisor restarts, reads `Report-checked:` and never re-runs the check.
13. src/guide.rs:4211 — The missing-line check needs `jq`, while the supervisor skill parses everything else with python3. On a machine without jq the pipe prints nothing, which can read as "no member is missing a line".

Fixed (1–11):
- 1: the supervisor writes only `- issue` lines and does not unfold when the line says the worker reclaimed it or the backlog item is already done.
- 2: step 12 adds one `Subagent ran: anthropic/<name> on <member>` line per subagent; 9-1 points at it; supervisor's 5 writes those lines.
- 3: both checks leave out members finished before the epic reached this worker, and say that writing your model on work you didn't do is a false line.
- 4: the list is `none` for Codex workers, and `worker-codex.md` says `Subagents:` does not apply.
- 5: the list reads `bulk <model> (<effort>) · develop <model> (<effort>) · complex <model> (<effort>)`, and the worker's call passes `effort: <its effort>`.
- 6, 7: the check is `git -C <root> ls-files --error-unmatch -- .moai/issues.jsonl`, asked before the first tracker commit — the one in 2, or whichever comes first. The real-git test now runs it from a subdirectory.
- 8: the text says the heading follows the screen's language and may be missing.
- 9: the review brief's hand-back puts `Manual review` on its second line, and step 10 reads it there.
- 10: the test compares against `crate::i18n::say(Lang::En, "hook.vouch_head")`.
- 11: if `Agent` refuses a model, the worker does that piece itself.
- Test assertions added for each.

Skipped:
- 12: fixing it means reordering the supervisor's step 5 — a design change, low risk.
- 13: jq is already used throughout this repository's guides, low risk.
